content: On the whole I like Schiphol the signage to the BA check-in is non existent - I nearly always struggle to find them and I travel through several times a year. BA Lounge is small but tranquil the staff are always welcoming. It is a long walk from check-in and the walk to the gates is usually quite long as well. In some ways I prefer the gates that are the furthest as they have a mini 'central security' which means that premium passengers can have priority boarding. Most of the gates have individual security which means queuing up at the gate for security and again to board the plane. It seems an inefficient use of manpower. As I usually only stay in the Netherlands for a short time I avoid checking in baggage - the wait for bags to arrive is lengthy. The only other complaint is the taxi to the gate when arriving it can be in excess of 15 minutes. In summary not the worst used to be one of the best - but definitely needs more than a band-aid to put it in my favourites again.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: D Kennerley
content: Over the years used Schipol a lot but had a long break the past 10+ years. Facilities that a new since my last trip much appreciated - and used - Ryjksmuseum and library. Toilets were clean and fully stocked. Long distances as most people mention but with 5.5 hours hold over not a problem. Very poor boarding arrangements with long queue and slow process. Appreciate need for proper vigilance and doing a thorough job but something needs to be done to speed up the process - more checking devices/staff? Flight delayed all down to slow procedure. I was near to last in the queue and so far as I can tell no passengers were late. Could see staff beginning to panic as time went on. One issue I have is with Airport personnel zooming around on electric vehicles. They drive at breakneck speeds relative to the fact that the airport is always fairly congested with passengers.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: David Tjan
content: I made more then twenty flights this year mostly from Schiphol. This September I departed from Schiphol four times. 3 times Schengen lounge and 1 time intercontinental. I have to say that Schiphol is becoming more and more outdated and is rapidly losing ground with major Asian competitors like HKG SIN and Seoul Incheon and Munich and Madrid in Europe. It's overcrowded congested not passenger friendly and the terminal buildings are getting old and claustrophobic. During peak times going through security on the Schengen side is like standing in line in Disney world with endless waiting cues. One time it took me over 40 minutes to pass security. For the first time I noticed how dirty it became especially the dining area above the Schengen departure hall. All tables were full of dirty plates left behind for several hours without cleaning. Food choice was also very poor. The staff tends to be arrogant and non service minded. I am also surprised how uninviting the immigration area is. A small dark corner when entering the Netherlands. Baggage claim is terrible small long wait and sometimes I feel as If I'm on a marketplace with no space at all to move. Usual wait lasts more then 30 minutes for baggage to unload and counting. I wish I could be more positive but I do think Schiphol needs a major upgrading to maintain it position as a big player in Europe.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: D Macleod
content: I come through Schiphol probably four times a year for the last twenty years or so and still say it is my favourite airport. It is a sizeable airport and consequently we have to walk distances but I have never found a problem with signs or with time available. There can be long queues at passport control and at security at times but I have always found the staff friendly and welcoming. Yesterday incidentally transferring from a flight from the UK to a flight to Finland I was through passport check and security in less than five minutes; not always so I know but the staff have always made the transfer relatively easy as far as I am concerned. I also love the opportunity to use the excellent Dutch bars and the attractive shops; probably the only airport I use where I really take an interest in the retail opportunities.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: P Dalloz
content: Clean and good facilities but badly managed security. Cant take drinks (even duty free) in hand luggage. Long queues waiting in the tunnel to get off the plane. Officious security people and intrusive body scanners.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Azlan Hashim
content: I arrived from Kuala Lumpur on transit for my flight to Helsinki on the 7th of September. For some reasons I had to collect my luggage and recheck-in at AMS. There were huge queue on both at the check-in and passport control area. A long walk at this airport is very common. Eventually it was almost an hour from the beginning of my check-in time to the departure gate. My suggestion to those are going to use AMS for their start or transit point have yourself present at least 2 hours at the airport before your departure time. On my departure back to Kuala Lumpur on the 14th of September I was surprised when there was almost no queue at the check-in counter. Especially the designated counter for web check-in service. The agent was friendly. As usual there was a long queue at the passport control and a long walk to the departure gate. In general the airport is clean. The food chains and toilets are plentiful. 2 or 3 hours of free wifi is a regular practise in most of the airports worldwide. I hope AMS would apply that in the future and I bet passengers will happy and appreciate it!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Andrews
content: Three hour transfer at Schipol. Lot's of seats food outlets and toilets all very clean. Long walk between gates but was OK as I had plenty of time. Lots of shops for those who like that kind of thing. Museum was a fun way of killing time. Security at gates was quick and efficient but many passengers ignorant of security at the gates and wandered up for their flights very late causing delays (read the boarding pass for goodness sake). All the airport staff I encountered very friendly and all spoke English.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: A Sandhu
content: DEL-AMS-IAD. We had a 6 hour layover on the return flight airport was good with easy to access facilities but a long walk to the gate lots of stores and shopping and many things to do to pass time such as taking a tour of the city which you can schedule at the airport.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Alan Finch
content: Usual efficient experience in Schipol large distances to walk but as travelling to Canada no need for Schengen. Only disappointment - can only access roof terrace from departure hall otherwise trouble free.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: C Neville
content: Very good airport friendly staff - who even have a sense of humour! Easy to get around excellent connections to UK and elsewhere good facilities and very nice Business lounge.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Alastair Finch
content: 2 long layovers at Schipol recently can stretch ones legs walking the long distance from one end to the other. Facilities excellent only downside is one can only access the roof from the arrivals hall. However it remains one of my favourite airports.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: A Van de Wiel
content: I always enjoy Schiphol airport. It is clean has good facilities and great shopping. There is even a library. The distances between gates are sometimes quite long but everything is easily reached. Luggage handling is excellent there is a fully automatic luggage drop off and a passport scanner so you do not have to stand in line anymore. Even at the busy holiday season these processes are quick and efficient.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Cioboata
content: Great and efficient airport. Facilities at the airport are excellent I especially enjoyed the annex of the Rijksmuseum which had very interesting paintings on display. Numerous shops to browse and plenty of eateries. One thing I missed was a proper sit-down service like. Signage and layout is easy to navigate however distances can be long but on a positive note it at least allows for healthy exercise between flights. One thing I really appreciated was that the security check is done at the gate which makes it less stressful and prevents endless queues as seen at airports with a central security check however reviewers seem to have a different opinion about it.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Pat Theo
content: We flew in and out of Amsterdam. I don't mind walking a bit but this is a large airport and it was a bit much especially if you are short of time. Full body pat down I moaned to the woman doing it and she was sympathetic and said how much she hated Amsterdam it was too busy and dirty for her! As for transferring nothing would induce me to go via this airport to anywhere even if it is the cheap option! The loos we used weren't very clean and needed maintenance. Food options looked good but we didn't have time to get more than a sandwich. We have friends arriving there today (and coming on to the UK) en route from Detroit I just hope they don't have much hassle their flight was already put back 5 hours so will have missed their connecting flight and we will have more hours to wait and a full body pat down might be the last straw! I suppose being able to look at some exhibits from the Riksmuseum whilst they are waiting might compensate a little.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: G Cramer
content: I frequently use Schiphol Airport. The terminal is clearly labelled. The facilities are clean the stores are interesting. Food service is varied and also good. Parking and transportation is very well organized. It's an excellent airport except for one big thing: passport control. It is completely unacceptable to routinely wait between 30 minutes and an hour just to show your passport (mind you this does not include going through scanners and such it's merely showing your passport). The lines are typically enormous hundreds of people squashed into one area. Usually there are several booths unoccupied even though the lines are enormous. Despite all it's many great qualities Schiphol needs to serve people better at passport control. Below it asks me if I would recommend the airport. Of course what other choice does one have in The Netherlands.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Farouk Mogheth
content: Flew through AMS on my flight from Prague to Cairo and return. The Airport is easy to navigate through loads of venues to eat and relax in the walking distances can get a tad too long if you connect from the EU to non EU terminals. Self transfer counters are great still with some nice staff assisting. SKY Priority works well in all parts of the airport. Unfortunately the self-passport control gates were not working so the lines were long even in the EU zone passport holders. Each passport and ID were closely controlled by the officers under magnifying glasses. The remainder is a breeze a very nice airport to fly through no complains at all except the "charged" internet.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: N de Goffau
content: I fly often through this airport and for me I consider this as one of the most convenient airports. Plenty of facilities are available and the intelligent lay-out provides the advantage that no bus transport between terminals is needed what is unique for an airport of this size. Also every plane has its own gate what allows you direct walking access to the terminals. Handling of luggage is usually quickly finished and the transition below the airport makes that you can be very quick in Amsterdam. In summer times queuing might take a while but on average I have seen it much worse. Prices for food are relatively high. About transfers I cannot judge.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Ludewig
content: I find this airport well organized for transferring flights. Less hassle than CDG for sure. Calculate some walking time but overall it works pretty good using AMS to change flights. I have been doing this quite a few times and it always was no problem.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Brian Hunter
content: I traveled through Schiphol Airport twice in June 2012. Since I was there in 2009 they have made Schiphol the most invasive airport from a security imaginable. Not only is a full body scan required but now all passengers (except children) are then subjected to a manual pat down. Are these multi-million Euro full scan machines less effective than the previous scanners requiring an additional fondling of passengers? I noticed that that the children are not placed in full body scanners but rather are walked though the old type scanner and after that are not subject to pat down. No doubt the scanner manufacturers have made billions of Euros selling machines that apparently have made the process more invasive and less effective. I will avoid this airport in future as this "new" technology makes the already ridiculous airport security process completely unacceptable.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: P Merriett
content: The airport is too large if you are transferring flights and are on a short time line. The restrooms are unkempt dirty and smell horrible. The security is inept and ridiculous they made me damage my own clothing in order to move through the security check point. The staff in the airport seem highly offended if you are just transferring planes in their country instead of staying. My family and I will be avoiding this airport from here on out. Highly unprofessional rude and unacceptable.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: L Dilling
content: Transit in AMS. Non-Schengen to Schengen return. Arrival time was 3pm and we found the Airport surprisingly empty. I am an EU-Passport holder my Partner is Mexican and I had no issues passing with her through the much shorter EU Passport holder line at immigration. Security check took 15 minutes. Distances at AMS are quite long we had 2 hours for transit which gave some time to stroll around the shopping mile. From all airports we visited on this trip AMS has the best Duty Free offers. On the return to Mexico we arrived in AMS in the Morning around 11 and the Airport was packed. Lines were long at immigration but we could again use the EU Passport line which reduced waiting to 15 minutes. Security check done at the gate which saved time. Staff friendly and efficient. Big Airport long distances AMS is stress free if your transit is 1 hour or less it might get stressful at peak hours.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: L Scott
content: I have transferred through Schiphol numerous times easily and this time was no different. The simple gate numbering system and one terminal concept meant I could rush though with ease and still go to the duty free shop with only a very short transfer time and Information staff are very helpful. Because of this when I book flights I only ever transfer through Schiphol (with KLM) and avoid going through Paris CDG (with Air France) at all costs.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: D Marshall
content: Used for flight transfer both ways. Toilets overflowing in both cases. System confusing. Worst of all was the security staff at gate D6 - very unprofessional and blunt to the point of rudeness. Very much a cattle market. I sympathise with some airlines who try to provide a good service but are let down by airport service providers in terms of the overall flying experience for customers. The airlines have enough collective influence to get things changed why don't they?

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Brian E Smith
content: A completely functional airport but not as good as expected. It seems very institutional with lots of stainless steel and many areas were crowded (check-in and at the gates). I found it difficult to transfer between a domestic European flight and an intercontinental one as the terminals were at opposite ends. Toilets are clean! Good food and shopping opportunities. Getting into the city is easy if you're going to Amsterdam. The security is fierce! The first time I've experienced a full body pat down.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Glazebrook
content: We will never travel through Schipol again. We had a long layover and could find nowhere to relax let alone snooze. Gates have fewer than half the number of seats needed for a flight and passengers line up like cattle in metal railing-defined queues. Security scanning is done at the gate. Process of checking in poorly handled by grouchy staff. The bathroom I was able to find near our gate was not very clean or private.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Bryan Clark
content: First time in Schiphol for 20 years and it is the easiest and user friendly of major airports. KLM ground staff and immigration made our transfer a pleasure despite time being against us.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Jens Jensen
content: Were very close on time arrived 10 minutes before check-in closed but still able to check-in just before check-in closed. Shuttle busses all the time which take around 10 minutes to Terminal 3. Passport control very easy and just after check-in. You can avoid the shops and walk straight to gates. Very easy to find with wide walkways and loads of rolling bands. Security check into waiting room was not so pleasant 5 minutes waiting time but the security guys were rude. On the way home passport control was very smooth but there was a long wait for our baggage.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: P Vandenbroeck
content: Antwerp-Bangkok via Amsterdam with KLM. Arriving at the airport was a mess airport staff very rude and unhelpful. We had to queue for 2 hours at check-in. We were then brought to another check in were they told us we had 5 minutes to get to the gate. We ran to the gate and just made it (last passengers to board). To top it all off the plane didn't move for another 45 minutes! Horrible experience will avoid using Schiphol.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Poultney
content: If you have a short transit time please avoid this airport. It is very large and there is a lot of walking to do between gates. The worst are the KLM staff who can be extremely unfriendly rude and dismissive when you need their help. Never fly into this airport when there is any delay in Amsterdam due to bad weather or any other unforeseen circumstances because staff can't cope. You will be left stranded for hours or days and they won't bother to help you find hotel accommodation.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Angelo Tzarevski
content: JNB-AMS-ORD return. Transferred at Schiphol both ways. This is a very clean and well organised airport. Gates are easy to find with maps and signs everywhere which are easy to understand and follow. There are a number of rest areas with very comfortable seating (especially the ones on the top floor of Terminal 3). They are very quiet and comfortable. The airport also offers shower facilities although I am not sure if there are any free ones. I used the facilities at the Mercure Hotel in the transit area which cost 15 euros but if you are transferring between two long flights the price is worth it. Staff are friendly and helpful. There are decent duty free shops albeit not many. Schiphol is an absolute pleasure to transfer through.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: S Triantafyllou
content: Overall the best airport when it comes to duty free smoking lounges cafes etc. The worst when it comes to immigration staff - expect a 40 min-1 hr wait if travelling outside Europe. Recommended if your layover is long!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Bergers
content: Overall it looks clean. The duty free shops are overpriced. Their system can be confusing mixing up arrival and departures. The biggest problem however is the security staff and police. Not friendly and at times arrogant or short tempered. Security is not well organized. In a short transit I would skip this airport. Travelling in Europe there are better options. Due to the very unfriendly atmosphere I would rate this airport poor.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Martin
content: In every other airport we have been in the departure lounge comes after the security checks on people and hand luggage. Therefore at Schiphol we threw away our water and left-over drinks before proceeding into the departure lounge thinking the next step would be the X-ray machines. However the main security checks in this airport are just as you are called to the gate before getting on the plane. Wish we had known. We didn't have a delay but if you do it's nice to know that you are able to keep your own drinks until just before getting on the plane. This does save paying extortionate prices in the departure lounge. Why don't more airports do this? We can recommend Schiphol airport.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: A Lepik
content: Clean and spacious (during the odd hours) toilet facilities are good. Signage is quite good sometimes a bit confusing. Immigration is fairly speedy but can be rude and arrogant depending on the officer. Airport staff is dismissive and has a definite attitude problem. Drink and food prices are extortionate many vending machines are not working. Too few resting areas for the amount of passengers during peak hours there are no places to sit. Getting around can be difficult as the trolleys cannot be taken to lower floors freely.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Martin Walker
content: What a great airport. Staff are helpful and kind it's clean the signage is perfect. Transportation into and out of the airport by train is very easy. They have even got smokers lounges. Recognising reality is a lost trait these days. Clearly Schipol has it's thinking head on. All airports should be like this.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Yevheniy Kahanovych
content: My last experience at AMS was 40 minute transit. Having had boarding pass issued at departure point for the whole connection with no AMS gate number I was trying to find gate number on monitors at the arrival gate - but no monitors! Luckily there was a pool of KLM self service machines where I printed new boarding pass that showed my gate number (the most remote D28). I went there to be searched at the gate and just made my connection. No issues with security staff (polite efficient and competent) no issues with KLM gate staff (nice and were able to track my baggage immediately). No issues with toilets (clean well kept) easy signage lots of KLM self service kiosks. But please put some more monitors at the arrival gate areas!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: M Stav
content: I have flown through Amsterdam more than 20 times. A big airport with a lot of walking to be done. Its clean and bathroom facilities are frequent. The central area is full of shops and bars generally overpriced as a beer will run you 6-8 euros. All in all okay however staff and security procedures could be considered intimidating. Most times you go through a security check twice you get questioned one on one about your baggage and your entire day. The only thing I cant understand is their policy with duty free. If you bring a sealed bottled in the duty free vacuum sealed bag with a receipt from another airport they will confiscate it. Originally I thought this was a one time thing but over the years I have lost 3-4 bottles in that airport. I have been to over 100 airports and this is the only airport where this is apparently policy. Besides the duty free stance the high prices and the over the top security procedures I can't complain.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: P Slumders
content: The airport has a lot of facilities plenty of room a nice atmosphere and efficient layout. Sometimes you have the problem with a short transit to have to run from one side of the airport on the other side.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Y Tabib
content: Airport Plaza is great better shopping options expected post check-in. Checking in can be crazy with long queues expect to do everything yourself self service check-in and baggage drop. Need more baggage drop machines and courteous staff.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Newt Paulson
content: I stopped in this airport for a couple of hours on my return from Italy to the USA since Amsterdam is a hub for Delta Airlines and for some reason I did not have a direct flight back to the states on my return. First we had to stand in a line for passport control to go from one terminal to another. If my flight were in the same terminal I would have just gotten on the plane but as it was not I had to go and have my passport stamped to enter a terminal - surely the workers realize the people going to the other side of the terminal are leaving Amsterdam and this was a waste of time. Then there was a huge line as they do security at the gate however the line was huge and there are not enough seats at the gate. I walked across the hall and sat for 30+ minutes until the line died down and then went through security. It seemed to me if you went through the line early not only would you be waiting in this huge line but then you would be in this "holding area" until you boarded the plane with no restroom. The screening is very advanced they scan a color copy of your passport and ask you questions and even have body scanner machines which I asked if I could bypass they agreed and were professional but still I prefer the Italian airports where there is much less rigmarole involved. Schiphol reminded me of a USA/TSA airport which I do not care for although they were mostly polite and efficient to me I think I would skip it next time.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: C Liu
content: A supposedly major transit airport. The priority lane at custom for flights with short connection time helps nothing at all people still queue up and the office allowed people with a small window of time before takeoff to jump the queue. Our boarding gate had even closed with no last call announcement. The high speed footpath was not operating we all had to run from one end of the pier to another. The flight reconnection kiosk supposedly to allow better access for passengers who miss the flight and reduce the staff workload. Yet the system simply couldn't find our entry. People still have to approach the transfer counter and the number of KLM staff were so few while people anxiously waiting to be helped were so many. It was another long queuing process. With all of the above do we still have the time and mood to enjoy the facilities this airport can offer?

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: A Crawford
content: OSL to MSP through AMS on Delta. The extra security check at the gate for the AMS to MSP flight was expected what was not expected was being physically hit by the Dutch equivalent of TSA. The trays for laptops passing through the metal detector are sized to handle pocket change. I was worried that my laptop would fall from the tray. I walked through the whole body scanner all the while pre-occupied with what was happening with my laptop. After exiting the body scanner I walked over to the metal detector to retrieve my laptop. Next thing I know this TSA guy is hitting me on the back and yelling 'I'm not finished with you'. I was completely surprised and taken aback. There were no signs or people waiting just after exiting the body scanner saying I should stay put. I told the TSA guy that I didn't know I had done anything wrong and he yelled again that he wasn't finished. For those Americans who constantly complain about USA TSA try flying through AMS. Unlike other reviewers I did find AMS to be a clean airport especially given it's size. As for walking times it's a large airport so what do you expect.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: L Thomas
content: Having travelled several times to Schiphol Airport twice with a young child I can say that the only complaint I would have is that we were delayed while waiting to board the plane we waited down the steps and with a pram and a small child had I not have been travelling with my mother it would have been extremely difficult to manage both. Lovely clean airport with numerous facilities.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Jim Elder
content: I transferred at Schipol and I had to go through 3 full security checks with large queues at 2 of these. Very poorly organised facilities only good thing was security staff were less unpleasant than usual. Airport is great for shoppers I guess but I would avoid it if at all possible.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Gómez
content: It seems a good airport but to make a transfer there could be a nightmare. I don't know if KLM is responsible for choosing the gates but if you by a ticket with a short connection is normal that from one gate to the other you have to run 2 km. Security control is awful but I have to say staff were very friendly.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Alastair Finch
content: Have changed here many times. Though it is very busy and walking distances can be lengthy the degree of organization is good though the schengen passport queue is tiresome. Facilities are good and clean. I do miss being able to go on the roof terrace however. A second security check while transiting is tiresome but a sign of the time however a single terminal albeit very large is great and my family love the shops.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: A Smith
content: Arrived at Schiphol 4 days ago for a 2 month holiday in The Netherlands. One passport check as I left the plane and easily found my way to the luggage area then to the customs gate with virtually no waiting time. Only showed my passport to the official and was asked reason duration and location of my stay in perfect English. Only moments later I was at the exit of the airport wondering how it'd been so easy after the nightmare 4 hour stop at Guangzhou airport.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: D Hartono
content: Its a good and spacious airport it also has a large variety of shops & restaurants. The airport itself is very clean and the washroom is also very clean and there is almost no queuing at immigration.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Azlan Hashim
content: I was on transit to BUD. KLM transfer desk staff efficient and helpful. The airport receives so many international arrivals in the early morning. To my surprise the immigration counters were understaffed. I was travelling alone and travelling light. However I was in the queue for about 45 minutes. Pity to those families travelling with small children. Obviously queuing after coming from a long haul flight is not a pleasant experience for them.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: T Bos
content: Airport is too big. The walking distances could be very long and it will take some time. In general the people working on the airport are friendly but not very helpful. The security people seems not really motivated.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Jerome Vanderberg
content: My wife and I flew KLM from Schiphol to JFK last week - the worst and most offensive security arrangement we have seen. The security check is done by a team at each of the gates prior to boarding. When the start of the security check was announced we stood in a long line and had no opportunity to prepare ourselves by emptying pockets removing jackets taking out computers etc. People standing in line finally came to the single checkpoint where a woman barked out orders like a drill sergeant to move on through quickly. The people operating the full body scanner were competent and professional. Once we had passed through security we assumed that boarding the airplane was to begin shortly. Instead we were kept for 2 hours. in an overcrowded holding pen that seemed to have been designed for cattle. The holding pen had no toilets and a single machine for selling water. I lost 3 euros in it without a bottle coming out and when I asked the KLM agent nearby she replied brusquely (without looking up) that the airline had nothing to do with the machine. A short time later I saw a Dutch gentleman go through the same procedure. I walked over to the counter where he spoke to the same KLM employee. He said that he had lost his money in the machine and asked if he could exchange a 5 euro bill for coins so that he could try again. The agent dismissed him saying "I am not a bank!". He was told a place in the airport where he could report the problem but came back later saying that they could not help him there. I elected not to go with him because I was informed that I would have to go through the entire security routine again and that we would be getting water on the airplane. Later on in the airplane the captain apologized for the long delay explaining that it was due to the fact that the airplane had arrived late from its previous flight. Obviously the security people knew this so it was puzzling why they rushed us through so quickly knowing that we would have to stand in the holding pen for hours before being able to board the airplane.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: R van Beuningen
content: Its signs are easy to follow many shops and bars/eating places a train station in the arrivals hall many connections and no annoying loss of time because for commuting between terminals. Security is slow (and not always performed by the most intelligent amongst us) taxiing can take some time as does the baggage arrival.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: M Jonkman
content: As a Dutchman I'm no longer proud on this airport. It has grown too big. It took us 2 hours from entering the airport terminal until arriving at the designated gate. Because we were flying inside the Schengen area luckily we didn't have to pass passport control.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: C O'Neill
content: On entering through the main door you are actually in the bus/train station. It takes a little searching then to find out where to go as most signage here is given over to trains and buses - through here signs are easy to follow. The only thing is the sheer distance to walk but there are moving walkways. Check in and security a breeze (they have the new scanners that 'see through' your clothes) with a good array of food and shopping outlets. Arrived at and flew from the 'economy pier' H the departure lounge of which was a box really a bit too warm with only a dozen or so seats!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: C Bekkelund
content: Schiphol is probably the worst organized airport I've been to. First impression was when we arrived from Gardermoen/Oslo airport to Amsterdam. The people waiting for the plane back to Oslo from Amsterdam was partly sitting partly lying on the floors in what seemed like a never ending tunnel from the gate to the main area. There were a couple of seats every third mile or so. When we were leaving Amsterdam and Schiphol the airport left an even worse impression as we first had to stand in line forever for security check. There were two lines/security check points to the M-gates so a long queue must be quite normal here. What are they thinking? When we finally managed to go through security check we wanted to buy the necessities from the tax- free shop (we live in Norway prices are much higher than in tax free so this is something we need to take advantage of) then find a restaurant to get some dinner. At the lounge area we were very disappointed. The tax-free shop was about the size of a large kiosk and the only place to get some food was actually a kiosk with sandwiches and a tiny desk that sold coffee and cakes of some sort. We did not quite believe it at first since Schiphol is one of the worlds biggest airports but it was actually true. After finding a couple of sandwiches it was not that easy to find somewhere to sit. The people behind Schiphol apparently think that people like to stand straight up for two hours. Well.. Amsterdam was great but the airport not so great. Bring a chair your own food and try not to come to early to the airport since it's actually nothing to do not even shopping. Which means you do not have to bring money since Schiphol apparently doesn't want your money.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: R Eveleens
content: Did quite a few flights with Easyjet I had to depart from either the M (schengen) or H (non- schengen) gates. After 5 flights not once did I have to wait longer for security then 3 minutes. The H-gates offer only a small overpriced place where you can buy drinks before boarding as do the vending machines at the gate area The M-gates offer a small lounge with possibility to buy a few items but don't go in there too early since there is not much to do you better of in Schiphol plaza. H or M gates use preboarding which means you are put into a holding pen but as they only open the gate when the flight is due to arrive you not have to spend ages. Trainstation is below Schiphol it offers easy connections to Amsterdam or other cities.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: J Steele
content: Transit via Amsterdam on return to LHR from GRU. Someone told me Schiphol was a great airport and especially easy to navigate. Well that aspect might be true but everything else was awful. The worst thing is there's just nowhere to sit - there are about 20 seats by each gate (hardly close to being enough!) and we couldn't find any anywhere else. I guess they want you to have no option but to wander round the many shops (the same repeated over and over) and spend your money! Starbucks was packed with people who'd finished their coffee and stayed in their seats because there was nowhere else to go. Then 'boarding' started - except they re-screen all your hand baggage before you can go through and with only one person and one x-ray machine it was absolute chaos! They did apologise for how long it took but we couldn't see how with that system it could ever take any less time! Be warned - take a cushion and be prepared to be late!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: G Bezuidenhout
content: I had the misfortune to travel through Schipol on my way to Boston. When we landed we were stranded on the plane for over 4 hours because we could not get to a gate apparently due to the snow. Once inside the filthy airport our connecting flight to Boston was cancelled but only after we had gone through security and forced to wait in the disgusting holding pen with no flushing toilets for hours. From the holding pen we were told we needed to rebook our tickets and that there were no vouchers available for food or hotels. At this stage nearly all the flights in the airport had been cancelled and there was queue literally a mile long waiting for rebookings. I waited in this queue for over 12 hours I slept in the queue I even met new people in the queue. There were contradicting stories being given by ground staff. There were no blankets or beds provided. The floor was filthy. It was the worst experience I have ever had. The worst part of my story is that when we finally got to the front of the queue the next morning we were told we could use our boarding pass from the previous day and just go to the gate. They made us stand in the queue for 12 hours for nothing! I will never set my foot in Schipol ever again.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: David Gordon
content: Two recent experiences connecting at AMS for onward flights to the UK (LHR MAN). Totally inadequate staffing of the security check at the gate both times - only one lane open security therefore so slow that flight departures delayed by ~30 minutes. This is unacceptable and KLM should press Schiphol to make gate security in the non-Schengen area much quicker.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Justin Bell
content: I have been through Amsterdam many times and know the airport well. My main comments today (2010) is that it is a fairly easy airport to use great shopping lots of airline lounges if you have time between connections and are a privileged member of a frequent flyer programme plenty of toilets / rest rooms some left luggage safes restaurants internet access etc. It has the advantage of not being as big as London Heathrow or some of the large USA airports (JFK or Chicago) and having lots of flights all over the place. I have used the Yotel (airport hotel where rooms are booked by the hour) and it is useful if you arrive late at night and leave the next morning. The airport has 2 main sections - international (Gates D - H) and EU (Gates B -D). Note that some of the D gates are in the international section and some in the EU section. The biggest problem with Amsterdam airport is if you are connecting between a EU flight and an international flight you might have quite a walk and will most likely (unless you are very lucky) have to wait in a ridiculous immigration queue to get from one section to the other. There is a separate queue behind each immigration officers desk so if you get stuck behind someone who is being questioned you could have quite a wait. They also never have enough immigration officers for the amount of passengers passing through here and so they have now started a first / business class separate queue. Basically this bit is a mess. Someone else's comment about security at the gates meaning you can't buy water after security is a good point. Just take an empty bottle and fill it on the plane. Also if you buy any liquids in any other airport make sure they seal it in a an approved EU plastic bag seal otherwise you will leave it behind in Amsterdam! Overall it is an easy airport to use. Pity about the immigration mess!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Joris Lammers
content: I have used Schiphol many times before and when eventually behind customs it is a very pleasant and vibrant airport. The train connections to Amsterdam and the rest of Holland are superb and cheap. There are plenty of shops and it is easy to find directions. Be aware though that there might be queing at check-in and customs so arrive on time. Schiphol really gives you a travel experience and I always enjoy staring my holiday or business trip from this airport. If you depart from Schiphol (not connecting) you must visit the panorama deck. Best in the world. Easy to access from Terminal 1 and 2 check in desks.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: W Simpson
content: Recently transited through Schipol from Edinburgh to Bangkok on KLM. The system is shambolic! The railed off lanes are supposed to allow Business Class passengers priority to go through security and to wait for boarding the onward flight. There are no KLM staff available and the airport staff misdirected me to the Economy queue. Once through security you are made to wait in an inadequately fitted cattle pen with insufficient seats and then a scum to get on board. Blame should go to both Schipol airport and to KLM neither of which seems to have any control over how this is managed.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Peter Goldsbury
content: I have used Schiphol many times over the past 30 years but as I grow older the advantages diminish. The one-terminal concept is a major selling point for this airport but the airport is too large for this concept to be viable. The last time I used Schiphol the planes landed on and took off from the Polderbarn runway and this added about 20 -30 minutes to the overall journey time. Both the incoming and return flights involved a lengthy trek to Gate E. Baggage handling was fine on this occasion but is not reliable. Since I live in Japan and use Osaka Kansai as my main airport perhaps I am biased.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Therese Doerum
content: I've travelled to and from Schipol a lot of times the last 2-3 years and my first impression was that it was well organized informative friendly staff and alot of things to do while waiting for a train. Now after being there a little bit too much there is a couple of things I don't like. Cleanliness in the dining areas (at least downstairs). Rats running around and when I asked for the money back for the food I had ordered the waitress just said with an unpleasant voice "its an epedemi just eat your food". Try to avoid food that is not sealed in plastic and made somewhere else.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Max Meijer
content: Why is Schiphol proud of it's one-terminal-concept? It may take up to a 40 minutes walk from one gate to catch a connecting flight and last week after landing taxi-ing and docking the plane took about 30 minutes - 50% of the flying time of my flight from ZRH. The whole enterprise feels like it has grown to an unmanageable scale for those who do the job on the ground. The core business should be efficient flight and passenger handling not operating a shopping mall.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Robert Mansfield
content: I have used AMS on numerous occasions and cannot fault it. Plenty of shops bars and cafes and well sign posted. The walk to and from D/H piers can be a bit of a pain.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Jim Keeney
content: On the whole quite a pleasant experience. Schipol Airport is large and spread out but sign posting is good. Ample shops and eating places and the airport seemed to be run quite efficiently. Security staff whilst very professional were a little over-zelous. I had to place my passport on a tray to be scanned. I was a bit puzzled at this. I see a previous correspondent has also commented on this.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Riccardo Lehmann
content: First time I flew from HKG to AMS with CX - arrival in AMS ok after night flight long taxi to the gate. AMS has a few construction projects it seems. Very long immigration queue due to only 3 checkpoints for non-EU passports and one EU passports counter open in a dark unwelcoming area. The few open counters are not enough at all when the flights from SQ Delta and CX are arriving at the same time (and many others)! I was through quickly as have EU passport but my friend had to wait nearly 30 minutes. Baggage delivered quickly. I love the great connectivity of AMS to trains bus taxi etc. On our return flight check-in very quick and no problem but again very very long queue for passport control there were two queues only for non EU passengers and one for EU passengers - my friend was waiting 45 minutes myself 30 minutes! There were 7 counters not open and it was busy lunchtime! This is a nightmare. Airport facilities ok but nothing special compared to HKG and SIN - I even prefer FRA!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: S Potts
content: When travelling to Schengen countries Schiphol is a pretty good airport. There are plenty of facilities although shops are a little pricey. If you're flying to a country where you're required to go through passport control (gates E and above) then things get a little silly. The security check is at the gate which results in very slow boarding times and long queues. It also gives you no opportunity to buy drinking water before you board which is ridiculous before a long-haul flight. There was a vending machine but this was for Coke only.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: N Baker
content: Found this airport very good with the train station below and the various shops. When I arrived the walk from the gate to arrivals was long with Schipol being a large airport. On return I experienced the same problem with a previous reviewer where the departure gate number appeared less than 40 minutes before departure and then when it did we were panicking we would miss the flight as the gate closes 30 minutes before departure. All in all though I found the airport convenient with transport links and it's selection of shops.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: A Galanis
content: You can enjoy shopping eating and having a nice cup of coffee on the Terraza overlooking the various airlines arrival and departing the gates from outside. Easy access taking a train to the city from the airport and the Sheraton hotel is fantastic to stay in overnight before you board connecting flight the next day.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: M Wilkins
content: I like Amsterdam as a transit hub - however on my most recent visit it was not as good as previously. True there are long distances between gates so for very tight transfers its not ideal - if you have time to spare though there's a lot of things to do compared to your average airport (loads of bars/restaurants the free art museum lots of recliner seats the casino). However the pricing in the restaurants/bars is now on the high side (4.6 euros for a pint of heineken 8 euros for an irish breakfast) and had the misfortune of encountering a very irate and rude cleaner on my return journey - they need to ensure all their staff are customer trained.

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Peter Harrison
content: Used AMS to transfer from flights from MAN and to PTY return. I found the airport easy to negotiate and containing every facility a transferring passenger could need. I agree with previous comments regarding the loungers on the first floor - If you can get one they are a comfortable resting place. The airport is huge and as I found on my return although I made my connecting flight in plenty of time my bags did not!

title: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport customer review
author: Kay Gebauer
content: AMS is not a Star Alliance Hub and you feel a bit discriminated there. There are no Quick Check-ins and only one person at the counter for one Swiss flight. Security check is more than 40 min in the morning and the fast lane is only for SEN not for FTL. So be there 2hr before departure even if you're FTL.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Frank W Mauz
content: Ted Stevens Anchorage Airport South (domestic) Terminal is a pleasure to navigate through. Modern, uncrowded, spacious, scenic with many wonderful Alaskan artifacts. Seems that almost everyone photographs the giant stuffed moose upon arrival. A nice variety of stores-even a McDonalds with a 50 cent ice cream cone. Comfortable and roomy observation deck. Short walk to be connected to People Mover (city bus), Alaska Railroad and rental cars (no need to ride shuttle bus). The most complete and careful security check I have experienced.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Daniel Re
content: The (south) domestic terminal in Anchorage is world class and beautiful. This new terminal is very modern spotlessly clean provides amenities expected at an international airport and offers a view of the surrounding mountains that is breathless. The displays of local wildlife native culture and art is unsurpassed by most airports in the world. However the old north terminal (which is now connected to the south terminal by a concourse) is sad. Anchorage is one of the five most busy airports in the world for international (cargo) airlines but not for international passenger service. The few international airlines that do provide passenger service (mostly during the summer months) are forced to use the north terminal as U.S. customs is located there. All the comments seen on this site are about the north terminal made by international travelers and are undoubtedly true. Wish they all could have been processed through the magnificent south building.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Christopher Dore
content: Be aware the International terminal has only one shop that sells duty free goods. The only alcohol sold is a restricted choice of whiskeys and they only sell a restricted selection of cigarettes.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: M McManus
content: Went to Anchorage in late 2011. Airport has some restaurants on the security side of the airport but not a good choice and the quality was not too good. The gift shops on the other hand are excellent especially if you are looking for Native American art. Be warned that quite a few souvenirs are like snow shakers with water which will be taken off you by security if you need to pass through them again. Information screens were useful. Plenty of seating and quite a view out of the terminal window.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Ellie Dale
content: I live in Anchorage so fly through here fairly often. The North terminal is old and outdated with little seating old and dirty bathrooms and few options for dining. The baggage claim in the north terminal is rickety old and often slow. The lines are longer and check-in just isn't as efficient. The north terminal is also very dark. The new terminal is great though lots of food and beverage options nice bathroom facilities plenty of seating moving walkways shorter lines efficient baggage claim and overall better design. There's also a lot more light and a better view of the mountains. The experience really does depend on which terminal you get. It will be either really good or really bad.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Peter Gloor
content: The airport lacks a transit area. Passengers are forced to leave the aircraft and pass immigration control. Passenger handling seems unprofessional. Gate waiting room had TV screens with commercials blaring out unwanted TV entertainment but lacked an information screen and a PA system. Airport ground handling delayed flight in spite of sufficient ground time.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: G Winters
content: I connected in ANC on a PDX-TPE trip and I agree with the previous review that the facilities and nice in the main terminal and shameful in the International one. I arrived via AS in the South Terminal and waited 30+ minutes for the shuttle bus to the North (International) terminal. Check-in at China Airlines was smooth and after I cleared security I began looking for the lounge and I was amazed at the pitiful facilities for an "International" terminal. There was no Business Class lounge no restuarant only a kiosk with expensive and silly souvenirs. I was reminded by the clerk who sold me a $4 soft drink that "It's 1am..what do you expect?" When I pointed out that the China Airline flight I was taking was the only true "International" flight at ANC she suggested I call someone who cared ! About 1:30am my 744 arrived from JFK and I was surprised that the thru Pax had to disembark and were herded in to a sterile waiting room with the rest of us going to TPE. Four days later I returned and once again experienced the inefficiency of this Airport: all Pax must deplane at ANC and clear Customs - even those going on to JFK. There were 3 stations open - for an entire 744 that was 80% full. Despite 2+ hours of connecting time I barely made my flight in the South terminal. As far as I can tell the International terminal serves no real purpose with 1 International flight that operates 3x weekly ANC would do well by moving everything to the South terminal and demolishing this relic of the cold war.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: G Hillier
content: Your experience at Anchorage International all depends on which terminal you arrive in. The Alaska Airlines terminal shared with Northwest and AA's seasonal flights is quite nice and renovated. There are decent bars and restaurants and many good shops. Then there is the North Terminal - used by Delta Continental US Air and Air Canada. This was the former International Terminal used before Russian airspace opened up and before the 747-400 and 777 came along and eliminated the need for a refueling stop on flights from JFK to Asia and Heathrow - Asia. It is indeed a relic of the Cold War - a dirty dated claustrophobic mess that needs to be razed. There are no facilities whatsoever. Avoid Terminal N if possible.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Robert Clark
content: Easy check in with the kiosks set up - even near the parking garage! I'd suggest taking advantage of Alaska Airlines' online check in as you can get bonus FF miles for doing it that way. Bars were nice - no smoking anywhere but the airport is small enough that you can get outside easy. Security takes a very long time even with a short time. I'd recommend 3 hours for even domestic travel - especially if there is a foreigner in front of you.

title: Anchorage Airport customer review
author: Steve Hedden
content: The new Alaska Airlines concourse in outstanding. Lots of light from the wall of glass along one side not to mention the breathtaking mountain views. Lots of moving sidewalks and flight information screens. Not many food places yet but these will come. The other concourses are quite dismal.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: Mehmet Arca
content: I have used it many times. New Esenboga Airport is excellent. Comfortable clean helpful staff. Duty free is small but can find everything. During the evening times its very busy for domestic arrivals (nearly 40 flights land in 90 minutes). International arrivals are also fair enough! Great airport.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: D Turkalj
content: Very nice airport however just a few international airlines operating. Domestic always full due to Istanbul flights. Very expensive food and expect to pay around 30 EUR to taxi from city centre to airport. Clean easy airport but simply getting old without being used.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: Guy Senior
content: Flew out on 23 October. No queues and the place is clean and all but empty no doubt because there is less than one international flight an hour. CIP lounge is comfortable and has nice views but a limited range of food. Expect to pay at least £25 for a taxi into or out from the centre.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: Frank Epple
content: The new Ankara Esenboga airport terminal is now operational - still way outside of Ankara maybe one hour from the city centre! Attention for passengers who changed plane in Istanbul with luggage checked through your flight will show as national arrival but you will be taken to international arrival to pick up your luggage clear customs and exit!

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: O Iner
content: Horrible drive from downtown to airport. There is a major construction in the route and new terminal. It could easily take hour and half. So give extra 30 minutes in case road is blocked. Current terminal is old dark and ugly.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: Phil Read
content: Ankara and Istanbul airports must be the most expensive in the world. Food is poor and expensive and beer is an absolute rip off. Expect to pay £5 or 7.5 Euro for a beer. Coffee which can only be described as dish water is £2.50 a cup. In Munich on the same day I payed 2 euro for a far better beer.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: M Gunduz
content: Ankara Esenboga Airport is a small airport and looks and feels tired. Terminal area is small and check in can be problematic when there are many flights. However TAV (company that built Istanbul Intl. Terminal) is building a new modern terminal which will probably enter into service before the end of 2006. I had to endure 8 hours there waiting for a delayed charter and the wait was extremely unpleasant. In summer the high season for air travel and three full planes delayed the departure hall was extremely crowded with very few seats available. The food was way overpriced with no coupons from the airline. For transport into the city I always use Havas buses which depart almost immediately and their seats are more comfortable than taxis also much cheaper. I have used it in May and June 2006 and the road to the airport is under maintenance detour is through dusty and bumpy stabilized dirtroads making the travel 1/2 hour longer and uncomfortable probably for the whole summer.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: Lawrie Hall
content: Domestic departures a bit cramped if there are lots of flights in a short period of time. THY check in very speedy and efficient. The real blight is the prices at the bars and restaurants which are simply scandalous. 15 lire for a grolsch (£6/$10) or 10.50 for the local EFES beer. Food prices similar. I thought all airports had stopped ripping people off at these kind of rates but not here. Is it because they have a high level of European business customers on expenses and locals bring their own refreshments? Anyway highly irritating.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: Takaya Ikezawa
content: This airport is quite unpleasant and kind of shabby looking for an airport of capital city. No place to kill time until boarding time except simple bar and restaurant which over-price everything. There is no boarding bridge and all passengers are conveyed by buses to aircrafts. Turkish airline's domestic flights delay often it could be because of Istanbul Ataturk airport's traffic control thought. It is quite far away from the city. If it is not the rush for you taking Havas (limousine bus) is the cheapest. 8.5 New Turkish Lira. Taxi will cost 45-55 from the airport to the city center. (usually 55 to Cankaya) From the city to the airport you may have a chance to negotiate with drivers for discounts if you speak Turkish language. From my experience 35 from Cankaya was the best.

title: Ankara Airport customer review
author: J Yap
content: Ankara Esenboga Airport is a surprisingly small airport considering the size of the city although a much larger terminal appears to be under construction next door to the current building. It is also lacking in amenities. That being said its small size makes it very easy to negotiate and I whisked through both arrival and departure formalities (although passengers on outbound flights have to pass through security twice - upon arrival at the airport and after check-in). The airport's only serious inconvenience is its location 25 miles outside of the city.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: C Pearce
content: Flew in to Antalya last week and it was easy enough on arrival although queues on visa check took about 20 minutes before going through to collect luggage. On departure however you are firstly required to go through a pre- security screening on arriving which includes putting you're belongings through for scanning. This was all over the place and the workers were very rude and unorganised. After this you queue again to show your passport and boarding pass before getting through this congested area to check in. Check in took over an hour with each queue having about 10-12 people/families in it. Staff did not have a clue. We went through the next passport check which was fine for us but if it was busy it could get very messy. Then onto security there was no trays left and when I got a tray from the next line someone tried to skip me. After this I think it was through to duty free where the shop staff are helpful enough on the floor but the till staff were rather rude. Finally it was boarding which seemed to take ages and when I got to the front my barcode wouldn't scan the machine had broken and the woman was very unwelcoming! Onto the flight and we where happy to have some friendly Scottish staff to greet us. Won't be back here and would not recommend to others.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Margaret Hedges
content: We travelled back from this airport on 13 January 2015 and were very happy with everything. All staff that we encountered seemed very competent and all the queues were short and fast moving. I acknowledge it was winter and therefore there were not many flights leaving. There were plenty of seats vacant although again this may well be because it was winter and not busy. What impressed us most of all was how friendly everyone was. The departure gates are very close to everything else so no walking for miles. I have absolutely no complaints about the airport: in fact I think it deserves much praise. We did not buy anything at the airport because in my experience all airports are very expensive and therefore we avoid spending money in them. Whist I realise that the time of year we were travelling made a difference I can only say that our experience there was excellent. No complaints.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: A Dethier
content: We arrived more than 3 hours before our flight but nearly missed it due to bad management. There was only around 10 persons in front of us to check in and drop their luggage but every family in front of us spent around 20-30 minutes each because of discussion around the baggage allowance. It was clear that they had more than allowed but each bag weight was discussed and argued with the staff for at the end agreeing to let them check in their bag after long discussion without paying for the extra weight. It was clearly mentioned that every extra kg would be 11 euros. We finally started complaining after having waited for 1 hours and a half then a third line opened and we managed to finally go to passport and security check and finally run to the gate to have our flight. This is not acceptable the staff was not efficient not respecting anyone who was not shouting at them. The rules were clear and should be respected. It doesn't need a long discussion or any argument.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Camilla Feiring
content: I just came home yesterday from Antalya I was so lucky to get to my flight in last minute because I spent 45 minutes in total panic waiting to show my passport along with hundreds of other passengers and no lines to stand in. Just pushing and fighting to get through to one of the two men checking your passport. All the time they let more people through to that area so you had to push harder not to let anyone pass you. It was horrible. Why was there no line-system like in every other country I've been to?

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: L Bradley
content: This was one of the most distressing experiences I have had at an airport. I was travelling to Manchester from Antalya along with hundreds of other people. Some people were travelling to different countries such as Holland Russia Germany. There simply is no queuing system. Everybody chooses anywhere where they can have their luggage and passports and tickets scanned. It doesn't matter where you are travelling to or what time you just pick your own check in point. This may sound ideal but believe me it isn't. If your flight it due in an hours time from check in then you will be very lucky to get on your flight. After checking In you then are scanned. Then you have to have your passport checked again. Believe me this was so traumatic!!! All nationalities were pushing and squeezing to get their passports checked. There were thousands of people some who only had ten minutes to get on their plane before take off. There must have been only 3 or 4 people to check all these thousands of people's passports. Travellers were becoming irate distressed and someone with a weak heart could easily have collapsed. There needs to be a much better system. I will never use this airport until I hear the system has improved. Somebody could have been very seriously hurt or even worse. Children were crying people were shouting at each other and the workers checking the passports were extremely stressed out. Please just put queuing barriers up so people can follow an orderly queue and no one will miss their flight and boo swill get hurt.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: N Fusto
content: Quick check in- Security and passport control very fast. But workers at the shops and duty free shop very unfriendly. Very expensive - water 3 euros Burger King menu more than 10 euros.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: John Wilson
content: Arrival big queues for entry visas and passport control but these didn't last that long and we were through fairly quickly. Check-in was standard holiday had to queue for a short while but through security fairly quickly. Not far to all the departure gates from the departure lounge. Reasonable selection of shops and bars but if you can eat drink and do your shopping before you get to the airport as the prices are silly. So expensive for everything which really lets the airport down.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: David Gartside
content: Domestic terminal. Used recently on flights from/to IST. My experience was very different from that noted by others. Calm efficient pleasant terminal in both directions. Screening to enter building and again after check-in is potentially a bit tedious but worked smoothly. Prices airside a bit steep but that's not just a peculiarity of ATL!

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: N Whittle
content: Awful Airport. Once your through passport control the prices literally sky rocket. Toilets very dirty floor covered in water. Oddly there is signs all around the airport saying it was awarded best in Europe don't understand how it got that.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Marc Pauquet
content: Poor and incompetent ground staff no English and foreign language knowledge and skills! Security the most inefficient I never have seen very rude and impolite officers; food and beverage exorbitant prices. Facilities very dirty. An airport to avoid.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: H Grimm
content: I hate the airport of Antalya on the return flight the experience spoiled the entire holiday! First incompetent counter staff which has no foreign language skills. Second the totally stupid security types which does not even work consistently. The beverage sellers in the duty free area continue to charge the most exorbitant prices. Announcements are also made with very poor foreign language skills.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: C White
content: Just got back and the airport was very quick and efficient on arrival - queuing times were not bad at all - however the departure was a sorry of constant queues and the price of food was absurd... 44 Turkish lira for 2 Burger King meals. This wasn't even the advertised price as an additional service charge was added. People were complaining but suddenly nobody speaks very good English. It felt like a dodgy Market trader ripping you off once you'd already accepted you were being overcharged. Avoid the food halls and duty free - duty free prices are the same as at home but the bottle sizes are different to make it appear a better deal.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: L Frederic
content: Been there quite a number of times. Terminals are wide apart only Havas Bus runs to city and is overpriced. There is a local bus but no apparent stop and schedule. Usually huge lines at terminal entrance due to X-ray and check in counters due to holiday travellers. Celebi and Havas check in agents which handle almost every airline are usually not friendly. Airside area usually very crowded not much place to seat long lines at security not organized. All airport outlets terribly overpriced. Only good thing is that it's quite modern and clean. A typical airport for the holiday travellers which accept this kind of customer service.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: J Parkes
content: Glad other people found prices ridiculous. And as for the Customs officers and immigration police. No "Welcome to Turkey". Instead you are met by off-hand unwelcoming officials who give the impression they are doing you a favour!

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: J Burrows
content: I remain totally baffled as to how the shopkeeper at the check in hall in terminal 1 is allowed the freedom to try and try being the operative word here and charge me 2.5 ytl for a newspaper the Turkish Daily News clearly marked 1.5 ytl and sold everywhere under the Turkish sun for 1.5ytl including as it happens Istanbul airport just twelve days before then tell me like some Bodrum con man that 1.5ytl is "Bazzar price" and 2.5 is airport price. He scanned it then over rode the price to slip in another lira for himself. Is there no-one in the airport looking out for this kind of thing. It can't be just me so this kind of thing is really really going to leave a bad taste in people's mouths as they head home more than enough to leave it as the most lasting impression of the beautiful city they've just visited.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: K Harragan
content: Flew to Gatwick from Antalya last week. Being off season it was fairly quiet and so no queuing to get in. The place was reasonably clean and looked after but not sure how it would have coped when really busy. Can only agree about the extortionate price of food and drinks. What made it worse is that you weren't told when handing over large chunks of cash for a bottle of water that the security guards would take it from you when you tried to board the plane - you can't take drinks bought in the airport onto the plane unlike at UK airports. Wouldn't be surprised if the bottles went straight back on the shelves! Can't see why the authorities are happy to let you leave their country on such a sour note - they'll get more money from a happy customer making a return visit than they will ripping you off at the airport.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Peter Haynes
content: The security arrangements at Antalya airport seem a little strange. OK you are screened on the way in and again when you go upstairs to lounge and duty free area. BUT having bought a bottle of water in duty free you are then not allowed to take it on the 'plane because you cannot take more than 100mls beyond the final screening point leading to departures. At Gatwick you are able to take what you have bought in duty free onto the 'plane. Much more sensible I think. Queuing to check in to a flight is also a long winded process.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Steve Bennett
content: I regularly fly to and from Antalya airport (10 times+ per year). The arrival facilities are fine. Baggage arrives fast - even during busy periods. The stairwell from arrivals to baggage reclaim is steep - hold on to the rail tightly! Howeverdepartures is another story. I cannot fathom any justification for the outrageous prices charged by those with airport food and drinks franchises at this airport. It is the most expensive airport. I was charged 27 euros for 2 coffees and an inedible sub. This not only left a nasty taste in my mouth but in my wallet too. My advice - take a doggy bag. Do not buy from these airport licensed criminals. The authorities in Turkey should act to protect their own reputation which is compromised by encouraging these bandits.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Horst Rotter
content: We were also shocked to have to pay about 4 Euro for a miserable small cup of coffee inside terminal 1 served in a plastic cup. This was our last impression of Turkey and we wonder whether the Tourist Authorities should not do something about this image harming practise.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Wolfgang Schuessel
content: Airport in itself okay. However prices asked at the airport restaurants are a pure chuzpe. 8 Euros for a cup of coffee and a dry tiny something-like-croissant. If you are picked up from your hotel at 1:30am to catch a 6:50am flight you will be stranded at the airport for long enough to end up buying at these ridiculous prices. It seems they are counting on this. If you ever have to go through that airport make sure to bring a doggie bag! Don't support this greedy attitude.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Gary Whittaker
content: Antalya airport is modern and clean the need to scan bags at the main doors is a pain especially in hot or bad weather as you wait outside the terminal otherwise it is like any other airport. But by far the biggest downer is the prices inside nothing short of extortion on a grand scale expect to pay 3 times the normal price for everything including the so called duty free goods.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Murat Nal
content: We arrived at Antalya airport 5am over the Christmas period the airport was empty - the only flights coming in were from UK. Airport was nice We went threw customs in two ticks. The baggage followed and we were out in half an hour. Departing from Antalya was also very quick but I put this down to the fact we were travelling of season and of peak times. Airport was okayish. I was very disappointed by the food and beverage franchises. £3.50 for a cup of filter coffee. I dared not ask the price of a burger at Burger King.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Mark Evans
content: As at other Turkish airports one must undergo security screening at the entrance to the terminal at AYT. In fact there are two terminals: the Domestic and International Terminals are separate buildings. For my flight to IST continuing to LHR I presented myself at the THY check-in in the Domestic Terminal but was told that if I wanted to check my luggage all the way to LHR I would have to go to the International Terminal some 500-600m away. To this inconvenience was added the simultaneous arrival of six tourist coaches which began to disgorge their passengers and hefty luggage. This prompted me to accelerate and get to the screening point ahead of the crowds - any dithering would have left me at the end of long lines that would snake out of the terminal as described in previous postings. A close call that. Check-in proved quick and friendly and a pleasant place to relax once within was the Zum Strammen Bar which clearly caters for AYT International's mainly German clientele.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: George Edwards
content: Antalya airport is the worst I have departed from in recent years. With huge queues and sweltering heat the government owned refreshment outlets were charging positively extortionate prices for bottles of water. The one good side was that despite all the threats and warnings about excess baggage charges by the holiday company the actual check in staff couldn't care less about the few extra kilos as they had several hundred passengers to deal with and knew it was silly anyway.

title: Antalya Airport customer review
author: Matthias Moehring
