content: Frankfurt-Hahn is perfectly adequate serves the purpose it appears to have oriented itself towards - low-fare shovel them in flights - and frankly can often be a joy compared with the sprawling chaos of Frankfurt proper particularly if your ultimate destination is an intermediate city such as Mainz. Bus connections are improving and expanding all the time and until an airport of the magnitude of Hamburg (for example) is finally connected to the rail network I refuse to accept any criticism of little old Hahn for failing to provide the same.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: R Hopkins
content: As at 16.10.06 Security has gone mad at this airport! Not only was I required to remove an unlined zipper top (by no means an outdoor jacket) but having done that I even had to remove a light chiffon see- through neck scarf! I was so astonished that I thought my necklace was the problem initially and didn't see any men being asked to remove ties. I am a white middle-aged woman conventionally dressed. Are chiffon scarves the latest terrorist accessory? What's going on?

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Steve Ward
content: This airport has grown from what used to a shed into a reasonable airport. However it is a long way away from Frankfurt. Great access (but only via car or private transport) to Rhine and Mosel. Airside is ok but final departure gates are grim with very limited facilities and poor seating. Queues on arrival at passport control can be long you may have to stand outside. This airport is high so can be affected by snow in winter.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: D Keenan
content: I have seen Hahn airport grow over several years. Looking back it has grown from a tiny little terminal which had only one little bistro to something that now looks more like an airport building. There are several places where you can now grab a bite to eat. Only drawback is that there is not enough adequate seating not even at the gates. Parking at the airport will set you back around €7.00 per day. Still very cheap when compared to other airports. Some of the parking lots are situated quite a way from the terminal so allow some time to walk. There arent always trolleys so make sure you have a suitcase with wheels. Considering this was a former US Air Force Base practically in the middle of nowhere the airport has come a long way and there is still room for expansion and improvement but they are getting there. The airport is actually located nearer to Luxembourg than any other larger german city. There are plans for a train terminal to be built but for now there is only a bus service operating into several larger cities. Keeping this in mind that Hahn is NOT Frankfurt you can plan your trip much better. PS/ Pack an umbrella in your hand luggage! If its raining you will get soaked walking between terminal and plane and standing again to board or waiting at passport control.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Mohammad Taha
content: You get what you pay I say If you're flying Ryanair. The airport is quiet good and fast but it takes one and half hour by bus to get there and it costs 13 Euros also that's 26 Euros if you are coming back. There is no railway station so you can't get there by train. The shops are also fine and there are many nice hotels nearby.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Leon Richards
content: Frankfurt-Hahn airport needs to get a proper identity even the Sat Nav system in my hire car couldn't find the place. Putting in Frankfurt sent me miles out of the way and I had to revert to calling a friend to tell me places close by that were listed. Having flown into Stuttgart for the Grand Prix at Hockenheim and having decided that the flight times fitted better for the return home would have been good. Only just got to Hahn for final check-in time. Do not intend on using this airport again. No links to anywhere

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Peter Dowling
content: HHN is quite good if you're heading to Bonn (not as good as CGN) but hopeless if you're going to Frankfurt. Unless you want to spend an extra hour and a half on the road after you land. However there are some very nice hotels in Sohren about 5 km away from HHN (where I stayed) and the scenery is very nice.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Ian Webb
content: Not only is Frankfurt Hahn miles away from Frankfurt but in a country like Germany with an extremely good train system this airport isn't on the rail network. I'll do my homework better next time and I won't fly to Hahn again.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Frances Tonks
content: You can't go wrong flying to Frankfurt Hahn airport if you want to enjoy either the Mosel or the Rhine regions. Within 1/2 hour you can be on the banks of the Rhine watching the steamers gliding along or sipping wine in one of the old but beautiful villages in the Mosel valley. Hiring a car is no problem at the airport but take time to enjoy a drink and a meal at one of the cafes first. Frankfurt Hahn airport will also benefit from the planned expansion of roads and railway in the next few years and the millions from Ryanair.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Nigel Hawkins
content: Hahn airport is on the line between Luxemburg and Frankfurt according to the Hahn Airport site map but as it is nearer Luxemburg Ryanair should really call it Luxemburg (Hahn).

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: John Charlesworth
content: Booking in a hurry for a meeting in Eschborn near Frankfurt I omitted to follow the golden rule with Ryanair and check the actual distance from airport to city - 90 miles this time! Made meeting as took evening flight and booked hotel but there was no way to make return flight. I appreciate that Ryan air is offering cheap flights on a caveat emptor basis but a little warning about the distance to Frankfurt would have been appreciated. Lovely drive back to airport having established that there was no earthly chance I was going to make the flight I left the autobahn enjoyed the Rhineland scenery and had a long lunch. Will use again but make time for the journey. Airport facilities not bad either some interesting shops not normally found in an airport but perhaps a consequence of the potential for missing flights and being stranded for a few hours.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: J Sullivan
content: Having left Adelboden in Switzerland to go to Frankfurt-Hahn airport it became quite obvious that somewhere between Frankfurt and Hahn we were lost. It was the middle of the night and quite worrying. This airport is the biggest kept secret in Germany. Although we found it eventually and in time for our flight I am still not sure exactly where it is in relation to either Frankfurt or Hahn. I think Ryanair need to give passengers more of an inkling to its location mystery tours can be fun but not when you are trying to catch a flight and not in a strange country in the middle of the night.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: M Ritter
content: This airport has always been neglecting and is now even making profit out of the fact that every passenger if not living in Lautzenhausen (this being in fact the name of the adherent village. Hahn is situated not far from Bad Kreuznach which is also some 80 km away.) cannot get there without a car or private transport. In addition to the flights you are constrained to pay bus fare or parking fees (parking in Lautzenhausen now forbidden really everywhere) and if you come by car only by chance will you find a lonely trolley for your luggage in the vast parking space. Tip: the coiffeur is tremendous and very cheap. I got a cute haircut for 10 EUR and made up the bus fare from Frankfurt to Lautzenhausen.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: K Faryniasz
content: Frankfurt-Hahn is not Frankfurt but Hahn. Once you realize this you can take advantage of some amazingly low tickets even if you factor in a night in one of the local hotels beforehand. An example would be $1100 to Stockholm vice $120 on Ryan. Yes it is an inconvience and you should always check Frankfurt prices first factor in the long bus rides at both ends and that cost. Then if you are still saving use Hahn.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: J Clark
content: Frankfurt Hahn airport cannot be given that name simply due to the fact of the airport is miles away from Frankfurt. I booked a flight which was cheap I thought I saved money I could never have been more wrong! The overall cost was the same as a flight to Frankfurt Main and it took me hours to get there. I will never fly to Hahn airport (which should be its proper name!!) again.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Lionel Bell
content: This one-time American airbase is situated about 80 miles from Frankfurt am Main and has nothing to do with Germany´s finance capital. Apart from the terminal building the whole place is a filthy ruin. As a single person it is impossible to unload baggage and then park and it is impossible to transfer baggage by hand from the parking lot  as there is nothing to move it with. The sight of small children pulling heavy luggage on the 20 minute walk through the dirt and to the terminal. Ryanair staff are OK but the airport staff are little less than disgusting requiring that complaints must be made in writing. As one offensive ignorant woman at the information desk so coldly stated after she had refused to contact the airport management: "if you haven´t missed your flight what do you want to complain about?" A great example of typical German service at its arrogant best. Motto: if you can fly another route do so.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Mike Flook
content: Depends on what you are looking for. We went on vacation to the Mosel valley area around Traben and found this airport to be convenient as we only had 20 minutes to travel. You cannot get better than that. Great location for touring the Mosel valley area!

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: D Krishnan
content: It is surprising that neither the Frankfurt Main Airport website nor the Frankfurt Hahn website openly admits to there being another Airport "in" Frankfurt! The Frankfurt city website also does not acknowledge the Hahn airport. Ryanair finds it unnecessary to inform passengers that they would be flying to an airport some 80 miles away from the city! I had to go to Strausberg - and after trying direct flights from London I thought I would fly Ryanair and save money! I paid less to the airline industry but my bank never noticed the difference!

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Sean Crookson
content: Research showed me that this airport is far enough away from Frankfurt not to have the name associated with it. 12 Euros for a shuttle bus one-way is quite steep when flying on a budget airline. Ryanair dominates this small uncomfortable airport. Duty free is available in a tiny shop about the size of my bedroom. Prices are not competitive and stock is limited. Security staff are in league with the airline when it comes to baggage weight limits and I was cautioned for carrying too much hand luggage by the person x-raying bags. Its' rival Frankfurt-Main airport is only 3KM away from the city and is a far better prospect.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Alan Miller
content: I have been using Hahn airport since April 2002 and have seen it grow quicker than I expected. But despite that it is still a pleasant terminal the staff are friendly and helpful and it is easy to reach. My only real criticism is the main entrance road layout - this needs improvement. I hope the airport service remains the way it is even as the site grows.

title: Frankfurt Hahn Airport customer review
author: Fred Deltgen
content: From Koblenz Hauptbahnhof take bus 610 to Flughafen Frankfurt-Hahn Terminal Hahn; one hour ride.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: A M Bourgeois
content: This is the first time I experienced such a disrespectful attitude when passing through security. My artificial hip, which is made of titanium always sets off the metal alarm. I also use a wheelchair when travelling since I cannot stand or walk for any length of time due to arthritis. In all other airports, the staff have been courteous and respectful when requesting a pat down. In Frankfurt, both times I passed through on the 8th and again on the 21st July, the woman who inspected me was rude and pushy. In addition to this issue, because I needed assistance between flights, my family and I were transported from one airport section to the other, with most staff seemingly confused over what to do with us, security staff were rude when we passed through the second clearance, and we nearly missed our connecting flight to Marseille. I will certainly never book a connecting flight through Frankfurt again as this was an unnecessary stress we did not appreciate.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: G Vice
content: Arriving at the airport having done online pre-check-in I headed to bag drop with Air Canada. 2 counters were open and one for airport check-in. After 50 minutes waiting I got to the front of the baggage drop. The check-in was actually moving faster. As my bag was processed the ancient computers crashed and I was set to wait. Once I headed to the security check point I was greeted by short queues and terrible service.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Peter Grant
content: Found the airport to be very clean and ordered. The passport control was quiet and we had no queue. We had been advised not to go through security as no amenities and this was great advice. Then we met the security check. They could hardly be more offensive, one staff member ripped my passport out of my pocket and said next time you take it out! I was being very polite, it was gratuitous and absolutely not called for.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Nick Wilcock
content: CDG to BHX via FRA with Lufthansa. As with my last 2 trips to this airport in the last couple of weeks, we were parked miles from the Terminal and had a 20 min wait and uncomfortable bus ride to be dropped off at an entry point which has no escalators - =hard luck on the elderly or infirm. A long trudge including the wretched tunnel and finally to Gate B47. Unsmiling Securitas personnel lacking in customer service skills than performed the secondary document check. We stood around for 20 or so minutes waiting for news of delayed boarding, then the Securitas woman screeched at people to have their boarding cards ready for her machine. Once on the aircraft, we had a delay 'due to heavy outbound traffic' - at 22:30? Then another delay because the pushback tractor driver was 'busy elsewhere'. A chaotic, unpleasant experience which seems to be becoming the norm at this airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Rishad Patell
content: Arrived on LH from LIS into FRA on our way to BOM. Got in on time and tried to get from one side of the terminal to the other. Bit confusing with the signage and very hard to follow at times. The airport seemed quite nice and the staff were pleasant. What was shocking was the immigration control where they had 3 staff for all passengers with non EU passports and 2 of them were looking down and chatting and doing their own thing. The woman officer processed over 10 people and they just sat there chatting and laughing. Very disappointed considering all that is said about German efficiency. Food options limited once you pass immigration and security. Duty free is okay.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: G Chandler
content: We had connections through this airport leaving and returning to the EU as EU citizens. Our connections were to Calgary - YYC (leaving) and to Helsinki - HEL (returning) with Air Canada being our intercontinental carrier and Lufthansa our EU carrier. We left through FRA in June and returned through FRA in mid-July 2015. The first impression we had of FRA was disorganization and inadequate information, including poor language skills by security personnel. Travellers are lost in their own struggle to get through controls and security and find their way to gates to make flights. This individualistic collection of various "struggles" makes for stressed and rude passengers combined with inadequately trained and uninformative airport personnel. We arrived from HEL and needed to get to the Air Canada lounge and gate in another part of the terminal. This involved a long walk to a small and overused elevator down to a sublevel with moving sidewalks, only to have to resurface to the original level via another inadequately sized elevator with passengers waiting in line or others simply giving up to use the similarly overcrowded stairs which are not unlike those in a regular office or apartment building. All in all, that experience was stressful but we had 4 hours and eventually found a place to sit and wait for our Air Canada flight to Calgary. However, with only a 1-hour connection awaiting us on our return, this did not bode well. Travellers such as ourselves who consult with Air Canada or even Lufthansa personnel will often be told that since flights are in the same terminal (Terminal 2 in this case), everything is "close and they will certainly have more than enough time to catch connecting flights". Nothing could be further from the truth! Be warned! Upon our return in July from Calgary going to Helsinki, the situation we had been fearing and about which we had been "re-assured" by Air Canada and Lufthansa personnel, was much worse than we had originally thought. Anyone with less than 2 hours to make connecting (non-Schengen, Schengen) flights should not consider Frankfurt. When we arrived in Frankfurt, automatic border control (for EU citizens) was not operational and a lady was running around trying to pursuade EU citizen passengers to use another re-entry border agent's line which was completely empty. We soon learned why more experienced passengers were avoiding that line. Border agents screamed at us for waiting a short distance behind another traveller - "one at a time!". There was no clearly-marked single line and no signage telling us exactly how far behind the other traveller we should stand. I ended up having to redirect my fellow passangers to a place further back, with the rude official glaring at me from the perch of his glass box. Another chaotic security control was required as was running up and down the same sets of stairs we had encountered before on our departure. I cannot recommend this airport!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Monson
content: Transited thru FRA from PHL to LUX on 17th June and reverse direction on 25th June, non-Shengen to Shengen, and had no problems at all either direction, even though we had to take a bus 3 out of 4 times to and from aircraft. Maybe we were lucky, but Passport control was less than 5 minutes each time, and agents were efficient, though surly. Walks were long, with several stairs, escalators,and elevators, but the signage was relatively easy to follow from Terminal A to B and B to Z on return. The trick is to follow the signs carefully! We are both retired and my wife and her bad feet did fine. Would recommend good walking shoes. Very limited selection of food and beverage areas - took 20 minutes to get water and snacks. We had 1.5 hours between flights both directions and were still able to use restrooms and waiting area at gate, but would recommend no less time than 80 minutes. After having read the reviews, we were very apprehensive about this transit, but ended up pleasantly surprised.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Cristea
content: Used Frankfurt International in June two times for transit, between Bucharest to Aberdeen return flights, operated by Lufthansa. Outbound flight was 6 hours layover, so decided to visit Frankfurt City Center.Easy to reach from airport using S-Bahn. Back in the airport, it is huge, well signed, amazing views over tarmac, not so good toilets/ lavatories, and terrible offer for food and drinks in 1Z terminal. Munich airport is much, much better for transfer.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Yannick Jehli
content: Entering from an Intercontinental flight from Sao Paulo for a transit. Waiting time at pass control and security check was extremely long and badly organized. Staff were not friendly. Direction to the new terminal has taken 1 hour walking through the airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: John Hill
content: Flight from Manchester to DFW on Lufthansa via Frankfurt. What a mess the Frankfurt airport system is. Landed on time after a great flight with 40 minutes to when our other flight to DFW was to take off, should be easy we thought! The jet bridges not used, so we had to climb down to the tarmac via stairs, then wait for buses to take us to terminal A. Bus took a while to get there, then we were ordered off with no explanation as to where we needed to go - we found someone who told us to follow signs to terminal Z. Followed signs which lead us to a train station, we boarded this and got off as indicated, then walked for 5 minutes only to find we needed to go back through security and passport control, all lines were long. By the time we got into the long line for security, our plane was already boarding, and there were a good 100 people ahead of us. After 10 minutes we managed to get someones attention and we were ushered towards security. What an attitude these security people have, have never been treated so badly in all flights I have taken. The passport control was not much better either. Next is the Duty Free maze, what a joke fighting your way through this lot trying to get out of there. We followed the signs to Terminal Z, our gate was 69(the last one) with over half a mile of walking to get to it. At the gate down at least eight flights of stairs to the bottom, only to find we are back out on the tarmac. The plane was parked at the cargo terminal on the other side of the airport. We did make the plane, and we were not the last ones on it, but never again will Frankfurt see us as visitors.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Bruene
content: Connecting in FRA is some kind of lottery! I arrived from Zagreb and had 55 minutes to catch my next flight. Docking in last corner of T1B I had to run to queue at immigration. After this another marathon to get to the security (EU to EU!). As my time was already short I queued at the "Fast Lane". When I started to unpack my laptop, a guy shouted at me that the lane is closing now and I had to queue at the normal lanes. It took another 25 minutes to pass the security. As my boarding time was already overdue I had to run through hallways, tunnel and elevators to get to T1A. When I arrived at the gate boarding was already closed for 15 minutes. If you have to change here, calculate at least 2 hours for non-Schengen to make sure you will have a chance to catch your plane. Try to connect via MUC, VIE or AMS.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Wagner
content: I traveled to and from this airport between May 23 and June 3. I had no problems at all with immigration and I avoided the shuttle. However All the bussing and waiting for the bus to leave and stair climbing was pretty horrible and the signage definitely not very helpful (but then again I find that this is a problem beyond the airport as well). My real vexation however was with the slow security that required the removal of just about every thing electrical or battery-related. I travel all the time and never had to take out my computer and phone chargers et al. Only two lanes were open because a third lane suddenly closed down. Both open lanes had few people in the queue initially but no one was moving. Worst of all having gone through the scanner with some guy barking out something in German this seriously efficient woman gave me a strict pat down like I had never experienced (believe me I travel a lot and usually get tsa pre-check in the U.S. I also have never had a problem with a little wand-ing but this was absurd). For that and other reasons I plan to use an alternate airport next time I am headed for Cologne or its environs.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: P J Alvarez
content: This airport is a pure nightmare. Bus rides from/to plane take about 20 minutes even after arriving at the terminal you have to stay on the bus and wait up to 10 minutes by closed doors. Overall the whole journey from the plane to the terminal takes about half an hour. Then follows very long walks through uncomfortable halls stairs and escalators always looking for a signs and finding hardly any. Toilets were overcrowded and dirty. The worst thing about this airport was the rude staff! Immigration officers were shouting loudly at passengers if you didn't understood their question immediately. Avoid this airport at any cost!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: David Killick
content: Such a big airport but it is very easy to get around. Just be prepared for long walks and leave plenty of time. Very busy and there can be long queues for immigration but they move fast. Even pressured border staff were friendly and smiled. "Ah Kiwis!" Lots of food places reasonably priced. Duty-free also very good. I can recommend the Ansbach Uralt.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Richard Eggerman
content: I concur completely with all the negative reviews already posted. So much of the delay could be remedied by better layout planning and training. There is not a trace of the famed German efficiency on display at the Frankfurt airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: A Narayana
content: I just flew from India to USA via Frankfurt. We had a little over two hours transit time. That would have been more than enough for any 'normal' airport but not in Frankfurt. Passengers are required to walk very long stretches of passages with no moving platforms anywhere to aid. And then a train ride security delays and more walking. Very poorly organized airport and nightmare for transit passengers. It is best if it can be avoided.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Fang
content: YYC to FRA connecting onwards to TXL: upon arrival one is greeted by a very long walk to immigration. Then a long walk through endless stairways escalators walkways and more escalators etc. to security. Security screening was very busy as there were a lot of passengers during the morning rush hour at FRA. Then more walking escalators down to a long tunnel followed by more escalators staircases etc. Then one has to struggle to find one's gate hoping that while navigating the above the airline has not changed the gate. I've seen worst than FRA but I've also seen better. If you're transiting at FRA be prepared for a maze and a lot of walking and be sure to allow at least 2.5 hours preferably 3 hours between your flights.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: E Worrall
content: Security staff were very rude and unprofessional. They approached my female friend in a rude manner questioning her about her country of origin (Hungary). I experienced a similar level of unprofessional heckling. My carry-on was a backpack inside of a hard roller suitcase because I plan to bring more back home than I am bringing with me. I unpacked the backpack and put it in a separate bin as asked. The same male security employees laughed loudly at the empty suitcase and called other employees over to share in this hilarious situation while I stood by awaiting my luggage. Overall I would never have expected this type of behaviour from supposed professionals at a world class airport. This was my first visit to Germany and from this first impression I can't say I will be hurrying back. Negative experience. Not recommended.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: W Calcutt
content: I have flown through most of the German airports and through Frankfurt several times but my last trip was the worst. As others have stated the security staff have to be some of the rudest encountered. I made the mistake of trying to push my bag onto the belt without permission. The security lady yelled very rudely "What do you think you are doing?" She then asked me three times if I had a laptop in my bag which I answered no each time. After passing through the X ray machine with no problems she had another guard pull me aside for wanding even though I hadn't set off the alarm. Very demeaning and unprofessional.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Joel Peart
content: Security control were on a charm offensive giving out Easter chocolate and asking for a satisfaction score man was pleasant who frisked me making small talk. Seriously though where are the toilets? only one i found was tucked in next to our gate and was very small. No free coffee/tea/newspaper stands like in glorious Munich.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Reynolds
content: Awful airport. Best avoided. They are well known for very long queues due to not having nearly enough staff on passport control or security. It is also sometimes necessary to go through two separate security queues for some gates. It is very easy to miss flights especially if you need to catch a connecting flight. If you point out to a member of staff that you are going to miss your flight expect them to me very rude and totally unsympathetic (even though it is totally due to the airport's very poor organisation). When I flew from Frankfurt today I witnessed two separate members of staff being appallingly rude to several people. Fortunately I was not one of them but it was still extremely distasteful to watch. I don't know how the staff at this airport expect to be able to be so rude and unprofessional and get away with it. My advice is fly to/from another airport. Hannover is far better cleaner easier less stressful and no one has been rude to me yet.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Janko
content: Arrived from ICN very unfriendly and almost insulting security staff at passport control. My wife and I made the "mistake" of stepping forward to the counter together after the previous person was done we were then told by a very rude lady that she was the one deciding if when and where we should move. Worst airport experience we had better transit via LHR or even CDG.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Edwards
content: I experienced long delays going through the T1 security check on the Saturday evening while making a transfer. It took 40 minutes to get through the line and I was fortunate to make my connecting flight which would have been the last of the day to my destination. I asked the staff member managing the line if it was always this bad and he replied in good English with his German accent "Sometimes it's worse!" Fortunately I am a European passport holder. After security there was passport control. The line for non-EU passport holders was almost as bad as that for the security check. It was all very disappointing and I would go as far to say disgraceful. What happened to German efficiency? Fraport could and indeed should learn much from how Amsterdam Schiphol operates.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Tydeman
content: Flew from Heathrow to Sao Paulo and back via Frankfurt. Never used this airport before and will avoid doing so again. Hate hate hate it! Designed to maximise walking distances. Disgraceful. On the way out everything was closed before 8pm apart from one poxy little (expensive) bar. On the return flight our luggage was left at Frankfurt. Not sure if this was Lufthansa's fault or the airports but both have been awful so it makes no odds.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Aisha Arynova
content: Terribly slow work of staff. I had 2hrs of transit time and all this time was in queue of passport control then endless running then again customs control. No clear signs stupid and ineffective organization the worst airport. Extremely unfriendly staff.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Walker
content: We transited Frankfurt and due to gross inefficiencies by staff in security and passport control we missed our connection on our outward journey. Compounded to this was the attitude of gross uncaring by the staff of not only the airport but the Lufthansa airline ground staff who obviously have seen the whole thing many hundreds of times before that they are totally unsympathetic to the point of rudeness. All the terminal staff I came across had the same didn't give a monkeys attitude to passengers. If we had not been very pushy on our return we would have missed our return connection as well. Frankfurt cannot handle transit passengers. They should not be in the market as a hub airport. This is the 3rd time in a couple of years that we have had problems transiting Frankfurt. Never again.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Jon Sloper
content: Unfortunately I have to add to this catalogue of very poor experiences. Having left Abu Dhabi (with its usual 5* experience) I faced a 4.5 hour wait at Frankfurt to fly to Birmingham. On trying to access wifi with no success I endeavoured to find some customer information - no joy as the desk had a position closed board (I've never seen anyone there!). I did find another member of staff who tried to help but after 4 further attempts to login I couldn't' pass the Register page and was advised to walk around until I found a better hotspot (which I didn't find). Four sets of toilets were full and when I did find a space there were no hand towels/drier to use. Generally overpriced outlets. I agree with others' comments about security checks which seemed overly slow with plenty of staff not having to do much apart from chat and joke. Spoke to three other travellers who were also experiencing difficulty accessing information easily - no surprise if there's no one to help - and of course not a 'manager' in sight or available to provide any solutions to all these problems 'on the ground'. I intend to avoid any lengthy stay in this airport again even if it means having to pay more to fly direct - it's worth the price to keep your sanity.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: A Moreitz
content: Just returned from a return trip SYD-FRA and even though I am German I must say I agree with many of the reviews regarding poor or inconsistent or confusing signage throughout the airport. The security checks to get to my CX flight took 45 mins with the plane leaving late due to more passengers being caught up at security. This was mostly due to a recent secret EU review which enabled secret staff to get explosives and weapons easily through security on every second attempt out of 50! Needless to say the news and press were having a field day. Security had been stepped up the day before and the staff are receiving more training now. Drinks are expensive and everything you buy has a bond of a few cents due to the German recycling laws and you only get the money back when you hand the bottle back in this is the same throughout Germany.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Tarun Gulati
content: This is increasingly becoming a very harrowing airport from a transit standpoint. Finding taxiing times after landing increasingly long. More often than not planes are parked on the tarmac and passengers have to be bussed to and from the terminal. There are long wait times when this happens because they use fairly large busses and don't leave till they are filled up. So if you are one of the first folks on the bus - it's normal to wait 15-20 minutes for it to leave. And finally the lines at immigration and the distances between the gates makes it very likely that you will miss your connecting flight if it is anything less than a 2 hour connection.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Imm
content: All but terrible. Passport check at the door of the plane (Lufthansa flight no less) on a flight from Athens (no kidding it was a passport check not a security check as only legally allowed by the Schengen agreement - I am a non-Canadian citizen legally residing in Canada permanently and evidently my citizenship was put into question until it was confirmed by the agent that I was traveling with my Canadian citizen spouse). Bus ride from airplane to terminal. Poor signage. Endless terminals and turns to reach a gate. Rude customs/immigration agents upon exit - I handed my passport with my Canadian PR card inside and he threw it back at me so spitefully that it flew over the counter bounced on me and landed on the floor plus after all that he denied the exit stamp (which they are required by law to stamp anyhow). Unfortunately we have to use that airport again in a few months - we avoided it on two other trips but we had no choice this time.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Man
content: Terrible! Avoid this airport at any reasonable expense. Bus ride from plane to terminal endless security checks that are unreasonably long and confusing gate navigation. If you don't have 3 + hours to make a flight there's a good chance you'll miss it and the staff has no sympathy for putting you in a sure fail situation.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: A Maddie
content: Seven passport and security checks between connecting flights. Poor signage. Interminable bus rides and long runs between terminals. Officials who don't care whether you make a connection. Baggage security screening is chaos. Things come out in random order with empty bins interspersed. Items pulled for further screening aren't announced. You have to notice that one of your bags is in a different area while any other carry-on's sit in the chaos. One long security line was diverted suddenly to a completely different area requiring a ten-minute walk with no explanation given. The signs indicated different terminal letters from the one we needed. When we asked for clarification we were just shouted at to do what we were told. Food and drink and far away from many gates. The systems are a mess or if they are intentional they are designed to make you miss your flight or arrive sweaty and exhausted at the last second.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Petersen
content: Very bad airport. Endless bus rides from/to terminals traffic jam with busses lining up to deliver passengers to terminal building. Facilities are old and tired the ways are extremely long and uncomfortable. Avoid.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Hansen
content: Always add more time for connecting in FRA for taking busses to the terminal from the plane. Very poor setup for travellers. They seem to care more about the stores at the airport than the airport facilities.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Chen
content: The staff at security control chatted to each while slowly doing their job. I was jammed there and almost lost my flight. The same amount of passengers in London or Manchester would only take less than half of the time I spent in Frankfurt airport. Even worse unlike other international airports the staff would not help people who have tight boarding time to pass the security control. They were just chatting and chatting.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Blanning
content: This must be the worst airport in Europe. Long coach ride to and from aircraft. Very long queues for security (and sometimes there is a further check before the gate is reached). Restaurant facilities minimal and overpriced. If one comes in to Terminal 2 one has to take a shuttle or bus to get to Terminal 1 and the S-Bahn or Long-distance railways stations. Signs few and far between. Latest horror - one has to wait in the entrance hall before a gate is posted.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: V Dandapani
content: I travel through FRA at least a half a dozen times a year and have never had a problem. Only once (yesterday - 27th August 2014) was I stopped for an "explosives" check but it took no more than a couple of extra minutes. The signs are pretty clear contrary to the complaints of some others on this forum. The only "negative" is the long walk and a short trip on a train from the "Z" area for flights to and from the US and gates to other destinations.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Luke Wilkinson
content: Avoid at all cost! It's an unmitigated disaster of an airport. We have transferred twice at Frankfurt once to Bucharest and once to Vienna and on both occasions we missed our flight. In the unlikely event you do make your connection you can be sure your bags won't! It's a vast confusing labyrinth of corridors gloomy stairwells endless checkpoints and astonishingly long queues for everything. We had 2 hours to make the connection from Frankfurt to Vienna which we assumed would be easily sufficient mistake! We were constantly frustrated by delays both disembarking the aircraft and a very long transfer by bus to the terminal. Trying to find our gate we got hopelessly lost in a maze of dark corridors which appeared to be for cleaners and maintenance staff where we met other passengers who appeared equally confused. It turned out our gate was at least a 2 mile walk away! The 2 bottles of Rum we purchased in Manchester airport were confiscated by rude security staff we missed our flight and upon finally arriving in Vienna our bags had been lost. This airport is like purgatory it's the most frustrating inefficient stressful airport we have ever visited without a doubt. Signage is non-existent staff totally disinterested and the whole place is badly designed. Try to transfer at Munich or Brussels if possible.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: F Nemhauser
content: Contrary to the experiences of many who post here my experiences at FRA have been good to excellent. I use FRA 5 to 6 times a year most often in transit though sometimes arriving/departing. I find the staff unfailingly friendly and helpful. I speak a little German but even when I use English the staff respond in kind. Immigration never seems to take too long and while the wait for baggage can sometimes be 15 minutes or so the wait is not too bad. For a large ageing airport I think FRA does everything well. I much prefer FRA over CDG or LHR.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: A Cai
content: SIN-FRA. One of the worst airports. My friends connection flight was cancelled and his time spent there (8 hours waiting for Lufthansa to re-organize one) was a lonely and stifling nightmare. Unimpressive concrete designs inside - ugly. Signs not clear/easy to follow like in Changi/HK. So many gates/walking was with feeling of "where is...which direction would be next". Had quite a stressful time. Opt for London/Munich if need transiting!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: G Kowalski
content: Used only for connecting flight but still required to go through full security check and passport control so any liquids purchased in the departure airport were confiscated. Massive queue for the security check. Unfriendly and rude security staff. Confusing signage. To be avoided.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Kuipers
content: Unfriendly staff sending us in all directions except the good one. That is particularly bad because it lacks a good system of clear signs. How difficult can it be to hang a transit sign pointing in the right direction? Security is a disaster. Time consuming. No way you can get duty free bottles through security if you travel intercontinental. Impossible. I have seen many airports inside and outside of Europe but Frankfurt is definitely the worst. Avoid it if you can. And if you can't avoid it: give up all hope and be prepared to endure the misery.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Manhas
content: Terrible experience with rude border control staff. As is now quite often the practise with a lousy airlines like Lufthansa our flight to London was cancelled and I was stuck in transit going from Istanbul to London. The border police gave me an emergency visa so that I could join my wife and 6 month old daughter overnight at the hotel. A group of 6 Chinese students were not fortunate enough to get this and got blankets and told to sleep in the terminal. Next day when we tried to board the plane a horrendous grumpy border control woman refused to accept the visa given by her own colleagues a day earlier. Had to go up to her seniors spend an hour of unpleasantries only to be allowed to leave. Really terrible airport and I would recommend all non EU members to avoid it like the plague.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Hernandez
content: Nice airport! Signs could have greater clarity. Arrival and departure boards were a bit confusing.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: F Bodenstein
content: One of the worst airports in the world. It's like they took the plans for building an airport threw them in a blender and then threw that on a blueprint. No is no logic whatsoever to anything in this disgrace of a European travel hub. Highlights include no signs for toilets arrivals and departures interspersed alphabetically named gates that do not follow alphabetical order and terminals that are unfathomably separated by the runways that cannot be crossed without renting a car.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Anthony Gibbons
content: Transited FRA twice in the last month from Rio to Barcelona (16/5) and return from Nice to Rio (31/5). Short transits both ways. Airport and security staff very courteous and quite friendly. My only gripes would be the distance between regional gates (A zone) and the intercontinental gates (zone Z) signage could be a bit clearer to find the train. The men's toilets near gate A38 were a bit grim (resembled a pub toilet on a Friday night! Didn't look like the cleaner had been recently). Near same gate I bought a bottle of water from the cafe kiosk adjacent. Disappointing that the price was a pretty steep 3.90 euro and it wasn't even Evian. To add insult the attendant then pocketed the change! But that's not really the airport's fault. Compared to Rio airport Frankfurt is paradise.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: K Pardoe
content: Arrived by train into this labyrinth. Wanted to drop off the bags in storage for a few hours before check-in so we could go into Frankfurt for a bite to eat. Kept having to go up and down escalators and had to ask 2 staff members for directions before finding the signs to the baggage storage area. Arrived back to check-in and had to travel to T2 in a little automatic train with bags. More ups and downs on escalators to check-in and again to the gate. Had no problems with staff members as mentioned earlier.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Andrew Mortimer
content: Dangerous. Transited via gate D1 and the escalator had to be emergency stopped to avoid a crush at the bottom. Booked my flight from LGW to SGN at very short notice not realising it has a transit stop in FRA. Staff were surly and this terminal was handling more people than I think it was designed for. I would avoid wherever possible.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Sue Tulk
content: This is a horrible place with horrible staff. Are all the staff - and I mean every single one - under strict instructions never to crack a smile or relate in any sort of humane manner to passengers? I echo all the remarks about accessibility mapping frequent meaningless and hostile checks that others have posted here. My advice is to avoid this airport at all costs if you possibly can.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Millier
content: I arrived as a transit passenger with my duty free in a sealed tamper proof bag. You have to pass through security again even in transit. Security here confiscated all my duty free even in the sealed tamper proof bag. I had the receipt but they wanted the receipt inside the sealed bag. If the duty free shop doesn't do this how can the customer know? Major over reaction so petty and terrible service. I will never travel to or via this airport ever again.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: L Chen
content: Absolutely the worst airport I've been to in terms of friendliness and convenience. I arrived on a United flight from SFO and had to go to Terminal B for a transfer to Athens on LH. I had a 5-hour layover so I went to Lufthansa business class lounge in Terminal B. Even though my gate and the lounge are in the same terminal I had to pass through security. All together from arrival to lounge to gate I went through passport control 4 times (getting four stamps just going through Terminal B) security checkpoints 3 times (including the same checkpoint twice) and customs twice. it's the most inefficient and stupid layout for a terminal. Added to that everyone I encountered was unfriendly. While I expect that from airport security personnel I don't expect it from Lufthansa customer service. I asked a simple question of the check-in person at the lounge whether this particular lounge has shower facility I got a curt and snooty reply: "Of course this is Lufthansa lounge." I had to change my seat assignment with LH transfer desk so my wife and I could sit together and the lady behind the counter acted as if I was a total bother to her. No one I encountered had a slight smile or any sense of courtesy whatsoever. Avoid this airport at all costs.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: YJ Hwang
content: Flying from US for a cruise vacation and need a transfer from gate Z15 to B60 at Frankfurt. We spent entire one hour running around the airport maze to reach gate B60. My husband and I are senior citizens and each of us has one carryon luggage but this airport has endless stairs (no elevators) with no clear road map. We went up and down for 30 minutes and finally reach Gate B security check. Not sure why need security check between gates. If you are inside any gates meaning you already been checked once and everyone is clean. The security personal on Gate B are extremely rude. They did whole body search for 4 US citizens (we and two strangers in front of us) with a single hand held scanner. Each of us has to wait until the scanner was available. Just looked at previous reviews and found people had same complains since 2013. If the airport refuse to change then please just avoid this airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Jackson
content: Transfer twice Calgary to Zurich and return in last month. Could not comment on Facilities given our entire time was spent reaching our Gate. Why the need for repeated security examinations after clearing at our check-in terminal? Why passport control between and within Terminals? Evidently the concept of an internally secured passageway eludes management. Signage also seems to be a foreign concept. If you know there are multiple passengers with mobility problems or families with small children on a flight perhaps try a little harder to get to a Jetway instead of having them struggle down steps and onto a packed bus. 1960's Heathrow at it's worst. We did however find the notorious Tunnel possibly a filled in drainage ditch with just as much charm. My wife is slightly mobility challenged. This makes endless stairs/corridors difficult and puts a premium on functioning lifts. I dare say even fully fit individuals would not enjoy the experience. Our only positive is an enormous bouquet to the staff member responsible for finding a wheelchair when it became obvious the ordered electric cart would not come and running us through the maze to our gate.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Luc Devroye
content: The long underground escalator corridor in terminal 1 has been an annoyance for years. I am sure many travelers have missed connections because of it especially the elderly who would have to count on 15 minutes to traverse that obstacle. In addition the passport lines are interminable. The security lines are not much better and come with unfriendly employees.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Felix Fischer
content: I had a one day trip to Frankfurt and was surprised because the last time I was there my experience was not very good. But I visited the observation deck and the McDonalds and back to my terminal I drove with the Sky Train. There was no queue at the security check and I find the gate fast. Only the toilet was a bit atrocious. But at all I would recommend the airport if you travel to Frankfurt Cologne or Dusseldorf. For connecting flights I don't like the airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Taylor
content: Huge airport requires walking miles to get from gate to entrance/exit! This airport has one big advantage: once you have trekked yourself to the exit its a very fast (10-15mins) but expensive (5 Euros) S-Bahn ride to centre of town where tasty German sausages and beer awaits! I had a 3 hour stopover and this is what I did. It's a bit confusing because there is basically nothing to tell you when you've left the secure area (no customs or passport control visible) but I quite like that - reminds me I'm back in Europe! On the way back into the airport for my flight (about 11pm one of the last flights and I cut it pretty tight) I had no problems going through security - the Germans were as always full of beans and extra friendly! In Munich Lufthansa have free coffee machines at their gates but not here it seemed so that was a shame but overall a good experience based on the ease of getting to the city for food and beers. I think that if I had to kill time in the airport proper that I would quickly get bored however besides walking up and down there's not a lot else to do from what I saw.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Federico Muscogiuri
content: A huge and complicated airport. Schengen to Schengen connections usually work fine. Berlin to Madrid was brilliant get off the plane walk a few gates and you're there. On the positive side at the gate you have free papers and hot beverages as well as a good view of the runway. Non-Schengen to Schengen are a completely different thing. My last connection Amman-Madrid was so bad that put me off flying again via Frankfurt. Arrived at 5am but for some reason we landed in the Schengen terminal. Could not use the airbridge and in pouring rain had to be bussed to the non-Schengen terminal where in the meantime another three/four flights had landed. The usual long lines for passport control/security where for some unfathomable reason the officer took a special interest in my binoculars then again a long walk back to the Schengen terminal. All in all almost two stressful hours. Facilities are ok and the railway station allows easy and fact access to lots of destinations within Germany but this is not enough to compensate the stress so next time I will try hard to give this airport a miss.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Van Hiep Hoang
content: Part of new A+ terminal recently opened - nice fresh looks spacious and much improved restrooms. Ample seating at gate in the "old" A-terminal on-time departure and upon arrival on the following day a mere 15 minute wait for the baggage from the time leaving the plane - even though the plane was parked on an apron position. in the old A terminal there are coffee/tea machine for passenger use but not everywhere. There are even newspaper stands for when you arrive early in the morning.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Yvonne Meletaki
content: On a trip in December 2013 from a connecting flight from Manchester to Athens nearly missed the plane with a 1hr connecting time. Landed at terminal 1 gate C and had to get to gate A. Walked for miles up and down then on a train then through security where the fast lane was anything but fast with rude unhelpful staff. I would avoid Frankfurt in future or at least allow 2 to 3hrs connecting time.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: R Howe
content: On a connecting flight to Narita from London. Incredibly long walk past closed shops a train and another security check (with long wait). Only just arrived on time to board next flight. A disgrace for a code-share flight.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Kathie Schoenleben
content: I am a LH frequent traveler and use the Frankfurt airport for domestic German travel very often. I also use other German airports such as Munich Dusseldorf Hamburg Cologne Berlin on a regular basis so I have a good basis for comparison. I never cease to be amazed at the back-level stage of this hub of Europe. Twice I almost missed flights because of long lines - even long lines at the baggage drop when you already have a boarding pass. Why does this mega-airport have no self service bag check? If anything goes wrong with weather anywhere not just Frankfurt this airport seems to collapse - and there is total confusion and lines with no one managing them. This airport made me finally break down and stop checking bags. Even worse though is the security lines - the area has been redone and modernized with the result that there is more space but the security people work in slow motion! After observing them go through their routine several times I think they are trained to go through a drill which has more steps than at other airports - at an incredibly slow pace. This airport has trained me to get to the airport well in advance so I can stand twice as long in the fast lane as at any airport in Germany. This has been going on for months and has not improved.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Kevin Barrance
content: Not sure why the other reviewers seemed to have such a bad time at this airport. My experience was extremely positive. On arrival immigration was quick and bags delivered in good time. Coming back the queues for security were quite long but they soon opened up a new line and we went through quickly. Plenty of shops and cafes and generally a nice place to fly from. I'm satisfied!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Lee
content: What an awful airport. It's huge. The signage isn't great. Checking in with Lufthansa is all automated so it can be confusing and time consuming for the first time user. Don't bother asking any airline staff member to help you - they were rude and didn't help. Getting on to a flight is ridiculous - wait in a crowded departure lounge then finally scan your Boarding Pass only to be stopped just beyond the boarding gate to wait (again getting crowded) rather than let you board the plane. Arriving into Terminal 1 is even more illogical. Follow the signs to Immigration and Baggage Reclaim. Immigration is straight forward but next is Customs before reclaiming your bags. To get to the Baggage Reclaim you have to continue walking beyond Customs where you'll find yourself in the Check In area of the airport. Finally the Reclaim is down into an unsecured area and once you have your bags walk back out into the Check In area. The whole path is convoluted and illogical.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Sasun Vartanyan
content: A big disappointment for an airport (and host airline) claiming to strive to be one of the best transfer spots. FRA is very user unfriendly if you are transferring most of T1 is outdated has the 70s feeling to it and gets extremely crowded in the security areas where long walks/rides are required flying in from London 1.5 hrs transfer time to another Schengen destination (Ljubljana) was barely enough with no time left to browse which is a shame as the airport claims to be a transfer wonder. In addition the signs can be confusing too. Munich is much more user friendly and convenient.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Chris Lenz
content: As a frequent Star Alliance (Lufthansa) customer in Europe I often transit through this airport. First the good points: The shops and it's clean! Now the bad points: Long bus rides long walks (or runs usually) long queues. Overpriced refreshments no decent restaurants airside. Security extremely crowded especially morning and early evening. Don't expect respite in the Star Alliance lounges! Terrible directions and unfriendly (and often clueless) staff. On the subject of security why must you go through again when transferring from a non-Schengen flight? Nowhere else in Europe must you do this. Do they help you when you have 12 minutes to catch your next flight? If you are lucky they will direct you to the "Fast Lane" to stand for 30 minutes with all of the other people who also have 12 minutes too! My advice if you are travelling Lufthansa through Europe from or to beyond then try Munich.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Ogilvie
content: I used this airport as a transit on a flight from Edinburgh / Frankfurt / Moscow. My baggage along with at least 3 others were left in Frankfurt. It took two days for my baggage to be delivered to my residence in Moscow. On the return flight I was informed by Moscow Duty Free that a purchase of gin was fine to be hand carried as it was packed and sealed by Duty Free Moscow. In the security check in Frankfort transit area I was treated like a criminal by Frankfurt Security who confiscated the gin called the police subjected me to a completely over the top personal search took my wallet and insisted it be returned through the x-ray machine whilst forbidding me to leave the area where I was being held. They were offhand rude and lacking in personal skills. I would add that the walking required between flights is extremely long with no moving walkways. I will take steps in the future to avoid Frankfurt Airport where possible.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: I Courtens
content: Not my favorite airport ugly building long walking distances with ridiculous short travelators no decent restaurant in transit zone. Very unfriendly staff at security check. This is not based on a one time experience. Today I flew with Lufthansa and had a transit in Frankfurt when boarding the flight we must scan our boarding tickets via the automated gates ourselves. For some passengers this was not so straightforward the staff member at the gate clearly lost his nerves and was scolding these people. We are customers in the first place is a little bit of help and a smile too much to ask?

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Harold Bush
content: If you are transiting at Frankfurt give yourself at least 2 hours because this is not a friendly airport the walks are very long no one is around to help and if they do they are very rude. I walked past 6 Lufthansa so called 'service centres' on my way to the gate of my connecting flight but all were closed. Why do they put them there if they are closed? I do not know what it is but some staff at the airport are just very rude and not willing to help. Frankfurt makes Miami and CDG look friendly and efficient. Avoid this airport if you can.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Webster
content: This is the worst airport we have ever used I pre arranged disabled assistance for my wife but at check-in I was rudely told that we should have known there was a separate 'Holding Area' for my wife and advised it would be 10 minutes walk away. Once we got there we waited 30 minutes before for help arrived this was a complete disgrace. I then requested to be taken to the business class lounge which was met with grunts from the helper staff were unhelpful and the airport was difficult to navigate.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: V Jovanovic
content: We flew from JFK to FRA to transfer to BEG. It's been several months and I still wonder if traipsing through that airport was a bad dream I don't understand how we made our connection. If Germany is known for it's efficiency then this airport must be the black hole where they dump all of their 'inefficiencies'. There does not seem to be any real flow sometimes we didn't understand if we were to go straight or veer to the right. We walked took a bus went around a building (outside) stairs stairs walking took a quick restroom break where I had to wait to wash my hands while an airport staff member brushed her teeth. I would have liked to check out the shops etc. but with all the schlepping I didn't want to miss my flight. Ironically I plan to travel through FRA again this January - I want to fly on the 747-800 so we'll see if it's worth it. Hopefully since I'll be on LH through to BEG my schlep time will be cut and I can shop.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Wong
content: Flew into Frankfurt from Florence and connected to Air Canada to Montreal. We landed in Frankfurt the plane taxied awhile before it parked on the tarmac. Deplaned to a bus and the bus took a long run to Terminal 1. My guess is that commuter flights get relegated to the remote areas of the airport without a direct jet way connection to the terminal. We then went into the terminal and tried to find our connecting gate. The first set of monitors did not have our flight listed. So we found another set of monitors and the flight was listed but only Terminal 1 Gate B. But it did not say which gate so we had to take the elevator to B and then a series of people movers to get to B. Finally get to B and our flight is not listed. We finally got to the gate. First you check in with the agent who checks your passport. Then when the plane boards you check in again with an agent who just looks at your boarding pass and then with another agent who inputs you manually in the computer. They did not scan the boarding pass. This was very inefficient. Frankfurt is a huge airport so leave plenty of time to get to your connecting flight. If you have to change terminals good luck! The airport itself of modern and clean with good bathrooms. So if you have plenty of time to get to your connecting flight and use the automated kiosk if your flight is not listed this is not a bad airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Fong
content: Having travelled from Orlando to Frankfurt for 9 hours we had the displeasure of encountering border control officers as we made our way to our connecting flight to England. They were very vague as to what we should remove from our bags to put in the trays for x-ray. I asked if we had to remove cables and wires and they did not answer so we left them in as you do on US flights. They then insisted that I empty a bag containing underwear in front of them. They then took my husband into a private room while they searched his bag. Surely a bit of kindness and common courtesy wouldn't go amiss? Later at the gate they asked over 150 of us to queue to have our boarding passes checked with our passports. We then sat down only to be asked to get up immediately to have boarding passes checked again as we boarded. It was laughable. We will not use Lufthansa or Frankfurt Airport again.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Peter Janoff
content: A very disappointing airport experience. Immigration processing was taken care off by a lone man who looked very unhappy and seemed like he wanted to take out his frustration on innocent travelers - really unfriendly. Once inside the terminal the walk from arrivals to departures in order to switch flights was endless and dull. It took forever to find a monitor and even longer to find out which gate to proceed to. I waited 20 mins at a customer service desk and was ignored. Finally arriving after much detective work at the right gate announcement concerning the reason the flight was delayed varied wildly from snow on the ground to maintenance problems to having to pick up the kids early from day-crew. All in all quite sub standard in terms of information and convenience. However it was spotlessly clean.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Sebastian Rhein
content: Great airport mostly friendly staff very nice shopping facilities good atmosphere!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Scott Wilson
content: This must be the most pedantic and inconsistent airport in the world when comes to security avoid this airport at all costs! I flew through 4 major international hubs including Heathrow and USA in a 7 day period but once I got to Frankfurt security confiscated and tested all my hand luggage. This would be fine if it was the same everywhere but it's not and this airport is one of the worst in the world for entry from another country just avoid.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: O Geddes
content: After 9 hours flying from YVR I arrived at FRA expecting German efficiency at it's best and was surprised to find one of the most cramped long and inefficient airports I've visited. When we finally got off the plane we stood on the hot tarmac for 10 minutes. My connecting flight left in 1 hr 15 mins so wasn't rushed. When the bus finally arrived we took a 10 minute ride and then experienced another 10 minute wait this time on the bus. When I finally reached the airport I was greeted by an extremely un-appealing old building with a construction filled hallway that went on for at least 2 or 3 km's. No air conditioning and it was an almost 30 degree day but I have noticed that this is a pattern in European airports. Reached what I thought was customs but turned out to be more security only 3 different security doors which caused a gigantic line the scanner must have been very sensitive because I saw no one make it through without a pat down including me even though I was cleared in Vancouver. When I got through I realized what was first over an hour was now only 30 minutes and I saw yet another queue this one for a train. When I got off the train and through another gigantic line for customs I had only 15 minutes. After another long walk through the depths of FRA the hallway split revealing another line when passed through I was running I just made my flight by seconds where surprise surprise I was loaded onto a bus And all this after a 9 hour flight. I would recommend for people to stay away from FRA if possible because it is a gigantic mess full of inefficient security and customs and long hot lines.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Graeme Spencer
content: My 20 year old daughter was travelling via Lufthansa on her own from Birmingham to Doha transiting via Frankfurt at the beginning of July. Her connection was 75 minutes from a Lufthansa flight to another Lufthansa flight. She missed her connection and ended up having to pay for another ticket and an overnight stay in Frankfurt as there is only one flight a day to Doha. On arrival at Frankfurt the plane was met by a bus which took 15 minutes from landing to her reaching the terminal. Then had to join a deep queue to pass through security. Repeatedly asked to be fast tracked as her connection time was quite tight but was ignored. She finally got through security and made her way as fast as possible to her departure gate in terminal B only to find that her plane had departed. She had to pay for a new ticket and would need to pay for a night in a hotel. To make things worse her bags hadn't made the Birmingham flight and were following on and on their advise waited a further 2 hours for her bags only then to be told they had gone via Dubai and would be waiting for her! No attempt was made by Lufthansa nor the security people at the airport to help my daughter catch her plane. My family have transited through many airports on our way to and from the UK since moving here to Qatar including Frankfurt on a number of occasions but since this experience we will not be using Lufthansa ever again and certainly would avoid Frankfurt like the plague.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Judith Wotherspoon
content: I have now had two transit experiences at Frankfurt am Main Airport terminal both in July 2013. I am travelling on a Star Alliance ticket so each time I want to fly in Europe Lufthansa takes me to Frankfurt. This costs me both time and money since it uses unnecessary air miles and if course one needs to factor in landing and take off time transit time and potential delays with each stage. Now I know that you also have to factor in potential very long bus rides to the wrong end of the terminal for your individual purposes. In my case the first time both planes were parked at one end of the airport but the departure gate was at the other extreme. In the second case one of the planes actually did connect to the terminal but the walk was still very long and even in the business class lounge I was warned of this. To my mind this terminal and Lufthansa ticketing and scheduling policy serve the interests of the airline and the terminal and not the interests of the customers!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: David Mitchell
content: This is the most abysmal airport flown through. I was traveling with my wife and a small baby with a stroller with a tight connection. The fact that the gates for the connection were far apart are not the airport's fault. However the overall experience at Frankfurt was extremely inefficient and caused us to nearly miss our connection. We waited 10 mins for an employee to get the stroller off the plane whereas at other airports the stroller is waiting for you when you get off the plane. Unlike other airports given the distance to travel no vehicle was offered to transport us to the next gate so we walked over 1 mile (with no moving sidewalks they were all operating in the opposite direction). Then you continue to go up and down levels (very difficult with a stroller especially when some of the elevators are out of order). Also some access is blocked for strollers requiring a staff member to open a gate. Finally for an airport that is known for transfers it seems bizarre that a passenger continually hits passport checks thus wasting time (isn't one passport check enough for a connecting passenger not even staying in Germany)? Bottom line I would never transfer in Germany again I would much rather use Heathrow in Europe which has proper processes for connection passengers.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Aikaterini Manou
content: Had to transfer through this airport from San Francisco and I must say it was the worst experience transfer I have had. They used buses to transfer us from the airplane to the gate. They left us waiting on the bus for 10 minutes with doors closed then left us walking to the gate. I asked at the information if there was an automatic water machine to fill my bottle and the reply was to go to the toilets! Extremely poor signage and the staff were very rude and uncivilized. You should definitely avoid this airport!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Helen Paterson
content: I recently passed through Frankfurt Main on a trip from Prague to Singapore. I found the signposting to be inadequate and spent 35 minutes walking around before we found the correct terminal and gate. For such a large airport staff are needed such as are to be found in Singapore Airport to assist travellers find their way.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Barnetson
content: Transited this airport on return Gatwick to Sydney via Frankfurt and Hanoi. After we arrived we where given transit cards and had Business class lounge passes to star alliance lounge. We could not find lounge very badly sign posted eventually found it with 3 other passengers. Then was told that we could not use lounge as we are not entitled to. After myself and 3 other customers explained we were transit passengers and this was a star alliance flight she begrudgingly let us in. No PA or flight board and very limited food even though this was 2 pm in afternoon. They need to fix their game definitely not up to the usual standard we experienced in Germany.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Derek Lightfoot
content: I've suffered more stress and missed more flights at this dump than all other airports combined and I've been commuting weekly on business for more than 20 years. My recent trip: Plane lands and taxis for 20 minutes to some remote outfield. Can't find any steps to get off the plane. Eventually they find 1 set so front passengers can get off. A bus arrives but it isn't big enough for all passengers. 40 minutes after landing you embark on the drive to the terminal itself and after 10 minutes in the bus you enter the labyrinth of tunnels under the terminal building only to come to a complete halt in a traffic jams. Stagger off the bus with only 8 minutes of your 1 hour connecting time left. Left to negotiate a series of steps and corridors back to the gate you just passed in the bus. Tunnel of Missed Connections runs for about 1km between A and B gates. To get to it you can wait for the inadequate lifts or carry your bags down about 8 flights of stairs before running. Another security check with huge queues and another passport control. Missed connecting flight. Lufthansa don't fly direct anywhere anymore so if you pick them you'll suffer Frankfurt too.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Hans-Dieter Janecke
content: I arrived with the ICE from Cologne and thought I would have enough time to work a little before departure. But then I had to pass security in Terminal 1 which is centralized for the A-gates. It took me 27 minutes even though the line was not extremely long and they do a good job in queue management by channelling passengers to the various check lines. Also I always feel that the air is good and it feels a little too hot - anyway not a comfortable atmosphere. This time I was lucky departing from gate A18 which is not too long of a walk. On other occasions I had Gate 42 and this took a really long walk.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Fabian Barth
content: Great Airport modern clean lots of shopping possibilities clear signs and friendly staff. However very long walks and often no moving walkways.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Diaz
content: Missed connections seem to be more common at FRA than at other airports of this size. Signage was good in some places extremely poor in others but other notifications are sorely lacking. I experienced a gate change with no announcement made over the PA nor at the original gate (they admitted they only indicate this in the electronic system which you must walk up to and enter you flight number or scan your boarding pass) and hence missed the boarding call. They claimed they called my name throughout the airport but I doubt it was throughout since it is incredibly difficult to miss the loud announcements.
