Security staff as previously mentioned were anything but courteous. Long distances and multiple checkpoints make short connections nearly impossible between airlines. Free Wifi is only available if you have a mobile phone that has international roaming allowing you to receive an SMS message. Clean bathrooms and premises decent food choices (though pricey as all airport food is) but if you're trying to make a connection then choose another airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Lipponen
content: I arrived early morning from Miami and I had some extra time at the airport. A terminal one is very big and walking distances may be very long. Passport control between Schengen and non-Schengen areas was a breeze as I was the only passenger in the whole area. Arrival gate was of course some Z-gate far away and I followed signs to my next flights departure gate. Quiet border control but I had almost the same distance to walk back to Lufthansa lounge and then back to the gate. Always look for signs carefully as they may be a shorter route but it was a refreshing trek after a long flight.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: R Roth
content: Having had a disastrous experience on my last trip to Africa connecting through the Paris CDG airport (the security personnel were the worst that I have ever encountered) I decided to try this time the Frankfurt airport. I was very pleasantly surprised. The airport was very well labelled so it was no problem finding the terminal for my connecting flight. The security lines were quite short the personnel manning these were very pleasant and helpful. The bathrooms were extremely clean and the food stalls had lots of interesting things to try. Frankfurt takes my vote over Paris or London for connections through Europe.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Cameron
content: My experiences of FRA mirror those of Jan Willems see post dated 27 Feb 2013. I travel through FRA almost monthly and while I can forgive the poor layout of the airport and expensive food the security personnel are the worst I have seen. As Jan said of security; "horrible attitude slow intimidating no consideration for travellers on tight connection. I don't expect to be treated like a celebrity but a minimum of respect and decency would not be outplayed". There is nothing I need to add to that! All other staff have been friendly and helpful but the security personnel definitely need some training to remind them they are dealing with ordinary people going about their business not convicts in a prison.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Xavier
content: USA to FRA on 23 February 2013 FRA is an unholy mess. Flight landed 5 minutes early plane then taxied for many minutes before unloading passengers onto tarmac at remote part of airport. We then boarded buses for trip to terminal which took many more minutes. Unloaded at terminal B had to go through full security scan then. Once through had to navigate many corridors to find our departure gate. Everything took far too long and we missed our flight. Airport itself is worn and tired bathrooms very small and old limited food options past security. Everything about airport was worn and dingy.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Stebeleski
content: Recent transit through Frankfurt excellent security helpful friendly and professional even though I needed additional screening they provided a plastic bag so my liquids would not be confiscated passport control fast and efficient. Duty free very expensive but there is a cheap grocery store stocked with chocolate and other German foods at the normal prices downstairs near the rail terminal. Showers are expensive at €9 and restaurants are very costly. Overall I don't mind Frankfurt for a connection.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Jan Willems
content: Passing through FRA nearly every month while in general just OK security staff is just the worst I came across globally. Especially the small team checking entry from non-Schengen into Schengen close to gates B1-12 have a horrible attitude slow intimidating no consideration fro travellers on tight connection. I don't expect to be treated like a celebrity but a minimum of respect and decency would not be outplayed.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Adrian Dix
content: I nearly missed my connection because of their passport control being understaffed. Check in was slow for some unknown reason. The airport is OK for food drink and the usual facilities. I'd advise that you give yourself plenty of time for your flight.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Zacher
content: Arrival by train at the long-distance train station. Check-in at the airline counters there. Within 30 mins I was at the gate. Easy if you know your way. Remember it belongs to one of the biggest airports in the world referring to passenger traffic and most flights are handled at one terminal (1) with four piers.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Sierra
content: Little consideration to weary travelers. No free internet anywhere very few places to sit down and relax while waiting for flight connections. Sure they have chairs but nothing comfortable certainly nothing where you can attempt to sleep. The restaurants are extremely expensive and of poor food quality.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: L S Davis
content: Bizarrely designed airport that grew from an earlier not very rationally conceived labyrinth to its present colossus of corridors - be prepared to encounter others like yourself wandering lost out in the outback areas of the connecting hallways. Don't ask security for directions they're just there to provide the discipline. One rushes from arrival to departure gate and finds almost an hour has gone by and suddenly you are once again required to go through security. Once they locate your luggage you may be able to get it in a day or two.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Pickering
content: Had to transfer through this airport and I must say it was one of the worst I have ever transferred through! I found the layout of the airport to be like a maze and the security to be the slowest I have ever been through there seemed to be no sense of urgency with them and it seemed to by vastly under staffed. On the same trip I transferred back through Munich which was a far better layout and well staffed.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: James Reeve
content: No airbridges for British Airways so bussed off and on BA Flights when I have connected there to Qantas and SriLankan airlines recently. Long queues and appalling security staff - rude and uninterested. German efficiency - you must be joking! What is more it has not improved over the last 18 months and one wonders if the German Authorities care about what impression they are giving the world.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: PM Stüben
content: Long queue at baggage drop off because of lack of staff. Be ready for worse at security again understaffed and under-equipped. Then prepare yourself for a long march to your gate to find out either that the gate just closed or that instead of the 3 available entries just 1 is open. If you arrive and want to get your baggage be prepared for a long walk. No need to hasten though as it will take ages for baggage to be delivered. Count 2 hours for a speedy operation. In short: avoid Frankfurt whenever possible.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Van Hiep Hoang
content: This airport has been upgraded and its improved a lot. Hot water for tea and coffee FOC. Walk way to international gates is far but there are travelators. Security is tight but fast. Rest rooms are not sufficient.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Andrea Chng
content: Transferring airlines is awful at this airport. I arrived from Heathrow and had 2.5 hour transit and 95% of that time was used to try and find an open transfer desk (we went to 4 desks and most were closed and then was told to go to the gate where our boarding pass would be issued contrary to the advice we were originally given. We just made it to our connecting flight. Long hikes poor layout and no one around when we arrived to assist us for directions. Frankfurt airport should learn from Changi and Hong Kong airports.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Darren Walker
content: Worst queues for check in that I have ever endured. We got our boarding passes from the self-service machine for the 10.40 Lufthansa flight to Manchester then queued for almost an hour until at 10.10 we reached the check in counter only to be told that it was too late to get on our flight. Got switched to 16.15 flight and given 30 euros food/drink vouchers. No apology from check in staff just a denial that they were understaffed or too slow.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Stanley
content: There are some very negative comments posted here. Sadly I have to agree with most of them. I passed through a couple of times in December. A lot of walking is required. I am not sure that this is because it is big terminal it may just be that it is not logically laid out. As many have complained. The queues or security can be incredibly long and the staff seem to work very slowly. I also had some problems with the poor signs - that adds to the distance you have to walk after back tracking a few times. Finally the LH business lounges are pretty poor. So all in all not a very good experience and well behind what the likes of Heathrow is offering.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: H Sipcer
content: Plane arrived late from LHR but there might just have been time to catch my connecting flight to Warsaw Chopin had there not been long queues at security and a long distance between the gates. Not just long queues but what must be the most badly organised security checks I've been through. Not enough trays very slow scanning and a body search involving taking your shoes away for a few minutes by officious and disinterested staff. Must have run half a mile to the gate be told that the flight had just closed and to go to the another long queue at the Lufthansa desk to rebook. No room on the next flight so had a 3 hour wait. Chopin LHR and Dusseldorf (which I returned through) all worked like Swiss watches by comparison.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Anna Jeliazkov
content: I had a connecting flight at Frankfurt bound to SFO on Dec 9 2012. Flight was cancelled last minute along with 350 other flights. There were no PA announcements or direction where to go and what to do for rebooking. Lines were forming everywhere but not clear for what. After 8 hours waiting for hotel/taxi voucher some people manage to go to a hotel but for the most there was no hotel and had to stay on the line until the check ins reopen for booking at the next day at 5.30 am. This was the case for everyone no priority for families with kids or elderly. On the next morning Dec 10th seemed as Frankfurt airport got it together. We managed to catch a flight but I want to leave a very strong message here that If Frankfurt/Lufthansa want to stand for a premier airport/airline there is a need to review its procedures and policies. Frankfurt airport was not a safe place to be at on Dec 9th.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Leston
content: FRA is getting progressively worse with really long distances to walk after being bussed to Terminal 2 from a remote stand. The terminal is dark and gloomy with long queues and little distraction in the way of shops/entertainment. Not a patch on T5 at Heathrow.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Curfs
content: I do not understand what everyone has against FRA. I feel that the signposting is fine security staff is friendly and cues never too long even the staff at bars and restaurants are actually quite nice. Parking is easy just as is checking-in. Really compared to CDG or LHR for instance this airport is better.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Bakke
content: Very long hikes on the airport! Came from Japan with transfer to Oslo. Missed the OSL left the lounge to late. Took about 20 mins to gate! No calls are made so pay close attention to the screens which do not warn that the gate is closing. Avoid this airport use MUC instead much better airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: H Vaneif
content: Although I arrived on time from Singapore I missed my flight connection to Amsterdam because the queues at security were extremely long and slow and the person from security services didn't allow me on the available fast lane through security although I had only 20 minutes left to boarding time. After more than 35 minutes queuing I finally made my way through security then had to run down the long alleys with my hand luggage to show up at the gate 15 minutes before departure. But as they use buses at some of the gates to transfer you to the airplane the buses had already left and the gate for Amsterdam was closed. Lufthansa made my day again by booking me on the next available flight 2 hours later but Frankfurt airport didn't do a good job here: this really was unnecessary. So in case you need to travel via Frankfurt and you have the choice between connecting flights then take your time to save yourself the hassle as the personnel might not help you.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Mark Evans
content: A curate's egg of an airport offering a mixture of the excellent and the unsatisfactory. There is a lot of trekking involved especially in the connections between Terminal 2 and the DB railway station. This station is very handy if you're using Terminal 1 but getting to and from Terminal 2 involves a bus shuttle for which you can wait a long time outside the building with minimal shelter. The buses used have not been well adapted for pax carrying heavy or bulky luggage. The bus journey itself takes between 5-8 minutes according to direction of travel. Surely there's a better way.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Brown
content: This must be the worst airport in Western Europe. Arrived from Abu Dhabi heading for Chicago and had a 3 hour layover. Needed almost every minute of it to get through the airport. The airport is confusing has long walks is cold has unhelpful staff and is in need to an upgrade. The interior tram was broken causing passengers to be re-routed by staff who didn't have a clue. An entire security section was malfunctioning and the doors were shut leaving passengers stuck outside the area. Eventually we were sent to many different lines and waited in confusion only to be redirected time and time again. Does anything or anyone work at this airport?

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: A Tee
content: The airport has confusing check-in counters and boarding gates since that all use the same alphabets. Some domestic flights like Niki air were not updated on the flights main board and information staff were not all that helpful. Overall a terrible experience.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: John Perkins
content: Transferred from Anchorage on Condor to Manchester on Lufthansa both Terminal 1. After disembarking had the longest bus ride ever about 20 minutes and then walked about 2 miles between drop-off and gate. Signage a bit confusing. Went upstairs then downstairs again! Although we were in transit we had to go through security yet again with quite a long queue. Only just made our call despite layover being nearly 2 hours. At least our luggage arrived okay! Never again if we can help it.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Margaret Robinson
content: Went through yesterday for a connection from a Budapest to Manchester (UK). Landed in A and took off from B. Dreadful experience. I don't consider myself disabled but I do have a rheumatic disorder which makes walking long distances without a break difficult. I had an hour for transfer and only just made my flight on the last call and that was walking without a break and walking fast down the moving walkways. It's as well there were no queues at security as I would have missed my connecting flight. It will take several days to recover. I will avoid Frankfurt in future.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Jones
content: This was the first time I travelled through Frankfurt with our new baby. It really hit home how family- unfriendly the airport is. I spent most of my time in the Z gate area but travelled there from the B gate area. When travelling we put our baby in a regular sized stroller. Apparently to stop people from using carts on certain lifts and moving walkways the Frankfurt airport has installed barriers. Unfortunately unless you're using a very thin umbrella stroller you are blocked by the same barriers put up to block luggage carts. My wife and I had to lift our stroller over a high barrier simply to get to the elevators allowing us to travel from B gate to Z gate. Not helpful! Another family unfriendly aspect of Frankfurt airport is the location of the ubiquitous Camel Smoking Rooms. If you want to light up that's fine. But the Camel Smoking Rooms are located directly adjacent to the lifts. If you have a child you know how important the lift is when you're using your stroller. Even though the rooms are ventilated a lot of smoke and stench comes out. At Z gate there are two baby-rooms for changing and cleaning your baby. On my recent layover in Frankfurt I stood outside one of the rooms for a very long time waiting for it to be unoccupied. Presently a janitor came by who asked why I was waiting for a closed baby changing room. Astonished I searched fervently for a sign mentioning that the room was not in service and found none. I'm leaving out quite a few problems that were more adult oriented to simply focus on what could be improved for families. Move the Smoking Rooms away from lifts and baby rooms and widen the cart barriers to allow strollers to pass.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Casper Yap
content: SQ25 we had a stop over at FRA. The transit was unremarkable. No need to recheck through security transit around B gate. Time for a snack and children playground. Easy. The SQ26 was different. This time we had to go a long route through connecting flight security with the long lines. Some passenger were confused because it looked like you were walking to the immigration area. Time consuming. T1 is clean with good transit facilities. Constructing has stopped and that makes things much better.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Jezrel Sabaduquia
content: Transferred twice at Terminal 1. The ceilings were low seating area was plentiful but it felt cramped otherwise. Some of the bathrooms were awful although luckily I found a decent one (which wasn't clean still) near the gate which was tucked away so there was less traffic which meant better condition. Gate area had a nice little restaurant which offered decent options and a shop with souvenir items some snacks and drinks. Second return was a horrible experience. Security was chaotic low ceilings once again made it feel really cramp. Plus side is that the security agents were efficient polite and friendly. Good signage though both English and German. I will try to avoid FRA in the future especially Terminal 1.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Albanes
content: Recently transited LIS-FRA-MEX. I had an 1 hour to transfer and I hated the long distances the dreadful "rainbow tunnel" and the stairs connecting the Schengen with the non-Schengen area. I was lucky and I found no people at migration queue otherwise I could have missed my flight. Waiting lounge was crowded and claustrophobic restrooms in bad conditions. Boarding was chaotic. On the good side staff are polite and always try to help you. This is an airport to be avoided better try MUC AMS or ZHR which are excellent.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Michael Robinson
content: Flew through Frankfurt twice in last month for connecting flights. A reasonably nice airport experience other than the prices over 9 euros for a small bottle of water and packet of Pringles. Outrageous. Positive smoking rooms. If LHR wants to stay ahead of the game as a transit airport it seriously needs to consider if people would perhaps choose other routes if they fancy a smoke in transit. All the main transit airports in Europe and the Far East have them Singapore having one that is actually outside surrounded by butterflies!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Andor
content: Recently flew through FRA with Lufthansa from SFO and then connecting to Budapest. I am not sure if the whole airport was like this but the 2 Lufthansa terminals I was in were terrible. I have flown through FRA on other airlines in the past and have had much better memories. You would think that the home airline (Lufthansa) would have the best terminal facilities but that is definitely not the case here.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: P Swain
content: Had no problems negotiating this airport in transit from Dublin to Bangkok. I was pleasantly surprised. Just like another reviewer said follow the signs it's not rocket science and we reached at our next gate with ease and in plenty of time. Some people seem to complain about the most minute niggles I has the same experience after reading reviews of Mumbai airport only to find yet again transfers were smooth. Having travelled through many airports Frankfurt was one of the more pleasant journeys.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: I Lowrie
content: Great experience. I put it down to being well prepared and reading in advance the do's and don'ts and tips. Flew in 6pm from Seoul terminal B. Long walk but if an overweight 60 yr old woman travelling solo can then anyone can! Next flight was 7.55am next day. Went to check in and got my own boarding pass and Checked bags in that night while it was quieter and had overnight bag. Next morning at peak time I did not have to queue and it was smooth through security. Through the whole experience I stopped and asked if I didn't know where to go or what to do. I approached with a smile and an 'excuse me' and I received courteous service.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: E Brydges
content: Recently we had to transfer through Frankfurt airport and it was a very frustrating experience. I will never do that again! The airport itself is very confusing no help from staff few seating areas and you are running from one end to another. If you don't have your boarding pass for your transfer you have to go through a line-up for passport control go out of the security area to be sent from one counter to another. After you get your boarding pass you have to go back through another line-up to passport control then another to security check and we still had to line up to the gate for boarding pass check and another line-up for actual boarding. Not something you want to do after 9 hours of travel.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Saketh Rahm
content: For a modern European airport hub this airport falls very short - reminds me more of a hospital with no lighting or color anywhere just grey cement and flooring. Arrived from DEL to transfer to IAH spent endless time walking with no shops anywhere. Arrived at terminal C and there is one duty free shop before security. After security and TSA pre-screening there is nothing but gates. The lounge for he A380 is a joke - worst I have seen anywhere for C class passengers. Many parts of the airport need repair with cords hanging from ceiling throughout. For a better experience try T5 at LHR or even CDG.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: I Sobkowiak
content: Arriving from BKK passport checking and security check in Transit took almost two hours. Very unfriendly staff. Being even more late now we were running for 20 minutes to our gate (it was changed shortly before). Lufthansa staff told us the flight had boarded. Transfer Desk staff very helpful and managed to get us on next flight. FRA is a very big airport with long walking distances few facilities but lots of unfriendly staff. We will avoid FRA and Lufthansa in the future.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: B Ashby
content: We arrived at Frankfurt airport having been delayed for two hours by the crew of our Lufthansa flight being "stuck in traffic" (strangely none of the passengers had the same experience). We were told by the flight crew as we landed that we should contact the ground staff for further information on connecting flights. Unfortunately there were no staff to be found to provide the said information in arrivals. We had very few minutes to spare to catch our connecting flight to Brazil and so made our way to the relevant gate with great haste. There were no queues through security but the rudeness of the security staff was quite unbelievable. Two of our group were told to take our bags into a side room for further search. It was explained to the staff that we were about to miss our flight. This had the effect of making them slower. Swabs were taken of the bags and then they walked away leaving the bags open and not saying anything. When we enquired whether we could now go a shrug indicated that we could. After charging through the airport as fast as our legs would carry us we made the flight as the doors were closing. Unfortunately our suitcases didn't make the journey. Thanks to Tam airlines they did catch up with us 3 days later. I will avoid Frankfurt in future.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: T Hoeh
content: Although a busy Saturday morning quick LH-baggage drop and no wait at security check. Part of new A+ terminal recently opened - nice fresh looks spacious and much improved restrooms. Ample seating at gate in the "old" A-terminal on-time departure and upon arrival on the following day a mere 15 minute wait for the baggage from the time leaving the plane - even though the plane was parked on an apron position.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Roberts
content: Just recently transferred through FRA and was amazed at the difference in staff attitudes - people were either friendly or went out of their way to be nice. While the airport's layout can't be changed and is a negative the improvement in staff attitude has made this a much more pleasant airport for transfers.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Daniel Summer
content: Transited through Frankfurt many times both from USA within European cities and departing for Asia directions. The immigration regime remains very confusing and signage as to which connecting gate and their locations are very inadequate adding to the confusion and stress. Recent experiences include international transit allowance of 2.5 hours which by travelling consensus is adequate. Not so. The usual lame excuse of a sudden and unexpected influx does not hold water. Airports deal with these things everyday and even if it happens it is really and merely a test of its own capability ie this is what they are there for. The official position was 45 minutes being the promised benchmark. That time we used 2 hours 10 minutes walking quite briskly from one end through controls and locating and checking directions as we hurried: no second chance at that moment. I think the fact the Lufthansa had dominated that European region and the Frankfurt hub so much no one there thinks there is anything wrong or requiring improvement. We travelling public have to arm ourselves with this shared knowledge.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Murphy
content: Never transfer at this airport if it can be helped. The staff are unhelpful even at the transfer information desk who are supposed to assist. The queuing at passport control and security takes ages even when it was explained to staff that we needed to board another plane. Security are very unhelpful and there is no fast lane for transfers. The airport is very large and it is hard to find your way about. A number of passengers missed our transfer going out and the most upsetting thing was it was repeatedly inferred that it was the passengers fault and not the woeful inadequacies at the airport. This is obviously a regular problem as staff at the other airports are very helpful when they learn that your flight involves changing at Frankfurt. A very stressful couple of experiences.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Rishi Saluja
content: My Wife and I had a very harassing experience last week when travelling back to India via Frankfurt. With every flight that I take from this airport my opinion about the Security personnel becomes worse. They are rude and extremely rough in their behaviour. I understand that the extensive security check and screening is being done in the best interest of the passengers' safety. But definitely this can be done in a more polite manner. The Lady at the security check insisted on re-checking my wife's baggage again and again in spite of being told by other security personnel that everything in the baggage was ok. My Wife was asked to move the baggage from one security counter to another and if this was not enough a special screening was done at a third counter. All this for a chocolate cake that she was carrying in the trolley bag from Vienna. Unless it is very necessary in the future I will avoid using this airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: G Zilic
content: I and my spouse recently flew thru Frankfurt airport to connect to another EU destination and found the airport to be a nightmare. Their airport staff were very rude and never really gave us an answer to our questions except that you are too early for your flight and you need to come back. In the US you are told to be at your gate 2 hours to get thru security screening etc. Not in Frankfurt. They rush you thru their security 30 minutes before flight and then hope that your gate has not changed by then as well. Very poorly run airport if you want your guests to shop at your airport stores etc make them more accessible to the passengers. We felt like we were in this huge unplanned maze and the staff were very rude and unhelpful. We will avoid Frankfurt airport at all costs in the future!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Batterly
content: Terrible experience in this airport. Arrived with a 3+ hour layover (onto another European country) and the process of going through immigration and then security was extremely disorganized and far too long. Immigration line closed forcing all people (who had been waiting for a long time) to move to another (already long) line. Security lines long and slow even priority lanes. Everything took so long that I arrived at my gate just minutes before boarding time. I will avoid this airport in the future.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Tilo Weger
content: Frankfurt is an airport which should be avoided. Distances for arriving passengers from an international arrival to your rental car is like a marathon. Also the missing escalators in concourse A from the upper (international) level to the jetways are a catastrophe. When you board from there you have to carry your hand luggage down the slippery and small staircase and when you arrive on a 747 then 300 passengers have to drag their hand luggage up the stairs. A total mess especially for older or handicapped passengers. In Munich they have solved this problem with a short escalator but it seems Frankfurt does not care. Next time I'll use Dusseldorf or Munich. Frankfurt should learn from Hong Kong and other airports how to get rid of their inadequate signage.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Kurt Mueller
content: As many contributors have mentioned this airport is plagued by queues for almost anything. What always baffles me is the inability of immigration to enforce the segregation between holders of EU passport and non- EU passports. This often leads to extended waiting time - particularly for arriving passengers with EU passports - who rightly expect smooth processing at immigration but are then held back by people with obscure passports who are in the wrong line. Sadly immigration officials rarely send them back to the proper queue and seem happy to see those pax take a hit who adhere to the signage.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Case van Hattem
content: Came through on way to Vienna. Flight and gate info clear on electronic boards. Ask questions in English if necessary. Don't give up first time you get a growl. Use Sky Trains to get in between terminals. Use several escalators they simplify things and there are friendly people to advise the way. If you have a boarding pass printed for your onward journey that was printed outside of Frankfurt go to the Lufthansa help kiosk and have a local one printed for all Schengen trips if possible. There are showers reasonable price reasonable wait. Food courts very good. Shopping ample. Go through gates as early as possible. Don't take liquid through. Buy coke water etc at boarding gate vending machine. security take off belt all metal in tray or bag to be scanned shows will be checked. Will always try to go through Frankfurt even at a higher cost.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Laurens Verkade
content: One of the most poorly managed major airports in the world: poor signage inadequate directions masses of people lined up and waiting for security passport control or immigration - we even had to line up and wait for access to the Business Lounge. Not enough sky-bridges to handle all incoming flights so many arriving planes must park on the tarmac; passengers disembark using mobile stairs and are then bussed to the terminal (about a 10 mins ride). Passports are checked at disembarkation then again upon entry to the terminal then again at a security checkpoint. There is a checkpoint to check boarding passes in the corridor between the security checkpoint and the lounge between gates B42 and B44. For a nation which prides itself on efficiency and effectiveness this airport is a shocking disappointment.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Ferguson
content: Horrible experience on recent trip from Aberdeen to Florence via Frankfurt. Staff were rude unhelpful and patronising. Despite a 3 hour connection time and thinking we were in the right terminal with adequate time we were held up by having to go through passport control and baggage again then getting to our boarding gate to find it had been changed - resulting in our missing boarding and refused on the flight - which still had 20 minutes until take-off. We had 3 young children with us. Passport control staff were in particular extremely rude as were the Lufthansa staff at the gate. We were held up for at least 20 minutes at passport control while numerous people pushed their way in front because they had to rush for their flights.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Jose S Rodrigues
content: Criticized by its enormous size and sometimes unfriendly security staff I feel like this airport is pretty functional and you should be fine as long as your connection is at least 1 hour.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Weiss
content: After reading the reviews I was dreading our transfers. If your connection requires changing from terminal A to Z you'll have a very long walk. Signage was perfectly clear restrooms plentiful and clean. Security was polite and fast. I'd have no hesitation to book through Frankfurt again!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: W Pavlinec
content: I fly through FRA twice a year and have never had a bad experience. Indeed the walks can be long (especially from B to A) and the airport maze-like. After a 10 hour flight I'm eager to stretch my legs and get some exercise so I'm not bothered by the distances. The signage is first rate and make the airport easily navigable. Without question the airport is ageing but gracefully. It's unmistakably German; it's functional without much fuss.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Frank Sutters
content: Security personnel at all check points very rude and slow. If you transfer from one flight to another you will need a lot of time to find the right gate. Frankfurt is like a huge labyrinth. There is no transportation service if you have to change the terminals or a long distance from one gate to another. Even Munich is much better. Compared to other airports it is terrible and unhygienic.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: H Lee
content: BER-FRA-SIN. It felt like a labyrinth from one terminal to another. Cant wait for long haul flights out of BER. Security checks thorough but quite slow since one needn't proceed to the specific terminal for their hand luggage to be checked. Most passengers were nervous about being late.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Alain Kupferman
content: Frankfurt Airport is a catastrophe in two aspects. Distances to be walked with ridiculously short conveyors and no Skytrain connection between terminals C and A/Z. Waiting area before immigration in Terminal B far too small when several planes from non-schengen countries arrive; in addition queuing is pathetic with passengers from the non-schengen countries blocking the EU lanes.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: R Spaargaren
content: Having had to transfer a number of times in the past few years I dread having to transfer at FRA again next month. Too big an airport with unclear or no signage no staff to be found (especially when arriving late at night on a long haul flight) impossible layout. I recognise many of the situations described on this website and avoid going through FRA whenever I can.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Thomas Hoeh
content: Departure from Terminal 1C. Slow passport control but no lines at security screening and very friendly security staff. Quiet and clean spaces friendly but somewhat sombre atmosphere. Wide range of competitively priced duty-free goods.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Thomas Hoeh
content: Check-in for a flight on a Saturday morning. Absolutely no queuing at security check friendly staff and quick service. Good update of restroom facilities in the B/C terminal area. Seems like the installation of a service evaluation button has helped to increase cleanliness. Ample seating facilities in all "A"-terminal area. Both out-going and in-going on Lufthansa flights use of airbridges so quick boarding guaranteed. Considering the amount of passengers using this international airport on a daily basis the service they provide is commendable.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: K Squire
content: Booked a return trip LHR-SIN via FRA in June 2011 for travel in November 2011. Connection times for each leg where 1hr 40mins and 1hr 35 mins respectively. Read the reviews on this site about FRA and was very concerned I made a big mistake and not left enough time to make the transfers due to the confusing nature of airport. Having now made the trip I can wholly recommend the airport. On the outbound journey we parked at a bus stand and was bussed to B terminal. Our connecting flight departed from a C gate. The signage at the airport is clear. Follow the signs to C. The return journey was just as straightforward. We arrived at a C gate and had to transfer to B22. However this gate was changed to B47 during the time we were at the airport. But there was at least two clear announcements and flashing indications of change on departure gate boards. I agree the walks can take 15 mins or so but it is a big airport. What do people expect? Walk off one plane straight onto another? In conclusion if anybody is like me and is a rare user of FRA do not be put off by the negative comments on this site. There are plenty of signs and they are clear. Queues were also reasonable for large airport. Still had plenty of time to make connection.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Amrinder Arora
content: My main complaint about this airport is simply that there are far too few gates compared to the number of flights. 90% of time there is no gate (no jet bridge) available rather you get on and off the airplane using stairs and then walk to people movers. I saw plenty of elderly people and people with kids being severely inconvenienced in those things. For that reason alone I do not recommend this airport. Also this airport has one person restrooms with people lining up outside.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Leston
content: If like me you're arriving on a remote stand at Terminal 2 be prepared for a very very long walk. There was a massive queue at passport control and a surprisingly large number of 'repairs in progress' making the terminal look scruffy.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Alan Friend
content: I've made two round trips through this airport in the last 6 months. Each time has got progressively worse. In 8 arrivals and departures the only time a jet way was used was for 2 departing Lufthansa flights to Zurich. All others used a stairway from the plane then herded you onto a bus to get to the terminal. Once in the terminal it is a half-mile walk to get to the gate up and down stairs or waiting in a long line for the very small elevators. Never again will I connect through Frankfurt.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Matthias Mayer
content: I use FRA frequently and cannot understand most of the complaints. True signage is in dire need of revamp and first/business class lines are not strictly enforced at security. But cleanliness of the airport or lavatories has never been an issue. It's one of the world's biggest airports so walking distances can be significant. But this comes with the convenience of connecting flights.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Bowling
content: Never again. Bad signage (twice I went into dead ends finding myself alone with no one to ask) few arrival/departure boards no available customer service in terminals really long walks (I don't know how anyone with walking impairments can connect in this airport). Where is the German efficiency we hear about? US Air allows too little time for its connecting departures out of this airport. I was on the run yet nearly missed my flight. Never again!!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Y Kahanovych
content: I did learn all the maps to understand layout so was well prepared to transit trough it last week. It worked. Signage there is useless as it doesn't explain difference between Shengen and non-Schengen wings. Went through both terminals. Overall impression was very depressing. Badly planned and poorly managed. I had no problem at security due to late departure time. Otherwise ten minutes spent on scanning my bag wouldn't work in big crowd. Immigration had just one manned desk for all outbound non-EU traffic. Regular passengers crews fast track - all served in one line in total chaos by one officer. I gave up my turn in the line for 12 crew members 2 business class passengers and one family with a baby. So many people jumping the queue before me! On arrival with Lufthansa from Nice we were parked somewhere within 10 minutes bus ride. Arrival hall had just one narrow escalator (supermarket type) for 300 people with hand luggage. On departure we were asked to use automated gate with bar code readers with no staff to assist. Many people with home printed and mobile boarding passes were confused with no help at all. Staff at the restaurant landside near b24 gate didn't speak English. Toilets near gates packed with people and not very clean.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: C Volz
content: I will gladly pay a good deal more for an airline ticket if I can avoid this airport. Endless queues rude customer service and very confusing signage. Both my husband and I speak German and this did not help. There are decent places for food in the main area but once we got to our international gate all that was available was a wurst wagon that charged 5 euros for one sausage. We all got herded into a closed offgate area for a couple of hours that had one toilet for everyone on the plane. Never again if I can at all help it!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: N Miller
content: My latest visit was a little disappointing - some of the elevators were not working and no staff available to assist the passengers waiting signage was not clear. I was travelling in Business Class and therefore able to use the Lufthansa Business Class lounge once I finally got near the gate for my intra-European intra-Schengen flight. The Business Class area was spacious but again the food and drink were average and there was not much to read. I was surprised airport authorities didn't handle the issue of passenger traffic control better as I'm sure they knew the elevators weren't working.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: K Chua
content: A group of 6 for a vacation in the Far East. On our return transit flight to Frankfurt we were informed before boarding at Shanghai that the weather in Frankfurt was bad and the flight was delayed 2 hrs. As the plane approached Frankfurt the flight was re-routed to Nünberg due to bad weather. The plane finally returned to Frankfurt airport 3 hrs later. At 22.30 to our disappointment there were only 2 custom gates open for approx 1000 passengers. I was disappointed because Frankfurt should know this and make the necessary precautions to accommodate such a big surge of incoming passengers. After customs check our airline ground staff informed us they had re-booked our ticket on a Lufthansa flight to Zurich. They encouraged us to do a re-checking at Terminal One to catch the first flight to Zurich at 06.10 hr next morning. We followed the instructions and queued up at Terminal 1 check-in to obtain a new ticket. There were again long queues. We were advised us to be at the ticket counter 2 hrs before departure - another disappointment. The next morning there was no one at the counter until 06.30 hr. Only one counter was open after 06.45 hr 3 new counters were opened and the queue was getting very long. When we arrived at Zurich airport 3 bags did not arrive. I do not need to explain much about our dissatisfaction with Frankfurt airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Chattopadhya
content: The security personnel are extremely rude and highly disrespectful. I was flying from USA to India in June. Due to the time difference in USA time it was past midnight I was sleepy and forgot to take few items out of my pocket. The officer ridiculed me by saying loudly 'Is this the first time you are flying go back to scanner'. I was co- operating and took all my items out and scanned them through. Then the officer harassed me by scanning me thoroughly and getting me off balance. In the name of security they are abusing passengers. Airport is old and confusing easy to get lost long lines mis-managed. Nobody seems to know anything.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Muenzel
content: Connected in Frankfurt today and once again the airport showed it's ugly side. Having been in a holding pattern we arrived 15 mins late. As seems usual there were no gates so we had to wait for a bus which added about 15 mins to the delay. Upon arrival the promised displays which were to tell us our connecting gate were nowhere to be found. Airport personnel were unfriendly and obviously overburdened trying to handle the many people demanding to know where to go. All I got was a general direction 'go the left'. I followed that for a few minutes and found someone else to ask and was given a gate number which at least was in the general vicinity. Finally I found a display monitor which showed the correct gate which was 10 gates away. My recommendation is to avoid this airport if you need to make a connection.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Lutz
content: We returned last week from Australia to Germany and I realized once again how awful Frankfurt airport truly is. A confusing dingy rabbit warren with impossibly long walks no clear signs. We always feel confused when we are there and we have flown in an out of Frankfurt a lot. And it seems to be getting worse.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: R Fife
content: Recently travelled from Oregon and connected here which was a disaster we were directed out of the secure area re-processed and required to walk nearly a mile back to the same area we disembarked but one level down. Toilets are tiny and dirty with lines 6-10 people long to get in. Security staff are at a level 2-3 times worse than in the USA which is bad. Flying in on Lufthansa and out on the same carrier did not help. I would suggest 1.5 hrs is not enough for making a connection here.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: J Coya
content: I flew Lufthansa BOS-FRA-BOM return. It was not a good experience at all. Staff are extremely rude and not helpful. The internet access computers were not working and the prices everywhere expensive.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Thomas Hoeh
content: Check-in at terminal 1B for flight to Sweden. Surprisingly friendly staff at security check and very short wait for week-day morning. Sufficient seating at gate good selection and price in airside shops. Unfortunately no airbridge for boarding LH flight. Coming back bus service to terminal again but quick baggage delivery.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Susan Tooke
content: We flew Condor Air to Frankfurt. We got in late and had to find our way with no offered help to Lufthansa Airlines Service which was a great distance from our arrival gate. When we asked for directions from security a vague 'follow the signs' was the only offer. By the time we got to the service area our options were limited to a flight 3 hours from our original connecting flight to Paris. Lack of signage discourteous security and absolute ignorance by the airport personnel made us determined to never ever fly into Frankfurt again. We also had to exit and re- enter security.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Brett
content: I am an avid Star Alliance Gold traveller and Frankfurt is the main hub for Europe. I recently flew from Istanbul- Frankfurt -Newark. I had 1.5 hrs connection thinking it was suitable enough. My plane at Istanbul was delayed an hour due to air traffic in Frankfurt. Once I arrived at FRA the jetway was not in use so we were bused over to terminal 1B. Once I got there the walk was 1/2 mile and took a train to 1A (US flights) and then a security screening. At the security there was not even a Business Class/Star Gold line which I though was unacceptable. Luckily my flight to Newark was delayed an hour or else I definitely would of missed it. Terminal 1A has to be the ugliest part of Frankfurt Airport because there are very few shops and it is worn. The Tower Lounge is pretty nice but would expect it to be nicer for a 4 Star airport. No matter what anyone tells you you need at least 2 hrs if you are connecting from a European flight to an Overseas flight.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Colin Lusty
content: I recently travelled from Seoul to Oporto which involved a 5 hour transit time. Signage is confusing staff are rude and not at all helpful. Returning to Seoul this time from Milan it didn't get any better luckily once again I had a long time in transit. The only positive feature of this airport are the Senator lounges.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Y Botteron
content: Very unfriendly and stern security control personnel. They tend to bark orders instead of welcoming people with a good morning. Not to speak about the patting down of the passengers done in front of everybody.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Frank Bauer
content: Frankfurt Airport is by far the worst airport that I know. The airport has the advantage for travellers to/from Germany that it is directly and conveniently connected to a train station serving the ICE highspeed trains. However that is the only positive thing that I can think of. As many others have noted transits from the Schengen to non-Schengen-area are extremely difficult and if you don't have a lot of time they become reminiscent of an olympic decathlon. You have to run down extremely long hallways while trying to look out for the few small signs that might indicate where you have to go. Then you have to carry your stuff two floors downstairs (only to go two floors upstairs again in the next terminal). Of course there is an elevator but if you are in a rush then you don't want to wait for it. The gates are often overcrowded and there are very few places where one can sit. And one can not point out often enough how rude the staff is. As a German I can only say how ashamed I am at how rude many Germans are when they are placed in a customer-contact situation. It is both the reason why I avoid Lufthansa and why I avoid Frankfurt Airport.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: M Preston
content: I stopped travelling via FRA about 3 years ago after several unpleasant for all the reasons mentioned by others transits in a short space of time. Last week I had no choice but to use this airport and was expecting it to be bad. It was worse than I had imagined with impossibly long queues for check-in and passport control between non-Schengen to Schengen long walks poor signposting everything that others have stated. It's a pity and for this reason I will avoid flying LH in future unless I can hub through MUC. I know LH don't own the airport but they are the biggest operator and ought to be able to influence better service delivery.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Yevheniy Kahanovych
content: After reading horror stories about transit at Frankfurt I booked a ticket with 6 hour layover - how smart decision was it! Not just because Lufthansa delayed my inbound flight by 2 hours but even then having 4 hours to spend on transit I just made my connecting flight. I was connecting from non-shengen to shengen area of the airport. Immigration was open in the following proportion: 6 desks for eu passports (fairly empty) and 4 desks for the rest of the world. No line management no idea of what waiting time is and around 300+ pax from ex-China flights arrived at the same time. After 20 minutes of looking for someone who should expedite us to the right line I've just came to the eu desk (I'm not eu citizen) and went through it however need to say that the officer was quite rude asked me for "invitation" despite the valid visa been in passport so it took twice the time it needed. Then another escalator flight down and quite long line for security where all duty free alcohol is confiscated even if sealed and cleared for being taken aboard. Then 20 minutes of trying to get to the right lift going to Schengen A gates. There you're locked into a long wing of the terminal with couple eateries and nothing to do even for a short stop. Toilets smelly and not properly cleaned. In no way this airport is 4 star facility. And never again will I use it for transit.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: George Attwood
content: After a very long flight from New Zealand via Thailand I arrived at Frankfurt airport and can honestly say that I have never met such rude and crass staff in 20 years of international travel. Transit from one terminal to another was fine with a shuttle train but the security queues were chaotic and managed in a very rude manner. I noted that few of the staff were actually proper Germans. The spectre of staff shouting at each other at 530am was not civilized. The Lufthansa ground staff are shockingly rude and I will not use Frankfurt airport again. There are more civilized alternatives!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Peter Rejchrt
content: Travelled through here en route from LHR to JNB and from CPT to LHR - Frankfurt is now close to being the worst in Europe. A once great airport for connections has been transformed into hell. Long walks along dingy dimly lit corridors many without travelators. Security checkpoints are a disgrace with mostly rude staff EUR1 charges for additional LAGs clear plastic bags and horrendous queues. The separate queues for premium passengers were closed on both legs of transiting this airport. After the landing we were met with closed doors something in which LHR used to specialise. Even with First Class tickets on the return leg everyone must go through the same security checkpoints again with no premium lanes and long queues already at 5.30am.It is a shame MUC does not have the number of connections as FRA as this is a much more civilised airport. FRA as a connecting point should be avoided unless desperate. Also the provision of internet connection facilities lags behind anywhere else in the world - not sure if this is an airport or airline user issue.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: K Chen
content: We flew out of this airport two weeks ago. It was the most frustrating airport experience that we've ever had. They have the doors leading to the check-in area blocked so it created a huge bottle neck of people trying to get to the check-in and baggage drop off areas in Terminal 1. There was a nice gentlemen who looked to be a manger. He stepped in and helkped us and even let us skip in the first class line. If it weren't for him we would have missed our flight. We got there 3 hours early and got through security and to our gate right as our flight was boarding. Security was ok but once we passed there was a second security set up for Lufthansa which took a long time to get through and we were number 4 in the line. Once we got on the plane we had to de-board because security had somehow messed up. So we spent another hour or so driving in circles on a bus around the airport before being taken back to the airport and had to go back through security. They were nice and let us through early since we had two small kids. Then we had to go back to the bus and wait for everyone to show up. Then we were taken back to the plane. After waiting to have the plane de-iced we finally departed. We arrived at our destination 5 hours later than what the itinerary was set for. We got there just in time to secure our rental and call the hotel before our reservation had been cancelled. I love Germany but I hope to never fly from this airport again!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Mathias Binder
content: I arrived from the US with one hour delay. I still had more than 2 hours for my connecting flight. Unfortunately the gate was not available so we got apron parking. The buses waited until the very last person left the plane. it took me 110 minutes to get trough the security. Like many people around me I watched boarding and flight times come and go as they waited. But nobody cared about that. They had only 3 lanes open for all departures from A Gates. The staff were unhelpful. They urgently needed to open more lanes and wouldn't do so. A Supervisor explained that the staff was having lunch. But after 90 minutes still only 3 lanes were open. They were also incredibly slow. May be they were on go-slow but it has never taken me so long to get myself and my bag through. Almost everybody set the scanner off and was searched completely unnecessarily. Almost every bag was searched after X-ray completely unnecessarily. A very very poor customer experience. It will make me think twice about flying Lufthansa again so that I don't have to use that terminal.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Tyler
content: Frankfurt Airport Terminal 1B is obviously not properly set up for international departures. If took me 90 mins to clear security. Fortunately I had allowed plenty of time and just made my flight. Many people around me watched their boarding and flight times come and go as they waited. They had only 2 lanes open for all departures from B Gates. The staff were unhelpful. They urgently needed to open more lanes and wouldn't do so. They were also incredibly slow. May be they were on go-slow but it has never taken me so long to get myself and my bag through. Almost everybody set the scanner off and was searched completely unnecessarily. Almost every bag was searched after X-ray completely unnecessarily. A very very poor customer experience. It will make me think twice about flying Lufthansa again so that I don't have to use that terminal.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Kurt Mueller
content: Whilst the German populace at large had been made aware of impending cold weather and snowfall for the preceding five days the operators of Frankfurt Airport were clearly caught with their pants down on 27th November. Our EK flight scheduled for 1425 departure was finally serviced by the de-icing vehicles at the gate at 1505. Then the aircraft was not pushed back until 1600. Why is such an antiquated de-icing process used in the first place? Much easier and more efficient to de-ice aircraft at the end of the taxiway immediately prior to take-off. As a result of Fraport's wonderful incapability our flight was also put in a 30-minute holding pattern overhead DXB. I am puzzled to see that Fraport advertise their "expertise" for sale to other airport operators.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Dave Stanley
content: There are substantial and ongoing improvements to Freetown Airport. They have been rebuilding the terminal building around the old structure for the last few months. Departure and arrival procedures are now quite painless compared with the hot and basic conditions before. The check in area is large and clean and I did not have to queue for long. They could still do with increasing the air conditioning in that area though. Security is good and immigration is using new computers and biometric systems. The departure lounge is now quite big and comfortable. There are a few well stocked duty free shops. The original restaurant is still available as well as a new one upstairs. The new one is not well signposted. Overall a big improvement. FNA now compares favourably with other airports in Africa.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Dave Stanley
content: Few improvements to report. Check-in is still slow and chaotic. There are a few more air- conditioners inside so it is not quite so hot. There have been recent problems with theft from checked luggage. Some reports even suggest that bags had been cut open. Definitely do not leave money or valuables in luggage. And do not let airport staff see if there is anything valuable in there. Business class passengers have a better experience because the initial queuing is reduced and the lounge provided some good food.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Dave Stanley
content: I have been using the airport almost every month during the last year. Some improvement in arrival procedures has been made. There are not usually long queues at immigration and baggage arrives quite quickly. For departures the entrance hall is still busy and too hot but if you take a fan and pay a porter you can survive. A couple of positives the duty free shop remains good and cheap and the food in the upstairs bar/restaurant is good. The check in area has been improved with modern counters. Hopefully this will reduce the queuing time in the entrance hall once it is fully up and running.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Peter Goldsbury
content: Other reviews have emphasized just how awful changing flights is here and my experience was no exception though my return flight from Geneva to Osaka was an exception. And my experience has been confined to Terminal 1. On a recent trip it took two hours to go from Gate C13 to Gate A40. There was just one official checking passports at the immigration gate for entering the Schengen zone so loads of passengers were pushing in with varying degrees of politeness because of their earlier flights. On the other hand transferring from Gate A34 to B23 was very smooth with the moving walkway in the connecting tunnel being fully functional and hardly anyone at the passport control. However after passing through passport control so quickly I had to waste time checking the departure gate for my flight. The departure gate for my flight to Osaka was posted on the monitors at Gate A34 but not on the monitors just outside the passport control. So I was wondering if there had been a gate change. Finally boarding the flight by row numbers proved chaotic though this might have been due to Lufthansa. Transferring via Frankfurt is like being an out-patient in a very poor ill- equipped hospital. This is because the publicity suggests that it is a wholly therapeutic experience.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Silverstone
content: While brusque or unpleasant security and border checks are hardly unique to FRA I've never encountered shop staff so unpleasant as in a recent trip connecting through the US flights area. At one coffee shop they even began mocking a customer (in German of course) who had the nerve to request a bag to carry a muffin with her to the plane (and what kind of airport coffee shop doesn't have containers to let you carry stuff aboard with you?)! Beyond the obvious personnel problems FRA is cursed with a horrible design that goes to extreme lengths to sort passengers into areas based on their destinations - and clearly wasn't originally designed to do so. Signage is atrocious - one sign actually had marker scrawled on it by staff to clarify just which gates were in which direction. A horror to navigate made worse by the constant fear that turning the next corner will accidentally take you outside of one border/security area and require you to pass through that whole process over again. All this makes for a horrible journey point and I haven't even got to the interminable busses between plane stands and the terminals.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: D Wilson
content: Arrived FRA by RailAir from Stuttgart with 3.5 hours before onward flight to Manchester. Took 2 hours from leaving the train to getting thru security and passport control and sitting down for a cup of coffee. Just read previous posts. Massive lines at bag-drop/check-in desks in the main hall (so we went back to the bag-drop close to the station) 15 minute line at security gates and only 4 out of 12 staffed 20 minutes wait at passport control during which time one officer disappeared for 5 minutes and another disappeared completely never to be seen again so suddenly my line was effectively twice as long. Very poor signage compensated however by very helpful and numerous ground staff.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: L Davis
content: Looks like my experience was not uncommon. Confusing signage and building design but its the security that's the most confronting. They are rudest and most aggressive I have experienced - not just to passengers but to their own colleagues as well. The full body frisking was done in a very aggressive manner - I don't know what they expect to get from Xraying my passport and boarding pass. I passed through Tokyo transit security and the end of the flight wearing the same clothes and with the same luggage without any incident and all with a pleasant smile from security.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Peter Bedson
content: Much better than it used to be - they seem to have clamped down on the baggage handlers and general hangers on trying to extract dollars from you on the way in. On the way out no real problems aside from a few panhandllers trying to take a last opportunity to rip you off. Don't miss the duty free shop - it looks awful from the outside but is really well stocked and cheap.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Dave Stanley
content: Back again at the end of March. This time not such a good experience. On the way in baggage was late because the handlers could not be bothered to do their job. On the return we suffered a very long wait in the extremely hot entrance hall. This is caused by the very slow and beauracratic check in procedures. The air conditioning in the main part of the airport is proving totally inadequate and many units do not work. Some of the staff are quite unhelpful. Sierra Leone needs tourism but no respectable tour company would let their customers suffer this.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Dave Stanley
content: This airport has improved significantly over the last 5 years. It was badly damaged during the troubles. The only facilities were a partly destroyed hanger. Now the main terminal has been refurbished it is quite respectable. Arrival is easy enough. You will need to be firm with the baggage handlers. They have been clamped down on recently but they will still try there best to relieve you of a few $. If you let them one will carry your bags to the door another for a few more feet etc. Just say no and try not to look as if it is your first visit. Once you have got your bags you have to visit the customs bench. You will now need transport to Freetown which is the other side of a large estuary. There are helicopters a ferry and a hovercraft. Take the Paramount helicopter the other two take too long and are unreliable. It is cheap $37 on my recent visit. You may have to change this into the local Leones before buying the ticket. There is an exchange office which gives respectable rates. The helicopter departure area is the old hanger that used to be the main terminal. It is dirty and hot so try to get the first helicopter. These are old but reliable Russian MI-8's. You will arrive at the Mammy Yoko heliport. Here you will most likely be met by your local agency or whoever you are visiting. If not local taxis are available. A trip to most parts of Freetown should cost no more than Le10-20000. If you do not have accommodation booked go to the Cape Sierra Hotel or Bintumani Hotel which are very close. On the way back the helicopters leave about 6 hours before the time of departure. You then wait outside the Lungi terminal for an hour or more before suffering the long and bureaucratic check in procedure. This is typically African and can take an hour+. The main lounge is air conditioned. There is also a very good duty free shop and a reasonable restaurant upstairs. You will probably not be hassled by airport officials for bribes unlike other countries in the region.

title: Freetown Airport customer review
author: Francis Ellis
content: Freetown Lungi International Airport is a small airport terminal building. It recieves very few flights the majority being international. It has so positive attributes like no congestion speedy check in and checkout. A hotel is conveniently located near it. There is a duty free shop and restaurant. There is also a VIP Lounge for the elite and other first class passengers. Beware that the airport is very small. It needs renovations and a series of expansions effort due to its small size. The government is in the works of expanding it to accomodate the international passengers.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: R Persson
content: Signs are many and very confusing. Granted everything is there as far shopping and conveniences of all sorts are concerned - but to find them and to find your flight elsewhere is a problem. I think that the architecture and structure of the airport is flawed. It has grown too fast and changed so many times to accommodate new legislation and growing number of passengers that travellers do not manage to get a feeling of direction anymore.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: E Pope
content: I travel to Frankfurt every year on vacation usually May-Sep. I am a German-American and speak fluent German and English but I always have to ask several times at this airport. I know how to follow signs but here they often lead to nothing; the signage has to be upgraded. The personnel I have asked have been supportive but not always clear. I have had layovers at many airports internationally but Frankfurt has been the worst. This is coming from a German who loves her country!

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Kurt Mueller
content: I was just reminded why so many previous contributors have awarded this airport low ratings particularly for surly and rude staff. Arriving from Dubai the other day I lined up at one of the immigration counters marked "EU EWR CH". Just when it was my turn a woman in a fluorescent jacket moved in from left field. Feeling my physical resistance she then muttered "Excuse me we have priority". She had two passengers in tow without EU passports. I suggested she might make her own job easier if she asked people prior to trying to push them aside upon which she replied (with a straight face) "I just did ask you". As a native German speaker I can safely say that there was neither the intonation of a question or a please (usually associated with asking) involved. I usually avoid Frankfurt but was forced to use it due to my original itinerary having been disturbed by the volcanic ash saga.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Paul Van Alsten
content: Departed from Terminal 2. It is quite time-consuming from the long-distance train platforms to Terminal 2 building - long walks to reach the shuttle stop followed by a 10 mins bus drive. The terminal itself is modern and clean. Check-in and security screening hassle-free. Staff polite though not overly friendly. Airside there is not much to do in the Schengen area - a duty-free shop a small kiosk and an overpriced cafe. Toilet facilities are clean but hard to find.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Reiziger
content: We arrived at terminal 1 and went to the passport control where it was confusing and crowded with passengers just arrived and did not know which lines they supposed to follow to get their passport checked. The signs were all in German! Inside the terminal though the signs have English subtitles which make it easier to find the train station. Departure gates were also confusing and very far apart with no place in between to buy refreshment.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: S Sayers
content: Flying from Copenhagen to Asia. Signs not clear. Difficult to find the transit check-in counter. Bad planing of traffic flows. It can take more than an hour to pass the security and constantly people arriving from the other gates can cut the lines. or you think you're close to the security but the lines are merging constantly. Baby changing table only in the ladies restroom.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: John Bachinski
content: Warning about taking a taxi from the Frankfurt Airport. We decided to take a taxi instead of the hotel shuttle as we were tired and did not know how long until the next hotel shuttle. Also the phone service at the arrival level to the hotels did not seem to work. The taxi driver went insane when he found out we were going only a short distance fare. He was very vocal and aggressive and then started to drive wildly with speeds in excess on 170 KM/hour. We noticed that he was had no intention to take us to out hotel but then accused us of giving him the wrong hotel name. He wanted to take us downtown. I demanded the driver call his supervisor who I advised that we were not going to pay this driver for the driver's error. The hotel staff advised us that the normal fare was 12-14 Euros and he wanted 30 over Euros.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: Michael Allan
content: The buses? The security? The service? We flew in from Venice to Frankfurt connecting back to the US (Philadelphia). Our flight from Venice (Lufthansa) was delayed by a mere 20 minutes due to snow in Frankfurt which wasn't a problem I could have spent the day in the Venice airport. Arriving in snowy Frankfurt we taxied out way out somewhere near the border with Belgium near as I could tell and waited for the guys to get out of the truck and move the stairs so we could get out of the plane. Took about 20 minutes for everyone to decide it was time for us to deplane not sure what the high-sign was must be a secret. They didn't make much of an effort to clear off or dry the stairs (can't imagine how scary it must have been for people with larger pieces of luggage or carrying children) and we got on the bus for the "terminal". After a leisurely drive we got to a "gate" which was some stairs escalator and an elevator. Then the rush through the rat's maze to make our connecting flight began. Which entailed up escalators down some stairs moving sidewalks signage covered with colored tape (presumably as a result of new security procedures) back to a long line leading up to another security screening (we'd already had a full screening before departing Venice). Security consisted of a line leading to an escalator (there were approximately 75 to 80+ people in line) where the attendant would allow 4 to 5 people up at a time to be screened. This would have been reasonable had there been more than one metal detector. When we were finally allowed up about 1 in 10 people made it through without requiring additional wanding or patting down meaning things didn't go very fast. The staff was also pretty abusive calling people "stupid" (in English why insult someone in German if they may not understand it) and having a general disdain for the entire process not to mention ongoing conversations with one another not having anything do with the screening process (I would have understood if they'd insulted me in German). Then more dashing off to the "gate" - okay it's not a "gate" it's a "bus stop" stop calling it something it's not. We got on the last bus for the plane which meant we had to sit in the tunnel waiting for the last of the poor suckers still in the security line to make it through. Which meant that we were sitting in the tunnel inhaling exhaust fumes for about half an hour. They didn't bother to close the doors to the bus. I will plan any future trips avoiding both Lufthansa and Frankfurt airport. I will also recommend to anyone that asks to avoid any connections through Frankfurt and Lufthansa they just didn't seem to care. Advice for fellow travelers if you are coming from the US I'd make any connections there in order to get a direct flight to your location. We'd have probably been better off flying into either JFK or even backtracking to O'Hare then flying direct.

title: Frankfurt Main Airport customer review
author: G Thomassin
content: Transit between LH flights (from BKK then to GVA) at terminal 1.
