There are two ATMS around the corner, neither of which worked and no place to exchange money until you have passed through passport control - for which you need a visa. Insane. I had to give the woman behind the counter my lira; she then had to go and change it for me and then I could pay for the visa. The stupidest arrangement I could imagine. This is I think, a scam to collect on the difference of the exchange rates.  No free airport wifi - not even the poorest kind that will boot you every five minutes. You have to pay for WiFi. The departures sign had plenty of delays of over 30 minutes posted and the PA was extremely active with gate changes. This was a light night, past peak hours and on a crystal clear day. No reason for the delays other than disorganization. You probably already knew this but Sabiha is on the Asian side out near the shipyards. There is nothing here, so unless you're transiting as I was, you will be sorely disappointed with your 2 hour trip into Istanbul across the straits just to get into town. My flight ended up being delayed 40 minutes officially, but in reality, because we sat on the runway for twenty minutes after boarding so, an hour - no reason given in any language.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Martin Mrvik
content: This is the worst airport if you need to change flights in Istanbul. After arrival you follow the transit signs only to find a fully functional and running escalator back to the transfer lounge guarded by 2 officials sending everybody back to arrivals. Even if you have only a short time you have to exit through the customs avoid all the people waiting in arrival lounge make your way to the departure security again and find your gate.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: D Leston
content: Transited via SAW on my way to and from TLV 3 hrs and 1 hr transit times respectively. Both connections were easy and the terminal is really impressive. Plenty of facilities and pretty friendly staff. A nice surprise as I had low expectations.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: B Barrett
content: Arrived from the UK 14/03/2014 for a connecting flight to Gazipasa Alanya. I had 65 minutes. There were huge queues for passport control and no system for filtering persons connecting with internal flights from all the other arriving passengers. In a word it was chaotic and very stressful. I did make my connection but only by asking fellow passengers if I could go before them and luckily the flight was 20 minutes late departing. Why oh why can't they have dedicated passport booths for passengers connecting with internal flights. It doesn't take that much imagination. International transfers were catered for.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Mary Ayhan
content: My advise is to avoid this airport at all costs. My daughter and I were travelling to Barcelona this was to be our second flight of the morning. We landed on time (from first flight) had 1 hr 10 minutes to make the second flight. The gate for international transit passengers to proceed from domestic flights to the international terminal was locked. Told to go through the baggage control area exit into the arrivals hall then make our way to the international terminal! When we got to the departure gate area of the international terminal we were greeted with the most chaotic sight I have witnessed in an airport. There were 400 people queuing (if you could call it that). 4 passport control desks were operational. After 40 minutes in the queue I knew we would miss our flight! When our flight was called for final boarding I started to move forward asking people in front of us for permission to pass. I became very irate as my flight had been announced 'ready for departure' but still no call for us by name to come forward for boarding. We eventually cleared passport control where a very rude/ignorant official stamped our passports. We were running to the gate when an airport official asked us if we were on the Barcelona flight? He got on his walkie talkie and said 'don't take the bags off I have the passengers with me' then reopened the departure gate to let us through. We got on the flight. I will never travel through this airport again.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Michael Davies
content: Nice clean and modern airport. But it is miles form Istanbul and transport options are not great. Very high prices for food and drink. Higher than any airport I have been to. This is counter productive as I didn't spend anything! £8 for a beer. The same applies to Ataturk as well. Advise to airport Managers - lower the prices and earn more revenue!

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: A Milossavlyevich
content: SAW-ASR. In physical terms the airport has a nice wooden interior full of natural light yet in the terms of staff and organization it is a nightmare. Almost nobody speaks English excessive and rude security controls. Wi-Fi is available only through an authorization system available exclusively for people with Turkish sim- cards. Disappointing and infuriating. An international airport managed in a mindset of a local bus station. If the fares were right I would always fly to/from Ataturk instead.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Ahmed Jaber
content: Improved from five years ago in that public transport does reach airport. 80 mins from Taksim for 12 Lira. The airport is spacious and modern. Security were unfriendly and borderline rude. The business class lounge is very basic with only cold food and no wireless internet.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Marc Pauquet
content: SAW-KYA. Ground staff have little English langauge skills. TK employees at TK counter. Same for security staff very impolite and rude no English knowledge in an international airport.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Chris Matthews
content: Flying Easyjet to LGW. A pleasant enough airport no long lines but not much choice of food before or after passport control and very expensive. Duty free shop had a good choice and was reasonably priced. The down side was a totally disorganised gate check just before boarding; we were allowed to walk through with a water bottle we bought into the airport with us but other passengers had bottles taken off them they had purchased at the shop next door to the gate. people seemed to be wandering in and out of the gate area without any checks at all. A sign at the entry to the departures informs people that this is the worlds best airport!

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: M Dil
content: I regularly fly through SAW airport for domestic flights especially to Izmir. The airport has a car parking sufficient enough to capacity however the desk for payment is with one clerk in an unfriendly and rude manner. After having a 1 hour flight you might face with long lines before the payment desk if you have the chance for on-line check-in remember to check-in to the front seats so that you will be able to get on the bus and pick-up an easy location to reach the airport first and if lucky enough you will have a front place in the payment line.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Lorna Watson
content: Probably the worst airport experience I've ever had on departure. Ridiculously overpriced cafe (the airside section of which is upstairs no escalator or lift) duty free shop was closed. We were almost forcibly frogmarched into very narrow crowded boarding queues for our Easyjet departure over 1/2 hour before the incoming flight had even landed. Eventually we were loaded onto a crowded bus which pulled out onto the tarmac then the driver got out switched off the engine and left us sweltering (it was a very hot day) for 5 or 10 minutes - only when a riot almost ensued did he get back in the bus and switch on the air conditioning. Our arrival and immigration however was very smooth with good transport connections. The E10 bus from the airport to Kadikoy ferryport then ferry to Eminonou is a very cheap and pleasant way to transfer if you are heading for the Sultanahmet area.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: David Bole
content: A bad experience with this new and quite small airport. On arrival we had to wait at immigration control and after a long wait it turned out that we were sold the wrong tourist visas. The counter for visas was already closed when immigration officers noticed wrong visas so we had to wait for the counter to open again. Oon the positive side - bus connections to Istanbul are cheap and very efficient. On departure: only a small part of departure lounge was open and about 300 hundred people had to wait in a small hall with about 50 seats!! People were lying and sitting on the floor and it was not very pleasant. The duty free shop is a comedy (expensive and virtually empty) and the only bar is overpriced.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Ahmed Al-zuhairi
content: This is the airport used by Easyjet. Altogether there are about 10 flights a day. The airport is 1 hour by car from Istanbul city centre and will cost you about £30 by taxi. The airport terminal itself is very small. There is only 1 duty free shop and the prices are ridiculously high. The drinks as previous people mentioned are ridiculously high. Very basic airport and struggled to spend 1 hour waiting for boarding.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Firat Sevil
content: This is a new modern but a small airport. Passenger amenities could be improved. I suggest you take your own drink with you - a can of Pepsi costs 20 Turkish Lira which is around GBP9-00.

title: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport customer review
author: Hakan Ersoy
content: Turkish Airlines fly some domestic destinations from this place. Germanwings and Corendon Airlines fly international. Check in etc are fast but the domestic terminal could get crowded sometimes due to its small size. The airport has a good future and will be most likely low cost paradise for Istanbul people and tourists. But they need to expand the domestic terminal before it gets very crowded.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Ahmet Altiner
content: The new domestic terminal is fantastic. Clean spacious and I am told the largest domestic terminal in TR (certainly much larger than IST domestic terminal). The Turkish Airlines business lounge is beautiful and they drive you to the plane right before take off so you do not need to go back to the gate.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: D Cahalane
content: Having experienced this airport's money grabbing extortionate prices first hand I would seriously consider ever visiting Turkey again. I have just returned from a wonderful two week holiday in Kusidasi but the fact that I had to endure this airport in order to get in and out would definitely discourage me from ever again going there. They undid all the positive experiences of the country. A can of Diet Coke was 3.46. The facilities were OK but the prices were a complete rip off. They had posters up promoting Izmir as a candidate city for World Expo 2020. If you have the misfortune to travel through this place bring your own food.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: S Srinivasan
content: Small but efficient domestic airport. Large taxi stands are available in front of both exit doors and it's also easy to find the "Havas" shuttle bus or walk to the train station. Upon arrival security is quick and efficient and I got from the check-in kiosk to the gate in less than 10 minutes. The main downside to this airport is the lack of sitting space at the gates; there simply isn't enough to hold a plane full of people. Since security for each 3-4 gates is segregated it's not possible to walk down to another set to find a seat either. The bar/restaurant also looked overpriced.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Nick Paul
content: Late night arrival from IST. Quick bag claim. Arrival hall clean and well signed. Duty free shop available in bag claim if items needed. Collected hire car from in front of terminal - though if required undercover area in front of arrival hall has plenty of taxis waiting if not pre-booked or using a hire car. On return through security to access departure hall for domestic flight. Few shops to choose from but note refreshments at cafes are expensive. Prompt service from helpful staff at THY check-in desk. Further security check to access departure gate. No delays and a good facility happy to recommend ADB airport.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: G Misioch
content: The airport is clean. Staff at information desk speak only very limited English. Facilities are quite limited there is no left-luggage and other amenities such as restaurants close down if there are no current flights which makes this airport not such a good choice for transit passengers.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Nick Paul
content: First departure of the day out of ADB so arrived at 0345. Easy directions around the airport if you are driving in - very clear to follow which route. Dropped off hire car at the entrance (same location for collecting taxis). NB: if returning a hire car and fuel is needed at this stage the first petrol station you come to off the O31 access road to the airport is open 24 hrs and is the best one to use for filling the car. Straight through first security to dept hall. No queues in the airport of course at that time at any point other than couple of mins. waiting at check in for flight itself. Airport very clean nice and bright facility. Ample signage for directions around airport. Cafe next to check in desks if wanted. Passport control prompt. Through to gate - further small cafe for hot drink / snack. Duty free open - good prices on most items. Further security check at gate plenty of seats for waiting. Free papers if required- German/US/UK titles (for Lufthansa flight). I must praise the check in staff who had a really nice approach to pax at that time of day and were friendly efficient and a pleasure to meet. Passed through ADB at different times of the day now and an excellent facility and happy to recommend.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Tom Maule
content: The new international terminal at Izmir opened in September 2006. Arrivals apart from a small delay in getting the jetway lined up was smooth and efficient. The area prior to visa payment and passport control is large and airy. Formalities took minutes. The baggage hall is also spacious with an adequate duty free on arrival shop. Being the only flight in or due in baggage delivery was very quick - althouth the angled conveyors do move a bit too quickly for some and I saw several people chasing high speed bags round the carousel! Through passport control there is a bit meet and greet area leading to a pick up and set down area with car parks opposite. Everything was pretty much a straight line from plane to kerbside. Departures is equally impressive. The check in area seemed to have about 50 desks although quiet at 7pm on a Friday night with only two or three flights checking in. Only British Airways has a single line check in system and I can see it getting a bit chaotic for other airlines if things get busy. Again very quick through passport control into a very spacious departures area. being a new terminal facilities were limited to a huge duty free shop (cheap) an 'english style' pub that is fairly expensive at 20YTL (£7.70) for a sandwich and coke a Burger King on the mezzanine level (again expensive) and a small coffee area next to the BA Gate (you guess £2.50 for a small coffee). All gates have separate lounges entered after another security check - comfortable and adequate for B737/A320 size aircraft. All very modern clean and efficient - a pleasure to fly through

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Todd Muhleman
content: Not much of an airport no jetways just stairs and buses. The upside of using it as an arrival point instead of Istanbul is that it is very easy to go through customs / security. I've never had much of a wait. The only direct service though is to/from Munich on Lufthansa which makes connecting on the way back to the states a impossible without an overnight in Europe.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Nicola Akgun
content: My husband is from Izmir so we use this airport on a regular basis to visit family and friends. We have noticed the change in price over the last couple of years - prices for a burger king meal are ridiculous - 18YTL for 1 meal. We bought 4 coffees in the airport cafe which came to nearly 15 pounds. Anybody travelling through this airport should be advised to eat before they get there or take some snacks.

title: Izmir Airport customer review
author: Chris Pike
content: Take your own food and drink. This is one of the most expensive airports I have ever been in. A glass of Coke was 8.10TL (over 5 Euros). Very poor facilities

title: Jackson Hole Airport customer review
author: W Burke
content: This is a small airport. Check in and security are painless. Airside there are now 8 gates. There is floor to ceiling glass affording nice views of the Tetons. There is plenty of comfortable seating in the gate area that would get high marks from the people at "Sleeping In Airports". You still have to walk on the tarmac to board your plane. Sadly the food choices are unchanged from my last trip through. That is my only complaint. Still this is a very nice tertiary level airport. As always be sure to book an F side window seat for your daytime flight in.

title: Jackson Hole Airport customer review
author: W Burke
content: This is a small airport to say the least. It only has 4 gates and this is after it is being modernized and expanded. Construction is still going on so it can be a bit noisy. Security is fairly painless. There is only one restaurant/lounge airside or curbside. Hopefully this will change when construction is complete. Airside has floor to ceiling windows affording views of the spectacular Tetons. Almost as impressive is the array of private jets lined up toward the south end of the airport. If you fly here be sure to take a daytime flight in and book an F side window seat for a jaw-dropping view of the Tetons on approach.

title: Jacksonville Airport customer review
author: C Miro
content: Arrived on Southwest yesterday from Fort Lauderdale. JAX is modern. All public areas and bathrooms are clean and people are happy to provide assistance. There is plenty of good well-priced dining options. What a pleasure it is to use this facility!

title: Jacksonville Airport customer review
author: Mark Robinson
content: It is clean staff are friendly and TSA is a breeze. Plenty of food and drink options. It is a smaller airport and is very well laid out. I usually fly one of the larger airlines and connect to its hub. The fares for doing this are usually much cheaper with JAX.

title: Jacksonville Airport customer review
author: R O'Connor
content: Airport is Great. Security is very fast and I love the decor. The bathrooms were really clean. I also loved how you didn't have to pay for wi-fi and there are plenty of plugs to plug your electronics into.

title: Jacksonville Airport customer review
author: Steve Koenig
content: Have only arrived here since we departed from another area airport (Orlando). Wish we had also departed from Jacksonville since it is so much smaller and quieter than Orlando. Picking up and returning rental cars seems quite easy as mentioned in other reviews. There are a couple of hotels on the airport grounds and others fairly close in case you have a late arrival or early departure. We arrived about midnight and the airport was pretty much closed in terms of restaurants and shops but that is common in most airports of this size and there were still a few personnel around to answer questions. Managed to find the phone to call our hotel for free shuttle pick-up. When visiting the area in the future I would definitely look into using Jacksonville or perhaps Daytona in lieu or Orlando.

title: Jacksonville Airport customer review
author: D Valentine
content: Have used Jacksonville Airport on numerous occasions and enjoy this airport. I recently took a flight to DCA on 8-10-06 which was the first flight day after the terrorist incident in England. Security was noticeably increased however it was smooth as silk. Of course I did not bring onboard items that the news media had been talking about all day long as not being allowed but the security section of this airport is very very efficient. The TSA agents noticeably increased never once were unfriendly in fact it seemed that they were going out of their way to try and make a hard situation pleasant. This is a great airport and recommend using it whenever possible.

title: Jacksonville Airport customer review
author: Peter Roozemaal
content: Recently was in Jacksonville for business; on my way in I was so fast at the curbstone that I had hardly time to examine the facilities at the airport. On my way out today I had plenty of time to look around; the no-queue security check (something all airports should introduce) gave me plenty of time for window-shopping. I appreciated dumping the rental car and walking straight into departures over the moving walkway. Landside of the security check is a small food- and shopping court with sufficient choice for the hungry traveller. Past security is a health and massage salon and several "souvenir style" shops. In concourse A there is sufficient opportunity to take a drink and have a snack. I have a two suggestions for improvement: put a some clocks on the wall in the concourses and try to bring in a bit more natural light indoors; change the brown wallpaint to white or blue. All in all Jacksonville International is one of the better airports I've visited.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: William Lay
content: The airport was not clean. There is not enough seats to sit outside the gate. The airport was very crowded. But for an old airport and an over capacity we have to understand them. They are trying to improve their standards. The crew and Staff were very kind. I think the airport needs to tell staff at the information counter to learn more about the airport, when I asked them about where a shop was they were very doubtful with their answer.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Keri Riley
content: Why are there always long visa queues? Was here 2 years ago and nothing has improved! Have a legitimate 1 year multiple entry business visa but wait 30 minutes to go through immigration. Observe Changi in Singapore: World class airport for good reason(s).

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Franck Leroy
content: Definitely one of the worst airports in the world. Arriving from Singapore on an AF flight and trying to pay the ever increasing and exorbitant $35 tax the clerk would not accept my 5 and 1 dollars bills and insisted I withdraw money from the ATM machine nearby which I refused! Went into a scuffle with this unfriendly male and after several insults from both sides I decide to move to another more friendly clerk. Left the following day for DPS on a Lion Air flight from terminal 3 and the complete lack of information is unacceptable. Once in the departure lounge there is no signage gate numbers or any kind of information regarding the departing flights! Very few signs in English no FB outlets and you always have to approach the single gate manned by exhausted (but rather friendly I must say) gates agents to find out about your flight gate and departure time plenty of announcements but they are inaudible. My real question is since Indonesia is the only Asian country (and possibly in the world) to impose a heavy tax when you arrive and again when you leave the country what is happening with the money? Why no improvement in the passengers services? I have been visiting Bali regularly for the last 26 years and I think this will be my very last time.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Aria Dhika
content: Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport is clean not crowded and overall is good. But I recommend avoid terminal 1.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Timothy Black
content: I'm not very pleased by the airport cleanliness and I really hate the crowds. But for an old airport and an over capacity we have to understand them. They have given their best for us. They have upgraded their airport and now they have a project to enlarge their airport (Terminal 3). The airport is under construction and we have to understand them. The crew and staff are very nice so I will give another review after the airport's construction is done.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Subramanian Vilayannur Hariharan
content: Arrived Jakarta from Singapore on 16th December. There was only 2 out 6 VOA counters that were open. took 1.5 hrs to come out of the airport. The only airport with an old structure.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Fendy Kurniawan
content: I have flown from CGK quite frequently in the past few years. Having used all terminals in CGK from T1 T2 and T3 all I can say that CGK is getting better every year compared to four to five years ago. What needs to be improved is the cleanliness and airport management. It often gets very busy on arrival imagine 4-5 international flights with wide body aircraft arriving at almost the same time and the immigration gets very busy and might take you more than 30 mins to get through immigration. Some facilities are also old and aged. Toilets are also sometimes really dirty (although I know sometimes it is the people are ignorant of this situation). I think as the main gate and touch point of Indonesia CGK needs to be more attractive to show the progress Indonesia has made in the past few years. Aside from that it has a decent duty free shop but lacks of variety of restaurant.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Noe Purba
content: The airport was good. There are lots of projects to improve the airport. The toilets were quite clean. There are small boarding gates Some airplanes must board from a remote stand.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Dante Vargas
content: Visited CGK Both Terminal 2 and Terminal 3. Terminal 2 is a disaster and I recommend avoiding this terminal (if not Jakarta all together) if you can do so. Poor air conditioning Poor Facilities Poor signage Poor Hygiene. Old and Not enough restaurants for an airport this size. I cannot comprehend how this is one of the busiest airports in the world and look this way. Queues for Checks is a mess and amount of checks frankly not really logical. 1st- security check to enter Check-in Area 2nd- Immigration 3rd-Security check at Gate 4th- Collection immigration Card (not sure why the immigration officer cant do that as they collect part of it upon arrival) 5th Boarding Pass to Board Plane. Every single check means more Queues. However the Airport does reflect Jakarta in a glimpse. Surprisingly Domestic Terminal 3 is much more modern cleaner and easier to navigate. Better signage friendly staff and enough facilities considering the size of the terminal. Chaos outside of both terminals but that is everywhere in Jakarta.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: M Zaki
content: Terminal 2 Concourse E for both arrival and departure. The outer corridor and kerbside felt so crowded and messy that we just wanted to get a taxi as quickly as we could upon arrival. Similarly upon departure we quickly walked through these areas and headed straight away into the check-in hall which was fortunately accessible only to passengers. We traveled with an infant and we were disappointed to find out that a proper baby nursing/changing room was only available past check-in hall and before the immigration counters. Having gone through immigration we felt that backtracking was a hassle. Post immigration we found that the area did not have sufficient seating although the concourse was not particularly crowded and there were not that many flights departing at that time. We then stumbled upon a pay-per-use lounge called Mutiara Lounge. Entry was 80000Rp (approx. USD8) per person which we thought was cheap. F&B and facilities were just OK nothing fancy in fact basic compared to premium lounges. We just needed some comfort for us especially for the baby.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: K Ridwan Purantoro
content: I usually go to terminal 2 for international flights. I can say I am disappointed with the cleanliness of the terminal. The facilities are okay and the staff are friendly. Not very organized though. Terminal 3 is much better than terminal 2. I only went there when I arrived from Surabaya when it first started operating. Cleaner more organized and has a more modern concept than terminal 1 and 2's traditional concept.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Danzel Samuel Purantoro
content: Used terminal 3. Immigration was quick and baggage was already rolling when we cleared immigration. When we went for our outbound flight check in was fast and immigration was a breeze although only one immigration counter was open. Overall terminal 3 is better than terminal 1 and 2. Hoping that T1 and T2 would follow suit like T3.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: J Mcmyler
content: Flight in J class from AMS with Garuda arrived late connecting flight to DPS boarding. No assistance from anyone usually there would be a member of staff with new boarding passes or information. Finally got told to run to gate however no advice on where that was! Eventually got to gate with aircraft still there to be told unable to board as bags wouldn't make it. 3 hour wait now for next flight however still trying to get boarding passes in lounge! Garuda inflight product in executive class is outstanding it's a shame the ground team let it down.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Liam Moulton
content: One of the busiest airports not just in Asia but in the world. Was very disappointed given you'd think that an airport of this size would be used to handling passengers and meeting their expectations. The lounge in particular was appalling. I paid for lounge access but when I got in they'd run out of beer and I complained and all the staff said was "come earlier in the day". I then replied by telling them a high percentage of long-haul flights leave late at night. Another thing which was very annoying and this happened both times I recently arrived was that baggage trolleys ran out meaning I had to carry my big heavy suitcase. At the same time I could see porters who were possibly charging for their services using baggage trolleys. How difficult is it for the management of CGK to order more baggage trolleys? On top of that its not very well organised and can be rather confusing to navigate. Finally (I was lucky because I have a work visa) there was only one immigration desk open at about 4 o clock in the afternoon meaning those who had to get a tourist visa on arrival had to wait ages. Also there was no queue control system like a 'snake line'. On the whole this airport while not as bad as others like Charles de Gaulle and Manila is an embarrassment to Indonesia as it gives first time visitors a bad impression of the country as they get a feeling of chaos poor organisation and a lack of care for visitors.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Danzel Purantoro
content: Arrived in Terminal 3 after an international flight. Queues immodestly build up in immigration which took a while. They should put more immigration counters as there are increasing numbers of international passengers in terminal 3. Terminal 3 is very clean and is Eco friendly.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Juan Alana
content: The airport is undergoing a lot of improvements. They're trying really hard to make it one of the best airports in the world. Facilities are great staff are friendly with a lot of duty free and restaurants.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: T Kimberley
content: Arriving was straight forward with the visa on arrival service obvious to find and fast to use. Once through immigration the bags appeared fairly quickly and the taxi desk is located on the left as soon as you walk through into the arrivals hall. Departing was straight forward with cheerful check in staff who will also deal with your departure tax payment. There's a good range of shops and places to eat in departures but one annoying thing is that while the terminal appears to be no smoking cafes seem to used as the smoking rooms!

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Lie Kristo
content: T1: CGK - SUB with Lion Air. The architecture of terminal is great giving you natural and warm feel. however queue time is always problematic which is caused by overcrowded check in took roughly 15 minutes. Boarding room is adequate and more spacious after renovation. T1C offer more facilities as there are duty free shops. T2: CGK - SIN with Lion Air. T2 is better than T1. more selection of shops and feels much cleaner. Immigration on departure took 10 minutes on arrival however took almost half an hour. Boarding room is pretty much the same with T1. T3 Phase 1: CGK - SUB with Air Asia. Boarding room feels much more spacious and much less overcrowded compared to T1. Looking forward for T3 Ultimate under construction now.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Kuhan Kandiah
content: Despite the unique airport structure and exotic design CGK airport (Terminal 2) is by far the least favourite airport for me. This is because the airport is chaotic and it is overcrowded due to over-capacity and it is very disorganised for an important and the busiest international airport in the region. The toilets should be well maintained and the air conditioning has to be enhanced for a better experience overall. I hope that CGK will be improved in the near future to the likes of KUL and SIN.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: John Baker
content: Flew from BKK to JKT overall I still find it a very exotic airport of it's kind rather than boring concrete block of sorrowness that some other airports have. I loved the ceiling design and the garden view from the window. Its not as bad as many claim the airport to be and there is a free wifi in the airport and most of the lounges at the airport offers it the food offered at batavia lounge is excellent.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Austin Lee
content: The airport is a bit old and aged it could use few beautification and fixing up but other than that its a good looking airport it has this very warm welcoming environment. Staff could do with more smiles facilities are fairly adequate there are great selection of food and shops in the airport. Immigration are fairly efficient and surprisingly fast baggage came out fairly quick and it only took me around 20 minutes or so to get out from the airport. Illegal taxis needs to be dealt with. The airport could use a free wifi since its almost all over the world right now and its very convenient for passengers and businessman provided airport is likely to delay a flight due to queuing planes and definitely more seating is required.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Masaki Oda
content: The international terminal (2D) has a unique architecture. While it is old in comparison with SIN or KUL artwork plants as well as natural lights give passengers more relaxed atmosphere. However the structure also makes passengers' walking distance longer especially for arrivals. International arrivals are nightmare. You may expect as long as two hours (unless you have an Indonesian passport) to clear immigration. On my recent arrival from Singapore. The officer directed us to one of the visa on arrival counters available. However when I almost reached the counter the counter was closed and thus we were directed to the end of the line for the other counter. With four flights arriving only three immigration booths for non-Indonesians were available. Departure was much smoother however the procedure (Lobby - Security - Check-in - Passport Control - Departure Lounge - another security - gate) was different from many other airports. It must be very hard for those who depart from this airport for the first time as there is not signs to tell you what to expect next and it is rather difficult for us to figure out how far the gates are from departure lounge areas where shops and airlines lounges are. It may take another 10 minutes walk plus another security before reaching your gates.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: T Adams
content: The airport has made great strides in the past 5 or 6 years to get passengers processed quickly and efficiently. However with the exception of the new domestic terminal this airport is very old with poor air-conditioning. Check in process for the international terminal is easy. Plenty of room. Only passengers actually flying are allowed at the check in area. The next step of going through immigration is much quicker than before as more immigration counters and agents have been added. However beware the immigration officers at this airport are very rude disrespectful and overall have an arrogant attitude to all. Once through immigration the process to get to your gate is easy with plenty of shops and restrooms and dining. It's just that the building is old dated and not enough AC. On inbound flights the process of passing through immigration for foreigners has improved dramatically and I now consider it one of the fastest airports that I know of to pass through immigration. However where Soekarno-Hatta airport fails is in the baggage claim customs and parking. Baggage claim facilities are ancient slow and crowded. Once you claim your baggage you must than have all your baggage go through an x-ray machine. This is ok except there is only one queue and one x-ray machine which means standing in what resembles a queue with many people jumping in front. Once you finally exit the baggage claim area you will be barraged by scores of locals trying to provide you with transportation to Jakarta. Overall for foreigners the immigration process is very good.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Carlo Lang
content: The speed of the immigration service has improved slightly but additional immigration counters must be added to cope with arrival passengers. The worst service from this airport is the customs. All passengers are required to place their carry-on items through an X-Ray machine. To make thing worse customs only opened one lane for people to check through. As a result passengers were queuing in a long line to get out. This has been going on for years without any improvement. My other comment is the parking facility of this airport is like a bus terminal rather than airport. This airport needed to be privatized and run by experts from international airport management before is degrade further.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Firman Siahaan
content: Terrible Airport. I was there 4 times between 17 Dec 2012 and 7 Jan 2013 for international trips (SYD-JKT- SYD) and domestic trips (JKT-MES-JKT). Firstly the international arrival area looked quite old. Secondly the luggage handling was horrible. They mixed all luggage from 2-3 airlines in the same carousel. The problem was it took them so long to get all luggage out onto the carousel belt. There was a sea of human waiting in the baggage collection area with extremely long and messy queue. On the departure as usual we had to pay airport tax. We also observed a few people entering the lounge by illegally sneaking behind others who were being served by unsuspecting staff.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: P Novria
content: Over the year this airport just getting better and always tries to improve service quality. At peak hours this airport will be very busy the toilets clean but I think the main problem is the passenger itself - they lack respect of this airport by breaking the rules for example smoking. This airport has a smoking area. Overall this airport is good.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: A Samulo
content: I landed at terminal 2 pretty good with exotic designs. I've also been landed at terminal 3 which is the best terminal at this airport but a terminal for low-cost carrier such as AirAsia and Tiger Mandala. Terminal 1 is quite busy. Particularly in terminal 1 C a very chaotic and badly unclear where the notice board and the schedule all wrong and sound boarding announcements and other announcements are barely heard anything. I've also been to terminal 1A very crowded and chaotic.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: I Milono
content: In general overall service has improved over the years now the toilets are cleaner and free more shops built and everything is better organized. However there's still a lot of space for improvement. While Terminal 2 (which houses all international and Garuda flights) looks better and brighter Terminal 1 certainly needs a facelift especially Terminal 1A. One area needs immediate attention: the baggage claim area it's dark bleak boring and sadly it is the place where you would most likely stay for quite a while to pick up your bags and at peak hours where many domestic flights arrive at the same time it can be quite crowded. Outside things can be chaotic once you proceed to check out you will be greeted by many taxi drivers who endlessly tout at you attempting to persuade you to take theirs. One more word of advice: the biggest problem in CGK is not within the airport it is outside the airport area. CGK is located some 20 kms west of Jakarta leave your hotel as early as you can particularly in peak hours. Jakarta's notorious traffic jams are unbelievable and often unpredictable.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: D McNeil
content: The airport looks much more better than the last time I was here around two years ago. The toilets in the gate area are improved (still love the garden view) and immigration was okay no more than 10 minutes. Check-in was quick and fast duty free shops adequate. But generally the airport is better and improving with the banners showing the airport expansion hung all over the place.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Tia Traynor
content: The terminal for the domestic flight was awful especially terminal 1A - it was unorganised. The terminal for international flights wasn't so bad. There was no queue at the immigration when I was there decent duty free shops however toilets are never in a good condition every time I visit Soekarno-Hatta.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: J B Legrand
content: Used both the international and (new) domestic terminal last month. Facilities-wise it is no worse than airports in most developing countries and I have seen worse airports in many so-called advanced countries. International arrival involved the shortest walk from the plane to immigration I have experienced in recent memory. The visa-on-arrival counter had no line so no waiting. Bags took a long time to arrive but no longer than in any US airport. Paid USD20 to pre-order a taxi from the booth outside customs and was thus spared from having to deal with the bustle outside we were escorted personally to our car. International departure was also relatively painless in spite of having to put up with hordes of pushy elbowing passengers heading home to China and Taiwan. The gate area was nice with clean toilets and good views of tropical landscaping. The best experience was in the new domestic terminal; the local Indonesian traveling public is very courteous and well-behaved and the terminal had excellent facilities including a great lounge where USD4 buys you an all-you-can-eat buffet with excellent choices. Probably the cheapest and best airport food I have encountered in all my travels.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: W Pollitt
content: CGK-DPS. Used the Low Cost domestic carrier terminal. A new facility away from the Int'l facility. Everything modern no crowds whatsoever (maybe good timing) good shops and comfortable seating. So much better than the old domestic terminal. If you are using the airport hotel just get your own taxi to save time and not the hotel service. Hopefully more upgrades are coming to Jakarta and Bali airports.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Yvette Febrina
content: Overall cleanliness is very poor. Serious improvements in particular to restrooms are needed. Waiting times are relatively long and needs to be improved especially for check-in immigration and baggage pick-up. Airport is very hot. Lounge food is very bad and crowded all the time.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: M Fadjar
content: CGK represents most things that are disorganised about Jakarta. However I am a great defender of its traditional and distinctive architecture. If you are an arriving Business Class passenger and don't waste your time to get to the immigration desk (assuming you don't need visa on arrival) then you can get to the taxi in 10 minutes flat without luggage and 15-20 min with (priority) luggage. Immigration officers have improved a lot over the years. The problem with CGK is all the chaos happening outside the sterile area after the custom check (arrival) or before the check-in (departure). I agree that the place lacks discipline in this respect (unlicensed taxis shamble parking dirty toilets horrible traffic jam etc). Unless you are planning to do business in Jakarta avoid this airport and go straight to your final destination cities in Indonesia.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: T Nomad
content: One of the worst airports I've been in. Dirty hot limited seating not enough food options. I was in the international terminal (terminal 2) and I can't imagine how much worse domestic could be. Do yourself a favor and buy into one of the many lounges if you're waiting for more than two hours. The fact that this is the capitol's airport is shameful.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: N Sutherland
content: Fortunately I arrived in the middle of the day when it was very quiet. Immigration very surly despite having paid $25 for a day visit to Indonesia. I didn't have any baggage so didn't have to wait but the arrivals/meeting area is split left and right making it difficult to find your 'greeter'. In Departures the signs are poor making it difficult to find your check-in desk. Check-in (Philippine Airlines) was unbelievably slow with yet more taxes to pay. Immigration was reasonable and security efficient. Duty Free looked cheap with a reasonable selection of goods but poorly organised. Late at night there was nowhere open to have a snack and a drink other than some smoke-filled hole in the wall. Not a great advertisement for the country really.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: C Ng
content: I have to say this is the worst airport I have experienced. With the exception of the departure lounge area the whole place is a shambles. The building is claustrophobic and dark signage is limited or absent the air conditioner struggles to maintain coolness and toilets are filthy. The arrival exit leads out to a fenced-in area which cuts off the concourse into two halves. The Departure roadway also doubles up illegally as a pickup area and as a result cars are double parked buses coaches and taxis of all kinds obstruct the roadway and the end result is absolute chaos. Touts are plentiful. I have had the misfortune of spending 1.5 hours waiting for a phantom shuttle vehicle from the hotel. I finally gave up and spend the rest of the remaining time trying to stay awake in the noisy and messy departure concourse. I haven't even mentioned about the visa charges and the airport tax. Take all this into consideration before you even think about the airfare.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Mike Ratcliffe
content: The airport facilities have got even worse (if that's possible). Once you pass thru immigration there is nowhere to get any food except a Starbucks where you can get snacks. There was one restaurant where you could get a local meal or a sandwich its closed for renovation. There are however quite a few Duty Free shops. This is the Main International Airport of a large city its absolutely disgraceful. Although the airport does have its own Indonesian style about it I have to say it is now terribly outdated. Avoid at all costs!

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Pandu Waskito
content: CGK needs lots of things to be sorted out. I like CGK because of its Indonesian design and architecture. Immigration queue just so-so though sometimes it's very hectic. Toilet needs enhancement reasonably clean yet outdated.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Ramdisa Agasi
content: I arrived at CGK around 22.00 after a long flight from DOH. The Immigration queue was surprisingly organised. Indonesian passport holders now queue at the old counters while foreign passport holders queue on the new immigration counters. Baggage handling took quite some time my luggage was in fact the last to appear on the belt. Departing from CGK was smooth. There were new security check-points opened so the line to enter check-in halls were reduced. The Emerald Sky Lounge was adequate. At the waiting hall the toilets were clean. Although the airport still lacks free-wifi internet.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: R Tan
content: The arrival experience can be awful. Immigration lines are confusing and can be lengthy custom clearance is unorganized with porters cutting the line. It feels like a large bus station.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Michael Cohen
content: Arrival 1515 touched down a few 10 minutes early and by 1600 had bought my visa passed immigration changed money bought a domestic ticket to Semarang (Garuda same terminal) checked in and passed through security into departure lounge. As well as buying an Indonesian sim-card checking the tourist information office and gettting some fresh air outside the terminal. I only had hand luggage which helped. Toilets plentiful and reasonably clean and there seemed a reasonable range of food outlets landside at least. Departing internationally 2 weeks later was much the same story I left town with plenty of time to spare to beat Jakarta's fabled traffic jams - conspicuous that day by their absence. All in all a very reasonable airport experience.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Harvinder Singh
content: In common with most reviews here - the international terminal is awful and a disgrace to Indonesia. It is amazing that the nation tolerates this for its first point of contact with arriving foreigners - or maybe it just doesn't care. Immigration is totally inadequate with perhaps 4-5 desks open for multiple flights leading to clearance times of more than an hour. Perhaps the delay at immigration could be considered a plus as typically the wait for baggage is relatively short. But all in all avoid if you can.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: K Kagome
content: The airport is dark hot and humid. The toilets are dirty with cockroaches people are smoking inside the airport. The shops are boring and food choice limited. Long queue at immigration (with various people trying to cut queues) long waiting time for the baggage and chaotic traffic outside the airport as every vehicles are trying to stop right outside to drop off/pick up passengers.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Jeff Schmerker
content: Confusing. We arrived in one terminal had to collect bags and troop to another terminal -- each for domestic flights. The arrivals hall and baggage claim is particularly dumpy. No information on how to go to the next terminal or even where it is though persistent taxi drivers will take you. In departures long halls and no place to sit.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: C Barkei
content: Departing is fairly straightforward although the 150000 RP tax should be included in ticket prices - other countries can do so. The bookshop is good and the lounge is well-stocked. Arrivals is a different matter: I have been to Jakarta 3 times in the past year and have lost 3 pages in an overcrowded passport already. Why not emulate the Japanese and make the visa sticker smaller? T At least the Chinese give you the option of having multiple entry visas when they take up a page. The lines at immigration are confusing and the baggage hall is not a good advertisement for Indonesia.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Kurt Müller
content: Immigration used to be tedious - now it's simply awful. First you waste time lining up for the visa on arrival where they take all your passport details and waste a full page in your passport for the visa sticker. Elsewhere this is done with a stamp that requires perhaps a quarter of a page. Then you line up for another 30+ minutes for the actual immigration procedure where the previous action of acquiring your passport details is duplicated. With some travelers finger-printing is added taking more time. In Japan where they also finger- print arriving foreigners the entire process including lining up takes less than 5 minutes. Whilst arriving foreigners sweat it out there are numerous counters for holders of Indonesian passports open where the waiting time is 5 minutes max. In short Jakarta is worse than even India in terms of time wasted at immigration and - as a tourist - I would avoid a country with such a "welcome". As business traveler I have no choice.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: N Aziz
content: The architecture is a bit traditional and old but it is still beautiful. However the services provided by security and immigration was not that friendly. It is a little bit crowded at the entrance and the security clearance was quite log. Many people simply cut off the queues. Inside the airport directions are quite simple and easy to understand. Pretty straight forward. Although not many staff can speak English they are very helpful and always smile.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Kurt Müller
content: Visa-on-arrival desk now much more efficient as they seem to have found software that can transfer your scanned passport details onto the visa stickers (they used to have to type all data manually). However issuing a full-page visa sticker for a stay of a few days is ridiculous and simply wastes an entire passport page upon every entry. In Japan the sticker is about the size of a postage stamp. On departure unnecessary waiting time is created by the surprise raid on departing passengers' wallets of Rp 150000 in cash. Most foreigners are out of local currency at that point in time. Why not collect the airport tax via the ticket like everywhere else?

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: M Ratcliffe
content: I have been thru Soekarna Hatta airport (CGK) many times and I can say that the departure immigration area has improved somewhat although not up to the standards of Singapore or KL. The check in areas are OK staff friendly and professional after immigration there are a number of eating outlets but mostly local food - not international considering this is Jakarta's main international airport its disapointing. Recently I noticed two internet terminals which were free - neither have worked since the many times I have tried to use them. The arrival areas are another story dingy dim and many officials standing around doing nothing. Immigration is Ok but at peak times the lines are long which also goes for the visa on arrival counters. The bags seem to take forever to arrive off the belt and then when you clear customs hoards of taxi touts who don't seem to understand the word NO! The airport needs major renovation.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Kiran Param
content: CGK is a small airport and can't be compared with KLIA or Changi. However upon arrival there are always lenghty immigration queues and signage is pretty poor. At departures to check in areas are pretty chaotic. Decent amount of food outlets and shopping.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: F Hadi
content: Toilets in international departure hall were recently refurbished and quite nice. The newly refurbished Departure Immigration area is nice and bright. Arrival Immigration hall is dingy and unwelcoming with a lot of immigration officials hanging out doing nothing. I hope they do something about this since this area is travelers' first impression of Indonesia. The baggage takes forever to appear and the baggage pickup area is also dingy and unkempt. The public area both in departure and arrival hall feel like a provincial bus terminal. The inter-terminal connection are served by a ridiculously overcrowded small bus with random schedule. Poor lighting all around - are they trying to save electricity here? Taxi touts are the scourge of this airport. Watch out for a gang of well dressed youth who swarm around your luggage and "take the initiative" to "help" you load your luggage into your car they will then demand an exorbitant tips afterward. Parking lot is dark dirty and full of suspicious characters milling about. I'm not a big fan of this airport's traditional architecture - it doesn't help to cheer me up especially after a long haul flight. Either the designer failed to adapt traditional architecture for a modern airport or we may simply have to admit that traditional architecture are inappropriate for this purpose. I for one prefer Changi's nondescript yet efficient concrete box with plush carpeting adequate lighting and plenty of air-conditioning.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: R Tielman
content: Travelling through Jakarta International for many years now and I must say I'm impressed with the level of service they have inside the airport. However after you passed customs and going to the meeting point you felt unsafe and the officials need to start addressing these issues. There are so many taxi touts and they are getting so aggresive even after we said no. Once you are inside the airport you feel like different world.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Billy Sumuan
content: Been here once or twice a month during the past 2 years lots of improvements have been made especially for the toilets in both terminal. Terminal 3 dedicated for LCC is currently under development located right in front terminal 2 concourse F. Shuttle bus between terminal is available for free. Thankfully there are official airport taxis (the ones with airport taxi sticker on windshield) with metered-rates and reasonable surcharge. Just ignore the men offering (sometimes even pushing) you to rent their car as a taxi. Lightning is still poor some gloomy spots here and there. Good news for platinum credit card holders since there are many executive lounges available. Bookstore restaurants cafes duty free shops are still available after departure immigration check.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: A Prabowo
content: Many things are great many things are bad. Strong traditional architecture used in this airport nice immigration friendly check in. The bad things are poor quality of facility (especially the toilets) sometimes only few immigration tables open while many passengers waiting in a long queue unmaintained trolleys sometimes you can find beggars in the airport especially when you are having food outside of check in area. One thing I really don't like about this airport is the big differences between domestic Terminal (Terminal 1) and International Terminal (Terminal 2). Terminal 1 has bad quality of maintain while Terminal 2 has very good quality. In Terminal 1 you can't enter full air conditioned room unless you are a passenger. Waiting room for accompanier located outside. But overall this is a nice airport.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: G Darmadi
content: The arrival section of the airport need to be improved. It's dark along the hallway heading to immigration. It's very different and contrast compare with departure section. Only 1 Visa on Arrival window opened. Overall it's an okay airport.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: S Winata
content: Soekarno-Hatta has a good architecture inside but its facilities need reparation. Not very clean toilets are a bit dirty and started to rust. Lack of information center. Lack of immigration booths at arrival (many unused) etc. On the plus side tourist can make their visa at the time they arrived Jakarta terminals are well-built and a very good drop-off and pick- up zone.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Mika Passanen
content: Very negative experience. Arrived around midnight from Bangkok with AirAsia went to the Visa On Arrival Counter and found out that 1 out of the 4 counters were open which result in a large queue. After having done the VOA went to immigration and again there was only 1 counter open out of 10 counters again large queue. It was hot humid and no air conditioning. Although there were a lot of immigration officials standing but only one works the rest was watching TV. This airport needs some professional staff that work.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: K Param
content: CGK can't be compared to Changi or KLIA however pleasantly surprised with the lounge for LH passengers. Duty free limited and overpriced. Check in no queue at business check in however boarding the aircraft a bit chaotic.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: W Keeney
content: Transferred from a Garuda domestic to a Garuda international flight this last trip (Jan 08). Arrived at 2F left from 2E so finger piers are adjacent. You have to proceed into the inner ring concourse passing one security check; then find the proper check-in counter in the inner lobby (international flights check in at a different set of counters than do domestic). Once you check in and pay your exit tax (still currently Rupiah 100000 at Jakarta) you return the direction you entered pass an audit desk that makes sure you paid the tax then Immigration then back into the inner ring concourse where all the lounges and shops are located. Can be confusing but still only took me 20 minutes total at 1500 hours on a weekday afternoon. GA Executive lounge quite good with an immense buffet; lots of choices. You go through outbound security again on the way to the gate in the finger pier so allow time - but there was no queue either so very fast. All in all an easy- to-use airport with friendly staff if you start to get lost.

title: Jakarta Airport customer review
author: Mike Austen
content: As a resident in Indonesia have frequently used Jakarta Airport. Generally it works pretty well with always friendly staff at all levels ie check in / immigration/ customs down to lavatory attendents this of course is a good reflection of overall Indonesian courtesy. Entering and exiting the terminals always a bit of a hassle because of touts but the situation has improved and it's never overly aggressive. There is something very pleasant even uplifting about the architecture of the place as mentioned before especially in the departure areas and it never appears overcrowded. The Duty free is indifferent and the knick knacks a bit overpriced but probably good and unique transit purchases. The credit card holder lounges are a great idea especially for locals who often have to leave for the airport as much as 6 hours before take off due to the Jakartan traffic. However don't buy duty free on arrival as often the international branded bottles and packages contain pirated inferior products. All in all like Indonesia as a whole a safe and friendly enviromnment with reasonably priced and good quality food and beverages.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Paul Maley
content: We had no problems either entering or departing at the end of May. Umrah was in progress but in both situations there were very few pilgrims about and inside the non Hajj terminal (main terminal). All the reviews we had seen up to now made us extremely apprehensive. But none of the problems described up to this point were experienced including delays having to use taxis to get between terminals. We were really relived! The food court at the airport was not as varied as many other international airports but we found the few choices ok. No problem in getting boarding passes or checking in to Lufthansa. Signage was fine and security good. Customs and immigration were no issue. Maybe we were just lucky? There was no mass queuing or rushing to board buses to be transported to the aircraft. This was our first entry every into Saudi Arabia and it took us longer than others who had been there before. Women are treated differently than men but my wife got through without incident. Trying to locate the gate was not a problem and signage worked well.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Salim Bawa
content: Arrived at North Terminal for flight RJ112 to London via Amman as advised. A lot of passengers for this flight were diverted to Hajj Terminal without any valid reason. Had we been told in advance this would not be a problem but telling passengers at 0730 for 0900 am is totally unacceptable. No shuttle service provided I had to fork out 150 SR for taxi to Hajj Terminal. We were than ferried back to north terminal to board RJ 112 to London via Amman. Very frustrated and angry. Will not fly RJ again.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: S Zimmermann
content: When departing for a recent flight I was given a boarding pass with no departure gate. Moreover the electronic display in the departure area does not have all the departing flights listed. Trying to locate my gate was a real aggravation. There were no information desks or airport officials in sight. I could have missed my flight. When returning from the same trip the passengers had to stay on the plane for a rather lengthy delay before taking buses to the airport building. Then we waited nearly two hours to get through immigration. This airport is chaotic and inefficient.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: G Henderson
content: The airport is important for Muslim passengers going to Mecca. It should have better entertainment lounge F&B and shopping facilities staff attitude and queue management during immigration and security checks so it gives a better Umrah and Hajj experience. I hope it can be fixed for the later years.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Ivan Korompis
content: The airport is important for Muslim passengers going to Mecca. It should have better entertainment lounge F&B and shopping facilities staff attitude and queue management during immigration and security checks so it gives a better Umrah and Hajj experience. I hope it can be fixed for the later years.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Dave Houlihan
content: In short an award of greatest airport dump. Been through this "airport" many times. Always bedlam immigration a disgrace ranging from min of 1 hour to up to 6 hours. Staff rude  place filthy ancient no air bridges aircraft parked miles from terminal lack of gates etc. KSA obviously don't care about their image if this is Saudis hub as well as the entry for Hajj etc. New airport being built lets see.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: S Ahmed
content: This is by far the world's worst airport I have travelled to and I would not say so without having experienced airports throughout the world. This airport embodies the ultimate disgrace in the aviation industry and I do not even know where to start to comment. KSA Aviation Authority should be ashamed of the poor level of service provided at this airport despite the fact that this is the gateway to their country. If you are travelling for Hajj and Umrah brace yourself to be standing in immigration queues for up to 6 hours with immigration officers using batons to "arrange" queues. This airport is simply unacceptable.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Goolam Begg
content: Undoubtedly one of the poorest airports in the world. The airport officials display very little people skills. This is a nightmare airport. Compared to Dubai airport very far behind minimum airport standards. Then again the Saudis do not take advice from anybody to improve this.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: M Shok
content: Incredibly rude and careless attitude from the airport personnel. Very slow processing causing very long queues.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: R Spellman
content: I get that it takes a long time to build a new airport. In the meantime can they please clean the bathrooms? Or at least supply toilet paper? This airport is too small too gross and clearly mismanaged. There's a million things they could do to upgrade it with very little effort while the new airport is under construction. What's most amazing is that it's the second-biggest airport in KSA. You'd think they'd have a little more national pride. In fairness my queuing times have been OK. I'm sure I just got lucky.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: C Chan
content: The worst airport experience I have had particularly while going through the passport control checkpoint. I stayed in a queue for 45 minutes and had to switch to another queue (to start again from the back of the line) when the officer decided to have a break - he simply left without alerting the people queuing. I was in the second queue for another 45 minutes - with 6 people in front of me - but I ended up waiting for this officer to process 14 people before my turn. When it was finally my turn officer decided to take a break he referred me to the other counter he then changed his mind and processed two more passengers who were behind me and left me waiting at the counter. The officers were chatting up a storm during this whole process. The long queues did not seem to bother them at all. To take >3 minutes to process one passenger is simply too slow in any international airport and there is no queuing system in place at all. If you had to fly into this airport get logical thinking out of your mind and allow ample amount of time at passport control. In my experience there simply wasn't any logical (or what one would generally perceives as sensible) system in place.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: S Nik
content: One of the worst Airports in the world and I've traveled to over 350 destinations around the world. After a 5.5hr flight from FRA to JED we spent a solid 6 hrs standing in line to go through passport control. Hopelessly overcrowded terminal no signage to indicate which queue is for which type of visa no seating no water no information or announcements and a filthy toilet. The Immigration officers couldn't care less. At one point the guy just got up and disappeared only to come back an hour later leaving passengers standing around for nothing. After 90 min. in line we were told we were in the wrong queue and had to go back to the end of the line in another queue - there were no signs anywhere to indicate which queue is for which visa type. After we finally got through our luggage was all over the place strewn in the arrivals hall. Never again!

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: K Chaudhry
content: Hajj Terminal. One of the worst airport terminals I have seen. Undisciplined and unprofessional immigration officers. No information will be provided at all.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: John Konnully
content: One of the worst airports I have visited. The toilets are just wet and water everywhere smelt really bad. They closed off an entire section of the airport and put nearly 8 flights worth of people in 3 waiting lounges.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: P Upton
content: A truly awful experience. I spent 5 hours in a chaotic queue waiting to clear immigration. The immigration staff were rude and abusive and fights almost broke out on several occasions due to attempted queue jumping. This airport and the procedures in place there are a shocking (and fairly accurate) introduction to Saudi Arabia.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Moeed Khan
content: I've only visited the airport once and only the Hajj terminal. The worst thing about the terminal waiting area is that it is too hot. No air conditioners at all. The most annoying thing about the terminal is that it has air bridges but still you have travel in buses. The terminal gates are too air conditioned so you start to feel cold. But the facilities are good. The washrooms are clean and the duty free shops are good enough.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: S Ware
content: This is an airport from the 1970s! Poor surroundings staff with no customer service skills and the usual Saudi paranoia about gender separation and checking passports. Security at the departure gate is a complete farce.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: M Ahmed
content: No customer service no organisation luggage from different flights all piled up in the same place took me hours to find my suitcase. Complete chaos. Just very uncomfortable didn't expect this sort of service in a developed country.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: C Ferguson
content: I spent half of a day in the Saudi Arabian Airlines transit terminal. I had time and expected the airport to be like other new Middle-Eastern or Asian airports and so did not think twice about the long delay shopping hotels and restaurants are readily available at the aforementioned airports. The terminal is very small duty free shopping is very limited and there is only one place to buy food which is overpriced. Staff are rude and ignore customers. Seating is limited at peak times and wireless internet is available for an hourly charge. The bathrooms are filthy and stink of smoke. There is no place to exchange money and you will have to purchase an item from the duty free store with euro or dollars if you want to obtain Rials. As Westerners without visas cannot enter the country if you transit through this terminal you will be stuck here so bring some food and something to do with you.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Bjorn Hansen
content: Travelling to Jeddah on a regular basis for business throughout the past 6 months I seem to have been lucky with this airport. Departure was never a problem - from taxi trop off via business check-in passport control and security I am usually in the waiting lounge within 15 minutes. I have to admit though that I have never travelled on peak times such as Hajj or Eid.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: D Ahmed
content: There's been renovations and improvements and overall its good. Airport proximity is great less than 20 minutes from anywhere in Jeddah and you're there. Airport is easily accessible you dont have to walk for hours to get to your gate luggage comes out quickly. Overall I think its fine.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: A Khalid
content: I agreed with the negative reviews here about the first class lounge in the airport they have to see other airport lounges in different countries to get an idea of how to manage such facility. Service is bad jam sandwiches & cheese sandwiches. If you need milk for your tea you use the filthy coffee machine to get some. Floors and toilets should be checked. I hope that they re-consider providing a new management for the lounges and the duty free .. it is an international airport which receives hundreds of thousands passengers every year and it's a shame for a big country to have such memory for the visitors.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: A Dron
content: Either I used a different airport from comments on this site or I am extraordinarily lucky. My arrival was not representative as I was whisked through the VIP lounge (attending an airline conference that Saudia was hosting) but departure from the Saudia terminal was painless. Only complaints were a lack of signage to check-in desks (you enter the terminal then walk straight ahead 30 yards and go through another set of glass doors to find them) and the amount of smoking that was going on. Check-in was swift my bags being checked through Riyadh and on to London. The place seemed clean - I did not use the toilets so can not comment on them uncrowded and calm. Be aware that the security X-ray machines are very sensitive and you will have to remove even your wristwatch to get through them. Duty-free and Costa coffee shops airside. Generally an above-average even pleasant experience.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: M Khan
content: By far the worst managed airport in the world. I have travelled many times (approximately 20) via this airport. It appears to get worse each time I've visited. On many occasions I was a VIP ie. performing Umrah. Almost every other Islamic country offers a fast track or special treatment for persons on a journey to/from umrah. However the host nation ie. Saudi Arabia passport/immigration control make you queue for hours (5-6 hrs is the norm). No separate queues for elderly women or children or persons with other reasons for visits. Passport control then spend approx. 45 mins per person at the kiosk flicking through pages of your passport taking fingerprints of every finger on both hands. It gets worse if you have not completed the correct landing forms as you just get waved away without a proper explanation. And there are no clear signs or instructions on where to obtain such forms until someone from the mile long queue points or explains what you need to do. Saudi or Arabic speaking travellers jump the queues and there are just allowed to and we as foreigners aren't allowed to question. To make matters worse just as you think you are next in the queue the passport control clerk leaves/closes their station. No explanation no replacement clerk no moving of same queue to another kiosk. You just stand there hoping he will return or just join the back of another mile long queue.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: Ahmed Al-Zuhairi
content: The worst airport I have ever been to. Immigration took 90 minutes to get through. once outside you enter into a mafia of taxis where they all have agreed to rip you off with ridiculous prices. $70 for a 45 minute drive to Mekkah if you do not like it there's nothing you can do about it. Once we reached Mekkah the driver took me to the wrong hotel and so he had to do an extra 4 minute drive which he took $15 for. Disgusting manners and a shame for the country's reputation. Return flight was from the Hajj terminal which we did not know about until arriving to the main terminal. The Hajj temrinal is less than 500 metres from the main terminal however it is protected by barbed wires and so a taxi trip takes 15 minutes 15kms away another $20 and involves going round the whole airport; really badly laid out. The hajj terminal is chaotic and basic.

title: Jeddah Airport customer review
author: R Merritt
