title: Kirkenes Airport customer review
author: Michael Rapp
content: Kirkenes has a brand new airport terminal which really looks nice and may be adequate to handle some handful of passengers. I arrived with a Widerøe turboprop flight from Vardø and we were 2 passengers on board. We had to walk the few metres from the plane to the terminal building but unfortunately both doors to the arrival hall were locked. The guy who drove the little baggage cart for our flight suggested to follow him. So we entered the terminal through a "back door". Two suitcases were on the brand new belt immediately so we didn't had time to watch the modern interior of the terminal. Unfortunately both suitcases belonged to the other passenger. So I ringed somebody out of the closed SAS office to complain about my missing luggage. When he took the details about my blue suitcase he suddenly stopped went back into the office and came out with my suitcase. It arrived on an earlier and direct flight. As the airport bus runs only once a day on saturdays he offered to call a taxi. This will need 12 minutes to arrive from town because there usually are no taxis at the airport waiting. So I spent the time waiting in the sun on a bench in front of the terminal. NOTHING happened there during these twelve minutes. Overall it was a funny and sympathetic experience at this minor airport at the edge of Europe.

title: Kirkwall Airport customer review
author: A Rimmer
content: The airport is as good as you can expect for a small airport. There are check-in desks on one side and bar and cafe on the other. Security / departures are just past the information desk and open typically when inbound flight lands or is on arrival. The staff are good and helpful. The one area that is woeful is the parking. How can such a small airport have a permanently full car park?

title: Kirkwall Airport customer review
author: Peter Thackray
content: A fantastic little airport. Arrived from GLA plane pulled up outside the terminal building. One Luggage Belt very quick reclaim. The terminal is one open plan "shed" type building with 4 Check-in Desks for the main flights to the rest of the UK and Europe. The Departure Lounge opens about 20 minutes before the flight is due to depart (usually once the inbound flight has arrived). Once through Security large waiting area with seats and a toilet look out onto the apron. There are 2 Doors to allow for 2 flights to be dealt with. In the main part of the terminal there is a Tourist Information Desk with local information a Cafe offering a range of hot drinks and snacks/sandwiches and a small shop with a few basics and small souvenirs. There is also quite a large seating area connected to the eating section. There is also a 2nd lounge area by the Inter- Island part of the terminal - this deals with the flights out to the islands that form Orkney handled by Loganair. Here Check-in and Baggage Reclaim are handled and Departures/Arrivals are handled completely separately from the other flights. Maximum aircraft size is 8 passengers so it is all very cosy and informal but very efficient. Flew out to PPW for worlds shortest scheduled flight and back later in the day and could not fault the whole experience.

title: Klagenfurt Airport customer review
author: Etoile Brilliant
content: With about 5 flights a day there's not much to it. However I've never seen a queue of more than 1 person for security. There's free wifi and a decent duty free shop. Transit times from plane to taxi - less than 2 minutes with hand luggage.

title: Klagenfurt Airport customer review
author: I Andrews
content: Fast efficient little airport to arrive at your luggage arrives quickly and is usually carefully handled. It is almost impossible to get lost and the airport has good transport links for Carinthia and the ski regions of NW Slovenia. Flying from Klagenfurt is not quite so good the departure lounge could do with some toilets after passport control so if you need the toilet be sure to go before you go through. On the positive side the cafe upstairs is very good for the size of airport.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Kazi Ayetullah Al Mehedi
content: Kuala Lumpur (KLIA) is one of good airports thanks to all the available facilities. I traveled several times through this airport and found airport staff to be very helpful, and the immigration process took less than 10 mins.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Udo Anders
content: First and foremost it was nice to land at such a spacious airport, meaning this is one airport you will never feel over crowded, but you might as well think you have just landed somewhere that is too big for its actual occupancy, the airport is too far out of central KL, meaning you have leave plenty of road (no train options) time to get to your terminal. Service related issues I found were mainly around the food court, most servers are more content to talk amongst themselves than serve customers. Vendors, some accepted foreign currency some did not, most tables in the food court wee full of previous customers trash. Food court was modern with all of the usual outlets available. Only one other place to purchase drinks in the food court, serviced by skeleton staff, not really interested in serving any customers, I found it hard to buy a drink of any kind, I ended up just going to one of the many burger joints to make my purchase. Toilets, yes there are plenty available here, however each one smells. Cleaning equipment left out unattended in eye sight. Receptical over flowing, filthy floors and counter tops, I had to keep reminding my self I'm not in Singapore anymore, Malaysia please take some notes. Not very well managed or maintained in any capacity. Customs, going through the X-ray machines is quick and easy, I found the staff friendly, although their staffing for these areas is over the top, 10+ staff to each machine is over kill most staff stand around talking, in the way of passengers.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Mickael Chia
content: KLIA2 is a poor airport. The design necessitates long walks. Services are inconsistent. Most days there's a buggy service for the upper part of the walk. Today we waited more than half an hour but no buggy for passengers appeared. However there was a buggy ferrying staff with wheelchairs (to fetch passengers). Their attitude is: for passengers not our business.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Michael Walsh
content: I have flown into KLIA from Heathrow on average every two years since it opened in 1998, to visit family, with some regional/internal flights in-between. It is a well-presented and apparently well-maintained airport with reasonable functionality and transport links. I will focus on the truly negative aspect for this review as it needs highlighting: queuing at Immigration Control. This applies to both arriving and departing passengers, and the latter seems quite unique to KLIA. Upon arrival at KLIA, it is quite normal to join a queue for foreign passports that will last some 20 minutes or more. There doesn't seem to be much in the way of passenger-flow monitoring and accommodating peak periods. When going through ticket presentation from check-in to security, at KLIA there is a row of Immigration desks for passport/biometrics capture. My experiences over the last 17 years have shown this to be a very quiet area, so I was particularly surprised at the queues that I had to join last Wednesday (24th). I don't know if there was a unique event or incident that contributed to this, but everything seemed normal to that point. My queue lasted 20 minutes, and was the quicker queue as an extra desk opened up towards the end. Up to that point, there were three desks out of 7+ open for foreign passports, with an extra two for "First and Business Class" that did not call over any passengers to alleviate the queue when they were not serving anyone. That aside, it was the usual positive experience, if unspectacular. But the queuing desperately needs addressing.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Navatne
content: Airport layout is horrible. Immigration was quick when I arrived. Officer was pleasant. For departure, went through countless security checkpoints. Some staff rude, others refused to accept the smartphone Airasia app boarding pass. At the entrance to Departures one staff member said "go to checkin counter and get a boarding pass". His colleague looked at the smartphone and asked me "is it a screenprint" then I had to reload the app to show him it wasnt. Security staff at the bag check and metal detectors had poor attitude.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: C Ng
content: I travel through KLIA2 at least 20 times since its opening. In terms of infrastructure, it is a better airport than the previous LCCT. Lots of room, better laid out, bright and cheerful, good shopping, and transportation to and from the airport were smooth. However, one problem is the distance from the boarding gates to the terminal building. Insufficient (or absence of) travelators, has made the distance to the boarding gates demanding to say the least, especially for the elderly and the infirm. Confusing signage is another problem. And the widely displayed 3D map only adds to the confusion. I have seen people heading towards to the carpark when they were supposed to be heading towards the check-in counters. The 'official' airport staff were unhelpful when it comes to giving directions. The queuing for both the check-in and in-coming immigration counters were not cordoned off, and as a result, queue jumping, pushing and shoving is normal. Where is the security when they are needed? And the toilets are filthy.  Considering that this airport is only about two years old at the time of writing, I can't imagine its condition several years from now.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Lim
content: Immigration took more than half an hour to clear 9 people, the x-ray machine at customs broke down, and the walk from customs to the departure gates was ridiculously far (seriously, there was a large shopping mall between the two). Despite being at immigration more than an hour before take-off, I was held up for an absurd amount of time and had to run the entire way to the plane to just squeak through the boarding window, only to find the gate closed with nary a soul in sight. The airline staff returned 30 minutes later, claiming to have left their post only 5 minutes before take-off (yeah, right). I was refused a transfer to the next flight because, and I quote, "Everyday people complain customs slow." In the end, I was forced to purchase a new plane ticket at an inflated price.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Shane Walker
content: I frequently travel between Singapore and KL on AirAsia and unfortunately need to use the new KLIA2 airport. It is without a doubt one of the worst airports that I have experienced. In addition to being very badly designed (many of the gates are 15 minutes or more walking distance from the check-in / arrival hall with very few travelators) it is very poorly constructed and maintained. I used it in the 1st week that it was open and it was obvious that operations had commenced before it was finished. Now after little more than 1 year it looks like a 20 year old building. It is dirty and starting to fall apart. The check-in process is bedlam and getting through immigration can often take 30 minutes or more.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: T Erguven
content: I arrived to airport after 10pm I was looking to buy something to eat and I had to exchange money to do so or at least an ATM. But everything is "temporarily closed" in the airport. Even the convenience store.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: M Gother
content: We used KLIA1 four times in March and we had a very pleasant experience the only issue is the distance to and from gates other than that we found it clean modern and plenty of reasonably priced food outlets a word of advise if you arrive on a domestic flight and walk outside for a hotel transfer you are actually on Level 3 and its not obvious with all the taxis its easy to believe you are at ground level.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: William Webster
content: KLA2/AirAsia. This is Air Asia's hub airport. It is probably one of the worst designed "new" airports in the world. It is one big shopping mall with airplanes a long way away. The check in is chaos unless your in Air Asia's business class but if your doing a connecting flight you still have to go through customs and drag your bags to be checked in for your connecting flight and if your flight is many hours away you can't check in early to get back into transit to use the transit hotel. You can't stay in transit if you can get to transit for more than 10 hours so if your connecting flight is say 12 hours you have to stay in the country side of customs I believe this is all planned to get you to shop in their giant mall. Going from arrivals to departures for connecting flights is mostly a mystery as the signs are confusing and sometimes the moving stairs don't work and the elevators get jammed up with baggage carts. I had to go through three security checks. At Singapore Airport they check at the gate! Wise up Air Asia! The gates seem like miles away and you have to walk 99% of it. Avoid this terminal at all costs. If you have a short time between flights expect to miss your connecting flight.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Simpson
content: Flew LHR-KUL-PEN-KUL-MEL in transit at KLIA both times very easy to transfer from an international to domestic flight there is a separate escalator once you exit off the train in the main terminal which takes you to an immigration desk then after passing through there yiu are in the domestic departure area. The terminal is well sign-posted with colour codes directing you. The terminal is bright clean and plenty of shops bars and cafes to occupy your time in transit. I find this airport a pleasure to use.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Jay Sin
content: I have used KLIA dozens of times for transfer and I can say it is modern and clean. But there are really some issues: 1) Smoking area next to Burger King is a filthy empty box. people have to sit on the floor. You might dislike smoking but they are still paying guests! 2) Once at the gate there are minimal places to sit. Again the floor is the only alternative. 3) Misunderstandings and unnecessary crowding because of sharing one gate entrance for two flights while other gates are unused. 4) Nice public place (square) to sit is missing. You have to go to a restaurant to have a nice seat. Sorry but it is not my favourite place. Hong Kong is much better.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Kuek Soon Wem
content: The airport is very clean. The food is very good. Check in and passport is very fast.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Muhammad Alif Bin Zainul Abidin
content: Very interesting view in the satellite and I didn't expect to see the forest in the middle of a modern airport. Also the toilets were very clean and the check-in counters were very neat in arrangement which will make it easy for passengers to find their check-in counter.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Yan Wai Siong
content: I'm flying with Malaysia Airlines here. I don't need to queue for check-in because there are lots of MH check-in kiosk. The terminal is clean well always got workers to clean. The facilities are great and nothing to say it's perfect.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Brian Kidstonn
content: The Airport security was very poor all the operators were looking at their smart phones instead of doing the job of checking items going through I will never fly through KL again lack of signs etc and the girl at the info desk was busy also on her smart phone. Transit passengers had to exit through customs then enter again when you exit customs you come out in a shop with no signs directing you were to go I will never make the mistake of flying through KL again.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: H Richard
content: Well the first thing to say is that it's big - very big. I guess it's better than the old LCCT (the one advantage of which was that it was small). Be prepared to walk - a lot. Immigration was reasonably quick wait for luggage was about 5 or 10 minutes. Lots of landside shopping and eating in the adjacent KLIA Gateway shopping centre. Long walk to taxis buses etc from arrivals exit but train to KL Sentral is much closer - almost outside Arrivals. Be careful when flying long international flights: we went through security scanning after immigration as is normal with most airports then again on the way to the gate. People had bought water on the assumption that they had already been through security and it was confiscated from them. Airside is very spacious with lots of seating and a food court (prices consistent with an airside food court) and expensive shops.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: F Boersma
content: We flew from Sydney to Klia2. Disembarked desperate for a visit to a bathroom. I entered the first Ladies toilets we came to only to discover that they smelt putrid. I walked straight back out. This experience was repeated in each of the four bathrooms I entered except the last but on this occasion before I got to the cubicle a fellow passenger informed me that the only operable toilet had no paper. We then had to stand for 20 minutes for our baggage which felt like an eternity in my desperate state. As I was not prepared to subject myself to the odour or lacking hygiene again I waited until we got to our hotel which entailed the express train into KL and then the monorail followed by short walk and the usual time require for hotel check in. As I commented to my husband "There is little wonder as to why they don't have the cleanliness feedback touchscreens that can be found in Singapore."

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: David Butcher
content: Passed through KUL three times in a month once in transit once arriving and once departing. The transit was four hours long and was painless. Easy well signed transfer. The airport is clean bright and uncrowded (nearly empty might describe it better). Excellent MH Golden Lounge . Good Wifi. No issues with security/ immigration/ customs/ check in delays. Baggage processed quickly. Train service to/from KL Sentral first class. This airport and MH are both excellent operations.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Ross Clark
content: A good airport terminal (used for an arrival/departure on one flight and in transit on another). Shopping is ok the queuing for immigration and baggage took about half an hour. Also one can check in baggage at KL Sentral railway station (for MH and some other airlines as well - it works). My main issues are twofold. First the security screening at the gates can be quite slow - a lot of people at once - when it might work better to have one screening point. Second the free wifi coverage is poor when you can get it to work at all and the free Internet terminals weren't working. Also they are now using tablets instead of proper keyboards which are lousy to type on. I'd rather pay for a proper implementation of both.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Rohit Raj
content: Have used KLIA several times for arrival departure and transit as well. Airport very far away from KL city and if you have to catch a flight in the evening or have landed during that time be prepared to spend approx 2 hours travelling. The airport is of international standard and is very spacious but I didn't find the staff to be friendly or polite. Whether it's the airline staff at check-in counters or immigration officers I find them rude on most of my visits. This airport has plenty of restaurants duty free shops and ample seats. Its never been crowded.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: M Taylor
content: KLIA feels like it used to be a top-notch airport but has fallen to neglectful bad habits. It's just not well kept and feels a little dirty and cheaply run. The shops are okay (standard big-Asia-airport shops) but still have a sort of tacky make-shift feel about them unlike Singapore or Hong Kong and more like some Manila terminals or SVO (Moscow). My biggest complaint about this airport which I didn't spend a very long time in is the immigration queues. I didn't have any luggage but the queue for immigration was very slow moving. This is partly due to the number of Chinese nationals trying to enter (on my flight from Hong Kong) - and it certainly slows things down a bit when immigration staff insist on checking return flight bookings for certain passports (and in some cases rejecting them - something I have never seen before - telling passengers to contact their airline for assistance after being denied entry initially!). As a British passport holder getting past the lady at immigration was very smooth but there simply weren't enough staff for it to be acceptable by today's standards for big airports - particularly if they insist on checking Chinese peoples itineraries. My other gripe is the lack of reasonable coffee in departures - the best you can find is a McCafe without paying silly money: there is no other major coffee chain inside the airport (that I could easily find and at 6am I was looking pretty hard!).

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Farouk Mogheth
content: Flew recently with Malaysian from Bangkok to Kinabalu and back via Kuala Lumpur. The waiting times for both connections were quite bad with 9 hours on my way there and the same on my return. I have always had good or above average experiences with KLIA1 however my flights were always during the day. My last connection was with the same airline from Bangkok to Sydney and all went well without a hitch. My loudest criticism and a shame to KLIA's managers is the lack of support for "real late night" travelers. I arrived to KUL from Kota Kinabalu 2.20am (flight to Bangkok 9.10am) and was completely relaxed even if I found information regarding transportation non existent for anyone landing after 1.30am! Sama Sama express in the airside has more or less acceptable rates for a 6 hours nap but showed no availability online. Checking the reception I discover that the place is half empty and many rooms are vacant but requested the walk in rate close to a 100USD for 5 hours instead of the 50-60 online average. The other Sama hotel outside in the public zone requests a laughable high rate. This all was of no problem as KLIA2 (Low cost terminal) has been rebuild with a huge mall adjacent and the Kliaexpress train stops there and has 2 very reasonably priced hotels. However sadly last train service is midnight or 00.30. Kuala Lumpur airport around 2am and after is a sad sight. Many passengers sleeping where they can on the floor or benches. A gang (cannot think of a better name) of taxi drivers who ask 50 ringits (16USD) for the short drive to the other terminal. No shuttle bus to KLIA2 until 6.30 and all information simply pushed me towards the taxi drivers. Why is KLIA1 so inattentive and dismissive of passengers after midnight? If they offer their services to airlines landing that time then they have the responsibility of offering a shuttle to KLIA2 as many wanted to go there either to catch a flight or use hotel services. I felt total disregards as well as ambivalence towards me and many of my fellow passengers who were in the same situation. Otherwise clean food venues alright and prices manageable.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Ali Jacques
content: KLIA 2 I arrived on Friday afternoon 3 October from The Gold Coast I flew on Air Asia X. Arriving on a Friday there were a lot of flight arrivals hence masses of passengers. Now the bad news. To start with their are no signs pointing you in the direction of Immigration/Passport Control there were hundreds of passengers running around in a somewhat confused state. I found myself following a queue of passengers hoping that someone knew which way to go. Five minutes later I was still walking ten minutes later still walking fifteen minutes later still walking and no moving walk ways. In all this tine there were only two small signs pointing you in the direction of "Arrivals" blink and you have missed them. Passport control was quick waited only ten minutes to have my visa stamped. The baggage collection area is massive my bag came out on the carousel quickly in only ten minutes. Everyone needs to have their bags put through the scanner no problems quick. The airport is gigantic badly planned and disorganised. The return to KLIA2 was on Friday 20 October 2014 I caught the KLIA Express train brilliant and takes only 35 minutes from KL Sentral. Upon entering the terminal there was total "chaos" large groups of departing passengers (mainly Chinese) jammed into every available space it was unbearable had to get out so headed for the nearest Starbucks. I checked in four hours ahead easy you go through 5 security/Passport checks until you reach your Departure gate this Security business is ridiculous as with each step you go through the same procedure. Masses of departing passengers it never stops. The Duty-Free shopping is great plenty of outlets selling Designer goods chocolates (many of them) alcohol and many others the selection is endless. Finally boarded my Air Asia X flight to the Gold Coast - what a relief to say the least.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: J Steinert
content: One of the best! We were very satisfied with this airport. It was very modern and clean. It is quite big but still organized and you can find everything you need. You can get food all day. Some shops are closed later at night though. Food is not too expensive compared to other airports (especially Europe). You can find places to have naps and you still feel very safe. Once you arrive there there is a special service where the taxi driver can't rip you off but there is a counter where they calculate exactly what you have to pay for a certain distance. Other airports should do that too. Never seen anything like that anywhere before! We were very impressed.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Rishad Patell
content: Used KLIA to transit on my flight BOM-KUL-REP and back. Had a 4.5 hour wait on the way there and 3 hours on the way back. Landed at 7am and the airport was strangely empty. Very easy to use airport but seems to have little to do if transiting for a few hours. Shops were okay - the basics available and the eating options seemed all right. Would rather use BKK or SIN to transit as there is more to do there but all in all KUL is a pleasant enough airport.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: P D Berryman
content: After transiting in KLIA2 twice this year - not many improvements have happened. I agree with the previous post adding that dust build up the odd paint job unfinished and markings on the escalators from the tradesman or builder's. The terminal has a lack of greenery plants would really make a difference to the ambience of the terminal. I'm sure as the airport budget improves so will the furnishings etc.. more seating travelators information and directional signs wouldn't go astray. The time it takes to walk to customs is a really long way and a bit like a labyrinth you have to go up to get down and then walk some more. I think they have the domestic docking gates at the wrong side. The international gates should be closer to customs and the retail district for better and faster access and efficiency for international and transiting passenger's. I'm sure this would encourage more passenger's to use the fabulous retail precinct when on a time schedule between flights. Domestic passenger's will generally have more time to transit opposed to international. KLIA2 is certainly ready for future passenger growth I love the idea of a shopping mall inside the airport accessible to everyone.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Kenneth Backhouse
content: New budget terminal at KUL. Service was excellent - can be a long walk to boarding gates so give yourself a bit more time. wide range of food outlets ranging from self-serve a la carte local choices and fastfood. We used both terminals and had no problem with either.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Kuhan Kandiah Chelvanathan
content: The airport terminal (KLIA 1) is in need of a refurbishment. The airport now caters to almost 50 million passengers a year and yet little is done to improve and enhance to the terminal experience. KLIA 1 caters for 25 million passengers yet the toilets and surroundings are below average. Maintenance levels and customer service staff at this airport needs a lot of improvement and could do with proper training and sustainability. Check in agents and outlet staff are abrupt if not rude. Overhyped for its services this airport needs a splashing new look and trained staff.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Ahmed Nash
content: I first went to this airport in 2010 and I thought it was a superb airport. However my recent visit proved the opposite. The quality and surrounding of the airport is getting worse. There are not as many seats for waiting passengers not to mention their bad condition (broken torn cushion). The desks where airport staff check tickets are also very old with scratches here and there. The information screens are sometimes confusing which codeshare airlines names are put together. A lot of stalls around the terminal are also irritating to the eyes.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Liam Moulton
content: I'm a frequent flier on both full service and budget airlines though I try to avoid the latter. A major disadvantage of going with a budget airline apart from the lack of onboard amenities and punctuality is the low- cost terminals or airports from which they fly. I therefore expected a bare and plastic terminal with next to no amenities when I was on my way to KLIA2 which is used exclusively by budget airlines. How wrong I was. In all my years of flying I have never been so pleasantly surprised with an airport. The duty free shops and various cafes and restaurants on offer was excellent and better than most full-service airports from which I have flown. Also the terminal was so clean. In fact based on this experience the only airports I would say are better than KLIA2 are Singapore Hong Kong and Amsterdam Schiphol though in fairness they are mainly for full-service airlines. How KLIA2 heaps shame on many full-service hubs like Beijing Manila Jakarta Paris Charles de Gaulle Shanghai Pudong and Heathrow. Also public transport links are excellent for both efficiency and value for money. My only criticisms of this airport are the lack of travellators in such a large terminal building which could pose problems if someone was in a rush and the fact I had to go through security twice once right after immigration and then again before I went to pier P to catch my flight to Jakarta. Nevertheless I will not think twice about using KLIA2 again and I assume that KLIA's main and satellite buildings must be impeccable as they cater to full-service airlines.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Williams
content: KLIA2 is the most annoying airport I've been to considering its brand new. Its clear from the ground up KLIA2 is riddled with incompetence and flaws in design and execution. On departure you have a long walk through a shopping mall then after passport control a you have a long walk before you reach your gate. No exaggeration that the walking seems to go on forever. With hardly any travelators younger or especially older travellers will struggle. The Skybridge. Its utterly pointless adding nothing apart from extending the length of time it takes to reach your gate! Only 1 travelator which looks like only a mere afterthought. KLIA2 has bottlenecks everywhere both on departure and on arrival it makes for a very long slow walk and frustrating experience! Sadly even the quality of workmanship is laughable the finish of the whole place looks cheap because materials are low cost and plus in only a 3 months are in need of maintenance. Avoid.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: A Stenholm
content: Am starting to hate this place. Where is the seating for transit passengers? Signage is below par toilets not great loads of ludicrous high end shops with no customers. A stupid confusing layout. The Japanese architect obviously hasn't a clue about circulation and passenger comfort. The design might have looked good on the back of a fag packet before he handed it down to his minions but it's all a load of unconsidered nonsense. The stupid jungle in the middle which was close should be cleared and given over to passenger amenities like at Singapore. Yes it has free wifi though is bit patchy and it has nice high ceilings. Big deal! Give me Singapore any day. Having to spend six hours here will certainly influence my next use of airline to come this way in the world.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Mike Whitehouse
content: Terminal 2. Whilst the terminal is still new (May 2014) and possibly experiencing teething problems it is annoying that we (a party of 6) used it last weekend the baggage belts has stopped working at check-in. The check-in clerk said that she much preferred the old terminal! It is also very annoying that having checked in online at some inconvenience the queues at 'baggage drop' were enormous whilst the check-in desk has no queue at all!

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Mukherjee
content: We transited KLIA2 flying Air Asia to and from Singapore on way to Kolkata. Its one big empty space really with nothing in there really barring a couple of F&B outlets selling bad coffee pharmacy/departmental stores a 'do not enter' smoking room (but lots of passengers inside anyway) and toilets. They don't seem to have thought this one out because they make you walk a lot then subject you to x-ray and security check twice (once downstairs and then upstairs) and you actually land at a place 50 meters away from where you started from in the first place - completely insane. What's so ironic was all coming in to KLIA2 from both ends the AirAsia magazine was going on about the retail and entertainment options available at KLIA2. Of course there might be a lot but only after you cross Malaysian immigration. Better than LCCT it well might be (in some time to come).

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: J Ahmad
content: Flew a domestic AirAsia flight from the spanking new KLIA2 in the evening. Took the ERL from KL Sentral and arrived at the airport just after half an hour avoiding the peak hour traffic. Once you step out of the train station you enter the gateway at KLIA2 complex. It's really a public shopping mall within the airport and there's many to do and eat. Walk two floors up and you enter the Main Terminal Building where the check-in kiosks and desks are located. Looks brilliant at first sight but then at peak hours you'd get a feel that there's just too much retail and food and beverages cramped into this area. Security was a breeze and was cleared within 5 minutes. Domestic airside however is a different story. Limited choices of food and beverages and even the available outlets are just far too expensive for the ordinary traveller (bare in mind this is a low cost carrier terminal where majority of passengers would be budget customers). Do have something to eat before going airside if you're early for your flight. Our gate was at the west end of the terminal where it is really quiet and a good place to take a quick nap. There's a smoking lounge available and it didn't feel uncomfortable at all. Although considered one of the nearest gates it took me a good 15 mins walking to get there. Spare some time on this. I advise the elderly or the disabled to get assistance on getting to your gate. Overall experience at the airport was good. Much better than the previous LCCT. This terminal is well integrated and way more comfortable. The terminal can match the quality of the KLIA1. However after just over a month of operations there are already signs of deterioration missing screws from FIDS stands damaged signs paint of walls fading etc. are just a few examples. It would be a shame if this RM4 billion facility can't live up to its price tag due to poor maintenance.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Marcus Boehm
content: KLIA2: Not enough signage. I followed the crowd thankfully they knew where they were going. Long walks required. Unremarkable shopping.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: M Boehm
content: Staff pleasant poor range of food outlets. Little entertainment while waiting.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Edzhar Razali
content: A lots of negative comments actually referred to LCCT (belongs to Air Asia) but KLIA is one of the best airports in the world easy access friendly ground staff very helpful. Variety of restaurants and cafes though the price is quite expensive for locals but for international visitors is quite ok. Queue at the immigrations is quite fast and it goes with the baggage claim too. Overall it was a nice airport.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: B Vincent
content: I transited KLIA2 twice in the last 2 weeks so I can only comment on airside facilities. While KLIA is all stainless steel and glass KLIA2 is more white paint and glass. It's set up for much better comfort than the old LCCT terminal but unfortunately it's just not ready yet - there are very few useful facilities for transit passengers at the moment food options in the transit area are limited to MacDonalds and Gloria Jeans no bar no massage almost no ATMs limited duty free there are a couple of lounges but one shuts long before the last flight and the other is very remote and has no showers. Long walks to and from the gates with few travelators. Wrongly the toilets are already smelly and I encountered a broken-in-half toilet seat. Sure it's early days but I do wonder if it will improve from here or continue to slide.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: D Egginton
content: Arrived on time from Denpasar and caught the aerotrain to immigration and the baggage hall.No ques either arriving or departing for immigration. Easy check in at the Malaysian desks. Baggage arrived around 10 mins and easy sign posting for the KL express train into the City. Departing is another story. Most airports now seem to prefer high end duty free shops to passenger comfort. I caught the aero train to the other terminal as this has more choice of places to eat etc. The toilets were not clean at all and you could tell people had been smoking in them. Saw many passengers looking for customer assistance and if there was any they hid well.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Bwen Yin
content: A friend of mine landed from a flight from Abu Dhabi at 2200hrs local time. Aerotrain connecting the satellite terminal to the main terminal was down and there were no signages as to where to connect ourselves to the main terminal to clear immigration and baggage claims. Instead it was by word of mouth from the other passengers that the terminal buses were to ferry us across. To our dismay they only had 2 serviceable buses. And there was a mock of passengers unable to alight them as they were packed full. Even the bus doors were unable to close. As impatience grew in lieu of passengers rushing for their connecting flight and more poured in my friend was stuck there for more than 45 mins. There were no airport authorities at sight. Passengers at the bus stop was already pouring into the tarmac which dwells the question of airport security? Clearly this shows no part in monitoring security for such an incident and the airport authorities were clearly incapable of manning such a scenario. There were times the aerotrain was down and thus this may not be the first time they have to endure such a challenge. When the train was serviceable after 50 mins the long queue took up. But nobody inform some poor lads at the bus stop area that the terminal bus service was terminated! And the baggage collection had no signage on where / which carousel to collect from.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: L Sharp
content: I was in the Low cost terminal with AirAsia and it was my worst airport terminal in the world. Nothing to do in the airport hardly any food options.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: J Croozin
content: KLIA2. Obviously rushed into service after the schedule delays and not properly cleaned post construction. A very inefficient use of space and as usual the focus is on retail not passenger comfort and amenity. There were some long narrow ramps after the aerobridge which should be at least a meter wider. I had to change levels about 5 times and walk nearly a kilometre from the gate to immigration; very poor design. Someone sack the architect of this place. Signage needs improving with lots of A4 paper signs pasted to cover the shortcomings but since the place is only a week old I'll give them the benefit of doubt and assume they will fix this. Baggage reclaim was slow but again this airport is still in the teething stage so it should improve. The huge plus over the old terrible LCCT is that you can catch the KLIA express into Sentral (via KLIA) and not have to deal with the lousy taxi service or schlep in a poor old bus to KLIA to catch the train. This is a huge plus for regular users. I was arriving and have yet to use this place to depart but the F&B outlets seemed plentiful and it's almost like a shopping centre if you feel the need to buy some new shoes just before your flight. All in all a big improvement over the abysmal LCCT but the layout and design is disappointing.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: J Croozin
content: I am a frequent user of KLIA. The airport is OK but could be a whole lot better. The usual temptation for airports to prioritise income from rents over the smooth movement of passengers has prevailed. Many of the corridors in the satellite terminal have become narrow passageways because shops have been plonked in the middle of them. I'm sure the designers didn't intend it this way and it really grates on me that space and convenience for the users is sacrificed at the altar of the almighty ringgit. Add to this the propensity for people to shuffle three abreast in these narrow spaces and you have a number of unnecessary choke points. F&B outlets are plentiful but expensive and the airline lounges are generally pretty average. There are few places to sit in the terminal unless you're spending money (by design?) and the sanitation in the restrooms is not great although miles ahead of the disgraceful LCCT (thankfully now superseded by KLIA2) Taxi services like elsewhere in Malaysia are terrible and the access roads in the arrivals and departure areas are chaos with double parking in no standing zones the norm. Use the KLIA express train and forget the taxis.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Mickael Chia
content: KLIA2 on opening day. Feared the worst. Booked shuttle from hotel to make sure I got there right. Arrived early. Everything went fine. Temporary helpers every where to assist. Check-in was smooth. Immigration Q only 8 pax long. Kudos to AirAsia and MAHB. However some improvements possible. Have small trolleys airside. Signage at more locations. Don't like the non-intuitive layout too much walking unclear where-to next - but these too late to change.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: B Bartlett
content: Air Asia terminal is filthy. There is one toilet block that has thousands of people through it daily. The filth and smell is unbelievable. Ladies exiting the toilets had their mouth covered. Air Asia get your act together and clean the place up. The terminal is also in a poor state and dirty. The cleaners were standing around talking and doing nothing. The food is terrible as well. I have travelled many airports and this is the worst.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Joey Isaac
content: Great surrounding of the airport the atmosphere is relaxing. Airport staff were so friendly. Directions sign inside the terminal is near-perfect. Toilet cleanliness is ok but can be better. Waiting seat inside the terminal should be added more now seems not enough especially during peak time. Lots of restaurants to be chosen. Waiting time at check in counter is exceptional. Overall this airport is outstanding.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Hijaz Hasnam
content: The wide open spaces and the high ceilings are both a psychological relief after a long a flight and an architectural wonder. The choices are shops are decent. The choices of cafes and restaurants are decent but somehow scattered around the airport. The food court is a bit hidden and mostly visited by airport staff looking for a cheap meal. Toilets are OK cleanliness of them toilets should be better. Wifi is OK a few computer terminals would be greatly appreciated. What I find exasperating is that the waiting area at the piers are closed until 30 minutes or so before the flight. The departure area also lacks seats despite ample space.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: T Sworn
content: LCCT is a miserable dirty worn out and disorganised place. There is no flow of process and people wander around not knowing. The immigration is slow the queues are long. Even Starbucks is dirty and old. This airport brings shame to Malaysia. The sooner it closes the better.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Robert Jan van Pelt
content: Probably due to the recent dramatic events with MH370 security checks have doubled at KLIA. Problem is that there isn't any more staff so many empty counters at immigration. We are queuing at the premier lane and it will probably take us 45 mins to clear immigration just in time to board the flight. We might have been in serious trouble if we would have had to use the regular immigration counters. So it's certainly wise to allow yourself 1 hour to pass immigration at KLIA now. it's a pity as facilities at KLIA are nice but you'll probably have no time left for coffee or shopping.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Hijaz Kamal Hasnan
content: Used the bus service to KLIA which was cheap and took 40 minutes. The bus stop at KLIA was OK no problems sadly the escalator to the next level was not functioning. Some signs have flickering lights. As usual the steely and grey and cavernous KLIA was reassuring there were not many seats. KLIA does have alot of space for more comfortable seating areas learn from Changi. The shops seem inviting enough to warrant some window shopping there is a food court with cheap food but its is so hidden I doubt many first timers at KLIA know its there. Despite having used this airport frequently never seem to know where the smoking area is. Checking in was ok. Immigration was a breeze was one hour early for the flight so went to the gate what I didn't like is that the waiting area is closed until 30 minutes before the flight. Many passengers came early and there were not enough seats. Overall the facilities of KLIA are pretty good but the management and customer service is non existent.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: O Dominic
content: I'm hoping all the bad reviews are for the LCCT because surely the main terminal is one of the better ones in SE Asia. Even with extra security and immigration checks due to MH370 all queues moved quickly and the staff were very friendly. Even the gate security checks although poorly designed like most airports were still pretty painless. Plenty of facilities and easy to get around. Biggest gripe was that the airport's free wifi seemed to not be working properly although I was able to use the free wifi offered by a cafe.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Aizu Dean
content: I use the airport just because my family lives in Malaysia but the extreme inefficiencies in the usage of space and overkilling hand baggage checks really gets on my nerve every time. Somebody might've made some millions selling those metal sensors for each available gate but on the contrary it really shows how fragile the security system can be between custom clearance and the gates. How are we the passengers to feel safe with all these extra checks? Moreover even if it is necessary all the seats at the gates are inside the glass barriers. I really don't understand why these gallery of seats are only for show and we the passengers need to stand (or sit on the floor for some) waiting for the gates to be opened and be directly instructed to board the plane. This is clearly a management problem.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Debra Briggs
content: LCCT. This airport is awful. There appears to be only one toilet facility and this is extremely busy and filthy. No toilet paper so ladies make sure you have tissues with you. Food area is poor and seating very uncomfortable. We arrived from Thailand with AirAsia and had to wait over an hour to get through the one and only scanner to enter the airport. After enduring a 5 hour wait we purchased 2 bottles of water from one of the shops in the terminal. Travellers who are leaving from T14 beware you are not allowed to take the water through. Even though we had just purchased it the water was confiscated and thrown in the bin. A long walk across the hot smoggy airport to reach our plane. Yes I understand that this is the low cost option however I found this to be the dirtiest and most unfriendly airport that I have ever had to use.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Stephanie Mckinley
content: Arrived into KLIA at 3 am from Sydney. We had a 6 hour stop over on way to HK. KLIA is a totally different set up. Very spread out for shops and eateries. This really didn't bother me as such but there doesn't seem to be enough seating for passengers. I did like the free internet access and the chairs set up around the televisions so passengers could nap. I found retail terminal staff rude and as much as I'm an upbeat person and really value our service industry staff I was disappointed by seemingly everyone's attitude in thus airport. The cleanliness is an entirely different story. I was appalled at the state of the toilets they were below human standards of sanitation. We visited several toilet blocks and found them all similar. Shape up KLIA the Western Tourist has demands and simple hygiene should be an absolute given a lot of other International airports are meeting their guests needs. Follow suit. I won't be visiting again and therefor that reflects on your national carrier which I found very good.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: M Lau
content: For some reasons I find KLIA quite pleasant for weary passengers like myself. It has the comfortable ambience and its high ceiling really added to the whole relaxing atmosphere. I like the free Wifi which is not provided in other major airports in Australia. Eateries are pretty standard in comparison with other major international airports although I am finding the price a little expensive for Malaysians. Yes it does not have the reputation of Singapore Changi but it is after all a very good airport.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Marina Kuzmin
content: Took me 1.5 hours to get to transit area. There were no lines it was such a mess and after an hour staff tried to organize. Toilets always packed with people and are dirty could not find much to eat. Never again!

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: D Wilsson
content: The LCCT is an absolute disgrace. It is nothing more than a cattle yard with the dirtiest toilets ever and smug looking staff who I assume are the cleaners standing doing nothing about it. The food was terrible - could not even eat it and choices below standard for an international airport. The staff were unhelpful rude and unprofessional. Low cost travel should not mean being treated so disrespectfully. For this reason I will not fly AirAsia again nor any airline that transits in KL. The over the top security and scanning is unbelievable for a transit lounge and being herded into a glass enclosure with no facilities at all an hour prior to departure is no fun especially when the flight is delayed. Disgraceful place.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: John Piken
content: LCCT terminal. By far in any standards the worst airport terminal in the world. Signage is non existent and after landing you walk around the airport terminal outside beside airplanes so to get in into the terminal. The most disrespectful treatment of passengers starts here queues to immigration are mind-blowing. Took 2 hours to get through and once you reach the counter it takes 20 seconds to get a stamp this makes you wonder what is taking the time? Could be that one immigration booth is constantly chit chatting with each other or another one having lunch during work time. Also there were only half of the booths open. No aircon so with 1000 passengers and 2 hrs you will feel dirty as ever upon arrival to Kuala Lumpur. After immigration finding a taxi or bus is a joke again no sign. No taxi will run you on meter if you are tourist adding insult even more. This terminal is a joke to mankind and an example of how low one can go.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: N Althaus
content: LCCT. I would have to say that this would have to be the worst airline terminal that I have ever used. On arrival from Penang to KL the signage and directions were non existent to the point where half of the passengers on a local flight ended up in International Arrivals instead of Domestic Arrivals. A group of us were trying to get directions on how to get back to domestic and the ground staff were all but useless - usual advice received was just keep walking. The trouble was we did not even know if we were headed in the right direction. After finally sorting ourselves out I then proceeded to International Departures. I have to say that this terminal does not have one redeeming feature. I had a 4 hour wait - the food choices were poor and I asked if there was food once I checked through Customs and Immigration and was told no - so had something and then proceeded through Customs etc and then found that there were places to eat inside. This terminal is enough to put me off flying Low Cost Carriers into KL.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: C Lim
content: Dirty and wet toilets. Not enough luggage trolleys at baggage carousel. Extremely poor airport limousine service. Not friendly and informative staff. Extremely slow baggage handling system. Long check-in queues.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Lee Cheng Jun
content: Flown to KLIA recently and I was utterly disappointed by what they have to offer me. Firstly the aerotrain has no announcement that the doors are closing or where are we heading it just zooms off. The terminal was not very crowded when I first arrived and the airport staff are not that friendly and welcoming. There was a long queue to get the tickets on the KLIA Express and in my opinion they should get more staff to work on the sales of the KLIA Express tickets. Once again not much to complain about the arriving journey at KLIA. The departing journey from KLIA was a horrible journey. Check in was slow even though I had checked in online but forgotten to print my boarding pass which will let me bypass immigration and go straight to the gate. Secondly I was quite unlucky to get a queue with only 1 immigration officer while others have two I have spent a total of 30 minutes just to get through the immigration which is a lot compared to other international airports. I was also almost late for my flight. The immigration officers had grumpy looks on their faces. The terminal is not well lit and in my opinion they have chosen the wrong lighting colours. The KLIA Express trains are showing their age and have water dripping from the ceilings. The route from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur has a wide range of transport options. I may not fly to Kuala Lumpur from Singapore again as KLIA has gave me a very negative experience.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Fakhrul Ashik
content: It was a wonderful airport. I felt like I was the middle of tropical forest because of the green effect surrounding the airport. The design of the roof is great. KLIA is so worth it. KLIA2 is even more because although it's just a low-cost terminal I feel like I am in an international airport. Very clean. The officers are friendly with tourists. The police officers could communicate with us.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Rohit Thukral
content: I flew Air Asia recently via KL and was in transit for 5 hours - an experience I will not repeat. To be fair the airline has its own terminal so this review relates to that one. The Air Asia terminal has no transit facilities - so you need to enter Malaysia and then exit via Immigration. So be sure you have a visa if you need one. You can only check in for your continuing flight about 2 hours before departure and there are few facilities available before you get to the departure gates (after immigration). There are very few chairs and the crowds are huge so don't expect to find a place to sit. The air conditioning hardly works and KL is a hot tropical city. Its less comfortable than most Greyhound bus stops in the US in fact its the worst air terminal I have ever had to go through. Availability of food or drink in the check-in area is very limited. Bathrooms are dirty and several facilities are broken. This is an awful terminal in almost every respect - so I won't go on and on. Don't transit through this airport if you can help it and avoid flying Air Asia.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Alpana Keertikar
content: We travelled by Air Asia from Kansai to Singapore on 12th/13th Oct and had a transit in KL LCCT. If there is a worse airport than KL LCCT I have yet to see it. Filthy toilets dirty seats forget aerobridge not even a shuttle to and from airplane lazy staff at immigration and overpriced shops. After a wonderful Japan trip this was a nightmare. Really surprised how the domestic travelers don't take their airport authority to task. We are never again going to take any airline which has a stopover at KL LCCT.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Sin
content: Since around late August or early September 2013 Malaysian Airlines has adopted the policy of having all international check-in happen at row C at the KLIA. What it does is cause a huge line to form from row C right through to row G. This happens from between 06.50hrs to about 08.30hrs every morning. Travellers become very agitated and very fearful of missing their flights because of the long queues. Most importantly there are no Malaysia Airlines staff to help explain or assist passengers who are confused by this new system. Thick skinned clients cut queues and no Malaysian Airlines staff are there to help pacify the crowds. This is a very bad experience for any first time passenger with Malaysian Airlines or KLIA. Whilst one can understand the cost saving that happens with consolidating to only one row for check in of all international passengers the disinformation or rather the non existence of Malaysia Airlines staff to help soothe the nerves of the passengers is most unprofessional and shows a complete lack of customer service by the airline. It also makes the airport experience start on a very tense note. I have flown this airline for over 26 years now and this is a low point in the airline's airport check in experience. I do hope that Malaysia Airlines will at least put staff to help manage the long queue at row C and soothe passengers' nerves.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: S Amaya
content: KLIA: Quick passport clearance and baggage claim reasonably clean airport big with a lot to do if you are transiting. LCCT Crowded nowhere to sit dirty (the toilets) not much to do if in transit. But you get what you pay for.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: H Yaacob
content: KLIA used to feel like a modern airport. Unfortunately the airport has been under-maintained and it's beginning to show it's age. First up the Aerotrain system had no announcements. Several monitors next to the platform were dead. Trains looked old and tired. This was not the case before. It seems as if they've not bothered to repair the PA system. There were no queues at immigration but the area has poor and illogical signage. They gave warnings on Taxi touts before the immigration counters without little information on Foreign or Malaysian passport lines until we got to the counters. There were no lines and all counters were open so that they've improved the well-known KLIA passport lines. Then you're squeezed into a small hallway with small monitors detailing the carousels assigned. Upon exit booths for rental cars and airport taxis are cluttered and strewn about. The airport taxi counter has long lines forming blocking the exit. When you exit surprisingly there are other taxi booths all empty. On the way back we were assigned the last check in row which was did not have enough space to accommodate the crowds. Not to mention the oversized check-in portal was also located there creating a huge bottleneck. There were 3 flights being checked in at the same time for our row. We were shoved around because the airport staff needed to put up queue barriers to check in an Oman Air flight at the counters next to ours when there was a line already forming for that flight. They took their own time. Shops are worthless because they're either too expensive or are just uninteresting. Eating places haven't changed since three years ago and were terribly disappointing. Seating is terribly inadequate. Several seats were dirty and rusty and not to mention had come lose meaning that they were not in a straight line and were strewn about. Shops are disorganized and are cluttered around resulting in inefficient floor use and various bottlenecks. Trash cans are overflowing and some had their lids broken resulting in trash on the floor. Not a good experience. Departing and Arriving from SIN (a very well kept airport) you can definitely see the difference ironic because we departed from SIN T1 which is at least a decade older than KLIA. Goes to show KLIA's management needs to buck up.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: G Marsh
content: Nice bright if somewhat confusing. Little help from signage and totally rude and disgraceful attitude of the person on the transfer information desk. Had I been a manager there I would have dismissed the young lady instantly due to her rude and unhelpful manner. A smile does not cost anything. The shops are disorganised and all over the place. I did not think it was a very user friendly airport at all. The smoking room is rank and filthy. The toilets were just acceptable. It looks a nice new terminal but some of the staff need some customer skill training. Very disappointed with this airport. The inter terminal transit train is not sign-posted very well Although the general direction is indicated it does not tell you that it is on a lower floor and how to get there.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: A McNicol
content: LCCT review only. This facility is a disgrace to Malaysia that is otherwise a joy to visit. Over two hours in the immigration queue on a Saturday afternoon with minimal air-conditioning. Then another queue at the taxi counter and a massive walk past the domestic terminal to the almost unsigned and disorganized taxi rank. On departure the terminal is average nothing notable but it functions acceptably and hence the overall fair rating. This was so bad that I will reconsider using a carrier that lands at the LCCT. A real pity because the main KLIA is a lovely airport facility nowhere else in Asia does "low cost" mean "appalling".

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Azlan Hashim
content: There was a long queue at the online drop off luggage area for my flight to Istanbul on 21st August. However those check-in agents were able to clear the queue pretty quickly. The gentleman at the counter was polite and helpful. Most of the duty free outlets were closed by midnight but there were several of them were willing to extend for the last minute customer. In general the airport is clean and majority of the staff were friendly. Again those MH staff at the departure gate were helpful and polite when handling the busy flight that evening.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: C Kupper
content: Modern facilities that do not always work. Staff were unfriendly. Proof that a "new" building does not guarantee a good airport. On top the generous layout of the airport is clogged with medium range shops and outlets. Sad.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Y Ren
content: LCCT. It was my worst airport experience by far. First time flying AirAsia but probably the last time. It was nightmare. The whole terminal was chaotic. It felt and smelt like a fish market. Overcrowded disorganised and not enough signs. You need to go through scanning for your luggage first then check in counters. It was so disorganised. Nothing at waiting area not enough seats and dining options and very dirty. Then you will have a long march to the aircraft. Landing experience is not much better. First long march with no signs. Once you are outside the shed another chaotic parking and pick up experience. Our hotel car could not find us and did couple of laps around the airport we had to drag our luggage from one line to another. I would not recommend LCCT to anybody.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Adree Farhan bin Adam
content: Nice airport design and interior. Very clean. Fast check in.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Mark Ah Yee
content: KLIA works very well for entry and exit. I found it very easy to get through after landing everything well marked and plenty of signs the skytrain to main terminal was very efficient and the hook up to the KLIA Express and 25 minutes into central KL was brilliant. Try doing this at Sydney or Melbourne!

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Patrick Lee
content: Huge airport with great facilities. The toilets is clean and the airport staff are nice. Look forward to visit KLIA again in future.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: E Provan
content: LCCT: Very basic airport. Immigration is pretty slow and isn't very clean. Although not bad for a budget terminal.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Simon Chinn
content: LCCT: Miserable facilities grossly over subscribed passenger numbers this airport is the definition of cattle class travel. You pay little you receive little. Travel via KLIA if possible.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Gerry Clarke
content: Too many designer shops and expensive restaurants. It really says something when burger king is the only place with people in it. And as it's the only reasonably priced place to eat the queues were crazy. Also you have to walk to the gate to find a decent amount of seating. Not impressed with the airport facilities at all.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Halfdan Faber
content: I arrived 8 hours before departure only to find out that you can only check in for international flights 3 hours before departure. The public departure area is very crowded and with few seats. It looks like the secure area is almost empty. The airport management must be out of their minds; what a waste of facility and shopping space/time to have 60% prevented to go past security.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Chin Yee Meng
content: Visited on 18 June afternoon and returned on 21 June. From check-in until immigration no queue at all. All going very smoothly. Boarding gate at G8 which means no need to take a aerotrain to the satellite terminal. The entire atmosphere were quiet and not many people at that times. Back on 21 June arrived at gate G10 the entire terminal was very quiet. Very impressed with the cleanliness and free wifi.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: D Brown
content: Efficient airport our flight outbound was delayed and we had only 45 minutes to transfer but both passengers and baggage made it. We were transferring Intl to Intl - cannot comment on Intl - domestic time scales. 4 Hours to kill on return found to be very expensive in duty free shopping. Used one of the lounges which was very hot and filled with screaming children - so ended up back in the terminal to try and find a quiet spot. Aircraft loading and gates are quick and efficient.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: John Chai
content: KLIA is a good place to transit in very clear signage and the Aerotrain was fast and efficient to transport you between the satellite terminal and main terminal. Terminal and boarding gates were clean but KLIA definitely has to improve on its toilets. Toilets need to be of similar standard like Changi because the toilets in KLIA looked very 2 star and not 4 star. But still usable. Overall a very good place to transit in ambience and atmosphere very similar to Changi with free Internet.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Y Wong
content: Disappointed with KLIA. Had to wait 3 hours for transit at KLIA and was disappointed by the poor service shopping and restaurant choices available. We had to take the aerotrain to the satellite terminal to look for more choices. Restaurants were over-priced and when we finally settled on a noodle restaurant it took 30 minutes for 2 bowls of curry noodles to be served because they forgot our orders. Not a word of apology too. Airport staff were sitting down chatting playing with phones and occupying seats on the aerotrain while passengers with children had to stand. Toilet seats and floor were wet while the cleaning staff was standing at the entrance eyeing people entering and leaving the toilets. Nobody greeted or acknowledged our presence when we enter or leave a store. It's my first time transiting at this airport and if given a choice I would rather not use it again.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Geophadon Chin
content: Brilliant airport magnificent architecture good walking distance clean toilets good security and staff service.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: I Milono
content: KLIA is a rather odd airport. I prefer say it's like 2 different airports because the comparison between the 2 couldn't be bigger: the satellite terminal the main one where major airlines (i.e non low-cost ones) land is huge modern comfortable and has free automated train going among terminals and has express train directly to the city. The other one called Low Cost Carrier Terminal as the name indicates is where the low-cost airlines (mostly Air Asia) land. Unfortunately it is 'blessed' with the namesake as if it is of low-cost quality: Overcrowded passengers in the bland-looking waiting room long walk between the waiting lounge and the plane on the hot tarmac and no direct train connection whatsoever whether to the city and the satellite terminal (you can take the train to the city but have to use airport bus to the nearest train station). The biggest twist is LCCT is located next to the satellite but to travel between them by bus it takes 20 minutes or more. Restaurants are plentiful (and cheap enough). I'm impressed with the satellite terminal building and it somehow deserves a place for one of the best airport in Asia. The overcrowded LCCT is part of KLIA too and it should be considered to rate the airport as a whole. That being said with the LCCT factor the good rating of KLIA decreases pretty significantly. I even wonder why KLIA still applies the low-cost airline separation policy as Singapore had abandoned such policy (now all is integrated at Changi) and in other big airports like HKG and ICH low cost airlines is never treated as that of KLIA (means that by boarding low cost airlines should not prevent you from enjoying airport luxuries enjoyed by regular airlines' passengers). Let's hope that the new terminal KLIA2 which is said will open soon and replaces LCCT will make up for this.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Noel Desalisa
content: Malaysia Airlines adjusted my waiting time in KL airport by almost 10 hrs from my original booking (originally 14 hours but due to their adjustment I waited for 23 hours). Unfortunately there were no facilities for such a long waiting time.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: K Chye
content: Simple efficient terminal for mainline carriers (not AirAsia 'cowshed') but expansion works due completion later this year with AirAsia Terminal 2 opening. Current Terminal 1 has seen some minor improvement too with more food and shopping outlets and the train station downstairs has just been expanded.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: T K Hill
content: Very nice airport: clean good signage and spacious. Lots of shops and eating opportunities. Lots of security around. All were helpful and gracious. At no time did I feel like a criminal as I often do in the hands of the TSA back in the US. The buy in lounge is reasonably priced and the complementary massage was a real treat. One of the world's better airports.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Andrew Ford
content: Easy to use transit well sign posted food options were good however if you like a few beers before you fly take plenty of money with you - over priced! Pay for drinks as you go as I sat there I saw 2 groups get charged for drinks they said they didn't have.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Kevin Barrance
content: Brilliant airport. So clean quiet and efficient. Staff friendly and helpful. Makes travelling a joy not a chore.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Indranil Chakrabarty
content: KLIA is an excellent Airport however arriving at 5 in the morning I found few shops open and the terminal wearing a deserted look. The arrival area is like a shopping mall. You deplane and walk into a mall. The monorail to the immigration building is a nice setup immigration area clean but drab. Staff at customs and immigration are courteous but dour. Departure at 5pm was the exact opposite. Lively and well equipped the airport wore a modern look. The shops in the departure area are well stocked and everything looks spotlessly clean. The airport is never crowded and has a clean crisp and spacious feel. Prices are reasonable. The food court is large with a selection of Malay Asian Chinese Indian and the regular fast food outlets. Unlike some airports the staff are only too happy to help. This airport works better than some modern looking ports in the region. I highly recommend KLIA as an excellent transit point.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: A Syed
content: I always visited this airport very frequently as I used to fly with Malaysia Airlines before they discontinued their services to Pakistan and I always seemed to have encountered changes within this airport. First off some of my visits have been absolutely terrific with no problems at all. However some visits have been disastrous such as not allowing my son's formula milk to be carried with me after customs claiming to have CFC's. My last visit to this airport was also disastrous as we were the last passengers to board MAS from Pakistan and we had an 8 hour stopover at KLIA. Didn't offer us any accommodation whatsoever and staff did not care. These occurrences has tarnished my views of this airport.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: John Grint
content: Excellent airport. Always so clean and quiet wouldn't mind getting delayed here but that doesn't happen very often here well not to me anyway. MH staff superb.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Mike Jacques
content: Vastly improved since my last visit with so many options for drinking and eating that it is impossible not to find what you are looking for. I found the staff to be very helpful so much so that on a ticket enquiry where my airline had made a mistake with my booking every effort was made to get a satisfactory result despite the fact that I was in transit. Highly recommended.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: C Tan
content: I was impressed with the fantastic check in experience. It was done in less than 5 minutes and the boarding was smooth.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: S Sebastian
content: I travelled on 19th January 2013. KLIA is far better than LCCT. Check-in was efficient and easy. The skytrain was good too. Overall the terminal is very clean and spacious. However there are a few issues/problems: The toilets/bathrooms are not clearly marked on the map. The lifts to the mezzanine level are too few and far away from the gates. Due to poor lift access the food outlets are difficult to access. The pricing of the food (compared to normal KL pricing of food) is expensive. I don't understand why there are 2 security scans. The first is simple and quick (no taking out laptops and jackets etc.) but the second is more thorough (take out laptops etc). They airport staff should warn passengers about this. Security/airport staff at the security check were not helpful and attentive. I had to wait some time for the security staff to take the box I used to scan my laptop. Once at the gate there is no clear signage clearly stating which one is the boarding gate. I say this because none of the screens in front of the 3 gates told which one is our boarding gate.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Laurence Wheeler
content: Flew through KL 3 times this month both in and out and as a transfer. I was very satisfied with all journeys.. The airport is spacious friendly and reasonably priced. The transfer arrangements are especially well sign- posted and easy. Good retail outlets but plenty of places to sit and wait both landside and airside. The whole place is similar to London Heathrow terminal 5 but with much better customer experience.

title: KLIA Kuala Lumpur Airport customer review
author: Melissa Tan
