content: Having checked in at Edinburgh and onwards from LCY-Faro we bought water. Unfortunately it would appear that the security at LCY don't trust the people at EDI to do a proper security check as we had to do it all over again and much to the amusement of the security staff discard the water. We also got absolutely soaked in a torrential downpour there being no shelter between aircraft and gate again much to the amusement of the ground staff. A great way to start a journey - soaked to the skin. Then we had to endure a 1 hr delay because standby pax bags had been loaded prematurely and had to be manually recovered when there was no room on the aircraft for the pax. That's why they are called standby! We weren't there long enough to comment on queuing cleanliness and facilities as we merely walked in a very large circuit and eventually reboarded the aircraft we had arrived on. We rate them poor as we have to say something.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: B Smith
content: In and out of LCY last month. Passport check something of a lottery - if a couple of flights come in together you'll be there a while as UK Border Agency don't seem to work to demand. Security outbound rather more friendly this time round than on previous occasions - possibly as some kind of audit appeared to be going on!

title: London City Airport customer review
author: D Silverstone
content: It's small which meant a quick trip through check-in and security for me but little in the way of available services. Also a long walk to the gate for such a small airport - some gates are very close to the entry but others are a bit of a hike. All in all a good small airport with excellent connections on the continent.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Sebastiaan de Groot
content: A very attractive airport due to the small size and closest to London. Excellent fast service for check-in. The distances are very small on the airport. Also the trains are close by (less than 5 minutes walk from passport control which is only a couple of minutes from the gate). Check in is possible up to 20 minutes prior to departure.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: S Smith
content: LCY to Antwerp and back this week. Substantial improvement over the last month - extra capacity on security meant I was airside in a matter of minutes. Coming back baggage was on the belt when we got there. Even UK Border agency have shown some progress in separating EU from non EU passengers which speeded things up however half the desks were still unmanned. I suppose that's the public sector for you.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Rob Boyce
content: Arrived on delayed flight from Frankfurt very quickly through passport control with four positions open. Luggage also quickly delivered and outside the airport within twelve minutes of touching down.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: W Howell
content: For me very convenient but how the service has declined. Long lines for security with staff who are disinterested. What is the point of a 10 minute check-in when security takes 30 minutes. Arrival not much better as Border Agency staff always seem surprised that an aircraft has arrived. Departure lounge much improved but do not expect a meal before 12.30 on Sunday. The restaurants are not open!

title: London City Airport customer review
author: S Smith
content: Arrived at LCY from Antwerp. Long (and I mean long!) queue at immigration due once again only 3 of 6 desks being manned. When coupled with the increasing chaos at departures I'm increasingly looking to avoid LCY and use Gatwick instead.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Philip Keating
content: I only arrived at this airport. The connection with the Dockland Railway was good. The best bit for me was the arriving as we flew over the Tower of London and O2 Arena you have a spectacular view of London which you do not get at Heathrow

title: London City Airport customer review
author: C Stephenson
content: Second visit to LCY this year and after the horrendous queuing last time I made sure that we arrived well in advance of check-in time. But I guess that it was a much less busy time of day (early afternoon) as there were no queues and we breezed through security. This left quite a long time sitting in the departure lounge which is a pleasant place with a small number of shops. Anticipating problems we'd eaten before check-in so the restaurants were of little use. If you're not subjected to excessive queuing the airport is very good.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Miles Canne
content: City airport seems to be outgrowing itself. No problems at bag drop but queue for security snakes all round the place and into one of the landside restaurants. And limited airside seating and facilities for the number of passengers using the airport at peak times. Very courteous security staff. Comfortable gate lounges.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: J Kemp
content: This airport has completely gone down the pan. Queues for security clearance snake around the check-in area and just finding the starting point is a challenge. Airport staff mill around the snake dancing passengers shouting out the destinations of flights which are about to depart. Once a flight is flagged as "boarding" on the monitor passengers are permitted to step out of the queue and head directly upstairs for screening - what's the use of arriving ahead of time and queuing up knowing that you'll be able to jump the crowd when your flight is called. Once through a security clearance which is a total circus passengers are offered a free chocolate bar as a peace offering - really? The stress level of passengers are off the charts by the time they get through the most annoying queuing system on the planet and trying to placate them with candy as one would with children is absolutely idiotic if not insulting. I am sure passengers would prefer to find the City Airport that used to exist sans le chocolat rather than the carnival it has become.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Simon Smith
content: LCY to ANR. Horrendous queues for security back to the escalator although to be fair they did keep moving. Took about 30 mins from check in. They were trying to bring forward people with departing flights although this really just was an airport person standing in the corner shouting. My mood was partly improved by the free chocolate bars and coffee vouchers handed out. Departed gate 1 this has seen much better days.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Ross Clark
content: LCY-EDI on AF 3rd February. At 1600 no problems at all with queuing; at 1700 still seats available in the main lounge. Security was ten minutes and could have been less. The airport's website is now acknowledging that they have problems here; they are now a victim of their own success. The new gates 21-24 have far more space while you have the last wait for your flight than what the older gates do.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Paul Bews
content: Queues on 28th January 17.00-19.00 Horrendous! Just made my flight. Was the same the previous week. Shall be seeking alternatives if this continues.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: L O'Connell
content: The queues at London City were beyond ridiculous today no idea what was going on. It took almost an hour to get through security and that was only because we were allowed through more quickly once our flight got to final call. The staff helping with the queues were strict (quite rightly) about people trying to skip though. The security staff were poor I have never had a bag search like it rifling through my paperwork page-by-page and inspecting my clothes in quite a humiliating way. I'm all for enhanced security but this is not the way to do it.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: C Stephenson
content: I was lucky at this airport when I arrived for a flight to the Isle of Man. Lucky because I'd decided to turn up early (2 hours before departure) so that I'd have time to get a meal before departure. If I'd left it any later I'd have been queuing for Departures for more than the 55 minutes it took me and wouldn't even have had time for a quick snack. Clearly the airport is overwhelmed with the number of flights leaving on a Tuesday evening in January. Although staff were employed to help move the queue along and ensure that people who were on a final call were moved to the front the queue snaked up and down the upper floor then down the steps and into the check-in area (I couldn't see the end of the queue as it was growing all the time). Most people seemed to be flying to European destinations and were bemused by the chaos. Airport staff admitted that it was sheer number of passengers causing the problem which tells me that there is something basic wrong with this airport. It should be able to cope with all scheduled flights not just those at less busy times.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: David Merritt
content: A great airport with investment in making it work well all of the time. Almost every visit something has changed as they seek to use every square foot to it's best use. Best reached by public transport as car parking costs lots. Arrive early for morning departures and enjoy a great breakfast.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: S Smith
content: LCY to Antwerp return. Very overrated experience. Long queues at security in a small claustrophobic area. Flight was called to gate 2B but staff had omitted to change the previous flight (Nantes) causing confusion. Passengers herded onto a bus in zero temperatures where we all stood for 10 mins waiting for the last stray passengers and the bus then took 15 mins to travel 100 meters due to stops and starts for aircraft movements. On return only one of 6 Border desks was manned. In fact very little positive to say.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Mark Fleming
content: Having read previous reviews I would agree that coming in to London City was fine but the same can't be said for going out. Check in is OK but you could see confused people trying to work out what to do. We were waiting on a flight to Edinburgh which when we sat down in the lounge showed as "wait in lounge" on the arrival/departure board. It then announced a slight delay of around 15 mins but still advised to wait in the lounge. As the time due to depart approached the message remained the same. Suddenly out of the blue the message read "Boarding at gate 6". When you are travelling with young children you simply do not need this kind of thing. Harassed and upset we headed for the gate as quickly as possible to find that we were neither at gate 6 nor boarding. We were at gate 5 and the plane was nowhere near boarding. Another reason why I will be reluctant to use this airport in future is the DLR. When we arrived on a Saturday it wasn't working. A bus service replaces it but does not seem to go any further than Canary Wharf. We decided to take it to Canning Town then take the Jubilee line into town but again travelling with children this is not convenient. But be warned - a local chap told me that the DLR is never on at the weekend as they are lengthening stations and doing various jobs for the upcoming Olympic Games so be warned if you intend to come to this area.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: David Gordon
content: The present situation with check-in and security is very bad - long shuffling queues at peak times. The airport claim this is because more people are using online check in and more people are arriving by train. This sounds improbable. More likely is that they just did not plan for passenger flows at the time of their recent expansion. Going through security this morning made Heathrow look good.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Trevor Neary
content: I use London City Airport due to the normal speed of travel through the airport. However recently there have been major queues to get through the security check. Last week it took me almost a hour at 07.45 and on my return (19.11.09) I landed at 18.00 and as was leaving the airport the queue for security extended out of the building!

title: London City Airport customer review
author: A Hijmans
content: I think the praise for LCY proximity to London's city centre is overrated. It's still a long ride away on the DLR never mind the fact that only one out of every four trains goes to LCY. Apart from that LCY is an efficient airport and friendly staff also help.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: N Farrow
content: LCY to AMS and back. Perfect airport for short business trips to Europe and also for connecting on to an AF/KLM or LH flight at the usual hubs. The real benefit is being able to get from aircraft to taxi in 5 minutes on the return journey. I dont know anyone who enjoys spending an hour getting through LHR.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Peter Cullen
content: The first time I have used London City for about 10 years. The airport is excellent as others have said small very fast processing both in and out. However the cost of the car park is truly breath-taking (£74 for 36 hours - over a weekend). OK if you live in central London or Docklands there is the cheap DLR alternative but I don't and there appears to be no 'park and ride' alternative. Nice airport but at a price which just made me feel ripped-off (we are not all merchant bankers).

title: London City Airport customer review
author: A Gabbai
content: I have used LCY numerous times over the past six months on the LCY-ZRH route. It is a great airport built for quick check-in on the way out and quick pasport control on the way in. The staff seem to be well trained and understand that this is a businessman's airport. A pleasure to fly in and out of.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Simon Welch
content: A great little airport. It is small easy to find your way around and now easier than ever to get to. Any airport where it takes 90 seconds to get from plane seat to taxi gets my vote!

title: London City Airport customer review
author: N Barnsley
content: A great airport! Only twenty minutes from landing to DLR and then another twenty into central London. Luggage waiting on the belt polite and efficient staff at passport control. Well signed easy to navigate and short walking distances.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: A Patel
content: Having used this airport a few times I always have had really pleasant flight in and out of city airport. Seeing they are upgrading the airport now it would make a travel from this airport very pleasant. It is small and well managed airport and all basic facilities are in place and the place is easy to navigate and staff were friendly.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: D Johnson
content: Excellent Airport. Found free wi-fi (usually have to pay at Heathrow) which meant I could work whilst waiting a good bar (bit pricey at times) and the new lounge is very smart. They are doing up the old lounge at the moment so it looks a bit worn but it is work in progress and they say it should be completed in about a month's time. The check in and arrivals process is a breeze (security is quick but can be a bit noisy at times but there is no hanging about). No queues smart terminal generally friendly staff very quick arrival times from plane to train and into central London - 35 minutes last time from the airport to Westminster.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Jonathan Granato
content: Aside from the ruinous black cab fare from Finchely Road to LCY smoothing going. If could have taken the Jubilee Line and connected w/DLR but this being my first time I chose not to take any chances. Once inside the terminal there is a vast feeling of space. Check in a breeze. Surprisingly KLM contract staff friendly and efficient. Security draconian and intentionally unpleasant. Terminal laid out just fine. Coming in AMS-LCY you're off the aircraft and through passport control in around twenty minutes.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Dan Ross
content: Flew out in the Friday evening peak. Check in for VLM had changed to machines since the take over by KLM/AF which is a shame. Machines take credit card or passport for id. If you use the credit card you need to swipe it in and out. which the machine doesn't tell you. Still a quick check in process. There was one idiotic business woman yelling in her mobile phone that she would never come back here because she had to check in via the machines. Obviously a "status" passenger missing the express lines. We sat and a had a meal in the restaurant before security. At GBP12 for the main I thought it was a bit pricey but the quality and portion size was very good so shant complain. Security was fairly quick. Tip - go behind a business traveller and not a tourist. Seasoned travellers have the routine down pat while infrequent users slow the process. The lounges were full once inside. We had a look at all the new shops. Shame there is a WH Smiths there now it loses its classy feel and a bit more downmarket in my eyes. Our plane started its boarding call about 45 minutes before the flight was due to leave. It was from one of the new gates. When I was looking for signs to see where they were there was a big board in the middle of the floor with directions. But two women had parked themselves in front of it and were blocking it. I had to get the idiots to move so people could see where these new gates were. They are through the bar and you have to dodge the waiter delivering food to the tables on the other side. The departure gate has strange stools to sit on. Very strange. But still better than most other airports I've been to.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Alan Parker
content: I have used LCY over 30 times this year and can't speak too highly of the airport. It really is the way forward and makes the trip to LHR (for short haul) a waste of time. Improvements to the terminal have been most welcome and baggage is often ready for collection as you arrive in baggage claim. However the bar prices are eye watering (£4.30 for a beer!) and car parking the most expensive in Britain (£120 for three days) so take the DLR at £1.50 to Greenwich.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: R Clark
content: Very nice airport check in and security very quick. Has a tendency to get busy at times with standing room only. Good selection of shops and eateries. Expensive prices though £4.30 for a beer is excessive. Only frustration was on return flight to LCY was delayed at Zurich due to fog at London. However the fog at Zurich did not stop flights arriving and departing there. Will except that there may be some technical issues at London that restrict arrivals for this reason

title: London City Airport customer review
author: J Bailey
content: Crazy little airport which you have to love. Very convenient to get off and on the plane. very convenient connections into London centre on the DLR. Tiny little airport with a lounge like your sitting room. Check-in way too small in theory but it all works because they only land mad small little planes that only hold a few people.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: T Maddern
content: I flew out of London City Airport on October 24. Airport was total chaos because it was closed for several hours due to a security issue. The check in area was densely packed but I think all staff in this area were doing the best job possible to get everyone checked in flights rearranged and upstairs into the departures area. It's easy and quick to get wherever you want in this airport and if you are interested in watching aircraft coming and going there are plenty of areas to do this. On the way back the approach was interesting - circled London to make an Easterly landing past the office high rise buildings then a sharp nose dive towards the ground. Passport control and baggage delivery were quick and efficient.

title: London City Airport customer review
author: Ross Clark
content: LCY-EDI. Second use of the airport in a year. The main downside of this airport are the 'gate lounges' which are far too cramped for the load of even a Avro RJ-85. AirFrance also has the quirk of asking for ID along with your boarding pass when you get to the gate. Have not come across this before for a domestic flight. Upsides: the DLR access (the train was packed going out eben at 415pm); the security (through in about five minutes this at 4.45pm); compact size; the lounge capacity (enough seating even at 5pm. Probably my preferred airport for getting to London and likely to get more popular with the OK to increase the # of flights they can handle.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Linda Empson
content: A nervous flyer and flying alone on a return flight for the first time in ten years. I arrived back at Gatwick and by mistake joined the queue for epassport, by the time I realised, I was too far into the queuing process to leave that queue and join the manual passport check, plus I had been on a delayed night flight and just wanted to get home. On reaching the front of the queue I explained to the lady that I did not know what I was supposed to do, she slammed down my passport on the scanner and left me to it, despite my asking for assistance. It didn't seem to scan, so I asked again for help, she snatched the passport from my hand, slammed it down and left me to it again, nothing seemed to happen and I picked it up and she actually shouted at me! Then, finally through that bit, I was unsure of what to do next. She was at this point busy shouting at someone else who also did not know what to do! Finally she shouted the next part of the procedure at me. To add to that it seems that I have become unrecognisable since my passport renewal five years ago as it did not recognise my features. I then had to be carefully looked at by an actual person, who clearly decided it was me after all. Massive queue here, that could have been speeded up by the lady actually assisting people who are not 'seasoned flyers' through the process. I'm sure it is frustrating for her but no reason for rudeness. Not a good experience on that final part of my trip.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Pamela O'Cuneen
content: Gatwick North Terminal has recently re-organised its security services. While I am all for safety on board, the set up is now complete confusion and chaos. The planning is non existent. Cases disappear onto any one of a number of belts, and people are completely confused as to where they should pick up their possessions. Staff are picky and unreasonable in their insistence on the letter of the law. Searches must be conducted, but the system needs rethinking and the staff need to be trained to use their discretion.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Tim Barker
content: Thompson flight lands at Gatwick at 0130. All passengers tired and just want to get home, many with young children. Cant get into passport control hall as too many people there and access blocked by staff. Everyone frustrated and angry. No information available as to why the delay, no apologies, absolutely nothing apart from one man shouting that the electronic passport checking is available. We queued for over an hour. It is very fortunate there were not any problems as the situation was very tense/unhealthy and prone to angry exchanges. The lack of information makes it worse. The place is an absolute shambles and nightmare and it appears nobody cares as nothing seems to be done. The solution appears to be more staff and more space but at least tell people what is going on to stop the frustration. The customer service is non-existant!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: John McCrackle
content: Flew in yesterday with Easyjet from Brussels. At the gate the ground staff couldn't find the chocks for the wheels so we were delayed getting off the plane. Then we were so far from the terminal we had to get a bus which caused further delays. But the best was yet to come. The passport control was an absolute shambles. Massive slow moving queues, the electronic passport section wasn't working at all. They just don't seen to be geared up for the volume of passengers. It took longer to get through passport control than it did to fly from Belgium! I will think twice before using Gatwick again.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Steven Cox
content: Just been at Gatwick Arrivals North Terminal off a BA flight from Naples. What an utter shame of a place. Staff are hopeless if you can find them. The queues are horrendous for everyone. The whole experience is a total disgrace. To think Gatwick is competing for a second Runway over Heathrows third is laughable. Whoever is in "charge" should be brought to book'.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Thomas Moore
content: My wife, myself and 2 grandchildren were traveling from Orlando through to Gatwick on Wed 15 July 2015 and had to get a connecting flight to Glasgow. We got off our flight from Orlando on time and made our way to passport control. I was horrified to find the size of the queue, I told a staff member that we had a connecting flight to get and was told there would be no problem making it on time. What a shambles. 40 minutes later I got through and we all hurried upstairs to find the plane had left on time. They helped us get our connecting flight to Glasgow 6 hours later. You will never see us again in an English airport.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Brian Watling
content: South Terminal Departure - The Check In is one of the worst I have experienced. The Check In was like a scene from 'Come Fly with Me'. We were checking in for the Riga flight, the agent tried to charge me for a hold bag we had paid for in advance, the agent could not or did not look at the correct booking. Security was quick and a painless experience, with it taking approx. 15 minutes to complete the checks and searches. After security, you are subjected to walk though the Duty Free shop rather than straight into the terminal and you can then decide if you want to visit duty free. The Terminal is a silent terminal which means you have to watch the monitors for the gate number to be displayed. The food court is on the second level and does not have that many monitors. Arrival - This can be a route march from the gate to passport control, and you also have to battle with impatient disabled buggy drivers who think they have the right of way. We cleared passport control in a matter of minutes and then had a wait while they made up their minds which belt the bags would appear on. On the whole Gatwick is reasonable airport but they have allowed a cowboy handling agent to get a foot in the door.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Karen Parrett
content: Passport control at Gatwick North is a shameful example of incompetence and has to be sorted out. No matter what time of day I have arrived, it has taken over 45 minutes to get through. I have an electronic passport which is slower than you can imagine and there just aren't enough barriers to cope!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Steve Deacon
content: Although the departure was good, the arrival tonight 12th July was a disgrace. Passport control was a shambles and although my family have e-passports, the queue was incredibly slow and took us 45 minutes to get to use the passport electronic machines. These are obviously not working effectively as they were taking over a minute to do each passenger. NORTH terminal is not a good representation of the UK for anyone entering our country or for any national wanting to 're enter. The staff were rude, gave bad service and little information to the public. One member of staff refuted that epassport were designed to make passport control easier and quicker for the public. I can now see why Gatwick has a poor reputation and why the next london additional airport capacity will not be going to them.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Kevin Barrance
content: What complete chaos at this airport. Was meeting my family and it was terrible. Long queues to get into the short stay car park at the North Terminal and once inside the terminal it was awful. Nobody there to control the mass of people exiting from flights and my family told me it was around an hour's delay at passport control. Disgraceful. What a poor impression this dump must give to overseas visitors.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Paul Ginnifer
content: Travelling to Corfu by easyJet North Terminal. Check in at easyJet  was brilliant but only because I had upgraded my seat and had speedy boarding. The queue for none speedy boarders was huge the famous Gatwick snake. At security I was stopped as usual because I have a replacement hip, I told the security guy of this as he asked me if I had anything sharp on me as he needed to search me. He replied I know you have I can tell. I asked him why he needed to search me if he knew what had set the scanner of. He then called his supervisor, I explained what had happened and he glared at the security guy and said sorry its procedure. Interestingly coming back from Corfu I didn't even set their security equipment off. Why do I need to show my boarding card to buy a newspaper at Smiths? On return journey for some reason the aircraft parked away from the terminal and we were bussed back. But we were dropped of miles from passport control, where I encountered a massive Gatwick snake at least 15 rows long. All the passport desks were open and manned. The guy at passport control was pleasant, obviously hadn't had the scowl and be miserable chip inserted yet. I then waited at least 15 to 20 minutes to be informed which carousel the luggage was on? Will I fly from Gatwick again - yes, but only because I have to. Gatwick will have to improve vastly in many areas if it is going to expand as it wants to and become a 1st class international airport.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: M Ferguson
content: We arrived from Marseille which was traumatic enough as the plane coming from Gatwick arrived at the time we should have departed. Blamed on Gatwick air traffic control. Some of the travelators weren't working and this is unfortunate for someone with arthritis. Gatwick seems to delight in offering long distance treks to get to or from planes. The good thing is that the taxi booth is close to the exit, and fairly easy to find. It was the following day, when we were travelling to Aberdeen from Gatwick North, that we experienced Gatwicks inefficiency at its worst. To be fair, I believe easyJet needs to take a lot of the blame - they are never that efficient at check in but excelled themselves here. We got to area C/D for a 07.20 flight at 05.50, with our boarding cards and flexitickets which technically entitle us to speedy bag drop. The area was roped off. We were directed to a queue about 100 metres long, by Gatwick staff. There was no attempt to prioritise by flight time, you just queued. Beyond the barriers was teaming with people trying to get to easyJet check in desks. We got to the head of the queue after 25 mins. Another Gatwick staff lady directed us to speedy bag drop in the top corner, where there was a queue of about 5 ahead of us. We got through after about 10 mins - it was now 0650. A solid hour when you have paid extra to get through the check in process, and have checked in online. I had requested special assistance, which was lucky. I can't praise the assistance staff highly enough, but that's the only part of Gatwick that deserves it. Our names were being tannoyed at this point. We boarded a packed bus. The moral of the story is - beginning of the high season with Gatwick and easyJet, just don't work! Avoid!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Vanessa McCarthy
content: Arrived on Aer Lingus EI238 from Dublin. The arrival gate was a long way from the terminal building so we had to get a bus which is not very convenient when travelling with an infant. On arrival to the main terminal building there were a lot of stairs which is fine if you are not carrying a child or luggage. There were some older people on our flight carrying their suitcases and appeared to be struggling with the stairs. After an overnight stay our departure the next day was straight forward enough. Thomson check in desk was fine, queue wasn't too long and we got through security quick enough. Unfortunately, the return leg of our journey was not as pleasant, walked for ages to get to passport control without a buggy, we then queued for around 30 minutes to get through passport control. Lucky we decided to stay over because if we had a connecting flight we definitely would not have made it. Another overnight stay with a departure on a Saturday afternoon which was an absolute nightmare, we were on our way through security when we told to use the family entrance so we turned back. Staff were not organised at all and didn't seem to know what they were doing, we were queuing for ages before we were allowed through. I found the whole experience very frustrating I had put my bags through security took my baby out of her buggy and then had to wait before I could walk through the scanner. In the meantime my bags had already gone through the other side. By the time I had got through my bags were at the other end of the conveyor belt I then had to put my tray with my belongings and my husband’s belongings over to the other side whilst trying to hold my child and wait for my buggy. My husband had been brought over the other side of security where he was getting a thorough check. I found the staff to be unhelpful and not very considerate there was absolutely no organisation whatsoever. It had been 3 years since my last visit to Gatwick and considering all the transformation and upgrade it was supposed to be getting I didn't see any changes if anything it is now worse than ever and based on my experience it would make me rethink about using Gatwick again for connecting flights.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Dominic Carney
content: I think this is one of the airports to watch in the next few years. It's going to bloom. I know it has a bad reputation but it is growing up and away from this by the day. We flew to Sicily from Stansted and back the end of May and there wasn't much at all to find fault with. Staff were cheerful and helpful, facilities were all working, food outlets were good, parking was fine. I think it's about having an open mind and not carrying around old prejudices and preconceptions. Give Stansted a break.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: D Stevens
content:
I recently flew from Gatwick Airport. (Thursday 4th June, 06.30am flight to Palma). I was shocked at the check in staff for Monarch.  The woman who checked us in seemed totally uninterested, was unfriendly, did not smile once and did not wish us a nice trip.  I also overheard one of her colleagues moaning that a lady had "attitude" and
she had refused to deal with her.  This is the most unprofessional check in I have ever experienced.  This would make me think twice about booking any more flights with Monarch, but I must stress that the cabin crew on the plane were very efficient.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: S Dale
content: We travelled through Gatwick North Terminal. Going out was wonderful our Thomson flight was on time and not too long to queue for baggage drop. Aircraft was parked up very near the terminal building and we were really impressed with the North Terminal and said how happy we would be to fly from there again. On our return it was a different story. Aircraft was at farthest gate which meant an extremely long walk for us. I would say it was a mile and a half but the official distance is 840m to passport control. Whatever it was it was too long to expect people to walk. There should be transport for those who would prefer it. I did phone before we left home and requested assistance but was then asked if we could walk 500m. I explained that yes we could but as we had both had recent operations we found it hard to stand queuing. We were told that there was no assistance available to us as we could walk 500m and in any case we would still have to stand and queue for passport control or baggage drop etc. On arrival back to Gatwick there was no-one to ask for help although we passed many little trucks just parked up with no driver. Surely it should be possible for people to get help more easily. By the time we eventually arrived at baggage collection we were exhausted and in discomfort. It seems ridiculous that no help is available to people with temporary disabilities.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: P Nunn
content: Outbound only to DXB from north terminal. North still undergoing 'improvements' (it feels like it has been for the last 3 years) and north terminal check in area feels half empty. Security wait times have improved but some staff attitudes need looking at. The main waiting/shopping area has no windows and can feel enclosed. Some gates can have a long walk.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: A Parke
content: Passport control in the North Terminal is a joke. 45 minutes queuing in cattle market conditions is not acceptable. Gatwick should sort this problem out urgently!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Russell Kaymer
content: North Terminal. Immigration queues are very long both for EU and ROW and Electronic. I arrived on the Emirates 380 on a UK Electronic passport. I waited 45m. The queues for EU and ROW were far worse and went all the way out of the hall down the corridor. The owners of this airport have increased capacity (Eg: Emirates now fly 2 x 380 into the airport and the airport is busier in the summer) but they have not spent the money on increasing the amount of desks or terminals. Surprise surprise the summer comes and Emirates upgauge and the waiting times go through the roof. I spoke to the Border force people who to be fair had all the desks open they said that they could not keep up with the throughput due to lack of desk and terminal space. Two thoughts: 1) Why do we give visitors and residents such a poor first impression of our country. 2) How can Gatwick possibly expect to add another runway if they cannot even cope with the one they already have? Furthermore the bridge connecting the terminal with the midfield gates does not appear to have been cleaned in a long time and their air bridge we used had litter strewn all over it. I couldn't help feeling that the whole LGW (N) arrival experience is hanging on a piece of thread. I used to opt to go to LGW as they spent a lot of money on the departure process and it worked now I go to LHR as the arrivals is much smoother.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: A Chinnery
content: We generally fly Easyjet or Virgin from Gatwick and as it's there main hub they do things there way. This time we flew WOW and found the overall experience good. Check in started around 3.5 hours before our flight and didn't take long. They had more staff for one flight (7) than WOW did at KEF for 3 flight (5). Security did take longer than usual but still only took 15mins which is better than Stansted. The departure lounge is large however there is no view of the apron at the South Terminal as the one restaurant there was is now going under redevelopment. This is the one thing in the departure lounge that needs to be changed. The gate opened one hour before our flight before the plane arrived. Boarding was chaotic as they where boarding in rows and people didn't listen. It took far longer than it should have and is probably why our flight was slightly late. On arrival we landed early and disembarkation got away quite quickly. Immigration took really quickly and the staff where friendly which was a good thing. Baggage got on the carrousel after a ten minute wait so probably took 25 mins from the plane to the carrousel and 35mins from us leaving the plane to getting in the car. Very good. Our experience yet again showed us that Gatwick airport is a great airport that runs efficiently for it's large size. The airport remained clean.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Brian Watling
content: North Terminal - We used this airport last week to catch our flight to LPA with Easy jet the Bag Drop Security and wait were excellent and some of the best I have experienced. However that is where the good part ends! In most airports including the South Terminal there is a separate queue for flyers who have speedy boarding priority boarding or the like but not at the gate(50) for this flight. The gate staff just made everyone queue in one line regardless if you had paid extra for speedy boarding or not. I thought I was at a different airport than the one I had dropped my bags off at it felt like the gate staff just could not grasp the concept of speedy boarding.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: J Cole
content: Rude immigration officer treated us like criminals we were staying in UK for 9 weeks holidays couldn't understand why we would want to stay in UK for 9 weeks couldn't understand that Australians get Long service Leave very disappointing first impression of England (the rest was great). We are in our sixties I still work full time which I had proof. We were very polite and didn't answer back and were treated rudely.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: A Percival
content: Gatwick airport itself is fine but Border Control at the airport is a joke. On the last two occasions I have arrived at Gatwick north terminal the wait at border control was in excess of 40 minutes. Some of the manned kiosks were unmanned and the automatic kiosks would not read the new passports. There was an automatic system in place called Iris that worked speedily and efficiently yet it was scrapped and no one seems to know why. I understand the need for border control but please men the area appropriately to stop the inconvenience.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Ravi Mene
content: Used the North terminal last month to fly to Vietnam and back by their National airline. The fast track security was a breeze and stress free! Not the very long trek to a far away stand. long walks several escalators then again kept walking it was like a an endurance test of fitness same again on return. Felt sorry for those who found it difficult but wouldn't complain!! Why can't they have a warning about distances involved and have some help or simply bus in the passengers to/from the plane. They want a second runway at Gatwick? This will make it even worse? I have a choice to use other airports and I'm going to use it!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Kev Stevenson
content: We flew into Gatwick from Glasgow in order to fly to Thailand. Arriving from Glasgow all was straight forward deplaned and baggage collected in good time - no problems. Departing to Thailand our check in was around 9am from North Terminal. So the queues for our flight weren't too bad as most of the Thomson long hauls had already checked in / departed. Getting through Security took about 10-15 mins. Not ideal when your wife is heavily pregnant but it could have been much worse. Through to departures lounge and I have to say the North Terminal was starting to look well used and a bit tired. I've flown Gatwick several times and it's the first time I've felt the North Terminal needed some love. There are plenty of options for places to eat so you can waste some time that way. Our actual departure gate was absolutely freezing. You aren't there for long though but it wasn't good. Coming back from Thailand again deplaned fairly quickly. Immigration queues were pretty long but loads of staff on to get through. We would normally use the new automatic immigration kiosks but we could see they were very slow so just stuck with the human process. Flying back to Glasgow we had to check out of our hotel at 12 and didn't fly out until 4. Spending even more time in North Terminal Departures just confirmed that the terminal is very tired looking. There is a variety of options but if you just want to sit and wait it out it's not the most pleasant of places to do so now.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Antony Clarey
content: This is not so much a review as a warning to others who use the North terminal. I recently flew out to Gran Canaria and not for the first time was disappointed by the way myself and other passengers were treated as we negotiated security. Quite honestly we were treated like cattle I myself was spoken to extremely patronisingly and rudely. I do not wish to go into details but if possible I shall look for alternative departure points next time.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: M Allen
content: Arrived back from Dubai on an Emirates A380. This plane (biggest commercial aircraft) is put at the gate in the extension to North Terminal which is linked by a long bridge across the airport taxi-way. As far from the terminal as possible. Result-400 plus passengers have a 20 minute walk to get to immigration. What a contrast to Dubai airport in every way!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: H Bartlett
content: Not having flown out of or back into Gatwick for 22 years my review is with fresh eyes. Flying from N Terminal to Naples. Smooth experience plenty of space in departure hall. Could do with a shop or two more though. Everything is airside. Security had a large crowd but passengers were processed quickly. Short walk to gate for departure boarding a pleasant experience. So pleased with this airport that I will use it for future flights.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Allen Hill
content: We arrived at LGW from DXB at 0645 it took less than half and hour to deplane and leave the airport 10 mins walk from the gate to immigration through immigration collect our luggage and leave the airport. Everyone we dealt with immigration and ground staff very helpful and polite. On the return trip our flight was at 13.35 again within 20 mins of airport arrival we were through check in security. Again all the people we interacted with were helpful and polite. Not a long walk to the gate overall much better organised the LHR the staff much more polite.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Anita Lumsden
content: Flew out on December 1st returning on the 15th with Monarch Airlines. It was the first time I have had to take my mobility scooter abroad and was understandably a bit anxious. In the event every member of staff I came across from check in - assistance handling - security - movement to boarding gate and to plane were delightful. All extremely pleasant and calming and a credit to the airport. The experience on return was equally as good with happy and good humoured staff right through from plane to past arrivals area where my taxi driver was identified and told to follow the buggy to car park area. All absolutely brilliant and to be commended. Do not be afraid of seeking assistance - it makes the holiday experience start even earlier.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: David Trevose
content: E-passport what a joke. Who designed it? Like about 50% plus of Easyget passengers I had a trolley bag. Not expecting an unmanned passport control I was a bit surprised by this 'innovation'. In the instructions I didn't see any mention of how to take your trolley bag through this contraption. So I just pulled it behind me. Imagine my surprise whilst standing there being processed two glass doors closed the space behind me by the glass doors coming in from right and left behind me at 90deg angle. So the handle of my trolley is in the gap but the trolley attached to it is blocked behind this glass barrier. What a joke. I couldn't go forward when given the green light. Fortunately someone in the queue behind me thinking out of the box and being very kind lifted my trolley over this glass obstruction so that I could move forward.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Russell Ashley-Smith
content: Bad points - the distance walking to/from the most distant aircraft stands at North terminal - my personal view is that buses would be better than the seemingly endless hike. The inability to take luggage trolleys as far as the rail station platform. It should be possible to put barriers at platform level rather than have to lug cases to/from escalators or lifts. Good points - the rail station location. The efficiency of the link train between south and north terminals. The speed and pleasantness of staff as we passed through security and passport control at the start and end of our recent journey.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Jonathan Sumpton
content: If you are arriving at Gatwick allow a minimum of 50 minutes for the arrival of luggage on the baggage carousel. Allow 10 minutes to get from baggage collection to rail ticket collection machines but allow 20 to 30 minutes queuing time there to get access to the machines. There seems to be constant delays on the trains from Gatwick to St. Pancras.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: P Cullen
content: I suppose I have to commend Gatwick. Due to appalling traffic congestion (we had allowed an extra hour due to the M25 causing 'difficulties' but it was much worse than reported) we arrived in the short stay car park for South terminal 27 minutes before departure time - and made it with 10 minutes to spare. This was without queue jumping and by making a polite request to security to be quick. On return we were back in the car 20 minutes after leaving the aircraft the e-passport reader worked very quickly for me but my colleague was held up for a couple of minutes. However it was very annoying when in a hurry (or not) to be diverted on what appeared to be two long detours after security simply to take us past endless retail outlets in a straight line I reckon we could have cut another couple of minutes off our time in the terminal - and it was a long way to the departure gate.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: N Rishi
content: The technology at e-passport customs/immigration for UK passport holders is not very user friendly. I had the experience of using it yesterday it took several attempts and assistance to use it I could see others having the same problems. In fact the regular non e-passport queue was much faster. I had similar experience at Heathrow last year.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: J Tydeman
content: Flew from Gatwick to Gibraltar and back. Queues were reasonable but the departure lounge very early on a Saturday morning in October (hardly peak time) was extremely busy and stressful. This airport needs investment but I think the idea of it being the main London airport is fanciful. Heathrow is far better and has more shops.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Oliver James
content: Flew from Australia (Perth) via Jakarta stopover in AMS. £1 or €1 for a trolley rent at LGW - no warning no visible assistance or change facilities. Thanks for the welcome back to London. Could be worse actually no UK residents might be used to it but not expected from other international arrivals. Our warm welcome leaving LGW (due to delays on M25/M23) check-in was as what you expect from check-in but security comment was 'you're boarding card does not scan and you're late'.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: A Chinnery
content: London Gatwick trips 2014. LGW-PSA 10/4/14 PSA-LGW 13/4/14 LGW-UVF 25/5/14 UVF-LGW 02/06/14. My experiences at London Gatwick are positive. Departing: I was last there in 2011 and it has improved. All times on departing we arrived 3hours 30mins before The queues at South Terminal have been extremely short (All times we used south) including Bag drop (UVF only time we did have hold luggage) which took 5mins security which took 10mins at the most. The shopping is great with a large walk through world duty free then an open departure lounge (Stansted is terrible with a small alleyway with all the shops in it (20 or so)). Boarding is allocated between 90mins and 45mins but clearly tell you when (Stansted you have to figure out what time and if it's delayed i.e. Boarding in 129mins). The gates are 15min walk at the most so it was fine there was a lot of seating and boarding was boarding not get in queue. (Stansted you have to queue up for 30mins before walking on to tarmac). Arriving: The immigration queues are quick which is good as after sometimes a 10hour overnight with no sleep you want to get home. There are several e-passport checks as well. It took 10mins to queue both times arriving and the baggage was out quickly. Overall: My favourite London airport with sort queues open spaces and good boarding process and of course a good image for foreigners making their first trip arriving in London.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: I Ackermann
content: Very quick and professional Services (Immigration safety gate) and very friendly staff. Very well connected by public Transfer (coaches railway). Definitely recommended.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: D Whalley
content: This is an airport which is difficult to assess. Out from South Terminal. Excellent. Staff at security were helpful. Plenty of seating and the place was clean. Return into North Terminal was a different story. Queue of nearly 45 minutes at passport control. Staff helpful but overwhelmed by the number of returning visitors. Five aircraft landing at approximately the same time. It is difficult for staff to control when some flights arrive late and others early but these delays are unsatisfactory.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Glenn Biffen
content: You really have to gear yourselves up before you walk the seemingly endless halls and walkways of this airport. I have flown from Gatwick more in the past two years than ever before (from both terminals) and it never seems to end. If you were using this airport for the first time it would certainly be a shock to the system. A few more seating areas would be advantageous. However (on a positive note) my partner and I were pleasantly surprised by the security in the South Terminal; easy simple and quick - and the staff were human!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Gary Lineker
content: I have not been to London Gatwick Airport for several years and visited recently to take my sister and brother-in- law to the Airport and pick them up two weeks later. I understand that LGW is no longer owned and operated by BAA but is now owned and operated by an American Company who are responsible for the recent revamp. What the new owners have created at least Land Side in Departures is awful. Not many seating areas and they have got rid of most of the places where you can sit and get a reasonably priced meal. You are now left with just a couple of very and I do mean very expensive restaurants: £9 for a hot dog!! What a rip off. There are now no shops Land Side and I understand the Airport Information Desk is to be abolished. The Airport Information Staff all appeared to be of foreign decent and their uniforms looked tatty and dirty and the ones I approached for information where simply unable to answer my questions. I am not at all impressed with the new make over / revamp. It was far better when it was under the ownership of BAA. I cannot comment Air Side but from reading the reviews here it would appear that the new owners have even made a total mess of that area. Something is clearly wrong with Arrivals as the Information Flight Arrivals screens advised that my sister's flight had landed and it was almost an hour later before it advised that the flight was now in the Baggage Hall and them almost another hour later before my sister and brother-in-law came into sight in the Arrivals area.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: R Orme
content: Going through security is not a good experience - you have to go upstairs (and down again afterwards) - presumably to maximise retail space. Also there is a problem if you're 'patted down' or sent through the body scanner - the tray with your valuables has now gone through and anyone could pick up your phone/tablet or take your handbag - not a good experience. Then when you get back downstairs you're taken on a long detour through retail but unlike IKEA there's no cut-through. Do they want you to feel a valued customer and offer you a user-friendly experience or are they trying to get you to spend money? It's definitely a lot worse than it used to be.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: S Paterson
content: A needlessly stressful experience which will make me think twice about using LGW in the future and flying regional instead. Checking in for a flight to Edinburgh the airline's computer system crashed for approximately 30 minutes during which time the increasingly long queue of passengers was kept in the dark. All in all it took me one hour to check in for a domestic flight; so it's a good thing I arrived with time to spare. Our flight was delayed by the fact that there was an insufficient number of dispatchers available (according to our pilot) so we had to wait on stand until one became free thus delaying us 45 minutes. On the return leg dispatchers were again unprepared for our early arrival and had left a flight of mobile stairs blocking the gate so we were delayed in disembarking the aircraft too. The pilots on this particular airline had no qualms in strongly hinting at their frustration with the handlers. I live closer to Southampton and will probably just pay a bit extra next time in order to avoid London.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: John Flynn
content: Flight to Canada on 2/09/2014 from South terminal and return on 9/09/2014  all I can say about this terminal is that they have created a multi million pound dump the management seem only interested is getting passengers to "shop" by having to walk through the duty free to get to the seating areas the smell / stink of the perfume counters is enough to make you choke with the fumes. The walk to the gate is a joke as they seem to be at the furthest end of the terminal there are many international airports who try to give passengers a fairly good airport experience Gatwick South terminal is not one of them.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Ian Johnston
content: Tuesday 2nd September. Just flew in from Dalman airport in Turkey. Arrived at Gatwick south terminal and what a shambles! You have 300 hundred people trying to access passport control with one small girl directing passengers to the new e-passport system. Couldn't go wrong? Umm yep literally 1 in 15 people was able to use it it simply does not work! Most people fail and go back into another queue. You have three people who are sat behind a desk who are meant to be supervising but do nothing voiced my concern to this desk only for the staff to say the system works when clearly pointing out right in front of them it does not. Wont be flying from Gatwick again.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Peter Gordon
content: Arrived with easyjet from AMS at the North Terminal satellite. This has very long walk to the terminal including going over a bridge but I rather enjoyed the novelty (I was rather hoping that a plane would taxi under me). E- Passport worked fine - fortunately it was a quiet time. I have a gripe about the lack of water fountains - luckily I had been able to refill my water bottle at Schiphol. I don't know if the airport wants to force to you pay for expensive bottle water or if its an oversight but please do something about it if you don't want to annoy your customers. I also found the passenger information in the South terminal confusing - screen give a check in location for each airline but I couldn't find anything to say if a given flight was operating on time or find any details of codeshares. (You can probably guess that you should check in at Virgin if you are flying Delta but its not clear). Overall not a bad airport.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: A Wood
content: Travelling out of Gatwick and travelling in on our domestic flight were fine but returning from the US passport control at Gatwick South is ridiculous returning to your home country should be straightforward yet despite the whole family having e-passports we could only admire the fantastic new automated machines (which we only saw a handful of people utilise) as our children cannot use them. I understand there is some sort of child protection issue which I can appreciate but why can they not have a more appropriate system to ensure you are not made to feel unwelcome by having to join a longer line than visitors without British passports?

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: G Burton
content: Flew into Gatwick airport from Orlando on Sat 16 August. Great flight but tiring. Long long trek to passport control with 2 small children only to join a queue of hundreds of people. When flying into the States there is a lot of extra security which I personally welcome but a US citizen does not have to join the throngs unlike us when we are trying to get back to our country. There was a line for Channel Island passport holders why not for UK citizens? Yet another way that British citizens are treated unfairly. There was no extra visible security. You need to look at the way the States run their airports!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Mark Simons
content: Mixed experience. Travelling to Barbados the outbound security check was very swift all systems manned and minimal queues. As this was peak summer the eateries were incredibly busy with in some cases no seating available. On our return we encountered several problems. Firstly the aircraft landed 30 minutes early and the pilot announced that "another aircraft has taken our gate" - surely a scheduled arrival with 300 passengers cant come as a surprise! After a long trek to passport control we encountered massive queues. None of the e-passport gates were working and the booths were undermanned. It was irritating to then have an airport employee shouting at the queue to "move along quickly and hurry up".

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: K Haghighat
content: Arrived from Edinburgh on Sunday evening (3.8.14) We were already running late. A full flight load of Passengers filed off the plane only to be trapped for 25 minutes in a narrow corridor surely contravening Health and Safety Laws. A young man from another Airline tried to let us out but didn't have security clearance. He was at least able to phone Security for us. Security eventually arrived and opened the doors directing irate Passengers to email their complaints to the Airport! Browsing on the computer I notice this isn't the first time that incidents of this kind have happened.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: J Donaldson
content: Airport management claiming last week's baggage shambles was isolated is simply not true arrived at this shed of an airport 28th June approx 8.15 pm no staff to connect pier to plane waited 30 mins for that proceeded (quickly) through passport control to baggage reclaim and waited 2 hours for baggage. (Only 3 flights on baggage belt screens so no huge influx of flights either). Absolutely no staff present to give advice only staff member present who I wont obviously identify told me that this was not unusual and that after 5.0pm on any day this is par for the course as there are simply next to no staff to deal with baggage. I'd absolutely dread to think the upshot if this place ever had 2 runway's-twice the shambles I'd think! I'll certainly never find out as I'd rather stay home than use this place again.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: C Spoor
content: I use LGW 5/6 times a year and I quite like the recent improvements however the main problem seems to be Swissport staff on zero hours contracts and Swissport can't force the staff to come in during school holidays. The biggest problem with LGW is Gatwick cabs. No other country would ration cabs like LGW. I have arrived back to LGW and been told that only 8 cabs were operating.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: R Smith
content: Returned home from Cyprus 11pm on 26th July. Swissport declare this is as 'traditionally the busiest day of the year' for flights yet still managed to have no resources available to offload flights at North terminal. When my family came through immigration there were 15 flights waiting for baggage. We had a result that we actually got our bags after nearly 2 hours waiting while others were sent home without after waiting for more than 3 hours. Although Gatwick declare this as a Swissport issue I would not back Gatwick for a second runway until they have service providers that are capable of delivering competent services for the single runway they already have.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: L Corbin
content: Whenever I fly from Guernsey I always try to fly through Gatwick yes there are long queues but it's an airport it gets you where you need to be to relax. There is plenty of choice in hotels I personally stay in the Premier inn. There is also choice in food and shops. People will always find something bad in everything but I honestly have always enjoyed flying through Gatwick.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: L Scanlon
content: Arrived at Gatwick today ZB737 from Malaga and yet again had to wait far too long for our luggage. Today it was 1 hour and 20 minutes! No one around to help and provide information. Avoid Gatwick if at all possible we will not use it again.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: G Wilson
content: North Terminal Swissport luggage handling is just rubbish returned from Innsbruck yesterday the flight took 1 hour 30 minutes luggage took 3 hours so it took me longer to get my luggage than it took to get back from Innsbruck then I missed my connecting flight home. Just useless.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: G Cooper
content: After travelling from Volos via Skiathos to Gatwick on the 18th July 2014 arriving at 7.35pm (flight MON7835). It took nearly 2 hours for our baggage to be delivered. At first there was an announcement saying there will be a 15 minute delay unloading the baggage from the aircraft due to problems. A further announcement informed us that we could take a seat on a carousel as there would be a further delay in unloading the baggage due to staff shortages. We were then informed sometime later that some of the baggage would be off-loaded soon and would be delivered to carousel 6. After a long journey we do not expect to arrive at a major international airport and spend almost 2 hours in an uncomfortable environment with minimum seating waiting for our baggage.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: M S Mills
content: Don't arrive after midnight passport control is a joke! In line for 1 hr and as a result missed last train to London. Airport taxi a top off at £97 for an 18 mile journey into Central London. A disgrace to UK to arrive at an international (supposedly) airport. Take a leaf out of any USA airport and learn how it's done.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: K Jones
content: Travel regularly in and out from Spain (usually ST). Just a few bug bears. Security can be very slow at times even in low season times. Never any trolleys at the top of the elevator from the train station so end up struggling with my bags looking all over for one. This has happened several times and I pull them up over it every time but they don't seem to be doing anything about it. I am surprised there is no dedicated smoking area through security as there are in several other UK airports. This is something that should be provided for smokers being a major international airport.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: K Osborne
content: Badly under staffed causing long delays at passport control. This delaying tactic works well for the baggage handling as there is another mass chaotic shambles to wait for your luggage to arrive. Next time I will allow 1 hour for passport control and another for luggage 2 hours our taxi driver had to drive round in circles at 1.20am to finally meet us at 2.30am.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Peter Fitzgerald
content: Having arrived from Istanbul on Turkish Airlines the contrast between Turkey and England was marked. The terminal at Gatwick is bland dirty and unwelcoming. The queues were long and moved slowly. Clearly not enough staff on. When we surfaced only one over priced taxi option was available. We had to wait 15 minutes for one to arrive. Could not get away quickly enough from this dreary airport.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: R Scott
content: Arrived at North Terminal at 00.10 hrs. No air bridge took 20 minutes to arrive. Immigration quick. Luggage abysmal arriving at 01.00 am. I spoke to BA desk who blamed lack of resource by Swissport. Desk operator said he had been on duty 10 hours and was dealing with baggage complaints throughout the shift. This just added insult to injury on the outbound flight BA/Swissport forgot to load our luggage which arrived at our destination 2 days later on next available flight. BA should take note as Swissport are getting them a bad name.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: S Tyrrell
content: South Terminal. Flew to Lesbos 14th June 2014 passed cases through security at 03.30hrs boarded plane at 05.00 which was due to depart at 05.35. At 08.50 we flew leaving behind 17 cases so that the Monarch airlines would not have to pay compensation only to the people without their cases. This was due to a lightning strike which affected the terminal and it was Swissport which could not get bags to the plane. 3.30hrs sat on a plane on the runway is no joke with only being offered half a cup of water after we had been travelling through the night. On the return journey there was no one there from Swissport to put the bridge to the plane so we had to sit on the plane for a further 20mins then when we arrived in the baggage lounge we had to wait a further hour for all the cases to arrive due to Swissport again. What a shambles for an International Airport. One of the airport workers told us that Swissport had got rid of all their long term staff and were now employing Zero Hour workers who turn up when they feel like it they also said that we were lucky we only waited an hour for our cases and some flights had to wait 3hours.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: R Smith
content: Seems the owners did not learnt a thing from the Christmas shambles. All the hard work in trying to turn the airport into something good is slipping away fast. The shambles awaiting luggage from flight from Palma to LGW North with Thomson on the 28/6. Landed at 15.41 - and after nearly 3 hours later - finally getting luggage. This is supposed to be an International Airport. Judging by these reviews this is becoming a regular occurrence. No need for a second runway as people/clients will take their business elsewhere. Have always tried to support LGW and would rather use than LHR. But this is the second shambles in a month regarding collecting luggage and surely the owners need to step up here and take action with these handling agents as people patient is beginning to wear thin. No wonder none of the major airlines will fly from here.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: E Mcculloch
content: Seem to be constantly undermanned! No handlers available to connect power to the aircraft then a protracted delay (40 mins) for baggage. This was the same for both our flight and another Monarch flight due to no handling staff. The worst wait was for the oversize baggage for our buggy another 15 min wait. The one guy that was on shift must have been putting in the hours for his minimum wage that day!

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Simon Manning
content: Arrived into LGW NT at 01.00 Sat morning an hour and a half late. Despite being late had to wait 15-20 mins for ground staff to arrive. Then after winding our way around tatty corridors arrived at passport control to find it bursting at the seams. Almost an hour later went to get the bags and had to wait a further 20 mins before they arrived. All in all it took over 2 hours to get out of the place. Welcome to Britain in 2014. Compare that to Hong Kong where I've parked on the furthest stand from immigration passed through the airport onto the Airport Express and been in Central in under an hour. I've also been to 3rd world countries where the experience has been far better. When are people with some responsibility going to admit that the Airport is either badly run badly managed under funded over capacity or any one of a dozen more things that are probably also contributory factors? The only saving grace was that at 3 in the morning the M23 and M25 were quiet. Unless people in high places take some bold decisions that put the country first and stop pandering to various minority groups that swing their votes sadly nothing is going to happen and people forced to use this sorry excuse for an airport will see no change. I know a lot of good people try their hardest to make things work but the old phrase "you can't make a silk purse from a sow's ear" is very apt some serious modernisation is needed. One thing the whole experience taught me was to avoid the place at all costs unless absolutely necessary. Mind you having read some of the other reviews here I'm inclined to think we got off lightly.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: N Whick
content: Arrived Saturday 28th June 4.15pm on a delayed flight (by 4 hrs) from Kefalonia (not Gatwick's fault but French Traffic controllers on the incoming flight). It was however easy enough through passport control. Then I walked into hell - in the luggage claim/collection area which looked more like a refugee camp in a war zone. Swissport the outsourced airport handling company is apparently as I found out from a passenger from an earlier flight not unloading planes or is unloading but not getting the baggage to the customers. No one from the Swissport organisation is around to explain - the lost luggage desk do not want to know. So all planes from Turkey Greece etc ie those airlines serviced by Swissport were affected so about 5-6 plane loads were affected when I arrived. It was chaos with elderly people fainting - (too few seats) groups of passengers demanding information from the lost baggage people as they were the only ones around - no access to water/drinks etc - it was like the third world. It was embarrassing to be British and I felt I had to apologise to to some Spanish passengers from Madrid who asked me what was going on and were clearly very distressed. There were rumours about a strike/go slow not enough employees. Who knows? What I do know it's bad for UK and it shows Gatwick has no structure to deal with this sort of thing and does not care one hoot for the paying customers they could at least have somebody in authority there to provide information. Problem they have is - as everything is outsourced nobody takes overall responsibility for customer care and operations. Eventually the police had to come down to restore some sort of order and a voice of reassurance to the 3rd world chaos. After 2 hours the baggage arrived. Who knows what is going on but it is a shameful and disgusting welcome to the UK.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Jean Grogan
content: Arrived at north terminal on Sunday 22nd June no swissport agent to meet the plane from Larnaca so waited 5 minutes to get to gate then another 35 minutes for someone to operate the bridge so we could disembark. No trouble getting through immigration but then had a nearly 2 hour wait for baggage. Again no Swissport people to unload baggage.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: S Bowman
content: What went wrong? Well: Toilets upstairs seemed to be occupied by people who'd taken long term leases. I was trying to get in for at least 20 minutes and of course by that time I wasn't the only one. When I gave up and went downstairs all the cubicles bar 1 were cordoned off with major repair work going on. Surely if the major facility on this concourse is going to be out of action you'd have staff directing people elsewhere? Security - why don't they issue clear instructions about what you can and can't take how you can take them and what you have to do. I don't know why I'm surprised and it happens every time so I don't know why I'm bothering to mention it. But having to rip various bits of clothes off at the last minute on a whim balancing expensive electrical gadgets precariously because they've got to go through separately and watching them disappear out of your sight finding that although you've adhered to the rules about liquids the fact that you've put them in the wrong sort of transparent bag makes you a risk well none of these makes for good karma. Finally London News or whatever WH Smith calls itself airside get your staff some training in dealing with customers. Just because somebody questions the need to hand over boarding card details to buy some wine gums doesn't mean you can take it personally.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: A Williams
content: Waited 20 minutes for bridge driver to arrive so that we could disembark our flight. Then 90 minute wait at Passport Control in a hot sweaty corridor that clearly wasn't designed for such purpose. I thought that I was going to pass out it was so uncomfortable finally arrived in the main Passport area to find that the drinks machine was out of order. Abysmal.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Peter Standen
content: What a depressing entry into the UK. The sky bridge driver could not be found resulting in a delay of 35 minutes before the Aircraft doors could be opened. A further delay of 35 minutes after passing through immigration waiting for advice as to which baggage carousel should be used. The only seating whilst waiting for National Express coach was a concrete block on the pavement outside the terminal. The Airport buildings are tired drab and depressing. Never again.

title: London Gatwick Airport customer review
author: Shaun Hunter
content: 23 Hour delay outbound to Palma Majorca. Very poor communications from Airline Desk conflicting root causes and "Armed" police called in when passengers quite rightly complained. Return Journey was on time but Baggage Reclaim was an absolute joke. No communication angry passengers and 3 hours to retrieve our luggage.
