content: Taking a group thru terminal 4 today. It was so easy. It is so nice to be able to find your way around with all the signage. I found this building to be clean neat and easy to get around with a large group of travelers. Can't wait for all skyteam members to be moved to this terminal. Checking in was very fast. Employees where friendly and very helpful.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: David Gordon
content: Arrival at T4. Flight landed 20.25. A long wait (nearly 30 minutes) to cross the runway to reach the stand at T4. On stand at 21.00 - but baggage not on the carousel until 22.15. A dismal performance.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: S Smith
content: Used both T3 and T5. Flight connections worked as it should and I was pleasantly surprised thinking it would be harder than it was. T3 I don't particularly like with it's lack of daylight however it can't be helped. Gate area was freezing cold which was disappointing. T5 I really like apart from the flight connections area. Being shouted at by staff who obviously don't like working there herding you up the escalator to security. When you reach the top of the escalator it is crowded and you have to force your way off the escalator. This area is really badly designed and lets the terminal down. Plenty to keep you occupied even on a long connections like mine of 5 hours. Impressed with T5 so-so about T3.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Adrian Jenkins
content: Terminal 3 arrivals pretty awful Departures pretty good. Everything about the arrivals level looked old immigration hall is a mess. The queue was quite long for non UK/EU citizens - more empty desks than occupied ones arrivals hall wasn't much better. Departing from Terminal 3 was a pleasant experience. SIA uses check-in area A which is much more open than other check-in areas. Departures lounge had a good range of shops and cafes perfectly pleasant waiting here - a great improvement on the last time I had been through T3 ten years ago.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Michael Matthews
content: Have used T3 for four decades during which improvements have generally not made things better. The Duty Free area is way too large and the prices not at all that competitive: area should be halved for more comfort and seating places. Distances to the gates are unacceptable. A miserable places for arrivals; departures is much better but still not good.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: J Jensen
content: I have travelled through several terminals 1/3/4 and find them all very different. Terminal 4 is out of the way south side of the runways but is modern and clean. Not a lot of restaurants inside a lot of shopping for that last minute duty free item however. Terminal 1 is old but once terminal 2 is redone it is expected to be replaced. Overall it is crowded but seems to be well taken care of. Terminal 3 is huge - if you have a flight from one of the ends of the long concourses take comfortable shoes! I think most North American and Asian carriers are based in terminal three so mornings are busy read maps to not get lost which is easy to do in this terminal. London Heathrow is a great airport a lot of things to buy or if you like plane watching all terminals offer a view of airlines from all around the World. It feels a lot closer to London than Gatwick but it can be a bit more expensive to get into Central London from Heathrow.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Paul Harvey
content: Terminal 1 international arrival midday on a Sunday. Bussing to the terminal was prompt although there was a long walk to immigration. Queues long for both EU and other passport holders but he EU side moved quite fast. Between Immigration and Baggage there was only one small toilet which led to queues outside. Baggage worked well and the total time between the wheels touching the ground and leaving the airport with two bags was 1 hour.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: N Haynes
content: Terminal 5. I was amazed how good this terminal was (first time user). We had an early flight and ate breakfast at the Gordon Ramsey Plane Food restaurant. Excellent food and service plus it was peaceful compared to the rest of the terminal eateries. We used the bag drop service excellent and rapid service. Departure lounge good adequate seating and excellent range of shops. Good seating at gates. On return flight very smooth walk through UK entry checks and our bags came rapidly to carousel. Signs to T5 long stay car park (and other transportation) very good.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: John Wilson
content: Terminal 5. Maybe we were lucky due to flying out during the BA strike but there were no queues anywhere and the place was spotless. Decent choice of shops and eateries. So nice and light compared to the other enclosed stuffy terminals. On the way back we were disembarked at terminal B so had to get the shuttle train to the main terminal. We were out within 30 minutes of landing.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: J Tung
content: Departed from T3 early morning (Air Canada) and arrived back early morning. I frequently use T1 and T5 and have very positive opinions on the arrival experience - generally very fast and smooth with the exception of T5 when BA flights can't find a gate to park. T3 has improved significantly. The building is still very old and the departure hall is still like a third world airport. However it is not as crowded as it used to be not a long queue in front of security. Some annoying passengers questioned why they had to take off their accessories water etc but you encounter those kind of passengers everywhere in the world. After security there are plenty of shopping. Heathrow is probably the best place for airport shopping partly due to the exchange rate. Arrival was a good experience. Its a long walk as usual but for EU/UK passport holder or those using Iris scan there was no queue at all. You whip through immigration in a second. Then the luggage came out before I even arrived at the belt.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Luke Williamson
content: T5 - Horrific transfer took 1h15 to get from the aircraft and through security impatient staff chaos at the top of the escalator and security staff unsure of where Geneva was. However domestic transfer did not involve passport or security checks so no issues.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Daniel Katz
content: There is a huge difference according to which terminal you use. We used T3 and T4. T3 is very boring looks like it was built in the 1970's and not well maintained whereas T4 was a fine experience with good shopping possibilities. I wonder why there are no carts available airside - it is not good for shopping or the passengers which carries handbaggage.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: C O'Neill
content: I have come through Heathrow a few times now for domestic flights between London and Belfast. I've had no problem or mishaps and found the airport as I would wish to. Although the walking distance is quite long the routes are always well signposted and it is easy to get to where I need to be. If you have any mobility issues then assistance might well be advised to help you cover the potentially large distances involved with getting around such a huge airport. The shops and cafes that are available are also very good (although a little pricey).

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: M Preston
content: Much as I dislike BA and have avoided them for years I had no choice for a recent trip. T5 is almost enough reason to resume travelling with BA. It's light and airy no queues employees who clearly enjoy working in such a lovely environment and a quick and easy transition from arrival to departure. An example for others to follow. A pity that the cabin crew on the BA flight were surly and haughty which detracted from the initial good experience of T5. The ratings I have given refer to T5 not to Heathrow in general.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: N Francis
content: T5 is generally a great experience. Slightly odd desk staffing policy at check-in and it can sometimes be an issue knowing where to go - BA staff on foot around desks are not very pro- active in moving people to empty desks. Anyway security has always been quick for me and staff courteous. Loads of shops/places to eat but still never feels crowded and noisy even at peak times. Tonnes of natural light. In all compared to previous offerings in T4 (or the dreaded T3) this is a real haven for Heathrow!

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: A Makins
content: Terminal 3 has had a face lift but it's superficial improvement. I don't like the design of T5 with gates in the waiting area. Outbound flight to Amsterdam on BA involved a bus trip to the plane surprising requirement given the money spent on building a new terminal. Return to LHR from AMS was nothing short of a joke. Arrived in heavy rain airbridge at assigned gate wouldn't work because of the weather. A few U-turns around Heathrow later arrive at another gate. Airbridge makes it 2 feet from the plane and gives up - reason: rain. Have to wait for stairs to arrive so we can have a nice wet walk to the terminal. Time from landing to deplaning about the same as the flight itself.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Rob Boyce
content: Flew out of T1 to Munich: speedy check in using the self service terminal and quickly and efficiently handled bag drop. The 'queue' at security was just two people so no delays whatsoever. It definitely seems to be a better experience at Heathrow these days!

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Paul Bailey
content: Travelled out of T5 for the third time in 6 months. I use the Valet car park so from dropping off your car it's easy to be airside inside 10 mins. The terminal is light airy and no feeling of claustrophobia shopping and food options are good. Easy transit to the B and C gates.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Jonathan Kelly
content: Flew T4 to Houston and back. Last previous use of T4 was in March 2008 and the overall experience is much improved. Arrival at the terminal and check-in is now far superior although this has resulted in airside looking somewhat grubby in comparison especially at the gates. Arrivals was very busy with almost no space in which to queue for immigration. Overall a big improvement.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Tony McLaughlin
content: T1 is great now for passengers. I flew to DUB on BMI and the flight left from Gate 84 - this is 20 minutes from clearing security and where Aer Lingus operate their flights. Something to note because of the layout if passengers are disembarking doors are shut so you cannot get through - be careful if you are in need of the loo!

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Peter Hutchinson
content: In and out using T3 . Inbound transit was quick but surely the crowd controllers for non EU passport holders should be able to speak more languages. Outbound the waiting lounge was a disappointment. Having used T5 on a previous visit to UK the overall impression of T3 was not good.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Alan Wan
content: Used T5 for the first time a much better experience than T3. There is plenty of natural light the toilets are clean and there are great views of the runways. The seating could be better lots of bench seats akin to T3 but there was some comfortable seats and lie down sofas by gates A7.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: K Chelvanathan
content: Flew in and out of both Terminal 3 and 5 respectively and found Terminal 3 to be the same as it was two years back. Immigration queues for the non-EU passports were amazingly long and I wonder why the BAA authorities cannot work something out and make the terminal more user friendly and immigration friendly ? Terminal 5 on the other hand was a breeze and the modern architecture gave it a nice feeling. The Self Check In Kiosk is such a brilliant idea and saves a lot of time and hassle.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Gary Farrelly
content: Heathrow is a very impressive operation. The part I was in was a bit jaded and grubby and chaotic. But all in all my LHR experience was very positive. Loads of places to eat and shop. Some decent views of the apron from the boarding gates. What I like most about Heathrow is the sheer quantity off carriers operating on all manner of routes from that airport. It really is a world class hub. And I am sure that if I has been travelling through the new T5 - I would have found the upkeep of the facilities that more bit clean and aesthetic.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: J Tydeman
content: Used Terminal 4 to fly to and from Nairobi. It has improved a lot since the recent terminal changes and although busy it felt less crowded and claustrophobic than before. There were very few queues of any great length which helped make it less stressful too. Credit where it is due - this airport is improving.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: David Howe
content: Return trip from DUB to DEL transferring at Terminal One for Terminal Four. We found the transfer process relatively flawless even though our bags were not checked through. We took the elevator down to the train and found it quick and comfortable compared to many airports. This is a great improvement on previous connections made at LHR. Terminal Four lacks facilities airside not many eateries to choose from. Terminal One seemed better but the walk to the aircraft is way too long.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: P Littlefair
content: Terminal 3 quick check-in with Virgin Atlantic 2½ hours before departure. We were requested to go straight to airside then proceed to gate 2 hours before departure in order to allow for Gate security. However we were turned away from primary security being told passengers not allowed through until 2 hours before departure. Once allowed into security the queue was moderate. No gate listed until 1 hour before departure so had to endure the crowded shopping mall for an hour. BAA policy on using most of the space for shopping really does make using LHR terminals a depressingly uncomfortable experience.

title: London Heathrow Airport customer review
author: Tony McLaughlin
content: First time using T5 - excellent. BA land agent was able to tell me all about the terminal and where to go when I got airside. BAA had staff on hand airside to assist travellers. Departed from B gates to USA. Security at gate was thorough but good humoured. Had to get a bus to the plane - so what. Bags waiting at carousel on return. Excellent first experience.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: L Lyon
content: Arrived at Stansted airport from Spain on 20th July 2015, it was a nightmare, airport staff shouting at passengers as the e-passport control was down, staff stated lots of flights arriving was the reason for the chaos. Were these flights unexpected? Have never been in an airport in any other country where the passengers are shouted at routinely as they are in passport control at Stansted. The thought of arriving back there after a holiday abroad fills us with dread.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Nigel Tansley
content: Good experience at Stansted for a Germanwings flight to Cologne and return. Check-in very quick, security queue about 5 minutes at 6.20am. Walk though shops pleasant and will be better once building work completed. Had food in departure lounge which was priced ok. Train to satellite which was quiet with plenty of seating. Flight left on time. Return flight arrived at 4pm in the afternoon. Approx 30 minutes wait at Border control and from what we saw most of this queue was caused by travellers either having the wrong documentation or joining the e-passport queue with children under 18 then having to join the ordinary queues at the front. Baggage reclaim quick and then got an aiport taxi within 2 mins. Good overall experience which will I suspect improve when the existing improvements are finished

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Clifford
content: An awful experience. Totally overrun and ongoing building work. You have to walk through a shopping centre before getting to your gate (adding 15-20 minutes), regardless of your desire to shop. Only 30 minutes free internet - then you pay. Food prices significantly higher then outside. The experience is a nightmare. The staff I encountered were great.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Christine Straker
content: We arrived at 11.45pm with thousands of other travellers. The customs hall was overcrowded. We waited over an hour to get through the automatic system, with many machines not working, how has this happened? Why are so many flights landing at the same time? There has to be a better system, travellers with non EU passports sail through to the frustration of many. Perhaps our leaders should be made to stand in queues going nowhere for anything to be done. Try and avoid Stansted at night.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Andrew McKinsey
content: Simply terrible airport. No separation of passenger flows, opposite direction passengers just collide, long queues at each step, long walks to reach any point. All valuable central part is occupied by overpriced shops. I really like their application of zig zag to main passenger arteria when it comes to duty free shop.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Olley
content: What people have to remember is that airports are now less transport hubs and more massive car parks. Would be interesting to know what percentage of MAG's income comes from airline charges and what comes from car parking and retail. I think most people see the "airport experience" as a necessary inconvenience. Most people want to arrive for their departure, clear security, maybe eat and then depart, but are bombarded with poor quality restaurants and over priced shops. Compare the prices of say, Boots and WH Smith's in and out of the airport. MAG probably employ as many people in the "passenger experience department" as they do in the running of the airport. Can't see that anyone has mentioned the lack of toilets in departures, while the airport is an architectural masterpiece courtesy of Sir Norman Foster, he seems to have forgotten to factor in that people have to use the facility. For those that scoff about Immigration Officers commenting on the sun affecting the ability for them to see passports or for the e-readers to work properly, it is true. At certain times of the year and at certain times of the day, the Immigration Officers are blinded by the setting sun! Try Southend if you can.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Vinay Patel
content: Without doubt the worst airport that I have had the misfortune to use for both departures and arrivals into the UK. We landed last night at 23.30 and the arrivals hall was crammed full of people. It took an hour and ten minutes of chaos to get through passport control, there were 15 E passport machines but only 10 were working. The staff were panicking even though they should be used to this, staff were very rude and shouting to get each others attention. Our baggage ended up on a different conveyer belt to what the screen was showing, it was only by chance we spotted our very distinctive suitcase on the other side of the baggage claim room. When we notified the staff that the screen is misinforming people they did not seem bothered. I will not be using Stansted again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Stephen Simons
content: We landed last night at 23.30 and the arrivals hall was crammed full of people. It took an hour and ten minutes of chaos to get through passport control, there were 15 E passport machines but only 10 were working. The ground staff said that they had a lot flights landing and no airport could cope with that volume of passengers! Where is the problem, didn’t they know the flights were arriving, planes don’t turn up unexpectedly? Surely someone is responsible for incoming flights? Stansted love to grab the landing fees from the airlines and to hell with the passengers. We missed our coach and just managed to catch another with seconds to spare, the next one was at 3am. The poor chap in front of just missed his too, he was told the next one to Milton Keynes was in 5 hours time!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Adrian Murphy
content: Without doubt the worst airport that I have had the misfortune to use for both departures and arrivals into the UK. A few years back, prior to being bought, this airport offered an efficient, friendly and relaxed service. Now, on arrival you are forced to battle your way through a worm hole of bright swirling lights and 80's tack before being spewed out into an open space thronged with humanity and no place to sit. However they do offer an exercise regime by showing your gate number at the very latest time possible, thus ensuring that when your gate number blinks onto the screen there is a sudden panic and a human herd of people start running in all directions vainly looking for some sort of directions to where they need to get to in 5 minutes. Arriving into the UK at Stansted offers another unique experience. I think they are taking the spirit of an English queue just a little too far. Tired, hungry and dehydrated and just wanting to get home the airport security process has something waiting for you, but it is not a line of friendly smiling security staff. Rather you are faced with a long line of crushed people slowly shuffling their way down an airless and suffocating tunnel before you even get in eyeshot of the border control. 20 minutes later the blank stressed face of a staff member shouts in your ear if you have an e-passport and directs you to join yet another queue. Not sure where the airport have purchased their electronic gates from but I suggest they need to get a refund (shame they don't give me one) as normally only around a third of them work at any one time. Avoid this airport if you can.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Pease
content: Back again! This time in in the morning from Basel and out late evening for Edinburgh. On arrival I was delighted to see far more staff manning the border control checkpoints and more e-gates open. A really quick passage through, only stymied by waiting for our baggage for more than 20 mins. Some you win, some you lose. On my return, I was taking my first 'domestic' flight to Edinburgh. Once upon a time, domestic flights had a different part of the airport, and no security, but those days are gone. I was processed quickly and efficiently by security although the area was very busy. Having a lot of time before my flight I decided to investigate the shops, but wasn't tempted. There is a considerable choice of dining options and with a long wait ahead I enjoyed my meal at Giraffe. Once my gate was called, I had a new experience but not one that I'd care to repeat often. My flight was called to Gate 84, via a tunnel with streams of passengers walking in both directions with no separation of inbound and outbound passengers. Once in the gate area, there were no separations of the four flights due to depart - two to Edinburgh, one to Glasgow and one to Belfast. It was quite disconcerting to see people openly drinking from beer bottles and as there were no separation markers, it was very hard to find out where to queue (especially the difference between 'speedy' boarding and 'other' boarding in the case of my Easyjet flight). Passengers inbound from these aircraft simply walked up to the area where we were waiting and had to push their way through the throng of waiting passengers to get into the tunnel and back to the terminal. Is it always like this on a Friday night at this time? More security and segregation control is needed, too many people and not enough direction.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Martin
content: I hadn't flown from Stansted for a few years and after seeing a lot of bad reviews I was a little worried about my next visit, yet was pleasantly surprised. We did Meet & Greet car parking which I would definitely recommend. Security looked quite chaotic at first but moved through very quickly. The new duty free shopping and restaurant/bar areas are much improved and I think the new layout gives a better flow, do any shopping you want to do, then find a seat. The only people who complain are those who stress about securing a seat first then end up going backwards through the shopping area, which there's absolutely no benefit in doing. It did get quite busy with a slight lack of space in departures but I'm concious of the fact that a large area of the terminal is currently blocked off for refurbishment. Passport Control was far better than I expected at about 10 minutes queuing time and this was at 18.30 with still a fair few flights coming in. There's also lots of large signs and flight information screens about which can only be a good thing. In terms of getting to/from the airport, it's fairly easy and well served by good road and rail links. Overall a good airport and really not sure why there's so many bad reviews.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Carol Harris
content: Delayed departing. Staff rude at airport as well as very slow and extremely rude cabin Staff. On arrival at our destination we were unable to disembark because absence of staff to open stairs/corridor to the terminal. Our return flight delayed take off yet again, dismantling even worse. Once in the terminal we waited at least an hour before our luggage reclaim. Ridiculously late home. Outrageously bad service. We will never use Stansted again as this seems to be a regular occurrence. We have now booked from Gatwick for our next holiday.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Hazel Ingram
content: This is our local airport and always loved flying from here but not now! Since the supposed makeover the airport is an utter nightmare. You are herded like cattle through custom patrol with long delays going and coming back last thing you need when going on holiday. When you finally do get through you then have to walk through a long winding walkway past all the shops which you can't look at because you still have all your hand luggage to carry, an absolutely stupid idea. Eventually when you do reach the end we found it hard to find a seat, having found one I left my husband there to look after the bags while I went to look at the shops we had already passed, big mistake, you have to battle against all the people coming down with luggage, also it is a long way back to the beginning of the shops. Who ever thought of this dreadful design should have another think and put it back to how it was as it was much better. The shops need to be around the edges of the airport and the seating in the middle which would making it easily assessable, take a look at Gatwick by far a better design. Also what has happened to all the staff hardly any to be seen. We wont be flying again from here I would rather do the extra hour drive and go to Gatwick.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: B Khosa
content: Countless worn out, dehydrated travellers gathered like cattle at border control. Midnight with over an hour of queuing. No water provided. No easy access back to toilets.  Some adults carrying children for the duration of the queue. Border control booths mostly unmanned.  Over 40 planes landed in 1 hour and no planning by the airport to manage the influx? Disparity in speed of processing across the hall, luck of the draw in which cattle pen queue went down less slowly. Non-EU passport holders had a breeze getting through compared to the EU passport holders. Officer listened to our complaints, but powerless to do anything.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Warren
content: For the most part, the experience was seamless, and investment has paid off in areas such as security and the wider range of shops and restaurants. They have attracted premium airlines to the airport such as SAS. However increased passanger numbers have caused severe limitations in seating availability and ease of access throughout the departure lounge. You will often be "forced" to find a space to stand and wait until your gate number has been called. They need to focus on improving the gate areas, especially those which Ryanair uses, as many are lacking in sufficient seating areas and/or are confined in small, dark areas. A hugely unpleasant experience for elderly travellers and also those with young children. The airport must focus on improving the customer experience to make this airport more appealing.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Wendy Flack
content: Very early flight and very crowded security area at 6.30 am. Unfriendly young member of staff at security belt. Total chaos the bag system does not work and empty containers were stacking up and overflowing. Lady in front asked her if she could stop the rollers as containers were overflowing onto people waiting for their luggage to have secondary search after x-ray. Staff member was surly and rude. My elderly (84) mother had forgotten some scented lotion 200 ml crime and this same security lady relished telling her it would be destroyed. No niceties, no smiles, no please, thank you just orders barked at us like cattle. Design of airport has gone backwards. I do not wish to weave through duty free. Why site screens in the middle of a through route where people simply stop and stare upwards with queues forming behind. No excuses, design software now available to optimise traffic flow - why wasn't this used in the planning? Return journey - 6 border security booths open out of more than 20. No fast track route through. This has become a nightmare airport - parking rip offs through to take off and re-entry.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: David Ingram
content: This airport is the closest one to me and is now the worst. I would rather face an extra hour drive to Gatwick than go here again. Whoever designed the new shopping area needs to go to specsavers, you have to pass through it to get to the limited seating area, so if you want to look at them again you are forced to go against the flow of passengers to get to them again! The departure area has now been shrunk to a quarter of its size and is like a cattle shed, hot too. Worse than a queue at a theme park to get out. Upon arrival back, the passport control is utter chaos, it took over an hour to get through the gates. Stansted, you should look at these reviews.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Leahy
content: I understand the frustration of the lack of mobility assistance at Stansted airport. We did a day return to/from there and the attitude of the front of staff at the ocs desk was dire. We have complained on a previous occasion, as we were informed no assistance was available even though pre booked, and if my traveling companion in a wheelchair didn't make it up the steps they would be left behind! This time we had triple checked everything - but they informed me that the codes and used by Ryanair and themselves mean two different things.  On complaining this time they failed to even respond to our mails. Avoid airport at all costs but the people delivering the mobility service are lovely.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Julie White
content: I have never had a good experience of this airport. I use a stick but don't want to use wheelchair help. I find this time they now make you walk through all of the duty free shops. we were called for flight showed boarding pass went down the stairs to board plane. We were kept at bottom in a corridor no room on one of the hottest days of the year. No information was given as to why no seats to sit. I struggled to stand and had to lean against post. After 40 mins of this we were allowed on to plane I asked what the problem was and said how hard it had been for me. It turns out Stansted could not provide people to come and get 2 wheelchair people off the previous flight and we were not allowed on until they did. Then that caused us to miss our slot and we had to sit for 40 mins in a super hot plane as no air-conditioning until take off. On arrival back the trains were crowded jammed solid not helpful and then the queues to get through passport control were terrible stood for an hour and a half. No help for really old people or people like me no seats they just exspect you to get on with it. Staff were very unhelpful. We have said it before but after this last visit we are not going to use Stansted again. We would rather go to any other Airport than put up with there.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Tim Fairhead
content: On landing, there were no staff to meet the plane to allow the passengers off. After a 20 minute wait the stairs finally arrived and taken through to passport control. This area was separated into epassport and non. Both queues extremely long but seemed to be moving. Took the epassport route as thought would be faster, but took over an hour to get through. Only 5 machines out of 15 were active, but 2 out of every 5 people were sent back to manned control as the computer couldn't detect their face. The guy at the desk was frantic, the computers all failing due to the sun hitting the screens. No communication with public, no apologies and no attempt to rectify the situation. Would never chose Stansted again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Kevin Warren
content: Stansted used to be a great airport now all the changes has made it so bad. Forcing you through the shops to get to the monorail, Cancelation flight made it a herd to the train through thin corridors. Doors on the monorail broke twice causing 25 minutes delay causing 6 people to miss flight. No communication between airport staff and Ryanair. On return passport control took 1.5 hours to get through.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: T Diehl
content: Long queues and an IKEA like walk from security to the gates. Had an early flight at 7:30 and was there 2 hours in advance. Queuing at Ryanair baggage drop-off took 45 minutes. Queue at Security check 30 minutes. With a bad experience of Ryanair closing the flight 40 minutes early we were rushing through the newly designed duty free area, which leads you IKEA like around every single shop and makes the walk to the gate unneccessary long. Our Gate was at the end of one of the 3 Terminals with 2 gates side by side. The screens showing the flights where facing away from the approaching passengers. This led to massive confusion among the passengers whether they were queuing for the correct flight.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Hanley
content: Over the last three weeks I have flown from and to Stansted on three separate occasions for both personal and business purposes, returning on a Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday evenings so fairly representative of the week in my opinion. The long and the short of this review is to say how appaling and shameful the whole passport control "process" is. Wait times have been a leisurely 35 minutes and a really depressing 55 minutes. I known it's not Stansted's direct responsibility but that of the UK Border Agency however they run the place and need to exert pressure on the UK Border Agency to do something about the shambles that it is. Either they don't have enough staff or they completely misjudge the number of passengers due to arrive - hard to believe given the amount of pre-flight information that everyone is required to supply. Equally, when the automatic passport gates can't operate effectively "because the sun is in the wrong place (yes - that's what I've been told) and there's too much glare it's a very, very poor joke which no-one finds funny. Note to Stansted management - It's all well and good spending lots of money on improving the "pre-flight shopping experience" areas but remember this - the allure of shopping is easily negated by the Passport Control debacle.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Terence Graves
content: Our departure was perfect. Ryanair were brilliant, efficient and courteous. Security was no problem, very quick. 15 minutes in total. Unfortunately coming back was rather different. Hundreds of people waiting for passport control. Out of 20 booths 8 were unmanned. The E passport system was not working properly.There was an a announcement that the queues were due to the volume of people. Didn't they know this? They must know in advance how many passengers are arriving. Why weren't the booths manned? What on earth do people coming to this country for the first time think? Waited an hour, all buses full. Then crammed on like a sardine, falling over suitcases in an oven.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Laura Bordignon
content: I have never seen such chaos going through passports control, my late evening Ryanair flight was a little delayed, but there were thousands of people in the immigration hall. It was so badly organised you could not make out which was the queue for the e-gates or manual ones. The egates where malfunctioning all the time, some people after several attempts sent back to the manual check and join yet another long queue. It took me 1.5 hours to go through! Not impressed and next time will fly out from Southend or Luton.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Stefan
content: Strange organization of an airport. In order to get to most gates you have to take the train. That brings you to a building with gates only. Only other facility in this building is the toilet. If your flights delayed, you can't get back to the main terminal with shops etc because the train's only one way and would bring you back to passport control. So once you arrived at the gate, you are simply stuck. Because of that the airport obviously can't be bothered to update the flight information on the screens. So your flight will according to the screens always be on time and disappear after the original time. Thus you can't go away from the gate anymore since you'll miss the boarding otherwise.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Jon Wood
content: Over-priced fancy shops that you are forced to hang around, no seating for customers forced to endure the last minute rush to gates, Meet and Greet parking is a joke. Huge delays at passport control and many newer passports not working at the eGates (apparently my photo was too shiny!). Complete absence of customer focus.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Pease
content: I have been very critical of Stansted in the recent past, but on my latest experience - inbound 2 July and outbound 4 July - I have to say that security was working more efficiently as regards the number of E-gates in operation, and that the dreaded shopping mall corridor, transit corridor into the food area and the food area itself was much more acceptable because the overhead panels had been removed allowing plenty of daylight and reducing the feeling of claustrophobia and the 'hamster in a tunnel' feeling. The exit to the Ryanair 'wing' has been moved and the passageway along the windows has been narrowed and access to the toilets removed. This makes for considerable congestion - including a few brave souls returning to the terminal against the flow, and the narrowing seems to be also in force in the 'underground' corridor between the departures lounge and the steps/escalator to the Ryanair 'wing', which made some of the older people around me panic that they might miss their flight. The airport was extremely busy and the only new, but major, criticism I have was the queue at the Ryanair desk at the start of the Ryanair 'wing' which stretched back into the corridor and the escalator/steps area due to handling passengers whose flight had been cancelled. This made it very congested for passengers arriving at the 'wing' for their gates. It might be helpful if the queue for passengers needing attention from the desk be separated by ropes so that the flow of passengers into the terminal could be better controlled as there is a potential danger of 'overcrowding' in such a small, enclosed area.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Caroline Beynon
content: What a horrible experience. Long queues at Security, even at the fast track. Overcrowded in the terminal, too much focus on shopping and not enough on traveller comfort. Such a stressful environment. Coming back late at night there was not enough ground crew on and we had to sit on the plane waiting for staff to come to guide us onto the gate and then wait again for steps to be delivered to the plane. Just glad that it was an internal UK flight as I dread to think what border control would be like. Will actively try to avoid in future.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Mot
content: Stansted Airport is an awful experience. In particular, arrivals was carnage. After arriving at midnight on a Ryannair flight which was late, we were met by masses of other people all trying to get through passport control. Not all the e-machines were working and not all the desks were open. We waited ages for our luggage and my padlock was missing from my suitcase; thankfully everything was okay. Dirty toilets. Many of the restaurants were closed. People cramming onto one bus to get to the car park. It took 2.5 hours from the time we joined this 'queue' to reaching our car. Stansted does not appear to have either the infrastructure or manpower to cope. I will think twice before booking another flight at this airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Slattery
content: It took almost two hours to get through security. You are then forced to walk through a maze of the usual stores to a small area with very little seating - you have to wait in this holding area before being given your gate 30 minutes before departure. It is then a 10 minute run to your gate. In the few minutes I hung around Ryanair service desk, eight passengers had missed various flights due to being late reaching the gate.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Joyce Hollingsworth
content: After a tiring journey from Italy we were faced with the queues for passport control! There were 19 rows packed with travellers which moved very slowly. When we finally reached the booth the machine checking our passport failed several times. We are both in our mid seventies and will not be returning to Stansted Airport! Not a pleasant experience. Unable to comment on airport facilities as we didn't have time to use them either on the outward or returning journey.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Alan Clark
content: Arrived around 00.30 hrs on a Tuesday morning. Very few flight arrivals so expecting a quick entry to meet waiting friend. Initially a scrum to get into either the "chipped passport" or the "unchipped passport" queue. Impossible to judge as so crowded. No difference in number of people queuing at both. I opted for the "chipped passport" queue - Bad Move. So suffered at the long queue for around 1.5 hours, yes, 90 minutes at 1 am. Many of the automatic gates appeared to reject most passports and only limited help available, mainly overworked staff telling people with rejected passports to queue for the manned booths. What has happened to the Stansted that was a success story only a few years back. This problem has been getting worse for some time now. This is an airport fixated on making money from departing travellers, forcing them to run the gauntlet of "duty free" concessions before reaching the area where there is a shortage of seats.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: James Masters
content: The security gates were a disaster. Only three x-ray machines working making lots of people late. When people who were pushed for time (after queuing for nearly an hour) asked for help, they were told to go back out and pay for express security. Stansted used to be such a good airport, now it is a nightmare. All they want to do is rip you off. After getting through I went to the new James Martin restaurant and had the worst bacon roll I have had.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Chris Adams
content: Not a pleasant experience either from or to this airport now, they seem to have lost control. Much money spent, but upgraded shopping experience is misplaced, you need to look after your customers better. Over crowded, poor staff training, delays and very expensive. The perfect mix for forcing customers away, but you now already know this. Where does the buck stop?

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Lee Henderson
content: I travelled in transit through Stansted - it was hell and I have never experienced anything like it before. Arrived a good few hours before our flight and when Ryanair eventually put up our check in desk details it was 110 mins before our flight. It then took us 90 mins to get through check in and passport control, a mad dash to get our plane and just about missed our flight - and it was the same on our return with chaos being stuck in a corridor for ages to get through passport control. Never again through this airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: W Britton
content: I last travelled from this airport some years ago and I remember I was quite satisfied with the facilities and the throughput. Fast forward to this June and the difference is quite marked. Long, long queue at our pre-booked short stay parking, valuable time wasted driving round and round until a space miraculously appeared. Airport itself packed, queues everywhere. And then a delay of an hour on our flight which incurred a late arrival charge at our destination. On our return we were met with massive queues at passport control. Clearly Stansted fails miserably to cope with the demands made upon it. As another commentator has indicated, arrive at least a good 3 hours before your flight.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Martin Chandler
content: A total disaster of an airport that cannot handle the amount of business they have. Far too much has been spent on the new Duty Free passage and not enough on Restaurants and Bars. Border control going out is better than it once was, but still poor compared to all the others around London. The worst thing though is Border Control on arrivals, total and utter chaos and considering that people are paying to use the facilities its a national disgrace. 90 mins is now the norm according to our cab driver. They should be ashamed at themselves.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Valerie Fennell
content: Total farce - arrived 2hrs before departure. Had to dash to catch plane. You ask about airport shopping - it would have been nice to get the chance! Allow 3 hours to board. Allow same to arrive.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Rupert Staveley-Taylor
content: Arrived just after midnight 28 June from Mallorca and faced a huge crowd, not even a queue, for passport control. People overflowed from the long, long taped queueing lines into a vast scrum. It appeared there were two options, e-passport control or standard but no information as to which was quicker. There was no public address to offer apologies, provide information, nothing. Eventually, having chosen e-passport control, we got through in 55 minutes. To add a little icing to the cake, the Jetparks / Long Stay car park transit bus did not pull up where the signs indicated. Standard Airport management and UK Border Agency should be shot. Their job is managing capacity and surely know how many passengers / flights are landing. Lack of information. Absolutely no excuse.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Chris Kafetzis
content: This was my first time at Stansted since their refurbishment. I can now say that what used to be a very good small airport, is now the worse airport I have ever been to. Security takes for ever and once you are through security, you are then forced to shuffle through a tiny aisle with hundreds of other people because there are now duty free shops on every side. Once into the main part of the airport you are faced with hundreds of people looking for somewhere to sit. I was travelling at 6am on a Friday morning and it was wall to wall with stressed out passengers. I will avoid this airport at all costs.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: F Williams
content: Hideous experience. Checked in online and opted for baggage drop. Arrived two hours before our flight was due and very poorly and misinformed despite having shown our boarding passes that we had to queue for check in. Horrendous queues there and then again in security. As a result we missed our flight - the first time ever in our lives! No last calls for our names, no advice or cooperation when we informed security that our flight was leaving in 20 minutes. Rebooked flights at great expense to leave 10 hours later in the day - stayed within the airport. Tried to rebook car hire on computers in airport hall at great expense and huge frustration computers keys missing and system ridiculously slow! Internet connection on our phones (different providers) was poor and wholly inadequate. On our return we queued for 1hr 45mins in passport control. We cannot believe how shabby a system of queuing can make anything other than a very bad impression on arriving to England for visitors. Unacceptable and unnecessary attitude observed from staff and a lack of information regarding why there was such a back log and how long the average time of queuing would be didn't help either. We now know never to travel to and or from Stansted again - absolutely the first and last time ever.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Richard Procter
content: I have used Stansted for 15 years and how it has deteriorated. Trying to book car park when an offer was on and could not book - funny how I could book when full rate was applied. Border control on the way home really is upsetting, after sitting on a plane for hours, the last thing anyone wants is a queue for over an hour getting through border control. How come this doesn't happen in Spain? Seriously considering never to use Stansted again - Norwich or Southend may be getting my custom.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: David Turner
content: I thought we were lucky to be able to use this airport as it is so much closer than where we normally fly from - how wrong I was. It is running at far over its capacity. Immigration took us an hour during which there was no explanation or apology. Small children mixed with carry-on cases, average height people like me, slow people, fast people all thrown together in a claustrophobic space. Terrible.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Moor
content: Passport control is an embarrassment. Upon arriving from Egypt in May 2015 we queued for over 90 minutes from midnight. I had my 4 year old and a 3 month old, without pushchairs. We were told that the delay was because we got a cheap flight! A girl had flown alone from Hungary and had a ticket for the train which, by the time she got through, had ended for the day. She won't be flying to Stansted again. June 2015 we waited over an hour and a half to collect someone flying in from France. They won't be returning to Stansted again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Robert Parbs
content: I arrived at Stansted Airport passport control on 27th May. When I entered the queue for non-EU citizens, there were not many people in front of me. However, the time which elapsed from my entering the queue to the time my Australian passport had eventually been duly stamped was 97mins. For the first hour there were two desks being used to process non-EU passport holders but this eventually went down to 1 counter. No one came and explained the problem nor at any stage apologised for the situation. Many passengers became angry and distressed and a number missed ongoing flight connections. Concerned and outraged at the longest wait I had ever experienced in an immigration queue at any airport in the world in over 45 years of travel, I took the opportunity to speak to a passport control supervisor when finally inside the airport. I received what can only be described as a most inadequate explanation, delivered in a highly supercilious and cavalier manner. Apparently they really do not care about the unconscionable delays and have no compunction in showing their contempt for those who do. Avoid this airport if you possibly can.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Peter Maidment
content: Having used STN over many years since the takeover it is now showing a marked decline in service. Outbound, putting all ready stressed passengers through a shopping mall before getting a waiting area that has little or no seating shows the contempt the owners feel about their passengers. Return, taking over one hour to progress through immigration is totally unacceptable immediate improvement are required before I will use STN again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Robert Ryan
content: Arrived Border Control 01.40 on Saturday 20th June 2015. Had to queue 46 minutes to pass through. To the best of my ability I counted only 6 desks open and 9 closed. This is a disgrace.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: James Corbett
content: The new Terminal 2 is overall very good, particulary if you are using the Main Bus Station. The staff were helpful at the automatic check-in machines and the staff at the combined Star Alliance desk checking luggage were professional if not friendly. Things go downhill when you enter Security. A young man bantered with a female passenger and gave me a cursary glance. I didn't feel that the staff were in any way to be trusted with fighting terrorism. I went into WHSmiths to pick up a few items. Three staff were lounging around the cash register chatting and the customers were struggling to use the self-service checkouts. I didn't feel like interrupting their conversation so I did the same. I couldn't scan the items and felt like walking out. A young man appeared and mocked me for not knowing how to use the machine. Customer service is being replaced by self-service which is hardly nice from the point of view of customers. Oh, and a point about the toilets, which I expect we'll be cleaning ourselves soon. I'm traveling. I have bags. I want to use a urinal. There is no shelf or hook or anything to put/hang my stuff on. So I use the dirty floor. I also checked the toilet cubicles. One coat hook but again no shelf or anywhere to place a bag. Is this to cut the risk of people leaving items behind or for security reasons? Again, it's not very nice.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: NJ Wicken
content: I write this review on a National Express coach travelling from the joke that is Stansted passport control. I stupidly went the electronic passport route and it took at least 45 minutes to get through. The result being I missed the last Stansted Express train at 12.30pm for which I had a ticket and had to buy a coach ticket. It has added time and expense to my journey, but it was clear to all of us in the queue that the normal passport control check in was much faster than the supposedly quicker electronic check in. Infuriating. As other people say here, avoid the electronic passport Gates as you will regret it. Terrible boarder control. The worst I have experienced in Europe. Stansted, you are an embarassment to the UK. Avoid if possible.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Linda Brewer
content: Arrived this morning for flight to Berlin and as per usual security was manic. We are both oap's but were shouted at by very impatient staff who treated us like cattle. We were horrified and upset by this incident. We are very widely travelled and consider Stansted to be the worst airport we have ever used - shame on you Stansted

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Tom Smith
content: I arrived from a flight from Greece at Stansted on Tuesday June 16th at 23.30. I have done a lot of travelling around the world in my time but I have never seen a queue as long as the one I suffered at Stansted passport control. What made it worse were the monitors that advertised the wonderful things UK Border were doing for me. At one point it even said they welcomed feedback! Well look around. I am afraid that the UK is a police state in the sense that it prides itself on its security processes but treats its customers like their time is worthless. I will never use Stansted. I second another comment about the departure area being like a bazaar. It is so demeaning to have to struggle along a winding pathway through loads of shops before arriving in a limited seating area surrounded by high priced food shops. Why can't an airport be designed to make my travel experience as painless as possible.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Astrid Sebel
content: Stansted airport Management seem to defy all the basic rules of pax flows and minimum customer service. It doesn´t suffice to take all chairs way from the land side hall to maximise efficiency, nor does it help to apply American queing without any decent directions. Signage is a total disaster, leading to hurdles of confused pax walking around, deprived from all sense of direction. Imagine the scenario I encountered in June, at the start of holiday season, where the inexperienced traveller was trying to find their way to their gate. I understand that Stansted Airport is trying to get their revenue from retail income and parking, but that still isn´t an excuse for this totally failed lay out and not sure if retail is getting their results. Tills don´t show queues, even at peak times, Look there is an advantage here for the pax who are willing to spend some money, but take considerable more time than usual for your flight. Arrival is not even worth spending words. The last 6 times 5 machines out of 15 were open, where 2 of them were not working properly, whilst the man operated stations were trying to attend the massive crowd .Management revise your plan, whilst you still can: Make landside a tiny bit more pleasant (equipment and staff) and do something about the signage, flow and ridiculously high prices. Try to get some retailers in that are hitting your target pax (low budget).

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Paul Harvey
content: Most inefficient airport I have ever been to. I asked an off duty border control officer if this is as bad as it gets and she said no. They've been given 33% more flights and no extra staff. Tip: Use standard queue, not e-passport queue.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Jill ron walker
content: Departure from airport at 4am - noticed new shops making a narrow walkway and no seats to sit down, couldn't eat as no seats, it was heaving with people. At that time of the morning it was chaos. On our return 11th June it was even worse, passport control was awful we queued for 45 mins and that was at electronic passport, the other passport holders were just as bad. It was better organized in Crete airport than here, very disappointed, will try to go from Gatwick or Southend in future.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Smith
content:
Queues at Border Control are unbelievably long, in the past month I landed there twice and I had to queue 45 minutes the first time and 40 minutes the second time. There were a lot of elderly passengers and families with children but there are no seating facilities, no toilets and no water and it was also very hot. There were only
two/three Border control officers with hundreds and hundreds of people queuing, simply unacceptable, if you can please try to avoid landing here. Worst airport in London by far when it comes to Border Control queues.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Goggin
content:
I now know how cattle being herded feel. From getting on the train at Liverpool Street to getting off the flight at Cork Airport it was push and shove and frustration and stress. I pitied anyone with children in the security queue, which took 55 mins to negotiate, with not enough lines for the many passengers. If you have mobility
problems-forget it. The gate number is not put up until almost the flight time which means people were running and pushing along the narrow corridors. Lots of duty free items sold out as were the snacks as my flight was at 20.25 and the shops didn't appear to have been restocked since the morning.  I feel sorry for the staff working there as they must be constantly stressed. Avoid like the plague.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Roberts
content:
I have spent 8 years flying every week or two, mainly around Europe but also the Americas and Pacific rim. During that time I have been through airport security systems over 1000 times in many cities and countries. This morning at Stansted was the worst experience ever. It took nearly an hour from the time I put my hand luggage on the
conveyor. They insisted on checking my sleep apnoea unit separately, probably because the security man had never heard of the condition or the equipment. A first for me. They also insisted on separately scanning a solid deodorant, marketed as not needling to be separately screened. Again, a first. The security guy said they classed
the product as a liquid, even though it is solid, on the grounds that it could be melted to a liquid. I pointed out that this was true of metal as well. I spoke to a supervisor, who said she was a trainer, who produced a similarly illogical mantra. 20 minutes should be the maximum time taken to get through security.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Beswick
content:
Worst Airport in the UK? I have travelled twice in the last 18 months (twice out and twice in) and its a complete nightmare. Charging for drop off is disgusting. What are disabled people supposed to do? Also the entire experience is one giant queue. Queue for check in, queue for security, queue to get through the narrow maze path
that is the new duty-free, then finally end up in an open space to be greeting by a refugee camp scene. No Seats - probably to force you to shop even more. Again, what are people with disabilities of mobility issues supposed to do here? You then queue for an escalator down to a pier, then queue for the toilets (mens). On your way in you queue for ages and ages to get through passport control. Clearly this airport hates its customers. Why are they forcing so many people through a terminal that is not fit for purpose? I vow never to use Stansted again. Vote with your feet I say.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D Williams
content:
Stansted seem to be on a mission to prove they need loads of money to expand, why else would they be so determined to make the experience of flying to or from there so unpleasant? Everything involves a queue, from parking, security, toilets, food, self service tills at WH Smiths and they have replaced all the seating with shops so you
are forced into the overpriced food outlets. Then one hour before your flight you see the Final Call sign flashing telling you to run to some gate half a mile away so you can queue some more. Priority Boarding on Ryanair is great value, if you particularly love spending time standing in dirty corrugated steel tunnels with a stranger's armpit for company. Getting back is even more fun, the queue on June 6th for a 7.30 arrival started at the bottom of the planes steps and ended about two hours later. Don't use the e-passport queue it takes twice the time. Bring a folding stool, a spare battery for your phone and maybe a copy of War and Peace to while away the time with no air conditioning, water, food or hope. Half of the passport facial recognition booths didn't seem to like working in the sun, which makes their placement testament to someone's total incompetence. Fly to Heathrow and at least you won't ruin your holiday with a rubbish conclusion or arrive home enraged from a business trip.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Robert Cooper
content: What a disgustingly grubby airport this is turning into.  From money grabbing parking fees to filthy toilets. Arrivals passport control is a disgrace. 45 minutes resulted in a huge parking bill for my pick up.  I would strongly recommend that you avoid this airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Lydia Romero
content: The e-passport gates at Stansted are beyond a joke. Queues much slower than the traditional passport control. It took an hour to get through them this evening. Stansted needs to seriously rethink this policy. It works in other countries. Why on earth is it such a shambles at Stansted?

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: N Fox
content:
I have unfortunately flown into Stansted three times over the last couple of months once mid morning, once late evening and most recently early evening (around 19.00).  On all 3 occasions I have had to queue over 90-mins to clear passport control.  I have tried the manned desks and the electronic automated gates - no difference just a
long and very frustrating experience.  Will now try to avoid using Stansted an any cost as this is just unacceptable.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Parsons
content: My sister and I arrived at Stansted with 2 hours to spare before our flight on Sunday morning 7 June flying to Cork on the 8.05 am. flight. We were going to a funeral.  We were faced with extremely long queues in security and then had a very long hike to our gate number only to be told when we arrived at the gate that the gate was closing and we could not board the plane. We pleaded with the staff to allow us on the flight (plane still out on tarmac with door open) but to no avail. We were then told we would have to pay £100 each for another flight which we had to accept as we had to go to a funeral but could ill afford. While we were waiting for our new tickets to be issued another couple came to the counter and they also had missed their flight for the same reason. We had to get a flight to Dublin as the next flight into Cork was 4.50 pm.  The staff were very unhelpful and bordering on rudeness.  I will never fly from Stansted again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: V Wells
content: Having arrived at midnight on Tuesday 9th June, I was faced with an hour and twenty minute wait for passport control. Weary and dispirited passengers, moving along like zombies, returning Brits and foreign tourists shuffling through slowly snaking lines. For the elderly, infirm and those with small children, it was close to unbearable.  I see that this is a far from unusual scenario at Stansted.  After this, we had a seemingly interminable ride to the long-stay car park in a bus driven by a driver who struggled to make himself heard and understood over the antiquated/faulty speaker system. All in all, a horrible experience.  I shan't be using Stansted again until and unless things improve, though my wife has just informed me that.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Littlewood
content: This is simply the worst airport in the UK.  They charge £2 just to be able to pick up or drop off a passenger and then the automatic machine overcharged by £20 for the privilege.  Avoid this place if at all possible.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Banks
content: I fly a lot on European business and used to deliberately chose to fly from Stansted but I shall do this no more. Landed today (6th June) from Madrid to be met by a 100 yard queue 6 deep to get to the escalators which were being rationed and held back by staff to prevent you from joining the chaos in passport control. 90 minutes screaming kids in the heat no toilets no water Sadly this is the "new normal" - and the e-passport gates are a joke. Go to Madrid to see how it should be done. The place being half rebuild meant that I arrived very early for my flight as advised because of potential severe delays there was nowhere to sit I just ended up on the floor in a dirty corner.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Lea
content: Never use this airport if you have any mobility issues. 2nd time to experience deplorable service. Omniserve should be ashamed of the service they provide. How they hand pick the staff who work on the desk astounds me. Rude abrupt disrespectful and could not care less. I had even mailed before travelling to ensure that the service was in place. But no they are a shambles and don't waste time complaining as they don't bother responding. If you can't walk up the stairs to a plane they are happy to leave you behind. Shame on you Stansted airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ian Hamilton
content: Possibly the biggest drinks rip-off in the UK! We went to The Cabin (c) bar/restaurant airside. A large glass of house white wine - £9.80! When I queried this I was met with an offhand shrug. It's a ghastly airport at the best of times - poor access for those with mobility problems very few airbridges. Never if possible again!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Z Stefan
content: STN-DUB on Sunday. Flew out from other London airport. Quick walk through the airport since (unlike Dublin Airport) STN is following Common Travel Agreement between UK and ROI where arrivals are treated as domestic flight hence no passport control. In this instance pleasure to arrive to STN but I am dreading my arrival in July through usual route on my way from EU.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Matthew Brown
content: I echo most of the reviews about this airport I usually fly from Southend an easy quick and pleasant experience the reverse of Stansted I parked in the meat and greet as I had two young children  poor signage no trolleys and a 20 minute queue to get in. Security was slow then your led around a never to end amount of shops to be herded into a dirty overcrowded space with no seats luckily though as Stansted is so slow at everything even allowing 2.5 hours on a Europe flight still leaves you short of time and needing to run for the gate hence not having to spend too much time in the dirty seat less waiting space On return you then herded into pens by staff and left waiting an hour to clear customs Then poor signage does little to lead you back to the park aided by unhelpful staff All in all around 2 hours to clear. Avoid the reviews of this Airport are not unjust never flying from here again Southend or Gatwick in the future every time.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Whitelock
content: Arrived last night from Oslo at 7.30pm. Thought immigration would take the usual 10-15 mins using the e-passport system and then be on my way to drive back home 3.5 hrs away. Ended up standing in the queue for 1.5hrs! I joined the e-passport queue reasonably thinking it'd be quicker than the standard queue only to find the standard queue was twice as fast! By the time I realised this I'd been queuing for 45 mins so no point in changing queues - why didn't any airport staff tell me this before joining the slower queue? Absolute shambles. I've done a lot of travelling and this was by far the worst immigration experience I've had.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Christine Ralph
content: I flew out to Cork and will never use this airport again. Agree with all of the negative comments and it was hell on earth there! When I went through security I had to remove wedding rings earrings watch etc. I am used to having to remove items of jewellery and don't normally object to this. I told them my bracelet would not come off as has been on my wrist since I was 10 years old. It was obvious that's what was beeping but the lady insisted on searching me 3 times. Very undignified and unnecessary. My partner and I found a seat in Starbucks and stayed there until our flight was due to leave. Coming home we walked straight through no body there to even glance at passports. Meet and Greet found our car but others were not so lucky. Pleased to escape!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Mason
content: Worst airport by far extremely overcrowded which means you have to queue for everything for at least 15-20 minutes including the toilet. Also Stansted long stay car park is overpriced and the most disorganised parking I have ever seen had to wait 30 minutes for the bus then eventually told the bus could not get to the stop so had to walk 10 minutes to the bus then stand on an overcrowded bus clinging on as it travelled 15 minutes to the car park round several roundabouts! Absolute chaos from start to finish.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Tony Slade
content: What a shambles! Having experienced Manchester Airport (who own Stansted) I was optimistic about security queues efficient M&G car parking. However there were only 4 security desks open. One waits in a scruffy waiting area before the gate information appears and this leaves you with a very long hike with seemingly little time. Passport queues on return (June 3rd) were farcical with the e-passport machines being temperamental. My car's radio had been re-tuned. The driver's seat was covered in hairs. The airport desperately needs two terminals. I wish I could meet an airport Director and take him/her on a walk and give a commentary on what I witnessed and experienced. He/she would be ashamed.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Stephen Harper
content: Just returned from Dublin to London Stansted on 2 June at apx 5pm. Our flight contained many nationalities as was obvious from overheard conversations. I was amazed to find no passport control in use! No staff present! Everyone just walked straight through! It's reassuring to know how efficient border control is - not! Border control yesterday was a joke!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Grimwood
content: 30/5/15. Arrived back in the UK and had to queue for the train to the terminal explained as planned work and a two carriage train will be the next one as you can imagine this was absolutely filled to capacity as everyone pushing to get on. Then the hell of passport control and an hours queue due to travelling with under eighteen's as they cannot use the e-gates. The desks available were not fully manned which caused excessive queue time as appalling staffing levels. All the technology in the world and cannot plan for passenger numbers. Surely they know how many planes/ passengers are arriving it's beyond belief that an organisation can be run so inefficiently and get away with it. The staff are not overly helpful customer focussed or know how to treat people with common courtesy. Queues were the same when returning to Stansted in February. Will use a different airport in future due to the complete chaos.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D Johnston
content: I've always been under the impression that airports have some future visibility of the likely passenger numbers passing through passport control on any given day/time. Apparently this isn't the case as there surely can be no other reason why immigration is the shambolic de-humanising farce that it is. Interminably long meandering queues with virtually no staff visible. Lines of tired hot aggravated and in some cases confused passengers trying to get out of this awful awful airport getting frustrated and demoralised. I reckoned there were upwards of 800 maybe 1000 people being herded at 8pm on a Wednesday. For international flights I will do everything I can to avoid this soul destroying place.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: David Bunn
content: Arrived back from spotless Palma PMI airport at around 1.20am today via Easyjet. Rail transit to terminal not working so cabin crew had to request a bus - 20 mins+ wait for it to arrive. No baggage trolleys in baggage reclaim families with small children struggled. Ladies toilet in arrivals hall out of order queues to use disabled facility. The experience at this airport seems to get worse every time queues at departure security terrible even at the priority line. They just seem to be focussed on the duty free shopping 'experience'. What a welcome to the UK.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Steve Keeble
content: Arrived from Madrid to be greeted by a horrendous queue for Passport control both standard and electronic gates which is under government control who frankly don't care and can just say "tough" and genuinely what can we do? Then packed onto a bus like sardines which must have breached every health and safety rule in the book. All these complaints though will not improve anything the major airports have an effective "monopoly" and really don't care because they know that despite what we say if we want to fly sometimes Stansted is the only option.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Harper
content: I have travelled for years from Stansted and can only say that it has declined beyond belief. I flew out on 27 May and can only say that passengers are herded like cattle at security. Once through you are then met by an airport reminiscent of something from the Soviet block 30 years ago. The place was filthy no proper floor covering seats well beyond there sell by date and overpriced caterers. In all not a pleasant experience.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Keyworth
content: Never again will I use Stansted. The new layout funnels you past every shop then at end next to no seating no chance to get to gate early. This used to be best airport in London now it is the worst by far. I travel to Tallinn a lot and will drive the extra to Gatwick in future. Massive queue for passport control on arrival home seems the border agency have a point to prove asking people to remove glasses etc and generally working far slower than in other airports.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ross Worthington
content: Since the airport was bought by Manchester Airports Group in early 2013 the customer experience has deteriorated markedly. I gather that in commercial terms they paid too much for it and now are scrambling to recoup the money from the unfortunate traveller. I know they are spending lots of money revamping the terminal but so far it has all been aimed at parting you from your money and none of it on passenger comfort.
