Thus there is a shiny new "duty free" shopping area through which you have to meander before you arrive at the new food outlets. There is hardly any seating and even at off-peak times it feels dirty and crowded. There are queues everywhere- to get through security through the shopping area to get on the shuttle or walk to the gates and (when you get back) to struggle through passport control. I am a frequent traveller and have no real choice but if you can travel from any other airport my advice is that you do so!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Adam Stewart
content: I flew from Stansted airport recently a week ago to be exact and can honestly say the place is a pit. All I can say is avoid. The beautiful building Norman Foster designed and laid out is now nothing more than a Northern Supermarket look-a-likey with swinging signs hanging from the ceiling in check-in areas which may as well say "beans half price" as they actually relate to nothing in the building. There is also a passenger entry system to security which is just about as hidden as the secret garden whoever designed that needs to go back to design school who actually paces a key entry point in a corner hidden behind a wall. Once through check-in the departure lounge has very little seating and does not instil the wish to shop. I travelled with my young family and the experience we had trying to seat eat and enjoy was poor. Boarding the mono rail from the departure lounge is nothing more than a serious accident waiting to happen. With all flights being called at once the rush was mad. I have saved the best till last security - what a farce. Rude staff and slow processes make for a very poor experience. As you can see the worst part of my break was the airport experience its not hard to get it right. Unfortunately Stansted you have a long way to go to win back my custom and get it right.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Shirley Grimwood
content: 30/5/15. Know when you are back in the UK - first had to queue and wait for a train to the terminal building. Then the hell of passport control queuing to get through not helped by having just 4 desks open and a plane full of passengers just wanting to get home nor being able to take children (16 & 11) through the E gates. What is the point of issuing e-passports if they cannot use them. Also not helped by the lack of customer service skills by the staff who said to a sixteen year old "Oi mate are you eighteen" when going to the e-gates. Took an hour to get through-unacceptable. Why are the desk not fully manned as they know how many passengers/planes are landing? Fully appreciate the need for security but this should not be at the expense of customer service. Also queued in February so looks as though an ongoing issue.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Sam Yeager
content: It is hard to believe an airport like this is allowed to operate as it does. It is clear that this airport is the result of saving money at the cost of any customer service or customer facilities. There are hardly enough seats for anyone to sit at a peak time the seats are uncomfortable and this is specifically designed this way so you will visit one of their many restaurants which also are the only places where there are any outlets to charge your devices. On top of this rude tactic to bring in customers they have their reserved area which costs 25 pounds to go in just for the time you are there which is ridiculous. There are plenty of more seats and shops near the gates however they don't inform you of which gate you are at until just before your flight time. Because of all of these things I will never use Stansted Airport again if I ever fly again and it runs the chance of going through there I would gladly pay triple to avoid it.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Sims
content: Coming back a few days ago at 4.30pm the queues for immigration were horrendous and there was a loud collective groan from passengers alighting from the shuttle train. The queues for E-passports went on and on and it took 45 minutes and for the non-E passports it took about 55. Needless to say not all the booths were manned and the attitude of the Border Control staff (or whatever they call themselves nowadays) was dismissive and downright rude. When I complained and said that this was unacceptable and that there should at least be separate queues for older people or families with children or those with claustrophobia three bored-looking immigration staff watching the endless queue at E-passoprt control one of them (whilst chewing gum) said 'Ave you gotta problem mate with this?' and the other said 'well it's busy aint it!' and looked at me as if to say how dare I complain. So that's alright then! Stansted at busy times of the day is a disaster at security check-in and a disaster at arrivals immigration (and they are hoping for long-haul Thomson Dreamliners stuffed to the gills in the near future. Despair at what used to be a pleasant airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Gary Heather
content: Arrived from Madrid 26/5/15 and took 90 mins to get through passport control. Many of the e-passport gates not working poor assistance for passengers experiencing difficulties and no information given. It was chaotic enough through the airport on the outward leg of the journey - this was worse. Conscience dictated that we pay an additional charge to the taxi driver waiting to pick us up. Having read the reviews below I am left wondering if any attempt at all is being made to remedy the situation.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K B Brewster
content: Bad to worse. Emergency e-mail from Ryanair today telling me to be at Stansted at least 2 hours before departure. Must be completely gone to pot at this place. Last time I was at Stansted it was absolutely dire. Only around 5 belts open staff very thin on the ground. It's been cut to the bone at this place worse than third world country airport. Email stated that Ryanair had been advised of potential security delays at London Stansted airport between 21st and 31st May 2015 and were asking customers travelling on these days to arrive at the airport as early as possible preferably 2 hours before their scheduled flight departure time.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Charles Stephens
content: No comments here on this page about the recent chaos at Meet & Greet parking. Arrived on time and pre-booked on 21 May. Stationary queue to get through entry gate for 30 minutes (the back of which was completely blocking the main loop road). Once at Reception only one member of staff dealing with lost keys misplaced cars etc so the queue was out of the office door. Waited 20 minutes then had to leave key on the counter with a Post It note with the registration and no receipt. Although we got our car back immediately on return on 24 May our travelling companions were told their car had still not been brought back from the off-site store and would be about an hour. There were about twenty people waiting with similar stories: one had been told it would be two hours and another had been advised to get a rental car. Sent two emails to the "contact us" section of the website but despite receiving the automatic reply thanking me for my "valuable feedback" I have not received an explanation. Potentially then an hour to get in and park then another hour to get out. This is before any subsequent issues at Security. Avoid for the time being.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Harris
content: 20 minutes sat on plane after landing because nobody was expecting us! Followed by 1 hour queue yesterday at border control 27th may from 4pm-5pm. Pay attention when you arrive and you can be in the short queue! Very unfair and that is the airports fault!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Frances Holman
content: Stansted airport has become a nightmare it used to be a very user friendly airport. I use it on a regular basis and now the lay out and parking seem to change on a weekly basis. I went through on the 23rd April returning on 3rd May and again on the 9th returning on the 23rd May. The pick up is extremely stressful for someone with mobility problems I was charged £20 because I couldn't walk fast enough to meet my son who was picking me up they have done away with the pick up carpark which used to be where the Orange carpark now is.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Susan Chadwick
content: Outgoing: Used Stansted for the first time 17 May 2015. My husband and I arrived 3 hours early. The queues at check in were horrendous. The security queue was 10 times worse. Three flights going out at almost the same time. Hundreds of stressed people nearly missing their flights. Young and very old suffering hell. Few staff zero efficiency cattle are not treated this way! Incoming: Stansted passport control is a joke somewhere in the region of 700 people queuing many many foreigners and British nationals waiting over an hour and a half.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: V Ahlstrom
content: Since recent partial upgrade dislike the long walk through highly priced stores necessities and reasonable snack facilities might be more appreciated! Flying out last week went fairly well with security and baggage checks within reasonable time frame. The return last Saturday 23rd was terrible the plane was slightly late but after disembarking passengers were herded into corridors and up stairs because the main entry hall was packed full. There was little explanation or apology. My sister and I felt very stressed because of this whilst we had to shuffle along it felt like we were seen as cattle being herded. No toilet facilities along route no seating and no one to help if necessary. To be processed out took almost an hour almost missed train connection! How many people did? This truly was a horrible end to a holiday it needs sorting out.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Paul McCue
content: Just made a firm pledge to never use Stansted again. 20 minutes wait for a (packed like sardines) bus from Mid- stay car park. Then - while I accept there are building works going on at present to have so little space that literally hundreds of people are sitting on the floor on a Friday morning (22nd May 2015) at 5 am is ridiculous. And on return the next day there's no excuse whatsoever for the 10-15 minute queue for the escalator from the gate (poor design/layout/provision) and especially for the massive queue for Border Control - 35 minutes at 11.30pm on a Saturday night. It's not the first time I've encountered such a queue but I'm determined it will be the last. I travel all over the world and I can't think of any worse airport experience than this.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Kenny Alexander
content: An appalling departures area. There was clearly some work in progress but nevertheless the area was packed with passengers and getting a seat to sit on whilst waiting was impossible. Much better after the train journey to the boarding gate area. It would have been much more sensible to move passengers to this area earlier rather than waiting in an overcrowded departures lounge until the flight is called.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Fleming
content: Just arrived back from Amsterdam on a Wednesday night and over an hour to get through the automatic or E passports. A total shambles. What is it like at peak holiday time or bank holidays. Went into Amsterdam on Monday night and I waited about 60 seconds to get through passport control which was manned. Stansted is now a complete mess - don't use it.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Saward
content: What on earth is going on today 17th May 2015 - I use the airport every 2-3 weeks today queues to get through to security were the worst I have ever seen. Total mess and little organisation. Fairly speedy through hoards of people at security and then panic! Virtually every flight was showing final call even though most still had a 40 minute window - people running and panicking to the gates only to be put in a 30 minute queue - what was going on. People were so stressed this was unnecessary and pointless. Many flights missed due to the chaos at security - embarrassment at Stansted is global.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Lavender
content: Avoid. Arriving at 12.45 am we had to wait for nearly an hour to get through passport control. Only 5 of the 16 Biometric controls open so queues were back nearly to the doors.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Pease
content: Prompt processing on arrival is still luck of the draw from the number of cars operating on the terminal shuttle route to the number of Border Security agents on duty and the number of functioning E-Gates. I was surprised to hear a security marshaller shouting at straggling passengers doing the 'loop' waiting for their queue - 'I'm not shouting at you but' and then making a remark that he didn't want the system to descend into chaos! Security staff working hard at 5 am but doing so speedily and with a pleasant attitude. Shopping area is still dire but the food/waiting area is dark has no consistent flooring and has the feeling of being in a pen of doomed cattle waiting for the abattoir as they crowd to watch the screen to find out where their gate might be albeit in an hour's time. More importantly this is the first week of the Car Rental Village where all the previous 'on airport' companies (Hertz Avis Budget Europcar and Enterprise) are now in an area away from the airport requiring a shuttle bus trip of about 10 mins. These buses run approx every 10 mins except between 1 am and 4 am (or so I was told). This 'village' concept is becoming a regular feature of airport planning but means you have to allow even more time for your trip from the airport and returning your hire car to the airport (prior to check- in/bag drop/security/retail therapy) which is unwelcome at the best of times even more so with a 06H00 departure. On this occasion Hertz acquitted themselves very well but I'd hate to do this in the depths of winter.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Dave Cornwell
content: When opened this was a fine Airport but now lags behind most UK and Worldwide airports with the exception of the awful Heathrow. Queuing times and parking are beyond a joke. You can get a 2 hour flight from Europe and then queue for an hour to get through immigration. Last night there were just two personnel on passport control at Immigration arrival! The parking for pick up and drop off is worse than Draconian. If you want to pick up someone the only place you can stop is the Express drop off and pick up or if you are lucky enough to find one open the Short Stay car park. The former costs £2 for a 10 minute window but you can't leave your vehicle to look for someone! Then if you go over 10 mins they charge you £2 per minute! Yes £2 per minute. Bearing in mind the queues to get out (see above) this makes pick up virtually impossible. If you realise there is a delay and leave if you come back within 30 minutes you get fined Â£20. You couldn't make it up. It is an absolute National disgrace.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Helen Devries
content: I had an early morning flight to Valencia so took the coach from London and waited in the seating area until two hours before my flight time. Something has to be done about organising the queues to check in desks advertised are not all open and the member of staff organising the lines and pulling out passengers for flights leaving imminently was not efficient. Passing through security was a dream - fast efficient and friendly but the long trek through a duty free and then up hill and down dale to the gate for the flight was more of a nightmare - corridors which close to one lane causing bottlenecks for example. The airport was clean and pleasant the staff obliging but thanks top the check in chaos and the trek to the gate it took me all of the two hours to get to the gate.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Turner
content: This was my first time using Stansted. Parking was straightforward and a shuttle bus came after less than 5 minutes. Security was busy but the line was moving quickly. I got through in under 15 minutes. The departure area is nothing more than a shopping mall and rather pricey food outlets. Ryanair say that the gate closes 30 minutes before the flight but until 30 minutes beforehand you will not know which gate to go to then you will have to run. On my return I was through immigration in 20 minutes using the electronic scanner. A car park shuttle bus was waiting. All in all far better than I was expecting.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Byers
content: Beware if you are making a connection from a flight outside the UK to another flight. There is no way of doing this without leaving arrivals and going through security again (which could take quite a long time) and walking for miles. This means the time taken could be anything from two and a half hours upwards. Surely there could be a way for connecting without starting again as there is in any other airport I have passed through. People arriving from abroad and not knowing this could easily miss their ongoing flights.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: David Silver
content: Another trip to the uncivilised hole that is Stansted Airport! If you are tired and agitated after getting to the airport parking and getting a transfer to the Terminal and passing through security you are insulted by being forced to walk what seems forever through a parade of shops selling overpriced goods. You can't avoid it - you've to go through it. Once past that you eventually come out into the concourse where the masses are herded together to be preyed upon by the next set of vultures selling even more expensive poor value food and drink. If you make good time you wait and wait until your airline puts up the gate you are to go to - usually with Ryanair five or ten minutes before the gate is scheduled to close. All you want to do is make your way to the gate and sit and relax but you can't do it. Instead you have to sit if you are lucky to get a seat in the dreadful old fashioned cattle pen provided by whoever runs the airport anxiously looking at the departure screen.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D O'Brien
content: We travel regularly and use Stansted as it is the nearest airport to us. The passport control on returning to the UK is ridiculous we now have a electronic passport and the queue is smaller but even then it is rare that all the booths are working. The queue for the normal passport which you have to use if you have children with you is horrendous I would estimate that it is usually a 2hour wait and often 3 hours. Stansted have got to do something about this. On the last occasion airport staff were not even letting people into the area as there were too many people there and they were holding them back in the corridors. There is no assistance for older travellers who have to stand and wait I did mention this once to the passport control as there was a very old lady in front of us they said if they asked they would have been sent to the front of the queue but many are visiting. Please Stansted get your act together. I actually think that that may people having to wait so long especially with children may be a health and safety issue.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Anna Goodman
content: Embarrassing for a country like England having to wait over an hour in passport control queues! Landed from Turin just after 11 am and it was total disaster. A member of staff rudely shouting orders young children and elderly waiting in line tired and upset only 4 people checking passports when there are 18 posts. Don't they know how many planes land? Are they all on their elevenses break? It was a Wednesday: what it is like at weekends half term or holiday periods I don't even want to imagine. Total disgrace.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Violante
content: This isn't a developed country airport is more like a third world airport. The flight arrived on time from Lisbon on Saturday 25/04/2015 at 11.30 pm and then the nightmare started took over 1 hour and 30 minutes to reach the passport control. Hundreds of people queuing too many people for a tiny and close space.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Peter Brown
content: Use a different airport if at all possible. Queuing times are horrendous. For example it took well over an hour to go through passport control. I do not understand why the airport management just does not look at how any other airport in the world is run and just copy what they do. There are plenty of staff milling around the gantries while one person processes hundreds of passports and visas etc. If a person in front has some kind of dodgy ID or visa it holds the queue up for the hundreds of people behind. The airport is also dirty. Normally I wouldn't mind about this so much as generally airports are just functional and I try to spend as little time in them as possible - but in my recent experience I spent far longer in some queue or other than the flight took.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Vicky Loveard
content: What a diabolical mess. Whoever is in charge of Stansted should be ashamed. It used to be a great experience using Stansted now it's a massive chore. The refurbishment has been very poorly thought out and nothing flows. Security is pitiful. Sunday 26th April 11.45pm was total chaos. Over 1 hour to get through passport control is not acceptable. There were people who missed the last train because of your incompetence. The electronic gates take far too long there aren't enough of them and they weren't all operational. Lack of power sockets lack of seating and being herded though the shops to get to the gates is ridiculous. I always used to choose Stansted over Heathrow or Gatwick. I won't be in future. You need to start looking at these reviews and taking some action!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D C Sibley
content: Visiting Stansted airport was again a very disappointing experience. The new shops don't seem an improvement possibly a waste of money which could have been spent on keeping the airport cleaner and to provide more staff to assist people. The toilets were unclean on returning the walkways were dirty with rubbish everywhere. To get through customs people with new passports were directed to massive queues with only a few gates open. Two people were on hand but they just stood pointing and gave no assistance to people when their passport wouldn't scam! They only offered help to non - English speakers! No trolleys were available to carry luggage or staff anywhere to be seen! Such a disappointment considering the service we received at the small airport at Fuerteventura! Management should consider visiting this airport and Lucca in Malta to compare. Stansted is unfriendly dirty and a disgrace to Britain.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Mark Crowther
content: I think Stansted is a good airport overall. There are improvements being done to the shops and cafe which are already making the experience more to the level expected. As much as I'd rather not have to walk through duty free I get it. The security heading out of the UK is much improved especially with the new multi-person conveyor belts. They have them in Edinburgh airport and it makes the process far quicker. However regarding Arrivals security its a mess - as with other reviews mine is s typical story. Landed at 12.05am on Sunday 26th April and on arrival at passport control the hall was completely full. As always to the left we could hear the e-passport gates siren going off as a failed scan happened and to the right the half full line for non-EU arrivals. For us EU and UK citizens it took 20 minutes just to get from the off-loading area of the shuttle train to the point of being in the queue. It then took just shy of an hour to get through security others were tweeting the same so it wasn't just my bad timing. Half way through one of the UK Border staff wandered off (break time?) and 3 gathered around a desk with an issue with a passenger. I overheard people talking about just pushing through and maybe if we all start jeering. If this took place anywhere else there'd be a near riot being an airport people are contained let's hope peoples frustration remains verbal. The double whammy for anyone trying to travel late at night is the Stansted Express train finishes at 12.30am so the 3 or 4 plane loads of passengers have no chance of using it. Good job the coaches are available. But be warned they are NOT family friendly and the queue to buy tickets is often long with just 2 staff to serve customers. Your option from there is a taxi from inside the airport. But be prepared to pay around £100 to get to central London. I travel through Stansted almost every week and the story is pretty much the same. A good airport well served with facilities outbound security and transport ruined by an atrocious arrivals security. a) Get more staff checking passports (set a time limit from arrival to processing and publish if you hit/miss it) b) increase EU/UK staff and reduce non-EU staff due to volume of arrivals c) let families through in a priority lane you then switch to other passengers no one will mind people already usher families with crying babies through anyway.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: RA Zala
content: I arrived at Stansted at around 8 pm on Wednesday 22nd April. While Stansted airport is in itself quite adequate the arrangements at arrival passport control are a national disgrace. Whomever installed and passed as fit for purpose the new electronic scanning system should be ashamed. The system simply does not work properly. In my experience not only has the queuing time been extended but when one eventually arrives at the scanning "stalls" the scene is chaotic. Some of the machines were seemingly out of order a "sergeant major" type was valiantly but not always successfully directing people to available stalls creating an atmosphere of near panic; once in the stalls many people including my wife and myself could not be successfully scanned. In my own case I'd all but given up after three scans and had called for assistance when the gate unexpectedly let me through. My wife was not so fortunate and the scanner failed entirely in its purpose causing yet more delay when she had to reverse out of the stall and go through a manual check point along with others who had experienced the same problem. I should perhaps say that our appearances have not changed from our passport photographs which were issued recently.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Jan Carney
content: What have you done to the duty free? After waiting ages to get through security at 8am having to take boots belts coats etc off then put them all back on again all we were aiming for was a coffee and breakfast. We then had to walk for what seemed ages through the duty free to get to any restaurant. After breakfast we intended to buy perfume and after shave but quite honestly couldn't be bothered to walk back to duty free. The girls working there seemed bored as nobody seemed to be stopping to even look. A big mistake as I am sure you can tell by your drop in sales? The design and layout is completely flawed. I am sure I am not the only one with this opinion. We use this airport purely because of the location to where we live.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ian Silva
content: In my experience Stansted airport is without doubt the worst airport in London. Being a regular traveller having used this airport on several occasions in the past two years since Manchester Airports Group took over its ownership the quality of service and efficiency have deteriorated markedly. Understaffing particularly at security combined with high passenger volumes means the queues are lengthy snaking out into the check in area. This situation exists at all times of the day often with several hundred people waiting. I have spent nearly an hour just to get through security particularly at early morning when many flights depart. In addition the staff are rude and dismissive to passengers shouting at people and being disrespectful. After passing through security passengers are herded like cattle through a seemingly endless narrow winding path forced to pass shopping aisles on either side. This creates a bottleneck by slowing passengers down ensuring there is no option to speedily get to the gates. Manchester Airports Group seem hell bent on doing everything possible to increase revenues by cutting costs through understaffing and turning this airport into a shopping mall. If I want to go shopping in an airport it should be my choice. Why should I risk missing my flight because this company thinks an airport should feel like Oxford Street in the week before Christmas all year round. Once you have escaped this and boarded the plane you can look forward to your return to the UK arriving to massive delays at immigration. Also the electronic passport gates often are not fully operational and those that are open do not work properly. I would not be surprised if they use this "opportunity" to place shops there while people queue to leave. By comparison Gatwick airport is a model of efficiency. It is well organised with courteous staff even when busy. I have flown in and out of Gatwick over a dozen times this year alone with no delays or problems departing or arriving. Today my destination in Asturias Northern Spain has only one direct flight a day unfortunately from Stansted. If there is another choice of airport it is worth avoiding Stansted if you want a relaxing stress free journey.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Farrell
content: What an awful place! Our flight landed from Italy at 23.20 on Sat night 18th. We finally arrived in baggage hall at 01.00 on Sun morning 19th! Took 1 hr 40 mins to get through passport control. Hundreds of passengers herded in a corridor for over an hour - totally unacceptable at midnight to keep passengers standing for that length of time many of them elderly or with fractious toddlers and babies. There has to be a huge safety issue with this. Then when we leave the corridor and arrive into actual passport control hall we have to join hundreds more passengers queuing. The automatic checking machines are a disaster there were more red crosses than green arrows. It took forty minutes to get through there. If Stansted cannot cope with these volumes of passengers (and clearly from reading previous reviews it cannot) then why oh why are so many flights allowed to land at the same time? I don't hold a British passport but most of the passengers around me did to think they had to put up with these delays to get into their own country where they live and pay taxes - ridiculous carry-on.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Anu Mehta
content: At 2356 hours on the 21st April there are 400 people or more standing in the hall ways leading up into the terminal. Wait to get to official passport contr area around 1 hour. If Stansted have visibility of all inbound flights why is the business intelligence not being used to cater for the incoming travellers. The knock on effects to additional journeys home cat parking fees and general exhaustion should be transparently compensated for. This is the 2nd time in a month I've used this airport both times similar experiences.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Turner
content: Totally unacceptable. What do we pay taxes for when desks are not open in peak time school holidays? Returning to UK from Spain at lunchtime Saturday 18th April. The passport control queue was consistently around 400 people served by only 14 desks open. We were herded like cattle and it took 40 minutes to get through. The automatic gates are not open to any person travelling with minors. There is no explanation about why this is the case. Surely one person could be on duty to attend with those travelling with children who need to get through quickly after a long flight. My son who has a different surname was asked this question while standing next to me "how do you know this lady you are travelling with?". On previous occasions I have been told that "women like me make things very difficult for immigration staff and it's a good job I can see that he looks like you".

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Christine Gostling
content: What a great shame that Stansted airport has become somewhere I would now actively avoid and choose to fly from anywhere but there. I found the whole experience quite a horror story. Staff numbers are minimal and those that were around were less than helpful or happy. Entering security was appalling there was no method of queuing and people just moved along in a throng very politely considering the circumstances. When arriving at the end the security staff were rude and discourteous shouting at passengers and ordering them around I asked a simple question and was made to feel stupid. This is something I rarely encounter these days and I travel frequently and encounter staff who are helpful happy and make you feel as if you are really welcome at the airport. I never complain but always compliment unfortunately in this instance I found nothing to compliment.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Dow
content: Horrible. Customer comfort has been put second to shop space. No lounge. Couldn't find a free power socket. Scared to leave my seat to go to the loo.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: F Rasmussen
content: Not at all impressed with Stansted airport tonight! After arriving at Stansted at 23.25 it took more than an hour to get through security and passport controls before I could even make it to the baggage collection area. It was so crowded and delayed I was wondering if there was a security issue bit I don't think so. Stansted it seems were short staffed during the busy holiday period and didn't have enough staff to cover the night shift.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Buckman
content: Waited for 1.5 hours in the early hours of this morning kettled in tunnels leading from the plane to border control. When we actually reached the hall we were then told off because we had biometric passports and should have 'read the instructions and got through faster'! As we were physically stopped from moving ahead I would like to know what we could have done! If this is part of Theresa Mays initiative I think someone should tell her there's an election soon and I don't take kindly to being prevented from entering the country I live in! Appalling and unnecessary way to deal with travellers.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Stephenson
content: Well I should have known better. Came home from Italy last night. Greeted with 1.5 hour wait to get through border controls. Apparently due to excess demand because of the delays caused by French traffic controllers on strike. I knew this was going to happen on Tuesday surely someone might have had the foresight to put extra people on the check points to help ease the situation. At 1 point. 3 flights queuing and 5 yes just 5 check points open. Not the front line guys problems.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Biles
content: The Airport has quickly changed under its new ownership from being the best London airport to the worst. In particular the new reorganisation of the departures lounge is appalling - forcing all passengers to walk through the duty free shopping is causing delays and gives no opportunity for people to relax. It is a cynical and blatant attempt to increase shopping revenue at the cost of customer convenience. Are they running an airport or IKEA? The transfer shuttle is late and constantly only 1 compartment. Everything about the airport has deteriorated. It is a miracle that there are not punch-ups between passengers trying to get to their flights.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Bonamico
content: Coming back on a late flight started queuing at 0030 and got through passport control 1 hour later! Only 4 staff to screen thousand of passengers many with young children who cant be even carried on buggies as the airlines don't return these immediately after landing. It would make a lot of sense to have a fast track lane for families with children as would make the whole process a lot faster. I like this airport as convenient to Cambridge but it is really understaffed at customs! btw there's many e-passport gates but only a few work at a time so not much better there either.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Ahmed
content: I don't think I have been to a worse Airport in the UK and actually I've realised how could some of our regional Airports in the UK are! This airport is in a clear sorry state I generally enjoy flying and don't mind Airports for the most part but the experience here was utterly joyless. Firstly the Terminal as you walk in it is dark dingy and cramped with poor signage - not very clear where particular check-in desks are located. Then there is the zoo that is security I've been to third-world countries where security has been managed better - it was chaotic with enormous snaking queues which barely any staff controlling the masses of people going through security or to give any assistance. If you were running late you would have been stuck and most likely miss your flight. Once through security airside is no better again dark dingy and cramped with barely any natural light entering the building. Surprisingly there were some nice food outlets like a Leon but the environment is so poor and devoid of any joy you wouldn't want to linger here for long. At the Gate it is even worse decrepit waiting area with gates cramped next to each other and only a common seating area to wait for multiple gates which was obviously not enough room for the 3 flights taking off at the same time. This Airport clearly needs some serious investment - it hasn't got any hope of competing with the likes of Gatwick and Heathrow and is already at a disadvantage because of its location I would have thought some effort would have been made to actually encourage more passengers. I'm sorry to say but this is the first time an Airport has actually put me off from flying - it is unacceptable in this country to have third-world like airport especially when it is supposed to be serving what is the capital of the world. I will stick to Gatwick Heathrow and City if I fly or the train which was the alternative as was the case for this domestic trip.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: L Watt
content: An absolute disgrace in departure security today two days before Easter holidays I had to queue for an hour to get through hundreds of crowded stressed and angry passengers with no help just awful shouting security staff at the security belts. I appreciate they have to upgrade or fix the security belts but why only have 3 belts open at such a busy holiday time! Total madness. There were zero staff controlling the masses of people just snaking round for an hour trying to get through. Nobody to help or fast track an office of 3 people just looking at the scene. Useless announcements telling us what to do in order not to miss our flight which is a joke the ridiculous queues cause that themselves! The staff at the belts were curt and abrupt I was told by a remake to lift my own trays as her back hurt. Flights were missed mine almost and even when I tried to go through to the front as my flight was boarding a very rude female told me to go back it wasn't her fault of course not! Silly me nobody takes responsibility here for chaos and we are just the mugs that have to endure such rubbish service. Absolute shambles and disgrace to be British today. It is not rocket science just queue control surely.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ken Moore
content: Having to fly from Stansted airport is a truly unpleasant experience. We had to add an extra bag at the last minute which involved paying Ryanair a surcharge. After waiting about 45 minutes at the help desk and watching staff disappear for about 10 minutes at a time or watching them have long phone chatty conversations and apparently achieving nothing I complained. This was greeted with rude dismissal by a young women manning the desk. We only managed to get the bag paid for by going to a different aisle. This is not service. We were then subjected to aggressive rudeness at the security check by a member of staff managing the supply of boxes for the scanner. In this case I made a compliant to his manager who appeared to take it seriously. Finally there was a walk through a huge shopping mall largely void of customers to arrive at an overcrowded departures area. The problems here are compounded by only announcing the departure gate 15 minutes before closure thus keeping passengers in the food and shopping areas as long as possible. This then results in a dash to the departure gate. Stansted airport is both a stressful and chaotic place. Never again!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Wendy Barron
content: Travelled recently and on arrival had to wait 1.5 hours before our Ryanair Bag drop opened. There was no seating available near the bag drop facilities and the only place to sit was on the heating vents near the windows - not acceptable. There should be some seating available for passengers whilst waiting in this area. We are both in our 70s and standing for that time is really beyond our comfort zone.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Shead
content: During the days of BAA there were always queues at busy times going through security checking. However the longest I had ever to wait was around 30 minutes. Today (1st of April 2015) I waited 50 minutes and was still nowhere near the front of the queue. If I had not complained to one of the check-in managers I would have had to wait for over 1 hour and would inevitably have missed my flight. In-fact there were people in the queue who when their flight was checked had missed their flight. Why was this you might ask. Well when I approached one member of staff I was told it was down to the volume of people! Come on Manchester Airports group its the Easter break! The reason was that out of 18 or so security check in positions only 6 where opened and manned. I was then told they just can't get the staff as nobody wants to work there well which is it? When asked whether the flights would be held a member of staff said the airlines were aware of the situation which was not true as when I arrived within seconds of my flight being closed nobody at that desk knew anything about the problem at the security check-in. Stansted was sold to Manchester Airport Group to break-up a supposed monopoly BAA had over flights and passengers. This was supposed to be for our benefit so we were notâripped off and there was more competition. On the contrary. Costs at Stansted have rocketed since the take-over and the whole customer experience has plummeted. With little or no choice of airports living close to Norwich I am probably stuck with Stansted. However I'll think twice about whether I could do my journey some other way in the future.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Philip Butterworth
content: I live in Spain and work in London so travel every week. Unfortunately my wife booked a number of early morning Ryanair flights from Stansted. Security is the proverbial cattle market with long queues shuffling up and down seemingly endless rows to go through. I have a Priority Pass to the private lounge which made the experience just about bearable. The lounge was stupidly located at the end of one of the pods which was a nightmare if your plane was departing from one of the others. However this one little joy was terminated in January when they allowed it to close before they had even commenced building its replacement in the main terminal. My wife came to England for a week and got the whole 5am Stansted experience she has promised never to book me through Stansted again when these flights run out. The Airport management is a shambles and it is without doubt the worst airport I have ever had the misfortune to fly from.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Lowde
content: If you want an inefficient airport that is now so lacking in basic functionality it is no longer fit for purpose then look no further than Stansted Airport. Rather than concentrate on providing a service appropriate for an air passenger Stansted airport has now switched its function to operate seemingly as a Retail Park. Sure there are flights but it's a gruelling and deeply unpleasant mission to catch one. Passengers stand in queue after queue at inadequately manned check in desks before being shouted at and herded like cattle through confused multiple queues for a chaotic baggage check system. Passengers then find themselves lost in a long meandering and confused shopping mall experience squeezing amongst gaps in perfume counters to try and make their way to the departure lounge. Passengers are then spewed stressed and exhausted into an overwhelming chaotic and confused departure lounge crammed with a plethora of eating opportunities yet without sufficient seating clear signage for toilets or even departure gates. The passenger has to physically battle their way through a sea of stressed fellow travellers aimlessly wondering around this chaotic mess in an attempt to find a plane. It's an absolute appalling mess lacking basic functionality in need of urgent review.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Horsfield
content: Once again had the misfortune of the Stansted experience last week. I do not use this airport anymore but my schedule required I had to do so but nothing has improved. It really is the pits. As you enter the airport you have to weave through passengers now making their way to the new location of the security area. To be fair this was reasonably quick once we had walked about 50 metres back and forward through the ever wonderful queuing pens. You are then forced to wander through a shopping mall and into an unmade bottleneck to emerge into a building site. There are not enough seats and Stansted's owners then believe that by not telling you of your gate number you will utilise the retail opportunities. Really? Once you get your gate number and catch the silly little train you find a quiet gate lounge with plenty of seats and an air of calm compared to the dump at the main terminal. Returning into the border control is farcical. The automated gates take longer than the ordinary gates so don't bother to use them. And guess what? Despite the queues 5 of the automated gates were locked out of use. If you managed to get through with a single swipe of the passport you were lucky and many people were not. There was one helpless officer on the other side dashing back and forth telling people to simply try again. It really is pitiful. There is plenty of room to extend this area and add more machines (in return for the APD paid) but they have not done so as it would mean moving a large area reserved for unused luggage trolleys. Most flights are low cost meaning that people do not need luggage trolleys - they just want to get through the airport quickly and stress free. Stansted is unable to do this and this is because MAG believe that it is a third rate shopping mall that some planes fly from. Avoid it at all costs and use Southend City or Heathrow.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Eileen MacDonald-Williams
content: Even given the ongoing work in progress - apart from the glitzy duty free the passengers have to endure the other areas where the floor is uneven and pitted - the walls bare and dirty - and a definite shortage of rubbish bins - a most unwelcoming atmosphere.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D Shortt
content: Went through Stansted today. Long but moving queues in security which was to be expected. However when I got to the top of the queue I was informed my clear toiletries bag was too big! It had 4 items that were under the 100ml and a toothbrush and face wipes. It was also under the 20cm x 20cm size as specified on the Stansted website and clear resealable. I was told to use a smaller bag which was approx 12cm x 12cm. I'm guessing as my toothbrush was no longer able to fit in even when put in diagonally. After leaving the toothbrush to the side I was told "well done sir!"

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Brian Hargraves
content: Flew out 20th Feb back 6th March. Going out security staff checking hand luggage were a disgrace. Shouting demeaning and aggressive approach to passengers. I had my bag checked the staff called me over said 'you've probably got water in there'. Well I had no water and said 'I don't think so'. Next - Do you have a camera. I was able to say 'yes' as I did have one and as he turned the x-ray machine for me to view. His attitude changed a bit as he hadn't found the 'water smuggler' he exchanged pleasantries. In the meantime others in the queue were being belittled. We are not children. Tell us politely what you want and inform us of the need for the procedure you are doing or want to do and 'bob's your uncle'. Co-operation and politeness. Coming back the e-passport system and queues are a disgrace and shambles. Electronic age supposed to be a speedier and efficient age. It isn't at this Airport. Was the software even 'tested'. The wait is lengthy whilst the poor instructions if any do not help to create a speedy progress. 15 -20 barriers. 15-20 people puzzled red failure crosses showing try again messages. Staff rushing to jump one booth to next to help. Staff shouting empty booth numbers for people to go into. The length of the border queues and process are a National Shambles.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Janet Ibbotson
content: Truly appalling experience! My flight was cheap (though I didn't chose it for that reason) so I expected some inconvenience. I will be avoiding Stansted whenever possible in the future - shame because it used to be a nice little airport. So what went wrong? Delays coming on to stand - that's the second time in a row that has happened to me at Stansted. Then 45 minutes to get through border control and their 16 new automatic gates break constantly - several were not working at all while others were taken in and out of service while we waited. By this time Stansted Express had finished operating for the day. No sign on the station to tell you this until after you get to the platform and have already bought your ticket - of course I should have checked in advance but I assumed that as this is an "Express" airport line with lots of flights coming in after 11pm you don't expect it to operate like a rural branch line. How this clock off time makes economic sense for the train operator I don't know. Tried for the bus - hundreds of people milling about in confusion and a huge queue. The only bright spot was the taxi service. They were efficient unruffled with excellent drivers and clean cars and while it was costly their price seemed about right but how many people can afford a taxi? I'm used to travelling and though it was bad for me I was just hugely embarrassed for UK plc. What must all those visitors to the UK think of us.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Holmes
content: Travelled back on 1st March nightmare getting through e passport gates which rejected about 40% of passengers adding to the confusion and queuing. On the way out the temporary facilities whilst they rebuild are completely overwhelmed by the passenger numbers - really should stop being greedy and either close and complete the refit or limit the passenger numbers. We will never travel through this airport again however convenient the flight.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Jane Farmer
content: The queuing through security times on a Monday am are getting worse by the week. I have been using the airport every week for 7 years and its not getting any better its getting worse. This morning the queues through security were the worst I've seen I went through the ticket machine and there were people directly in front of the machines. heaving great throngs of very unhappy faces. There were a total of 5 security machines not manned by staff. When is this being resolved its all well and good increasing flights from Stansted and the great work into the re-furbishment. However for the security to be so understaffed on key obvious peak times and days is a real failure. Customers holiday makers and business travellers being stressed out by huge queues is a very poor way to start your journey they are therefore unable to enjoy a coffee or shop at the new refurbed shops when they are stuck in security and have to hot foot to the departure gate. Its a very easy change to implement - more staff please. I work in a business where customer demand vs staff is key to the overall success of customer satisfaction. Its a simple process to get right. If you went to a shop / restaurant and were met with those queuing times and an obvious staff shortage to manage demand you will vote with your feet and not use them and walk out using another venue where your needs were met. However this is not a simple choice for the air travel. On a positive side great improvements elsewhere.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Cole
content: I've used Stansted since before the current buildings were opened and for years it was almost a delightful experience (for an airport) but since Manchester Airport took over it has gone just one way: downhill and very fast. The cost of parking has rocketed (£19 a day for long stay) the car park buses are now shared with JetParks and are absolutely jammed. They've built a ridiculously shiny new Duty Free shop which requires you to walk about a mile from security to the departure lounge all with the money they've made from parking. They even charge you Â £2.50 to drop off so they must be making money faster than they can count it. But when it comes to landing after your holiday you are stuck on the plane after landing because they have no staff to unlock the arrivals doors. This has happened to me twice now. After 10 to 15 minutes you might be able to get off. Staffing at passport control is laughable well almost non-existent so this now takes 30-40 minutes. At the 'do it yourself' passports 3 out of 15 booths are in use and the single staff member is occupied with moving the barriers to accommodate the growing queue. By the time I got to the carousels the luggage was almost falling off it had been there so long. All in all it took an hour from landing just to get out of the airport. This is not a modern efficiently run airport it is an appalling experience for passengers and a cash cow for the owners. Yes bring back BAA the professionals.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Stuhr
content: Avoid travelling from Stansted if you can! I had to fly from this airport on 1 March 2015 with my 6 month old baby. I arrived at the airport at 15.00 my gate closed at 17.15. I just made it in time and was the last passenger to board the plane. To start with I needed to check the baby's car seat. Information on the screen just stated zone E desk 68-71. There was no one at those desks. Instead there were 3 other desks open no information displayed what flights are being checked in and no one to help. We joined the queue with people flying to Dublin Budapest and many other locations. Half an hour later we were stopped for another 20 minutes at the London underground barriers where you scan your boarding passes. There was only one official at the wide aisle gate and a massive queue of people who could not get through the barriers (everyone with buggies or whose boarding passes could not be scanned). Then we joined another massive queue to go through security. Many people were desperate as their flights were leaving soon crying and shouting for help to the marshals directing the queue. In all cases their reply was 'I can't do anything about it'. It took us about an hour to be cleared. Then a mad rush through a new serpentine of smelly perfume shops. I only noted the lack of seating in the lounge not that I had time to sit.. Our gate was 34. What a surprise it was to see a steep flight of stairs with no lift to get to the plane. Only thanks to the courtesy of other passengers did I manage to get the buggy down the steps. There were five (5) staff attending to buggies and none of them was willing to help hold my baby while I was folding the pushchair. It was very windy and it rained. We boarded the plane as last passengers soaked through. I have yet to fly back through Stansted and I already dread the experience. Avoid this joke of an airport if you can. I always used to arrive well ahead of time have a nice meal in Pontis (I did not seen it there anymore but might have missed it during my dash to boarding gate). Arrive at least 2 hours before your flight to avoid missing it!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: V Clough
content: On February 10th my family and I were due to travel on the 06.15 flight to Tenerife South (FR8166). We checked in on time and went through to the departure lounge and waited for our gate to be called. Once the gate opened we made our way to get on our flight with 5 children under the age of 10. The airport was extremely busy and we had to get on a monorail to catch our flight. As I'm sure you can imagine travelling with a large amount of children is hard work and when people are pushing and shoving it makes things that much more stressful. Due to us not being able to fit on the monorail and waiting for a long time for the next one we missed our flight by 4 minutes. Our family have never missed a flight before and this was all very new to us! I understand that we could have got to our gate quicker had we pushed and shoved like others but with the children it simply wasn't safe or possible. As I understand 30 other passengers missed their flight and the lady at the gate did say that she understood we were frustrated due to the monorail causing issues. We don't consider missing our flight to be our fault.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Tritt
content: When oh when will Stansted sort out their passport control? I use the airport about 6 times a year and no matter be it summer holidays or a Saturday in February the passport control is chaos. Another 40 minute wait to go through the automatic control with 2 members of staff helping - and another massive queue to use the normal passport control gates. Please Stansted sort this out - you know when the flights land and you really should be able to sort out passport control! Also the rudest security staff on departures. I really wouldn't use this airport if it wasn't on my doorstep.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ewan Simpson
content: Standing in a huge queue again at Stansted airport arriving on a late flight arriving at 11.15pm 6 months ago the last time we came through Stansted it took 2 hours to leave the airport because of queues and missing the last trains. Whilst waiting in a cramped corridor to come into the passport area no information was provided no attempt at crowd control. Only once we reached one small escalator was there any attempt to stop crushing or maintain control this was done by allowing only a set number of people at a time up the escalator. My wife who is Polish and traveling on an ID card was not allowed up with me at first as only British passport holders were allowed up at first. We are now standing in a similar queue the only difference is we have a taxi booked to pick us up which I booked with sufficient time to get through security under normal circumstance. If we incur any additional waiting time we will seek to claim back from Stansted airport as no warning was given as to there: 1. Management incompetence. 2. Attempt to cut costs. 3. Expected increase in business. I spoke to the manger supervising the arrival hall and she said it is like this most nights as they often have a large number of family's arriving late at night which slows the process down.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Conran
content: This formerly attractive airport has been reduced to a shambles by it's new owners. Because it was a weekend the great British tradition of the bus replacement service was in full swing from Liverpool Street (no reduction in fare) but that isn't the fault of the airport. Took well over an hour to clear security due to lack of staff. People were in a state of distress that they would miss flights. For no apparent reason my overnight bag was searched and the clothes including underwear and socks laid out in public view for meticulous examination by a man in white gloves. Most bags were being searched by glacially slow moving staff. Had to hurry through the maze of pathetic retail outlets which no one is interested in to find my departure gate. Fortunately because I was on an internal flight I did not have to experience the delights of passport control or spend any more time here. Speaking to others who have recently used this airport they concur with my comments. Come back BAA all is forgiven.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Gregson
content: I had the unfortunate experience of landing at Stansted at 00.30am due to an hour delay on a Ryanair plane. I unfortunately have not gone to the effort to get my British Passport even though I have indefinite leave to remain fly with my English husband and have resided in the UK for 9 years which is how I find myself in Non EU Passport holders queue. My husbands queue was right out to the arriving trains and my queue was never more than 10 -15 people long and yet it took over an hour to get checked through. My husband who had got through his queue of a 100 or more people in twenty minutes stood behind the counters waiting for me to come through was shocked by how people were treated. There is no basic respect as we watched people being shouted at goaded and told to wait when they struggled to give answers in English.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: H Brown
content: Used long stay car park. Waited for shuttle bus for around 5 minutes both arriving at and leaving airport. Going out checked in and went through security in about 20 minutes. Had good and inexpensive snack in airport. Ryanair flight left on time. On return (on time) some passengers had slight problems with passport recognition system as many people seemed to be using it for first time. Support staff observant and quickly redirected anyone with problems to manual control. Bags ready for us when we arrived at carousel. Took about 30 minutes to get bags after landing. Overall a pleasant experience. Did note that it was a long walk from plane to passport control. This may be a problem for older passengers especially as stairs were involved and escalators were not working (8pm Saturday).

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Michael Hope
content: There's no doubt about it - this airport is a shambles. We travelled back to the airport (from Germany - Christmas Markets) on 23rd December 2014 but a power outage at Stansted caused a 3 hour delay on our return flight meaning we arrived home at 3am. The airport is dirty facilities are weak and toilets sparse. The airport emailed and "apologised" for the disruption from the power outage. It's not the first time this airport suffered a power failure (Oct 2013) so its clear that lessons haven't been learnt. My advice - look at other London Airports before considering Stansted. Put Stansted at the bottom of your list if you value your own time. This airport is a national embarrassment to the UK. Something has gone badly wrong at Stansted and I think the government should intervene before a more serious incident occurs.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Clifford Hallion
content: I never tried to go through the automatic passport control until last week. Total chaos. The machines were not recognizing many peoples passports and we then had to go to another manned desk. Very long check ensued. Eventually when I reached Baggage pick up most of the carousels were overflowing with luggage because of the delays at the Passport check. They need to get their act together.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Tobin
content: Arrival - maybe I got lucky. Came through early Dec at 11am. Security for non UK/EU was only a 10 min wait luggage was quick to arrive and ticket counter for the busses was lineless. That being said buy your ticket at the bus stands. Reasoning? The company I purchased for had long lines and no busses (we waited over 20 min). The other company was selling 2 pounds cheaper busses were half empty and came several times while we waited. Thus go to the stands and make your choice then all companies have people selling tickets on the spot.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ron Husk
content: My trip on a northern lights internal flight and requiring assistance to and from the plane. Usually from other airports you get one on one assistance. To and from. Well my assistance was "here is your wheelchair follow me". Not impressed. No help whatsoever. Never again will I fly from London Stansted.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Stephen Willson
content: Again Stansted airport goes from bad to worse. The management seem to do there best to make the Stansted experience as bad as possible (maybe to reduce passenger numbers?). The current airport managers do not have a clue on how to run an airport or how to manage people and the customer experience. If any 'Normal business' was run like this airport it would be shut down in weeks. On the way out - Long queues at baggage security (this has been going on for years). A new pointless meander around the 'Shopping experience' is not what you need after a 30minute queue though security. Nowhere to sit rude staff dirty limited facilities. On the Way in - No stand for airplane (15 minute wait). 45 minute queue as passport control. Not what you need at 12pm (again this has been going on for years). Dirty. Getting out of the parking was a joke another 15 minute wait to get assistance. (Have you they not heard of number plate recognition). I guess they have at the £2 drop off zone. Please sort out this mess of an airport. It should not that difficult.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Anthony Burden
content: Dreadful experience yesterday. Due to a 'security incident' departure lounge passengers had to go through security a second time. The already inadequate security system and non existent queuing system was stretched to the limit. One member of staff standing on a chair with no way of amplifying her voice was trying to direct people with little time to catch the plane to the fast track channel. It was a nightmare for everyone especially those with children or in wheelchairs etc. The only good thing was that the IKEA style shopping mall you now have to navigate around was totally ignored by the rushing passengers with no time left. Stansted used to be OK it is now seriously over stretched and under managed. What worries me is this could lead to a serious incident one day.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Noel Bramley
content: 2 Jan 2015. Queued for 45 mins at security with 33 per cent of processing lines not operating-unmanned. The airport knows full well and precisely how many pax will be there at any hour of the day. Many pax are foreigners who do not have the means to complain and it is left for us the British travelling public to vent our anger at this absolute insult to the travelling public. I dare say there were more personnel vying for our hard won earnings in the so-called duty free shops. They are not duty free nor profit free. Those profits which are generated back to the airport are not re-invested in provision of smooth and swift security processing. The management should be changed.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Willis
content: Fortunately I have not had to use either Ryanair or therefore Stansted for some years both are shocking and a national disgrace to say the very least! On arrival we had to remain on the aircraft for quite some time due apparently to a complete power failure. On the return journey the airport resembled a refugee camp!Walking was almost impossible and sitting down let alone trying to find a place to eat impossible. Once on the Ryanair flight to Limoges we were told that there was a choice of hot and cold snacks but that we had better put in our orders quickly as they did not have much food aboard. What kind of ridiculous statement was that considering we were all belted into our seats and in our case half way up the cabin? Cabin crew were still serving what food they had when the pilot announced for all cabin crew to take their seats for landing! Hopefully I shall never have to use either Ryanair or Stansted again and I for one shall certainly try to avoid this total displeasure!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Thompson
content: Would not want to use London Stansted again. Arrived with pre printed boarding pass swiped through as only had hand luggage but unfortunately disorganised chaos with no one "official" in calling distance. When one did arrive he spent ten minutes arguing with a woman who was worried about missing her flight. He eventually let her through but then disappeared. I continued to struggle through the queue but my luggage was delayed and checked. I advised operator that I was in danger of missing my flight and asked if they could check it more quickly (in hindsight probably not a good move as this did not speed up the process). Once I had come through security had to get through everyone milling around the shops to get to gate 57 - a crazy system of going up and down escalators. I felt sorry for those who had to use the lifts. I missed my boarding time there was no one to assist with exit from the departure lounge. In fact several people missed their plane (not all same flight as mine) and when I eventually did find staff they were discussing how the system was crazy and that they did not have enough people in the right places. Unisex toilets were filthy. Bad experience all round. (December 14th).

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Copnall
content: Ok Stansted is still going through a major refurb and maybe just maybe when it's all finished it will be a nice airport to use but at the moment (travelled 13/12/14 ) its awful and I am dreading another trip through Stansted in Jan.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Sims
content: Not travelling through this time but previous appalling reviews say it all. My one-out-of-ten is for the bus-stop style waiting room for passengers to come through out of the domestic flights channel. It is the size of a living room with automatic doors that constantly open and close to allow blasts of freezing cold air to circulate. A few NHS style benches and that is it! Absolutely Third World (or worse). There is a stink of cigarette smoke from people waiting outside the doors discarded rubbish and paper on the floors and to get to it you have to go outside the terminal and along to the far end. Who came up with this idea beats me.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Donald Green
content: Security is a joke they seem unable to organise a proper queuing system and that's before you even get to the Shopping Mall.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Simons
content: There were no luggage carts on arriving to the airport so travelling alone with a small child hold-on and luggage was not an easy job At passport control pulling all the above it took too long to get through and because of the time to get through my daughter who was under 3 wet herself and didn't want to stay in line. On the return journey back to Athens I brought the pushchair to help me but the departure door to the bus that was to take us to the aieroplane was down a lot of narrow stairs so again I had hand luggage a pushchair and a small child to get down the stairs. If the other passengers had not helped me I would still have been at that airport today I have travelled to different airports and have worked at airports assisting tourists. I have to say it was the worst experience I have ever had as a traveller. The flight company I was happy with and with the service and the organisation at the check-in desks and with their organisation of the queuing system.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Callan
content: By far the worst experience at an airport in a long time nearly an hour going through security massive queues for this with minimal staff operating it. Staff members just shrug their shoulders when asked about it. I fear for anyone running anyway late or near their departure time. You are then funnelled through duty free towards a waiting area/corridor/warehouse where you have to wait endlessly because most flights haven't had their gate numbers allocated in good time. This would be tolerable if sufficient seating and or restaurants bars were available however this is not the case hundreds of customers are left waiting in corridors and sitting on floors because of a complete lack of facilities. Its like a scene from a TV movie where the airport is shutdown because of a freak weather storm but no its a modern 21st century airport which cant handle the numbers and doesn't give a toss about its customers.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Brittain
content: Stansted airport has been redesigned into an airport hell! Having been travelling through Stansted airport every month for years the new design is a complete loss to me. The new security system has resulted in longer queues and as for the redesign of what happens after security. Forced like a herd of cattle through a maze of duty free and sales opportunities - please! Accepted it's not finished but the whole layout and feel of the space is a disaster. The new owners of Stansted airport have made a very expensive mistake.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Phil Rhodes
content: The re-zoning of the interior seems to have resulted an expansion of the tacky shopping center (that you are forced to zigzag through) at the expense security floor space restaurants and other arguably more important customer related functions. As a result large queues build up all over the place. The most annoying of all aspects for me is the fact that arrivals from Ireland have to cram into buses from the aircraft to the terminal. The original designers of this previously impressive airport should be horrified at what's going on. And I hope someone's told Micheal O'Leary how his passengers are being treated. The 'turn-up on the day' long stay car park has gone up from less than £10/day to £19/day relatively few years.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Parry
content: Would appear that Stansted has maintained a consistency which would normally be applauded. However when that consistency is in ineptitude incompetence and ignorance then maybe the management should be ashamed or disgraced. To trot out the same old excuse that it was a clash of flights is both laughable and embarrassing. Maybe it's all a plan to introduce the many foreign visitors to our world beating ability in the art of queuing.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Ilersic
content: The Stansted experience is truly awful and has been for a long time now. Unfortunately I've had to use this airport on a weekly basis for the last 4/5 years. I will not be using it again after Christmas. I would much rather the inconvenience of travelling further and will now use Birmingham Airport after trying it in September and October (it is paradise in comparison with Stansted). The queues at departure are considerable. The space provided to shops at the airport in comparison to waiting areas / seats says all you need to know about the commitment to customer care. Queuing systems are hit and miss at departure gates - mainly miss. Gate numbers are frequently released with only a short time to go with the warning final call. Infrequent travellers are often seen running as if their lives depended on it. Arrival is much worse. There has been plenty of times when I've been held on a plane after it has parked for 10-30 minutes only to be told that we are waiting on ground staff to open the doors. When they decide to let us in we then have a middle distance race to get to passport control. Sometimes we have the privilege of queuing down two corridors even before we get upstairs to the main area. This process can take between 45 minutes and 1.5 hours in my experience. The border control and the ground staff blame each other. Last night border control also blamed the airlines for landing at the same time. I wonder who allows this to happen? The ground staff seem to take great delight in being rude/sarcastic or unhelpful - sometimes all three. Stansted management just don't seem to care. They know what a misery it is. They can see people. They can listen to people. Many travellers are infrequent so many will go away thinking they were just unlucky. Nothing could be further from the truth. The airport is wholly incapable of dealing with the capacity it has committed to. I left my watch one day at security. I reclaimed it the next day after being charged £20 for admin fees. Stansted may say that they tender the issue of lost property out to a third party but it is they who make the decision and no doubt are paid handsomely by the aforementioned third party. Stansted beats Ryanair for its contempt of its customers. I cannot pay it a higher insult than that.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Gabriel Chain
content: This was by far the worst airport experience I have had and coupled with a Ryanair start it started my holiday in tears! The queue to the meet and greet parking was half a mile long and the staff were some of the rudest I have encountered. Then a battle through security with a lack of staff causing huge delays. Finally through you begin the absurd walk through the infinite duty free along a path fit for single file! Bow through this shopping maze you try and navigate your way to a gate only and to wait another hour to board the actual plane!
