content: Dreadful queues at passport control and held like cattle in hot airless tunnels. Loner waiting at passport control than the flight! Its a joke. What a bad first impression of UK this makes to foreign visitors.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Adams
content: Arrived at Stansted at 23.40 last night. It took 2 hours to get through passport border control and to my car. We were all held in hot stuffy corridors which was unacceptable. The elderly and young were suffering in the heat. No staff or water was available and had there been an incident it would have been difficult for help to get through. There were annoying announcements about waiting but no real information. This also happened in February. I believe it is purely created by security staff at airport to get enough complaints to get their grievances sorted out.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Richard Watson
content: This used to be a nice airport but it is now a money grabbing joke. You can't drop off/pick up near the terminal without paying a fortune there is a free area but not well sign-posted if you don't know it in advance you end up paying. The road that separates all the bus and paid parking zones in a dangerous joke. The new scanning machines into security do keep queues down until you get in there and most x-ray machines aren't open and staff are rude as usual not enough chairs to put all your stuff back on after. The departure lounge is too small it looks like a refugee camp most of the time less shops more chairs please and the info screens are too small. On arrivals the passport control area is a joke. The other day there was one member of staff to meet all passengers off the tram and direct everyone possible to automated machines which she then had to supervise. There are only 5 machines one wasn't working and the rest rejected on average 50%. Forget arriving on a non EU passport. My girlfriend is American with UK rights and had to queue for 35 mins just to get to see someone who asked no questions at all. I'll be avoiding this where possible rather go to Gatwick which has improved or better still Southend which will take a lot of their business I hope. Stansted is not a relaxing start or end to your trip.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Noel Richards
content: I used to fly regularly from this airport around ten years ago. But no more. This is now a disgusting airport. Thousands of departing passengers herded like cattle in the terminal waiting for their gates to be shown. It resembles a refugee camp. Nowhere to sit at busy times. I never want to fly from here again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Juliet Clibborn
content: Disgraceful long lines yesterday for Passport Control. When I asked why I was told it was all those Europeans using Identity cards! For information to the managers most of their passengers come from the EU. Awful we were held inside one of the tunnels. It was hot and many felt faint. They don't allow animals to be treated like that!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Florence
content: Great airport but what have they done with the car parking? It appears you can no longer drop off passengers outside the terminal but have to use one of the car parks. The signs on the one way road accessing the car parks is terrible making it very difficult to find where your supposed to park whilst driving. I can only assume this is another money-making scheme to increase profits! This morning it cost me £2.80 for 3 minutes! I didn't even park up just dropped off passengers. It used to be simple and quick to drop off at Stansted Now they've made it difficult and costly! This almost amounts to obtaining money by deception in my opinion.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: F Peter
content: Dreadful staff behaviour today. Everyone was treated like cattle staff were rude and sneering to passengers and queues at security were dreadful. New security is terrible why they need to do anything with it no one knows. Probably to make room for those nano scanner. Witnessed passages ask for directions to security staff mocked him. After waiting 20 mins I put my bag in the tray and was shouted at and told to put it the other way round and at the same time told to take my shoes off. The bag fitted perfectly well in the box. Another woman was exceptionally rude to me and dived in my bag normal procedure is to allow the passenger to open it. Stansted is becoming London's Nasty Airport. Will be so glad to see the back of this backwater in March when Ryanair stop flying. Back to my car and the ferry for me!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: H Calmly
content: You know its bad when you spend longer in the queue for passport control then your actual flight duration! I'm a frequent flier across the UK and I can honestly say Stansted is my least favourite airport and I actually dread flying into it. Border control is manic and so unorganised its a disgrace. This Sunday it took me well over an hour simply to get through border control. My plane landed and we joined the queue then as another 2 planes landed the passengers from those planes were able to bypass half of the passengers from my flight and join the queue at any point they could squeeze themselves in- ultimately leading to a crush situation in one corridor. The airport staff moving the queue along were doing so 10 people at a time and with 3 flights you can imagine how slow this meant we moved. With no apology or explanation for the delay - I'm all for national security but there was no queue if you were a non EU resident and a whopping huge one for EU and UK passport holders!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Phillip Turner
content: The delays at border control at London Stansted is now absolutely ridiculous. I travel through Stansted 4 or 6 times a month along with many commuters from Brittany and have never seen anything as poor in the 7 years that I experienced on 10th and 14th February. You need to add an extra hour when you arrive to get through the queues or the chip auto security border controls. The check in has been extended by now having to walk even further to the extreme left of the airport building and the flow of people is just down to bad traffic management. Ryanair check in is now a chaos and worse than ever with multiple queues to get the drop off bag desks. Whilst waiting for my flight out on the 14th February we heard the new announcement the same as on the 10th February that you have to wait in the tunnel approaching border security as part of the process. This is not true it is because there are only 2 or 3 people now on border control checks and can no longer deal with the volume of people arriving. Those arriving on the shuttle trains from other airlines get precedent over those arriving on Ryanair which causes a build up in the tunnels. Since the BAA left Stansted it has got worse - please Stansted Airport - get yourself sorted out quickly before the summer otherwise I shall have to boycott this madness.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: David Blackwell
content: Well all it can say is there must have been a change of management in the last year as the UK Border Agency here us a disgrace! I use this airport on a regular basis and over the last year the queues on arriving back are getting longer and longer and last night queued 30 mins in the tunnel before being allowed into the customs hall and another 45 mins as long as the flight I had just had! Disgraceful. The reason when I question a customs member was management had changed working shifts and to cope with the thousands of passengers only 4 booths open. The new so called Security being moved nothing wrong the old one still new management and stupid ideas! Gatwick is working fine Luton Stansted be careful!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Thomas
content: I used all six London airports and Stansted is working just fine. It's easy to navigate even for a non English speaker. I have never spent more than 10 minutes in the queue for security check even my flights usually are during morning rush hours. Even on 23rd December I had to wait for security check maybe 2-3 minutes. Big plus. Shops are okay. I made a good deal in a duty free shop as I checked prices on my phone and they are really cheaper. That is very rare this days to be "duty free" and cheaper. Usually it's opposite just to drain your wallet. There should be more seats in shops areas and more power sockets - I always find one available but it's like last one free. Cheap way to go to and from airport is using a bus as it's from £5 one way and I bought these tickets online from one of the bus operator - just 2 days in advance.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Mouameletzi
content: Very expensive to get there the single train ticket to London is 23 pounds and to get there is no easier than Heathrow. Only one first class lounge which is located almost 29 minutes away from the main area where you see the gates announcements.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Z Stefan
content: What a horrible transformation of security area since my last flight! It took them only six weeks (since my last flight) to close a fairly efficient security area and move it to a horrible poorly organized grey chaotic area - pointless exercise. I think the queue moves slower than before and I can not see how is a new security area is going to add to this fairly OK airport (until now).

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: T Ragan
content: Currently in a queue for at least 1 hour. EPassport lanes are closed. UK EU PASSPORT lanes reduced. All other passports no queues. Apparently tougher checks mean longer queues. How about more staff on closed booths and EPassports mean shorter queues.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Steve Allen
content: Used this airport this week. Awful experience on returning to UK on Wednesday at about 23.30 which spoilt the end of a great holiday. Took nearly one hour to get through passport control. It's a national disgrace only 25 desks open for several thousand travellers arriving on Ryanair flights between 9 and midnight. Why can't they separate out the red-passport holders from the mass of identity card holding others. Surely UK passport holders could be given priority after all it's our taxes that pay for passport control! Non-EU visitors were getting in very quickly as several desks had been set aside for them and no-on was using them. If you go to the states the US citizens have priority so it should be the same in the UK for UK citizens. Will now look to travel from other airports if at all possible.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Sanders
content: This has to be the worst airport in Britain! Getting to the airport we had 3 diversions at 4 in the morning! Between 6-8am there is 50 flights leaving worst of all the majority of the flights gates pop up at the same time so it's the normal mad Ryanair rush to get to the gate only you have to board a monorail which is always packed and you have to wait 2 or 3 times before you get crammed onto one. The check in area is crowded the security is horrific and I've never seen such a bad departure area. Next to no toilets terrible eating options and constant building work. Too add insult we had to wait 20 minutes for a bus in the mid stay car park! Never again!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Parsons
content: For years have always preferred to travel using Stansted airport for convenience and the fact that it is clean new and bright. However that is not enough to make me ever use this airport again it is terribly overcrowded staff are unapproachable and it feels totally mis-managed when returning to the UK. Passport control was a terrible ending to a lovely holiday queuing for over an hour. Luckily my children are older and did not need to be carried etc there was no consideration for the tired babies and young children everyone looked extremely fed up and frustrated. Will avoid this terrible airport at all cost's in the future!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Mallinson
content: 30th October - Outbound at 6.00 am Monday morning a little late but no serious issues (security very polite). Return at midnight Thursday. Passport control a farce in fact a national disgrace what an impression to give visitors. 45 mins and I'm a UK national - outrageous. I fly twice a week for work usually Heathrow I cannot and will not consider using Stansted again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Cairnduff
content: I have used this airport a number of times as it is handy to a friend's house in Essex. I have good and bad reflections on it. Rail connections are fantastic. Security staff have always been extremely pleasant - on my last visit I was subject to a body scan and manual search and the guy that did it was very helpful and talked me through each stage of the process. What I dislike is the compact departures lounge - very tricky to move around without getting in someone's way - hopefully this will improve when the construction work is completed. I would welcome an airside fast food outlet couldn't find anywhere last time for a quick bite to eat and ended up buying a sandwich and taking it onto the plane. Would be happy to use this airport when travelling to somewhere close by but would most likely choose a different London airport if going to the city itself.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Mackay
content: Used this airport in mid October. Got a taxi in from Nearby Bishops Stortford cost £17 Two years ago it cost £5. Used one of the private lounges which gave us use of fast-track through security. I was through security in under one minute (During the early morning rush at 5.00am). Coming back used the auto booths at passport control and was again through in under a minute only delay was a 15 min wait at baggage reclaim for our bags to arrive. All in all was pleased particularly as I live in Norfolk which is only one hours drive away so really want this airport to work for me.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Payne
content: Nightmare. 7 Oct 9.30 am. Had to wait 20 mins for the long stay shuttle. Driver sat texting instead of driving. Queues right back into the foyer to even get to security. Only one channel open. Huge delays and many people missed flights.£110 per person to rebook with Ryanair is just profiteering. At least 10 minutes of fast walking up and down escalators to reach departure gates. Avoid this airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: F Mather
content: I have just waited an hour for my luggage to come through at stansted. No announcements to explain what was going on. I spoke to someone over the phone at the luggage enquiries desk (no staff available) who explained it was due to too many flights coming in at once. Do they not know the scheduled arrivals? In the meantime my taxi had to come in and out of the short stay car park being charged £2 a time. Why should I have to pick up that bill! Will avoid this airport in future.

title: Long Beach Airport customer review
author: Tom Sappington
content: I've always enjoyed flying in and out of Long Beach Airport but this time was a big disappointment. They used to have remote lots for long-term parking at a reasonable price but now those have been shut down. At this point the only option is the short-term parking which is a bit of a walk from the terminal with a cost of $2/hour maxing out at $17/day or $19/day depending on which building you use. That really adds up!

title: Long Beach Airport customer review
author: W Burke
content: At first I was concerned seeing the long lines at JetBlue's curbside check-in and at the check-in counter on my way to the upstairs restaurant to eat dinner before my flight. Restaurant is good but not cheap but not outrageously priced considering portions and food quality. Was through security with minimal wait less than 10 minutes. No jetways here so you have to walk on the tarmac to board your plane via stairs. Only complaint is terminal building is too small considering the number of people that pass through. Still I would continue to use LGB to avoid LAX every day of the week and twice on Sunday.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Livshin
content: I don't know which Stansted airport some of the reviewers have flown to and from but we flew in on Monday 30th September arriving at mid day and were through passport control collected our luggage and out of the airport terminal in under an hour of landing.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Alastair Reid
content: I was surprised having read the very bad reviews here to have a totally trouble-free experience in both directions. I flew out late morning 18 Sep and returned mid afternoon 24 Sep. Had booked valet parking with Aardvark (£52) you just drive up the ramp and stop right outside departures. Short 8 min wait at Ryanair bag drop. Less than 15 min wait for security with cheerful and pleasant staff. Shops/food etc quite satisfactory and clean toilets airside. On return flight landed punctually and queue for passport control took 10 mins. Bags waiting already when we got to belt. Very short walk down to short term car park where Aardvark rep was waiting with car. Drove on to M25 less than 35mins after landing. Well done Stansted! A good experience.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Andrus Rosenfeld
content: Last Monday 23/9/2013 was nightmare. Just arrived from Tallinn and there were passport check queues of more than 50 minutes. This airport is overcrowded. Too many flights at the same time this airport needs a second terminal.

title: Long Beach Airport customer review
author: Mike Rosenzweig
content: This is such a convenient airport. Reminds me of a small mid-west airport where you park close by check in and at the gate so quickly. While not a lot of fancy amenities like the larger international airports this airport is such a breeze.

title: Long Beach Airport customer review
author: Michael Parker
content: It is simply an airport and not trying to be a shopping mall or anything else. Very quick passage through the airport if you're only dropping off bags; TSA efficient but thorough; bit of a crowd in the north portakabin as JetBlue DL and AS had simultaneous departures but as you can turn up so close to departure it's not a long wait. Restaurant upstairs is good as well though not cheap and it would be good to have more of the balcony given to non-eaters (maybe it's busier midweek than on a Sunday afternoon).

title: Long Beach Airport customer review
author: W Donovan
content: Long Beach is a great little airport. It has the most efficient TSA checkpoint I have ever seen with the longest line ever being about three minutes and I fly through here quite often. While the south concourse is the only gate area I have used I am sure the airport is the same throughout the terminal. The staff is great and friendly and you can chat with everyone. The gate numbering can be a bit confusing but so long as you don't immediately exit the terminal to the left you should be fine. They even give you an umbrella when it rains to walk onto the plane.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Selden
content: Inbound passport control last Monday was dreadful. Hundreds of people backed up in corridors leading to the passport hall. Eventually spotted the new e-passport gates (they don't seem to be directing people to these) and thought I'd give it a try. Very long queues here too. They had 4 working machines. But they also had one person checking the back of the queue to make sure you had the right kind of passport one man supervising the general running of the machines (as in supermarket self-checkouts) and 3 people behind a desk overseeing all the photo- recognition images and the general output from the machines. So instead of 5 staff heading 5 passport queues they had 5 staff heading one very long queue for 4 passport machines. If you need 5 people to oversee 4 gates because you don't trust the technology then don't use it! Shockingly poor management and an entirely unapologetic tone in all the public announcements. A horrible experience.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Fry
content: It is a disgrace that the new owners of Stansted have managed to turn what was a well run pleasant to use airport into a nightmare. Until recently if you arrived by taxi or were dropped off by a friend it was outside the doors to the booking in desks. Now you have to pay to be dropped off at a ridiculously crowded area and push your cases up a steep ramp which is very unpleasant when you get to your 70s. And if the traffic queues are long you have to pay more for the pleasure of sitting in the queue to be dropped off. Coming back is just as bad controlling a trolley going down a steep ramp is very unpleasant and then you have the problem of locating your lift back home - a mobile phone is essential to find out where to go. After getting to the check in area for some reason or other the time to check in or drop your bags off takes a lot longer despite arriving 3 or more hours before take off. Then as has been mentioned by others there is the very long delays (almost an hour on our last trip) getting through security with rude staff constantly trying to push you through. Again a horrible experience when you are travelling with a family from 4 years old to the over 70s - alternatively of course you could pay (a rip off £35 in our case) to use the priority security gates. As has been mentioned in other posts coming back the queues for passport control are very long and the last thing you want to encounter after a long flight with very tired children. We won't be using Stansted again until they have made substantial improvements - despite being 40 miles further to Gatwick the time to get from home to the plane will be a lot less and much less stressful.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: T Rook
content: The ever growing delays at passport control 50 minutes last Saturday when returning home completely spoil any trip. Four out of five trips this year have suffered from excessive delay and the hot airless conditions of the corridors where passengers are held and the lack of information is completely unacceptable. I have asked the border staff why there is a delays and get different answers each time with the common thread that there is a complete lack of effective management of the function. Given known schedules and passenger numbers it shouldn't be too difficult to deploy the number of border staff necessary to keep delays to a minimum (on Saturday many of the desks were not manned). If possible I will avoid using this airport until this issue is resolved.

title: Long Beach Airport customer review
author: J Griffis
content: I'm not entirely sure you can call LGB an "airport". It's sort of like a few runways with some temporary-cum-permanent trailers (aka "gates") parked on the side strung together by covered chain-link fencing mazes for crowd control. All of that having been said it's enormously better than LAX and JetBlue does what it can to make your (hopefully) short wait at LGB pleasant (free wireless Internet is a nice little perk). My only suggestion would be to bring an umbrella... There are no airwalks from the plane to the gate just a stairway down to the tarmac. In the occasional event of rain in Long Beach it helps on the short jaunt from the plane to the "gate/terminal".

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D White
content: Shocking - Shocking - queues - looked like a football crowd waiting to get through security (afternoon departure). It was difficult to believe and yes the security staff are unfriendly. Missed my flight. Drove home and looked at other airports for next one. Previously Heathrow (despite being a giant) was very helpful (lots of people to assist) friendly clean and quick (well done to them). Won't try Stansted again - it's just not worth it.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: H Burton
content: We used Stansted for our family holiday to Kos during the last week of August and our overall impression was of a clean and well run airport with minimal check in times and small queues when we returned. The toilet facilities were clean and there was a good selection of shops in the departure lounge. Unfortunately we could not buy very much due to the meagre Ryanair baggage allowance. Time taken to clear through security for four adults was about 15 minutes with mainly helpful security staff. The transit bus journey from the long stay airport was only 10 minutes and the bus driver on the return was extremely helpful and provided clear announcements to his passengers. The only criticism is the lack of lower priced restaurants (McDonalds Burger King) in the departure lounge making a rather expensive meal for a family of four but overall I was very pleased with Stansted on this occasion.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: C Cerea
content: I have used Stansted regularly and often for the last 23 years hand have witnessed a steady decline in standards. The worst aspect are the unacceptable queues and waiting times at passport control by far the worst I have witnessed at any airport so far. This coupled with the average unpleasant attitude of the border agency officials the last one experienced only yesterday have made me decide on using other airports as a first choice. Stansted is the nearest in terms of distance and travel time to my home but the time saved with this is now overridden by the waiting transfer and wasted time on other aspects the main one being passport control. It is ironic that people from outside the EU get through this procedure faster than EU nationals in most cases.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K De Voil
content: I will never use Stansted again. The shambolic organisation just to drop your bags off coupled with the horrific security queues are bad enough but the audacity of charging in order to drop someone off is disgraceful. Not only does it cost £2 for 10 minutes or £3 for 15 minutes but if you stay in the "express set-down" area (and believe me there is nothing "express" about it when the queue to get into the area stretches all the way back down the road that runs parallel to the airport) for longer than 15 minutes you can expect a £50 fine. This is a cynical money-making plot by the airport's owners to extract every last penny from anyone doing a friend or relative a favour by dropping them off. Plus although the area was busy the parking spaces further away from the terminal were completely empty so the fine has no real standing when you consider that anyone who does actually overstay the allotted maximum time of 15 minutes isn't in any way depriving someone else waiting to park from being able to do so. It's the same at Southend airport you have to drive into a car park in order to be able to drop someone off as there is no set-down area to the tune of £5! Sadly this is just another case of "rip-off Britain" where we are continually squeezed tighter and tighter.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Harrington
content: I will certainly be trying to avoid both Ryanair and Stansted airport after arriving back to the UK last night. There were 3 passengers who needed wheelchairs on the flight and rather than allowing the able bodied off of the flight first so that there was then room to give assistance to those with special needs the ground crew insisted on sorting out the passengers with special needs first fighting their way through the crowded aisle where there was no room to move - this alone delayed disembarkation from the plane. This was to be followed by the most horrendous queues for passport control at a UK airport with the queue stretching all the way from the passport desks back to the hallways from the plane exits. Bearing in mind that it was now midnight and all the desks were open I'd hate to see what the queues would be like at peak time. I can only recommend to pay £20 extra and fly with a decent airline from a decent airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J O'Brien
content: My wife and I had the misfortune of flying into Stansted last week and out of it yesterday. Flying into it was good. No issues and the busses are a very short walk from the terminal. The issue with this airport is departures. We arrived back on our bus went to drop our bag and were greeted with a very long line for bag drop. We had pre- booked fast track security after reading some of the reviews on this site and we were glad we did that. Once though security is where our main issue with this airport started. We had 2 hours to wait and there was not enough seats for everyone who was there. The departures lounge was dirty too. The bar had no seats and when you did find one the table still had the previous guests trash on them. Also getting in and out of London takes a very long time from Stansted. If you wish to use the train it costs 4 times more than it does from Gatwick or Heathrow. My advise is use Gatwick or Heathrow and avoid Stansted.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D Collins
content: Arrived at Stansted at 23.50 on August 13th to be met by a one hour queue for passport control. Going out huge queues for security. Absolutely unacceptable. This airport is run entirely for the benefit of the burgeoning security industry. Complaints from passengers are met with rudeness or threats of police intervention. An absolutely horrible place.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Crooke
content: We flew from Stansted in July for the first time. We did meet and greet parking and was very simple and swift. The airport itself is very well run. We decided to get there earlier than needed as mentioned on other reviews but was not really necessary as there was no queue at check-in or security. This did however give us plenty of time to have a leisurely meal and drink before going to the departure gate via the train. All in all the experience was good at the airport with standard prices and good cleanliness.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: D Beale
content: I have been through Stansted at least 8 times in the last 12 months and it is obviously one of the more budget traveller suited airports in the country but remains a very acceptable airport to use. Just So there is no misunderstanding: The security has always been quite swift if not quick although reassuringly thorough with no major wait. After security the shops are centralized for the holiday travellers with food and bars etc as expected. If you are flying with Ryanair then the gates are situated a short walk away with their own smaller facilities such as bar newsagent and food. However the Airport always seem to hold everyone in the central area before announcing gates (probably to entice more from you wallet). I always drive to the airport and park with the mid stay being a short transfer excellent. Do not use the drop off short stay so cannot comment. The only negatives: Airport food prices. Same as everywhere but the quality has always been fair to good. So no complaints. There are normally complimentary newspapers in the mornings and Toilets etc have always been clean on the times I have had the need. Generally I think if you are a little savvy and do not expect first class treatment for a minimum cost then Stansted is a great value for money airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Isaac
content: Worst airport I have ever used coupled with Ryanair make it an experience to be avoided at all costs. The security staff behave like MacDonalds rejects. On 3 occasions have nearly missed flights despite arriving earlier and earlier. The whole customer service is appalling. Everything is designed to pick your pocket. The final insult was to have to pay £5 to get to a flight purely because they have deliberately created massive queues at the security checks with insufficient staff (and what staff they have are rude and ignorant). Makes Heathrow and Gatwick look like model airports.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Mein
content: The new owners have not changed the drop off/pick up arrangements to the old highly efficient system that existed about 2 years ago. I picked up my sister who has a disabled badge at the airport who is unable to take her case to the car. To reach the short pick up area she also has a long walk from the terminal. The problem is I cannot leave the car unattended even for a minute to help her as the patrol van will immediately start to put it on a tow away truck and then demand £180 to release the car the whole arrangement is totally disabled unfriendly. I am not sure how this complies with current legislation on disabled access. If this airport are going to improve their performance they will then need to have attendants available on request with wheelchairs in the terminal to escort disabled people to the pick up point and wait with then until their transport arrives. Also the vehicle "police" who operate at the pick up point need to be instructed to not impound any car where the person being picked up holds a disabled badge.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Colin Gibbins
content: Worst experience in an airport ever: Allowed over 2 hours to get onto a 6.30am flight. Firstly queued in the car park to be charged for dropping off - nice new touch to fleece the public. Absence of any organisation in baggage drop off area - "queued" (more like crowded) for over an hour. Queued again for security check - with everyone stressed as flights nearing gate close people cutting through cordons no-one in charge. Ran to gate at the far end of the terminal just in time to catch our flight. Returning from Naples no queues clean efficient airport friendly staff well organised.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: V Brown
content: I have long been of the opinion that Stansted has no concept of customer care. The whole place seems vaguely grubby staff are frequently rude and security is a nightmare. However dropping off or picking up passengers was always fairly simple. To drop off you drove up to the terminal your passengers got out (under cover) you drove out. To pick up you drove to the pick-up zone your passengers got in you drove out. Not any more. The whole thing has become shambolic. This morning I drove my husband to Stansted with the objective of dropping him off at 5 am for a 6.30 am flight where he had already checked in online but we were allowing at least an hour for him to get through security (see earlier comment about security). Arrived at 5 am discovered you could no longer drive up to the terminal and then took another 10 minutes to get to the so-called drop-off area where we were confronted by vehicles in the parking areas on both sides and also in the central lane which explained why there was a traffic queue trying to get into the drop-off area in the first place. As there was absolutely no chance of parking properly my husband got out and then wended his way through the melee. Fortunately he had no luggage to impede him. If the drop-off zone was properly sign-posted perhaps the log jam in the first lane would not occur but at the same time you cannot blame people for wanting to be as close as possible to what is anyway the far end of the terminal building. This morning was dry and warm so not a problem but in inclement weather with luggage? I wonder whether the designers of this chaos have ever tried it out as paying customers. In my book Stansted has gone from mediocre to completely shambolic.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ann Cox
content: This is my 2nd time using London Stansted airport and be sure that I will never use this airport again. The security staff are very unprofessional and obstructive. Expect a delay and unnecessary checking of your luggage if you question them. You feel as if you have gone back to school days. This is a very cheap layout inside the airport. Be sure to arrive at 4hrs before your flight departs security is slow unhelpful and rude. My 1st experience was similar and most definitely will avoid using this airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Rutherford
content: Sale of Stansted by BAA to Manchester Airport Group seems to have been a disaster what had been a pleasant well managed airport has descended into badly managed chaos in a very short time. Charging for drop off in the area close to the terminal was charged at££2 for 10 minutes - but only advertised on small sign after entering area. Generally signage was poor and amateurish - change machine did not accept debit cards ticket machine - what for? no ticket issued at entrance. Exasperated finally approached exit barrier relief to see cards accepted was short-lived when no reaction from machine at barrier - good 5 minutes before someone finally answered call to be told that that barrier was not accepting cards and to try another. Reversed out of lane and into next - barrier not working but at least display said cards not accepted; only at third barrier was I successful. Stansted seems to be descending to the levels of Luton.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Ben Stevens
content: I use Stansted regularly (and will continue to do so unfortunately). My advice is to arrive at least 4/5 hours prior to departure. Security were announcing that bags they wished to inspect - would take 1 hour for someone to get round to you - a poor passenger about to embark on their honeymoon complained as they would miss their flight - who subsequently did and left security. Do not question security otherwise they will purposely become obstructive as many of the passengers found. Set down costs £2 for 10 minutes but there are traffic marshals appearing to slow the whole process so you end up staying over 10 minutes. This as found out incurs a large fine - so if you stay any longer be sure to bring your credit card which is accepted in all their machines. Plastic bags must be Stansted approved plastic bags so expect to pay 2 pound for this even if you are using a bag given to you from another airport (including London Heathrow). When I called to complain about the parking situation was told "its the rules sir and if you have a problem with our charges perhaps you should use a different airport".

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Warren
content: Having used this airport many times I have noticed that its standards have dropped dramatically since 2007 and it is clear that the new owners MAG have a lot of work to do to restore Stansted to its former status. The experience itself is alright but there's no 'wow factor'. What Stansted really does need is a greater mix of airlines especially to long haul destinations such as New York or Dubai as there are currently no long haul flights from Stansted. Once services like these are introduced this will save many passengers having to use the busier congested airports like Heathrow and Gatwick. Furthermore we tend to travel to Romania frequently and it would be good to see carriers like Wizz Air introduce a Stansted-Bucharest service which would save us the hassle of using Luton airport. Clearly Stansted has a lot of potential to attract future long haul growth and new airlines besides Ryanair. Once MAG improves the terminal and its facilities I am confident that Stansted will improve and become more appealing.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Martin
content: I use London Stansted frequently since I find it by far the best of London's airports or indeed the UK. It is significantly busier departing in the morning and arriving in the evening yet the airport still maintains its level of great customer service. This is through consistently having short queuing times at check-in security and passport control as well the provision of a wide range of shops restaurants food and drink outlets throughout the airport plus a wide range of other useful facilities. Flight information screens are very clear and easy to follow and are closely located to all areas whilst staff are also very friendly and helpful making the airport even more stress free. Without fail the terminal is always immaculately clean and still remains fairly spacious as airports go at the busiest of times. Public transport to the airport is good but could be better. Rail services are regular and run directly from the Terminal Building but 45-50 minutes into London is a little long. Road access however is great as the M11 and A120 is always a breeze of a journey and rarely congested unlike the M1 and M25 serving other London airports. The only real criticism I have is the lack of choice of airlines since it is nearly all Ryanair and Easy Jet but overall London Stansted is a fantastic airport which I would highly recommend.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Kelly
content: I was flying from Stansted to Malaga on Saturday 8th June 2913 and in all my 50 years of flying I have never witnessed such a complete shambles at security. The queue was more like a queue you would find at a premier football match than normal airport security. The end result it took nearly a full hour to get through and I missed my plane despite checking in on line. I have never missed a flight before and would suggest that 'flyer beware' if you use Stansted as your preferred airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Z Mamon
content: We used Stansted for the first and last time! Ridiculous charges for drop off and collection. Difficult to find a trolley. Once inside the terminal impossible to move. Long queues for check in security and at the gate. Filthy washroom areas. Difficult to find a seat in the waiting lounge. The airport has all the facilities: bars snack bars restaurants shops duty free but the space within is very restricted and bumping into people was not uncommon.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: David J Hook
content: First Time I have used 'Express Drop-off' area having used the airport for years (since my honeymoon in 1973). This will be the last time I will use this airport! The recent change of drop-off is nothing but a transparent scam to raise even more money from the abused traveller. It is unpleasant and at £2.00 for 10 minutes so exorbitant that it ought to be in Westminster. Add to this the very threatening presence of a vehicle removal company it is just another example of how little the operator cares for the traveller as opposed to their money. Everything at the airport is aimed solely at taking more and more cash from the inadequate seating (except in refreshment areas where effectively you pay to sit) to the excessive number of shops taking up space that could be used by any caring operator to make the public more comfortable. What a rip-off!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Kane
content: I have just returned from Stansted airport to see off my mother-in-law and son who were flying to Germany with Ryanair. Having checked in online I was not expecting the lengthy queue at baggage drop off. After waiting about 45 mins to drop off one suitcase we proceeded to the departure security gate. Another lengthy queue and delay. When my mother-in-law (who is 80 years old and disabled) and my son (16 years old) reached the front of the queue they were directed back to the fast track lane as she has a metal walking stick (single crutch.) My son was informed he had to accompany her as they were together. We went to the fast track desk only to be informed my son had to pay £5 for fast track. The girl on the desk would not listen to our explanation that my son had been told to come here and he had to carry his grandmother's hand luggage but we refused to pay the charge. They would not listen to reason. Eventually a supervisor arrived who sensibly listened to us and apologised that we had been given incorrect information. She took my mother-in-law and son through. I have never experienced such a stressful time just dropping someone off for a flight and I will never use Stansted Airport again. I'd rather pay more and travel further than deal with uncaring jobsworths.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Keller
content: Flew from Stansted for the first time in 2 years. (Having used Stansted regularly over the past 15 years before that) I noticed a steady decline in the airport. I couldn't be dropped outside the door of the airport anymore. Forced to pay £2 for 10 mins to park in the car park just to get my bags out. I have a leg injury and wasn't pleased that I had to walk all the way up to departures. The trolleys are coin operated and having spent the last of my change already had to go without. Check in was fairly smooth and friendly but then to security. Queues were unbelievably long. The line took 30 mins to get through. I am used to traveling and had my laptop already out of the bag etc but the security woman still insisted on asking me several times if I had a laptop. Through security I went to Starbucks to get a coffee staff were exceptionally rude making it clear that you were an inconvenience to them. The duty free and shop selection is quite good but flying Ryanair I couldn't buy anything with their strict cabin baggage allowance. I was disappointed at the lack of free wifi a facility I have encountered in the majority of airports across the world. £1 for 10 mins internet is excessive I think. A long walk to the gate and a lot of bag checking and weighing by Ryanair staff more sets of stairs and I was finally onboard. Glad to be leaving the airport and the stress behind. I am very disappointed at Stansted it used to be a lovely airport to fly from. It's extremely stressful now and the customer service in general is very poor. I will avoid Stansted in future.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: N Smith
content: Having returned from newly renovated Billund Airport in Denmark early on Monday morning we returned to a very tired and shabby looking Stansted. The new passport entry facility for those with the new type of passports only let two out of each ten people through the automated gates the others having to queue like the rest of the hordes of arrivals. The people in security are surly and unhelpful using gestures to move people around the poorly marked areas where you are meant to wait for your fellow travellers who have failed to negotiate the automated gates. Compare this to the English speaking security guard who stopped me in Billund to check my case who apologised for keeping me waiting and could not have been more courteous. The ride back to the mid stay car park in the bus with the faulty speakers so you couldn't here the driver's instructions to be charged £51 for three days and then to see the litter blowing around the access roads is a terrible advertisement for visiting the UK.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Morney
content: I've used this airport around 6-8 times in the last 12 months. It gets very busy on a Saturday morning (departing) and Sunday evening (arriving). On the last 3 occasions I've used it I've done arrival only on a Wednesday or Friday at approx 10pm. One these 3 occasions there has been no queue for passport control and I've been out and away easily. On the few occasions I've landed on a Sunday evening (approx. the same time) it's been a different story - the arrivals area has been packed with long queues for passport control. So I'm giving a good satisfaction score for my recent arrival experiences and I won't be planning a Sunday evening arrival in the near future!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Haddock
content: I use Stansted currently 4-5 times a year and in the past more frequently. Unfortunately it is the only London Airport that has flights to my regular destination. Public Transport links are poor and overpriced as far as rail services are concerned - particularly if trying to get to the airport from the south coast for a departure before 10am. Bus services to/from central London reasonably priced and frequent but the same problem of how to get to Central London early enough by train to reach Stansted for a pre 10am flight. The terminal is tired and not a good advert for Britain particularly as on exiting the arrivals hall passengers find themselves in a burger bar. It is not any better when you step outside under the canopied area as it stinks of cigarettes. Toilets too few for passenger numbers overcrowded and not cleaned frequently enough. Security checks often suffer from overcrowding and can be slow. Charging £1 for plastic bags is a rip off. Border Control overcrowded - queues frequently spill into the corridors approaching the area and staff in recent times seem to have been generally trained to be officious in their demeanour rather than official - a polite smile and thank you costs nothing and does not in any way inhibit a person's ability to do their job properly.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: B Hemsley
content: Having used this airport many times in the past they have changed the set down area. The old system of a separate road that worked successfully has been closed to only "authorised" vehicles and is now empty. You now have to use an Express set down area with a charge! This is unclear until you have passed it and the confused motorists are harassed by a Parking Enforcement vehicle! The early morning drop off became a stressful experience which I will not repeat - other Airports will benefit. It does not take a genius to work out how much "simple revenue" is being raised for an inferior service. My main objection is that it takes much longer for a simple drop off. The old system was superior.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Mahaffey
content: Sadly this is an airport which arrogantly seems to think its customers owe it thanks and which is not aware that there's a choice. The facilities are tired the security is slow aggressive and pedantic. As for drop off and collection you cant get near the airport building now without huge extra charges (eg over £5 added to valet companies' charges £2 for car access both for dropping off and for pick-up with punitive rates if you over-run). Its all dressed up as some kind of ecological drive to discourage travellers arriving or departing by car but in truth its just a financial scam. Its a thoroughly unpleasant airport and deserves to sink probably along with its main user Ryanair. I use Stansted over 30 times a year because I need to go to a destination only served from there. But rest assured if there comes a choice!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Ekerete
content: Great infrastructure but is mismanaged. Fleecing the passengers of their money seems to be the primary concern. They actually charge people 1 pound for the see through bags for security check. They also charge GBP1 to use scales to ensure that your bags are not over weight limit and have the most expensive left luggage fee I have seen (10 pounds a day). On my visit the toilets were filthy despite the airport being very quiet. I saw no attendants. Shame on you Stansted airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Peter Cullen
content: Some good things some bad. Departure generally a good experience security queue less than five minutes with helpful and pleasant staff staff in shops and cafe friendly. Arrival though was very poor: first we were kept waiting on the aircraft for 15 minutes as 'the terminal doors were locked' in mid-afternoon (was nobody expecting us?). There then followed a very long walk indeed to the truly dreadful passport control area (always extremely crowded) we joined the queue for the automatic readers though an official said it would probably be quicker to queue for a conventional check - he was right. The long-stay car park is very expensive given its distance from the terminal (a 10 minute bus ride) and has the most confusing numbering system for the bus stops known to man - as I have said before be very careful to note exactly where you park your car and which bus stop you use.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Gary Smart
content: Great airport and good customer service. Just needs a refreshing uplift don't think anything's been done in 10 years!

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Anna Kleinzahler
content: I use this airport frequently and think on the whole it is pretty good. It can get crowded first thing in the morning between 5-8am) and on Sunday evenings but otherwise I find I just have to wait a few minutes to drop off my luggage and 5-10 minutes to get through security. I have found the staff polite and helpful. On the return flights the main problem is at passport control where there can be a lot of people particularly if several flights arrive at about the same time. The automatic passport machines seem to be temperamental - sometimes they recognize me and sometimes not. Luggage is usually on the belt in 15-20 minutes. Car parking as at just about all airports is expensive. It sometimes has cost me more to park the car for a few days then I've paid for the flight. Free and fast wi-fi is common in many airports in Europe (Paris Munich Vienna) and it should be also at all of London's airports.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: T Dan
content: This was a great airport when it opened but awful now. Security staff unfriendly and departure lounge area really crowded - seems Ryanair passengers are held there for as long as possible while the non-Ryanair piers connected to the transit appear under used. Good point was swiftness through passport control I must have been lucky from seeing other reviews. Such a shame as this is a great building and has been badly neglected.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Mark Evans
content: The early Friday morning rush was already over but it still took some 25-30 minutes to negotiate security. This is unacceptably slow and reflects not enhanced security arrangements but simply poor organisation. Of the nine scanners installed just three were in operation. By the time I had completed security procedures there was no time to sample the "retail experience". If I were a retailer paying top-dollar rentals at STN I would be wanting a word with the Airport Management about its failure to deliver customers.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: J Ingram
content: It would be a lovely airport if it wasn't for Ryanair's inability to check in board or disembark passengers in an orderly efficient manner. They ruin the airport. It is easy to get around with very little obstructions from drop- off to gate and a decent selection of shops but with pretty much only 1 toilet after security it bulges with the thousands that pass through every day. Its when you get to the gates were the real problems star they are basically long strips with not enough room for queuing and seating throughout. On the up side however it is kept very clean and immigration staff are cheerful and efficient.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Limmack
content: I am a fairly frequent air traveller but have nver witnessed such crass ineptitude as I did at Stansted airport on my trip this week. At check in for the outward flight only half of Ryanair staff were at their posts when the desks opened queues were mixed up with no member of staff helping or organising the queues. On arrival back at Stansted the custom checkpoint was inadequately manned resulting in it taking over 1 hour to clear customs and this was 'normal' according to the only member of staff who spoke to anyone. Pity help anyone arriving for the Olympics they had best bring a sleeping bag.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Hesketh
content: Mixed feelings about this airport - very affected by your flight time. If on an early flight you will find terrible overcrowding in the airport retail food sector areas because flight gates are not announced until 45 mins before departure. With so many budget airline flights leaving between 6am and 7am expect chaos which is a shame since food and retail outlets are very good. Why they will not let passengers go to gate early where there is plenty of seating is beyond me. Likewise if you land late evening expect very long queues and indifferent staff at border control 30-45 minute wait normal. Dominated by cheap flight airlines only fly from here if flight price worth it. How any further expansion of the airport or a second runway be considered is beyond me believe BAA has to sell this airport and lack of any further investment obvious.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Vice
content: I had always been happy with Stansted before Friday night took almost 2 hrs of queuing before my girlfriend could get through passport control. Only 6 desks open and hundreds and hundreds of people queuing right down the corridors leading to the hall. Visitors will hate the UK before they even step foot outside the airport. What made it worse was there was no announcements or info given out so everyone was just standing waiting wondering what was going on when flights had landed so long before but still no sign of their friends/family.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Adam Wood
content: I fly from Alicante to the UK (Essex) fairly often. I usually go into Stansted as it is cheaper but after the last few times will be paying the little extra to use Southend. As others have mentioned a large percentage of the staff would benefit from some extra or just some training in the art of customer service particularly the immigration staff who appear at times to take great delight at the expense of the so called customers frustration.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Wilson
content: Flying out Thursday no problem - flying back Sunday 22 April very different. Locked in narrow steel corridor before being allowed into hall for passport control massive queue when got to desk I politely queried what was happening I was she was just doing her job looking over her shoulder 2 police in full regalia laughing at us no apology just treated like animals appears either staff or facilities not adequate - will try to avoid this airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Beech
content: Flying out from Stansted was ok but how rude are the staff! The experience when I arrived back from Gran Canaria at 11.40pm on 14 April was dreadful. It took an hour to reach border control having been held in a series of very crowded and stuffy corridors and treated like cattle. At every turn we came across more rude staff who's only explanation for the ridiculous delays was '5 flights all arrived at the same time'. This is an airport that can no longer cope with the volume of flights that come and go and I will try to ensure I never set foot in the place again until they do something to improve the experience for arriving passengers.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Gordon Jackson
content: I now actively seek flights that do not depart/arrive from this airport. Outbound early in the morning was ok security reasonably swift but staff are bluntly rude at all stages. The fee for plastic bags if the one you have is 'the wrong size' is plain gouging. Customers are treated as an afterthought. From being unloaded from aircraft to being held in corridors while herded out back onto busses to be transferred to another in-bound gate. With no explanation as to why we went up and down at least 4 escalators and walked for 10 mins. Staff training of customs officers at passport checking another unwarranted delay. The signage is appalling. Do not attempt to navigate into or out of this airport in less than 60 minutes.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: S Timms
content: I use this airport and have no problems every week it seems people still do not understand all liquids must be in a plastic bag out of your hand baggage and then wonder why they get a bag check I am asked so many times if I have liquids before I put my bag through the scanner. Do as you are asked and you will not have a problem! The airport itself is looking tired and a bit dirty but on the whole is ok.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Yevheniy Kahanovych
content: I used Stansted for midday flight and was quite pleased. Last week I was leaving at 7 am so arrived at 5am. The airport was packed 50 planes were leaving around the same time. No problems with signs no trouble using bus station but when it came to security search it was terrible. When into the scanning hall staff were polite and fast. They are so inefficient about scanning laptops! When in the lounge it was absolute madness many flights were shown as "wait for boarding" without gate numbers. Hundreds of people waiting by the screens crowding and creating huge backlogs. My gate was called 15 minutes before departure together with 5-6 other flights. Hundreds of people went to the shuttle train which is capable of carrying up to 200 people but not the 1200 hurrying to the gates on short notice. Overall the facility is clean with plenty of eateries good signs and transportation connections but horribly overused and very stressful.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: T Haw
content: Very late for a flight I needed to get through the scanners and run to the gate before it closed. I had forgotten to put my deodorant in a plastic bag. They diverted the backpack and made everyone wait for over 20 minutes while they slowly went through all the bags they were diverting for a hand-check. The airport was almost empty but we were hugely congested. I begged them to let me take it out and throw it away they refused and kept on at an exasperating plodding place. I warned them they were going to make me miss my flight they didn't care and refused to help. I missed the flight by several minutes. I will avoid Stansted at all costs for any future flight - it breeds petty tyrants and hasn't heard of customer service.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Andy Martin
content: Queuing times are quick with check-in not taking any longer than 15 mins security is usually about 10 and passport control taking around 5 mins. The entire airport both inside and outside the terminal building is clean and well maintained. Both before and after security a large variety of shops and food outlets.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Schofield
content: Check-in queues are long make sure you allow plenty of time. Security queues are long especially on Monday mornings so make sure you have at the very least 2 hours before the gate opens to make sure you get enough time. Priority boarding at Stansted is wasted money as all it does is ensure you're at the front of the queue and queuing in the hottest part of the airport. On the return trip the automated passport control is the poorest system I have seen failing so often they created a special queue for those that the system didn't recognise. One of the main problems was the camera was to the side of where you placed the passport not directly in front.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: M Johnston
content: A small international airport with little to do during transit. Quite clean with a few shops and a cafe free Wifi and smoking room. Quite decent given its size.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Morton-Alexander
content: In fairness the car parking is good but the walk from the short stay car parks is grubby smells unpleasant and was poorly lit. On arrival having checked in online baggage drop for Ryanair was poorly manned and incapable of moving the queues with any professionalism. After queuing for 40 mins we were pulled out of the queue for our flight. Once through to departures there was no gate number showing on the departures board it is difficult to see what food might be available as the food court just runs on with no signs or layout guides readily visible. Toilets are remote and give no indication of distance. Airport was unbelievably hot. Suddenly a sign came up saying boarding at Gate 88 and then within a very short time gate closing was shown. Certainly insufficient time for an elderly lady to walk to Gate 88. Once we arrived hot and bothered having been unable to get to a loo on the way we found a huge queue and the ramp wasn't even out yet. They called priority boarding once and unless you were at the gate at a sprint you missed it. The airport is stuffy poorly air-conditioned badly resourced and serviced by grumpy staff who are indifferent to the customers.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Bob Scott
content: Stansted immigration control is a shambles. I arrived back Tue evening on time at 6.30pm and it took nearly 1 hr to get through EU/UK immigration control while my taxi had to wait. It would have been quicker if I was non-EU.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Keenaghan
content: We fly from London airports at least 3 times a yr last week we flew from Stansted-Malaga with Easyjet. All was well until we went through Security with our hand luggage. I told the official as I put my bag jacket and small bag containing a few items of cosmetics into the plastic tray that my bag contained insulin and other diabetic-related paraphernalia. My carry-on bag was diverted from the main conveyor without any explanation where it sat for more than 5 mins before a male staff member took it to a table and started to empty it out. When I politely asked what the problem was I was told that my plastic bag containing a few items of cosmetics was the 'wrong size' ( I have used this bag at Heathrow x 2 Miami Cork Dalaman and Luton) and was directed to a machine where I paid £1 for four bags. I transferred my liquids to the new bag and expected this to be the end of the matter. My mobile was inspected with a geiger like object as was my husband's i-pod. They were then taken to another machine and re-inspected. Nothing was found as there was nothing to find. After 15-20 mins the official indicated that I could re-pack my bag. I asked again politely what the problem had been. He then picked up my cosmetic bag rooted through it and pulled out my mascara - which he hadn't looked through previously. 'This' he said waving it under my nose. 'It should have been in the plastic bag'. So it took all that time and the emptying of the entire contents of my bag to tell me that. Ironically he didn't look through the diabetic items - insulin Novo-pens needles a glucometer and testing strips etc. I am fully aware that Security is of the greatest importance but perhaps their security staff need to undertake further training in dealing with the general public.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: K Spilling
content: Every thing was fine on departure except security control had massive slow moving queues with people everywhere. Other passengers were panicking about missing flights as it took about 30 minutes to clear security. There was just not enough security lanes open for the amount of people in the airport. Too many people seem to be held in the shopping area before being told which gate to go to. We already new roughly what gate our flight would depart from and headed to calmer atmosphere near the gates. I can’t believe this airport was pressing for a second runway when it can’t handle the passengers it’s got now. If you’re not an experienced traveller I would suggest that Stansted is best avoided! On return it took over an hour to get through immigration. Massive queues everywhere we were held in hot cramp unventilated corridors with no explanation as to why. Car parking very efficient at the mid stay prompt bus and very helpful driver. I’m seriously considering looking at other airports now even if they are further away. Since you will be stuck in endless queues at Stansted anyhow.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Maclean
content: Second time at Stansted and most certainly the last. Two main reasons. Firstly the truly abysmal and over- priced "fast and no fuss" train service to London. Our trip back to the airport was an shambles. Some issue on the line appalling communication and a couple of trains worth of passengers dumped in the car park at Broxbourne Station. Cue chaos. We waited an hour for the promised buses in 26 C heat and after concluding that they might never arrive ordered a taxi from Harlow (£40) and missed our flight. Then the shambles that is check in and security. It is almost as though the airport isn't expecting there to be any passengers. It took over an hour to get through security checks - more than half the xray machines were unmanned - and best of all we were told our plastic bags carrying fluids were the "wrong size". Luckily the airport can sell you plastic bags for £1. Even better the official selling the bags managed to keep a straight face when he said the £1 wasn't about making money. So in summary avoid the train at all costs. If you have hours to kill and want to stand in queues for ages then this is certainly the airport for you.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: T Ferreira
content: Used this airport to fly to Glasgow rtn Great staff support from special assistance and also polite staff through security who were very good with my friend who has a learning disability. Nice selection of shops and food outlets. Out of the terminal within 15 minutes of landing. Stansted Express train very good too.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Ettwein
content: Returned on a flight to Stansted on 15 June 2011. Flight arrived ten minutes early at 11.45 pm- then followed by a one hour slow moving queue from the arrival gate into the main terminal passport hall. No explanations provided security staff dismissive when asked why there is a delay-and no apologies from UK Border Agency. Hundreds of passengers stopped in the corridors. This is a disgrace to the airport. Surely they must know how many passengers to expect at any given time as there were no unforeseen flight delays from anywhere. Given a choice (which we don't have) we would never use this airport again.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: G Hall
content: Arrived back in the UK at 06:15 am on 9 June transit and baggage claim fine passports and customs fine. Toilets in the main departures area were disgusting and unusable. Departures drop off point was being vigorously policed by officials with cameras and would allow Pickups in this area so then tried to find our way to the arrivals Pick up point! So poorly signed I roamed around for 10 mins trying to find my way out to the 15 min Short stay eventually got the idea so called my friend who was picking us up but it was too late they missed the badly signed entrance and ended up in the Red Car Park instead where it cost £2.60 for a 60 second pick up.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Briggs
content: Why can they not close some of the utterly useless shops and put a proper number of immigration desks in their place ? It is ridiculous to have to spend an hour in a queue to get through non- EU immigration and the crowd trying to get through EU immigration cannot have enjoyed it very much more. Add to that the lies about 'every 10 minute departure' to the mid-term car park and you can only conclude that someone else ought to run this airport. And quickly. Avoid it if you possibly can.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Peter Cullen
content: I concur with previous reviewers the immigration queues at Stansted are a disgrace. I use the airport once or twice a year but I have never known anything other than lengthy queues no matter how many posts are manned. Last week (15 minutes) was better than normal but the depressing thing is that nobody seems to be interested in solving the problem; it has certainly not improved in the past 4 years. It is a shame because apart from that Stansted is not a bad airport - though I do try to travel with hand luggage only as check-in can be a lengthy process.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Marek Siwicki
content: There is one very big issue with Stansted Airport and that is the passport control delays that they are experiencing. On landing you are held in corridors in a holding pattern no doubt as other flights are landing they don't want the passport control hall to turn into a crush. I land at the airport at around 12.30am with two young children both of which were very tired. We then had to queue to get to the passport control area they were letting people out in batches of 20 or so then we had to queue to get to the passport check. This was a complete mess. There were no defined queues just a free for all for everyone to get in the best queue or the right place in the hall. For some reason some of the queues seem to move quicker than others and the passport checkers are just super slow. It took us around 1.5hrs to get through the security check to then get our baggage. This is not acceptable. It is an embarrassment to our country that the first experience for visitors to England is a 2 hour queue god knows what is going to happen with the influx of visitors for the Olympics.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: P Maidment
content: Queuing at Stansted Immigration put a total mood dampener on what was a very good holiday. It took us over 50 minutes to get through Immigration.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: E Blackwood
content: Flying Stansted to Rome I was not allowed to use my own plastic bags - forced to pay 1 GBP for four small 20x20cm bags. This is a per-passenger airport tax. What are the profits on this scam? On the way back arriving from Rome late on Sunday night there were disgraceful queues. Held in the corridor and released in batches because immigration was dangerously overcrowded. Then had to wait with my wife for over 90 minutes in the queue. Only two officers working the non-EU line six officers chatting in the EU section. Several people asked them to transfer staff to the very long queue of non-EU citizens but all were refused.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: W Ho
content: Queuing at Stansted immigration counters is always a mood-dampener at the end of a happy holiday. Queues are not too long but one or two immigration officers at peak hours means 45-60 minutes of waiting time for passengers! And you don't need someone to direct passengers to the officers' desks if there are only two officers on duty either we can see for ourselves so go take a seat and get passport-stamping. Other than that an okay airport with decent facilities.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: A Kan
content: I was surprised how modern this airport is considering its small size and used mainly by budget airlines. Minimum delays. Plenty of choices for food on departure efficient at security checks (departure time 7am Sat) . Arrival(10pm Sun) was different though. Very long queue at immigration for non EU passport holders however officers were friendly.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Yevheniy Kahanovych
content: I used Stansted last week for departure and arrival. Both times everything was fine: ok food choices fast delivery of bags no wait at immigration fast security control with need to pay 1GBP per pack of sealed bags. Tried to use my own ones but no way they were "wrong" so had to pay this small "departure tax". Nice and simple connections via rail and bus however not as fast as Heathrow or Gatwick. My only dislike was cheap and tired look of this beautiful building and shuttle trains. Not to say it wasn't clean but it is now kept as second rate US airport.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Brian Pope
content: Once through security you cannot go immediately to the gate but must wait in the shopping area until your gate is posted on a board. Then a train takes you to one of the remote terminals. We did this process twice since we missed our first flight. The strange thing is once you take the train out to the terminal there is no way back. We had to call our airline and have a representative come out and escort us back to the main terminal. I'm sure that the design is good for security and crowd control but someone hasn't thought through all possible scenarios. The second time we went through the process the remote terminal was freezing cold and dingy. Security people friendly and thorough but I got the impression that part of their job description is to enforce the luggage rules (weight and size) for the airline (in this case Easyjet).

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: R Hopkins
content: Ridiculously slow baggage drop no quicker than a conventional check in. Once through the cafe must be the world's slowest. This is a departure lounge - people are going places. We seemed to hit lucky with the car park transfer (for a change!).

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: N Edwards
content: Departure fairly smooth and wait not too long to go through security though finding security was a bit tricky as I didn't walk directly to it from check in instead ending up after a trip to the washrooms at flight crew security. Could do with better roof suspended signage visible east to west (security signage on visible looking north in terminal. Return to UK was pretty dispiriting - plane arrived on time but passing through passport control took an age with slow moving queues - took at least 50 mins. Then with the wait for the long stay bus I finally got back to my car 1hr 45 mins after landing. That's longer than the flight. Not impressed with immigration process at Stansted - I found Gatwick earluer this year much better in most aspects.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: John Rocke
content: If you have to park to drop off or pick up in the Pick-Up car park you will have to pay £2 for 15 minutes. If you stay there for 45 minutes you will be charged £30 (yes £30) for the privilege. Make sure that your intended party has already landed and cleared security before entering this parking area or you will be charged big time. There are no arrivals boards before entering the car park. My daughters flight arrived an hour late after midnight. I had to go into the Pick up but so did everyone else as the drop off point was closed at that time.

title: London Stansted Airport customer review
author: Peter Cullen
content: When departing you need to arrive well before your flight; I queued about 30 minutes at check- in (Ryanair) and 15 for security. Staff were cheerful and helpful but seemed to think this was fairly normal for a midweek morning in summer.
