I have commented to my international friends that as an American I am embarrassed when their first experience in the United States is landing at and passing through JFK Airport.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: P Leftridge
content: Going from plane to baggage claim is the equivalent of going through a Pavlovian maze. However that was just the beginning of my frustrations. Baggage claim itself was a closed-off room and you had to wait more than 30-45 minutes for luggage. After picking up your luggage and going through the second maze you are tired and beyond irritated. To add more fuel to the fire the information desk was less than helpful on where I can catch the hotel shuttle. She was more interested in stuffing her face and reading a book than helping me. Even worse getting to hotel shuttles was another nightmare. I had to go from baggage claim to air train to section c then go down an escalator turn left turn right and then see the shuttles. The only redeeming quality for this airport was Altitudes (Restaurant). The steak dinner I had was on par with some of the better steak houses I have dined at.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Nick Pierson
content: Depending on the terminal one uses JFK can either be acceptable or awful. There is easy access from Manhattan or car parks thanks to efficient airtrain. This also helps get around terminals. We usually use terminal 8 the American Airlines terminal. All our experiences there have been positive with short lines for check-in security hassle-free and short immigration lines upon arrival with bags already on the conveyor belt. This terminal is new airy and spacious and has many shopping and food offerings. AA staff are generally friendlier than the trashy TSA and Port Authority staff who seem like the laziest and most incompetent people on the planet. By sharp contrast terminal 123 and 7 are old and terrible. The oldest and most run down avoid these. Terminal 5 is the Jetblue terminal and is pretty good. So it all depends on what terminal one uses.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: A Bowie
content: We arrive at JFK late from Heathrow 23rd December after being delayed by bad weather. When we arrived at immigration we couldn't believe the queue. We queued for 3 hours because there were only 5 or 6 kiosks manned out of 20. When we got through the queue was the same length behind us and I think it was one in the morning by then. Two out of our party of three suffer from back pain which was made much worse by standing for this length of time. When we complained to the ushers in the hall they were completely indifferent to our plight "I don't want to be here either" "what do you expect its the holidays" were the sort of replies we got. In fairness to the immigration officer who dealt with us he was sympathetic and polite. If I can avoid flying into this airport in future I certainly will.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Kylie McNamara
content: We had the most frustrating experience arriving at JFK after a long flight from Sydney Australia. We stood in a horrendously long line for over 1.5 hrs only to get to the front of the line and be shuffled along by airport officials to another long queue where we waited a further 25 minutes. We were tired hot hungry and plain astonished to be subjected to ridiculously long waits at immigration. The booths were only half full and immigration staff painfully slow and disinterested. Customs and immigration dept is a disgrace. The whole experience made for a very negative start to our holiday.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: N Philpott
content: I have been to every continent in the world in the past 3 years and JFK stands out like a nightmare on the four occasions I have visited. This is not to do with the airport itself but the dehumanising and humiliating attitude of the immigration and security staff. We waited 1.5 hrs on arrival last week - totally unacceptable. On our return experience yesterday we were yelled at by a security guard in English which was probably only intelligible to New Yorkers. There were no notices informing passengers of what was expected - only this intimidating bully. We are passengers customers and human beings - try to treat us as such.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: C Jones
content: Having just travelled from Manchester to JFK on an 8 hr flight we were not happy at being met with the huge queues at immigration. It took 2 hrs of queuing to eventually get to the front only to be sent to queue at individual kiosks. There were only 3 kiosks open to deal with the huge amount of travellers. The room was very hot and the staff were miserable.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Alim Gelyastanov
content: Very surprised to find out JFK is in such a run-down condition. Arrived on a Delta flight from Moscow and had to enter through a dark and gloomy passageway with low ceilings and paint peeling off. Immigration lines were excessively long airport and immigration staff were very rude to the point of just barking orders at passengers. The TSA staff inside the terminal were fast and friendly.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Andrew Kohn
content: The main problem with JFK is the people. There is a complete lack of courtesy friendliness training and in most cases language skills. The signage is lacking. There are simply no signs in other major languages. The friendliest people are the Customs and Border Protection agents. I have always been treated courteously and often in a friendly manner. Most of the terminals are out-of-date or poorly designed. Restaurants are fair-poor and over-priced. I cringe when I need to change terminals. I am forced to use JFK because of the good flight schedules.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: R Liwag
content: Flew into JFK Terminal 4 and went through immigration after suffering through an extended wait and an overly sarcastic interview with the security officer. Customs was uneventful as was the brief AirTrain ride to Terminal 3 for my connecting flight. Terminal 3 Delta Airlines check-in went smoothly. TSA checkpoint to the gates was the worst airport security fiasco I have ever had to endure in over 20 years of flying. Three times we were asked to relocate to different security entrances due to extremely long lines and/or faulty equipment. One security entrance had 3 machines fail simultaneously. Staff members were loud but generally clueless on efficiently directing passengers to alternate security entrances. People at the front of one queue ended up at the back of the next queue when they were made to move. Overall it took me 2.5 hours to clear security.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Peter Schardam
content: Again JFK (terminal 4) lived up to its expectations. On this Saturday afternoon it took over 1.5 hrs to pass through Immigration. Don't they know that so many thousand visitors will arrive or don't they care? Officials were correct and friendly. No problems on that side. As insufficient baggage belts were available they dropped our baggage somewhere in the middle of the baggage hall adding to passenger confusion.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: P Keene
content: Prior to my wife and I going to Europe I knew we would be flying back to the US via JFK instead of ATL which we originally planned. We arrived at JFK from Rome (FCO) via Delta and I was surprised. Everything went smoothly from passport control retrieving our luggage and re-checking to going through security again. Employees were helpful and courteous. However given the layout of the airport and the heavy volume of passengers this airport handles things do have the potential to go south in a second. Additionally NYC was not my destination so I did not have to rent a car or take a taxi to Manhattan. Had I done these things maybe my review would be a bit different. I will say the layout of the airport needs to be updated and the food choices could be improved. However we waited for our connecting flight in another part of terminal 4 (I believe Delta gate 23) There were a few decent places to grab a bite to eat or grab a beer. You are not going to get the amenities that you would at the Atlanta or similar airports but this isn't the worst airport either. I would consider using JFK for a future international flight.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Gil Cureau
content: Prior to my wife and I going to Europe I knew we would be flying back to the US via JFK instead of ATL which we originally planned. We arrived at JFK from Rome (FCO) via Delta and I was surprised. Everything went smoothly from passport control retrieving our luggage and re-checking to going through security again. Employees were helpful and courteous. However given the layout of the airport and the heavy volume of passengers this airport handles things do have the potential to go south in a second. Additionally NYC was not my destination so I did not have to rent a car or take a taxi to Manhattan. Had I done these things maybe my review would be a bit different. I will say the layout of the airport needs to be updated and the food choices could be improved. However we waited for our connecting flight in another part of terminal 4 (I believe Delta gate 23) There were a few decent places to grab a bite to eat or grab a beer. You are not going to get the amenities that you would at the Atlanta or similar airports but this isn't the worst airport either. I would consider using JFK for a future international flight.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: R Dean
content: Arrived from Rome to Terminal 8 (American Air) around 1.00 pm. We have had poor previous experiences at JFK and we braced for another. This time was better. Facility was clean signs were clear along the way to customs helpful staff were visible with forms and keeping the lines moving. The CBP officer reviewing our passport was friendly and efficient. After retrieving our baggage and giving it again to American for the domestic flight to San Diego we then got our surprise. Terminal 8 is not fully secure meaning that cleared travelers exiting customs to go on to another American domestic flight must go through security again. That meant the duty free sealed glass items we purchased in the secure Milan terminal would not be allowed by TSA - they take it or you are escorted out right away. American Air staff at the counter went out of her way to find boxes to help us pack these items and checked it through at no additional fee. Either we missed something or there is a design flaw with terminal security.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: M Fisk
content: Arrived last night at Terminal 8 from Paris. The line for immigration was terribly long staff directing passengers rude and uninformative. The booths for the immigration officers were only one third manned. They know how many passengers will be coming through. It took over 1 hr for us to get through and we were in the short line for US Citizens. The Visitors line was at least three times as long. These poor people probably had to wait 3 hrs. What a terrible welcome to the United States.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: K Paskins
content: The staff varied from ignorant and rude to aggressive. We queued for an hour to check-in then queued for 30 mins to put our bags through the x-ray over 1.5 hrs to get through security. No signs at security in terms of how they wanted people to go through the x-ray. After watching people be shouted at for not moving forward quickly enough we finally saw the security gates. How this can be accepted at a major international airport is beyond me.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: D Sutter
content: Flew through JFK (transit) twice this year. Queuing was a disaster I had to wait more than 1 hr for immigration. Direction signs were confusing even staff were unable to properly direct me to my luggage. Air Train was confusing with different destinations leaving from same track. Terminal 2/3 (Delta) was awful - dirty and chaotic staff working there were inefficient and disinterested resulting in a 1 hr wait at the counter. Service at American Airlines (Terminal 8) was not much better a frustrating and expensive experience. All flights I took to and from JFK were delayed. I would discourage people to use this airport for transiting - or allow plenty of time.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: N Mundorf
content: Two flights were jammed in a long narrow hallway for 15 mins. Signage was bad so US citizens kept cutting in line after finding that short line was for visitors. Rude personnel many people missing connections. Baggage on different carousel than the sign announcement. Took hour to get through. Terminal very hot and stuffy.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: A Marquez
content: No free wi-fi which is disappointing for such a major airport. There are a number of iPads available for use but there connection to the Internet is painfully slow. Would have been better served using the money spent on iPads for providing free wi-fi. Finally facilities are not that clean.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: M Leystra
content: Touched down from Paris everyone is shuffled through a dirty hot hall into a tiny room with no windows. Waited over 1 hr in a line to just pass through New York to Toronto. Layout is awful it seems to be the only airport that doesn't offer free wifi. At my gate there was half the seats needed for the amount of people. Overall its a hot confusing airport.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: M Jensen
content: I've flown in and out of almost every airport in the United States for business travel and JFK has to be the most confusing design I've seen. The departure/arrival directions upon entering the airport are confusing and after check-in a whole group waiting to go through the security checkpoint were hustled outside across the street to another checkpoint that was just as busy. The security checkpoint was the longest most frustrating experience I've had at an airport. The TSA officials were rude and disinterested. Very long walk to the gate limited places to eat once I got there and absolutely nowhere to sit down. Overall not a great experience.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Fearghal O'Reilly
content: I have avoided it based on the horrible experiences of friends and relatives but for some odd reason decided to take a chance and experience it myself. Sadly everyone was right. It is dirty workers are rude shops are limited and it's just a miserable place. I will continue to fly in and out of ATL from now on.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: A Preisz
content: The situation at JFK has been horrible and it is getting even worse. Today at the Delta international arrivals terminal it took passengers (at least the non-US passports) 2.5hrs to get through passport control. 2 passport control stations were open. This is just unbelievable. Everyone has the impression JFK is trying to make passengers miserable on purpose. My family and I do Transatlantic flights many times a year but we all dread of JFK. Both departure and arrival. In addition most of the cases-not all-the JFK staff are arrogant and grumpy. And International arrivals at terminal 3 is a shame. No space no proper information displayed most of the time extremely crowded. You hardly find your pick up there and vice versa.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: David Danton
content: We arrived at Terminal 2 (Delta Airlines) at JFK no problems passing through Customs or collecting luggage. But we had the worst experience ever at an Airport when we went to the Ground Transportation Desk with Our email ticket for the journey into Manhattan by NYAS Airport Service. We were given a ticket by the girl on the desk but our email was not returned to us a taxi driver eventually came after 45 mins (we were expecting a bus transfer which were supposed to leave every 20 mins) There was much confusion as to where our email ticket was the driver said we would have to pay again and the girl at the desk was very very rude and accused us of lying about it. This was all very upsetting and we asked for a supervisor to be called he was a nice man and sorted it all out. By now we had been waiting over 1 hr for our transfer and we were very tired. Not a good experience.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: G Beauchemin
content: Arrived JFK last night from Italy around 8pm. Totally unreasonable connection experience. Had to walk down very long dreary hallway dragging bags over very dirty carpeting. A pretty unimpressive and difficult welcome to the USA. Then told we had to walk to terminal 2 for domestic connection outside up ramps across streets with auto traffic down ramps or stairs about 2-3 blocks in the rain no signage dragging bags to be rechecked. Airline rep said if we had been there before 7 pm we could have done it in same building as arrival. One of our party used wheelchair but no provision was made for their bag which also needed to be rechecked in terminal 2. Another member of the party had to drag both her bag and the one for the wheelchair person. Plus carry-on luggage for both. I expected a cleaner more attractive and smoother welcome to this country. I am a seasoned international traveller but have never had a transfer this difficult anywhere else. Where is the shuttle train or bus service? Where are the automated baggage transfer belts? It seems very unreasonable to expect customers to be subjected to this treatment. I am appalled and embarrassed to known that this is how the USA welcomes international travellers.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Li Chung
content: Immigration was a mess with US guards treating the passengers with ignorance and baggage claim was very crowded. There is also not a lot to do in the airport - very little shops restaurants and overcrowded. Departure Check in was easy but security even at this time was not easy to clear. Leaving JFK is the best thing I can say about this airport. It's a joke compared to most other airports I've been to.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: T Neyrinck
content: BA's Terminal 7 and AA's Terminal 8 compare very well to the better European airports. Not the same level of service as AMS or LHR T5 but better than CDG FRA or ZRH. Swift check-in short walks lounges easy to find decent supply of shops of restaurants. The skytrain between terminals works well. Immigration and customs much more friendly than at IAH (Houston) or ORD (Chicago). Would use JFK again when on BA or AA.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: K Eliott
content: I came back from the Philippines arriving at T3. Our first welcoming was a female doing her nails and yelling at people to get to the right side of the corridor and telling us to wait at an invisible line till she called for the next group to proceed. Welcoming two was a male yelling for us to go to the other side of the room to get on line for immigration. At the other side of the room were people in large crowds coming our way. I then realized the entrance to the immigration line was actually in the middle of the room meanwhile the agent was still telling everyone to go to the other side of the room. Welcoming three was the deplorable condition of the place. T3 looked like a state prison swarmed by dusty looking cab drivers and no entrance for regular traffic thus your only transportation from the terminal is taking a medallion yellow cab.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: D Feehan
content: If JFK is "where America welcomes the world" (as you see on every road sign on the way to and from the airport and hear via the regular tannoy announcement in the taxi queue outside Terminal 1) you could be forgiven for thinking they don't like visitors very much. We arrived at JFK Terminal 1 and straight into a huge queue for the Immigration Desks (only 6 desks open for the mammoth assembled throng). At our time of arrival Air France Lufthansa and Aeroflot all had busy flights arriving at roughly the same time so it is hard to see why more desks were not made available for us given the large number of visitors coming to NYC for New Year. Common sense eventually prevailed and passengers were directed to the desks for US citizens. The few Immigration officials that were on duty were courteous and professional and following a nightmare baggage reclaim (over 400 passengers ganging up on 1 baggage carousel) we were out of the Terminal but not before having to navigate a path through the huge number of cases just left lying around by the flight connections desk. Surely that is a safety and security risk?. Having previously used Terminals 2 and 3 at JFK (don't need to add to the horror stories already posted on here) Terminal 1 is a definite improvement - but not much.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: H Bailey
content: Not a great experience with this airport. Arrived early and in good time to check in however the kiosks used to obtain boarding passes only worked for half of the passengers. We were then told to join the queue for bag drop only to be told by another member of staff we were in the wrong queue and had to join the back of another line. When we finally managed to check in we walked to the area where suitcases for being scanned (I don't know why there was no conveyor belt from the check-in desk like other airports?). There was no indication where the line started and when we walked forward we were shouted at very rudely by a woman which was in all quite embarassing in front of other staff and customers. Going through security a young male worker pushing a lady in a wheelchair was also very rude when we were not moving up the queue fast enough and duty-free was awful. We were told to pick up the items at the gate we asked the woman at the gate who then said they would be brought to us in our seats. As they prepared for take-off we then asked a steward where our things were who said they were at the gate still. When we went back to the gate they said they would be brought to us again. I really was not impressed with this airport but the staff were the people who disappointed me the most.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: T Hinton
content: I travelled to Orlando via New York from Manchester with Delta Airlines When going through passport and visa control at JFK I have never life met such ignorant and arrogant staff not just to me but to others as well. The attitude of some of these immigration officers was unnecessary - you got the impression that they just didn't want to be there and were taking it out on the public. I personally hope it is a long time before I have to pass though this airport again.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: J Jensen
content: SLC-JFK-LHR return. Both times through terminals 2 and 3. These have to be the worst terminals in the world. Terminal 2 filthy very few places to eat. There is no way leaving terminal 4 (International Arrivals) to go to any of the other terminals without going outside of security and having to endure hours of standing in line at terminal 2 or 3 that has one person checking IDs and only two scanners in operation.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: A Newman
content: The Delta terminal at JFK is bar none the worst airport I've ever has the misfortune of flying through. I passed through transferring between an international flight and a domestic flight. Every aspect of the experience was horrible. Lines for customs baggage check-in and security all were terrible. Concessions were ridiculously expensive ($7 for a small bottle of juice at the deli) and of marginal quality. The terminal also had by far the most confusing layout and most useless signage that I've ever experienced. The re-ticketing line was so bad that I was actually grateful that my connecting flight was two hours late so that I didn't have to endure that after waiting in all of the other lines until well after my flight was supposed to have left.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: D Silverstone
content: Terminals 2 and 3 need to be razed to the ground and never spoken of again. While I might miss the "flying saucer" roof of Terminal 3's entrance hall that is the only thing that any sane person would possibly regret losing when this atrocity is finally replaced. As if it weren't outdated and uncomfortable and just terribly laid out for its current capacity and security procedures Delta has clearly given up on any pretence of trying to maintain the facility. To call it filthy and falling apart would be a bit like saying the sun is bright or basketball players are tall. Check-in security bathrooms waiting areas - all of it just atrocious. Whenever I'm choosing flights out of NYC I prefer to fly out of JFK because of the transportation but if the flight is Delta I always have to hesitate just knowing the ordeal I'm in for on the ground. Terminal 7 is the only other part of JFK that even comes close in decrepitude and that terminal is relatively servicable! Terminals 5 and 8 are superb (other than a really long walk from the airtrain to T5) and 1 and 4 aren't too shabby either. AirTrain is fast comfortable and efficient. Long Island Railroad from Jamaica is fastest and most comfortable connection though I'd advise tourists to familiarize themselves with transportation routes and options before arriving.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: F Dellera
content: Terminal 7 it's extremely complex getting to the airport using public transportation. Switching 3 subway lines getting to Jamaica station then the airtrain station changing platforms and wait there's more getting to the Terminal with dozens of other passengers going the same way and once you get through security check forget about going back to another terminal in case your lounge is located there since everything is so crowded. Staff was good but internal facilities were nowhere close to the ones expected from the cultural and financial capital of the USA.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Tom Grant
content: As the self-proclaimed "Gateway to America" this airport is an embarassment. I can't even begin to imagine what our foreign visitors think when they get off the plane and encounter the filthy restrooms in every terminal save Terminal 7. The Port Authority has still not learned how to operate the Air Train efficiently. The "Taxi" hustlers in Terminals 4 and 8 are also atrocious.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Julie White
content: I have just returned from a short break to New York with my disabled mother we had extremely bad experiences at Terminal 4 on arrivals and departures there were four disabled passengers on our flight and assistance had been arranged by out tour operator however the necessary equipment needed to transport wheelchairs from and to the planes were not there and so were kept on the plane (on arrival) and even asked why my mother couldn't walk up the steps to plane and so was taken back to terminal to wait for equipment to be found and put in place. This took 2 hours+ and so resulted in our flight being delayed by 2.5 hrs. the result of which some very unhappy passengers. The disabled passengers were made to feel humiliated and very third rate. I experienced some very miserable extremely rude ignorant unhelpful officials at this airport. and as others have said the immigration process and the security checks are awful no thought is given to those who actually find it difficult and painful to remove shoes coats etc and especially when being hurried and spoken to rudely. Disabled passengers beware - this airport is not disabled friendly.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: P Carson
content: Flew to JFK from DCA for a meeting at Terminal 8 Admirals Club. Good experience all around. Terminal 8 was magnificent in scale and services provided were excellent. Interestingly even the journey from the remote concourse was not that far and was aided by a moving sidewalk. Good steakhouse in terminal and very nice club. Arrival and departure were efficient.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Tim Limbach
content: My family arrived at JFK 4 having been very comfortable in Business class on KLM but the immigration experience was a nightmare certainly not fast-track! We were herded like sheep for about 90 minutes. I had already completed the new ESTA forms online but still had to complete the green form for each passenger which I had done on the plane. Only about half the booths were staffed and as we were already exhausted my back was very painful by the time we reached the baggage hall where the bags were already waiting! So much for travelling with hand baggage to speed up arrival process. The USA is a lovely place to visit but surely systems can be improved?

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: J Lockett
content: I would have preferred to make a complaint directly to the department in JFK that deals with customer service but I see there is no direct email address. I came through Terminal three at midnight on 16th October and I was traumatized by the whole experience . The place being run down the dirty floor your asked to walk bare feet on I can live with but the staff. Some one in authority needs to go through this as a customer and they would be appalled. You are screamed at glared at they make faces at other customers behind their backs. Even the official at the beginning of the queue said nothing other than chew her gum and flick her finger which was no doubt the JFK International symbol for go past ? We were all screamed at to get our shoes off our belts off etc none of which anyone have a problem with but we were all made to feel like criminals and the atmosphere was disgusting and a disgrace to the USA . The staff here are aggressive bullying and intimidating - as I found when I said in a loud voice "a please and thank you would be nice " all I got was a glare and despite no alarm going of when stepping through the alarm door I was asked to do it again.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: A Lamont
content: Arrived T4 connected to T2. Immigration at T4 was okay but officials were rude. Waited for a long long time at the baggage carousel (I think it may have been randomly searched). Connection to T2 was easy enough but the terminal was ancient and miserable. Was delayed for 2 hours in-terminal and 1 hour on-tarmac. Was exhausted and impatient. I will probably avoid JFK if possible in future.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: R Lord
content: Terminal 2. Other commentators describe it as a hell-hole how right they are. There are plenty of third world terminals that are better. The awfulness of the whole place is hard to imagine luckily I will never have to return.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: B Rooney
content: Used T4 for DL LAX departure with onward int'l flight. I am writing to alert people to a strange potentially alarming experience at security for the B gates in mid-July. I put my shoes coat bag of toiletries laptop and other items in the trays along with my carry-on bag. In the time it took me to turn around wait for one person ahead of me to walk through the scanner and reach my trays (20 seconds) my laptop had disappeared. I had read about this sort of thing before but thought I had taken the right precautions. No amount of asking staff to help got me anywhere other than a warning to "move away". After 90-120 seconds or rechecking and making a larger and large fuss some one I assume to be the manager asked me what I was missing and "was it a laptop in a black case". Item rescued and I was relieved - until I thought about this and it seemed more and more of a concern. I am not accusing anyone but it took an amazingly short period of time for it to disappear and a strangely long period of time to be "found". Just be careful and be warned. Otherwise T4 is among the best at JFK but shop eat and before security leave enough time to clear security (40 minute queue) and mind your trays!

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Dave Stone
content: Experience at JFK will depend entirely on what terminal(s) you're using. If you're not flying Delta you can disregard the gripes and complaints of reviewers talking about T3 etc. Terminal 1 international is good and relatively smooth but almost no food/shopping before security. T2/T3 (Delta) is old and run-down in the extreme. Very sad since it started life as the jetsons-like Pan Am worldport in the 60's. On the other hand I've always found T3 to be the fastest plane-to-gate trip for international travel - provided you know how to navigate the terminal and are a US citizen. T4 (International) is nice and modern has a huge shopping area before security - but security and after is miserable and dull. T5 (JetBlue) is a long hike from the AirTrain to the gates but has the smoothest security great food options and is very comfortable post-security. T7 (British Airways United) is old and poorly maintained. Reasonably quick to get through but hardly an impressive gateway terminal. T8 (American) is very airy and efficient and makes one long that the Airline lived up to it! JFK is a huge airport and international gateway and should be compared alongside Heathrow DeGaulle and the like. As such it doesn't look too bad -- though that's not saying much! Customs and Immigration are definitely a bit closer to being pleasant!

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Bill Kavanagh
content: I picked up my wife today from DL97 from Edinburgh at Delta's Terminal 3 International arrivals. The area can only be described as a "hell hole". Dirty poorly lit decrepit. Choose your adjective. This terminal would be right at home in some banana republic but what a horrific introduction to the USA.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: S Ashton
content: My 19 year daughter who had travelled from the UK alone arrived at JFK on 7th June 2009 at 2:20pm. As a worried parent I assured her that there would be people employed at the airport who would be happy to help her. How wrong could I have been! She was "greeted" by surly unhelpful staff that seemed to view visitors to your country as an inconvenience at best and a downright nuisance at worst. I assume these people do not have any form of customer service training. I suggest you rectify this and perhaps tell them they are supposed to welcome visitors to your country - and smile now and again not snarl and growl.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: L Zijlstra
content: Last week I arrived at JFK T3 and was shocked to see the state it was in. It's disgusting old and dirty not what I expected from an airport of New York. I didn't feel safe in the arrival hall. We were approached by dodgy people and it felt like we were in a ghetto. There was also no clear information displayed how to get to the other terminals (we had to pick up my parents) On the way back the departure lounge was even worse ancient looking dirty carpets rude people and security staff and duty free shopping was a joke. I think America should be really ashamed of the state of this airport it's a disgrace.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: J Adamowicz
content: Used T8 for a recent trip to and from FCO on American. Found the terminal to be clean with a fair amount of service choices. The customs process on the way back was fairly smooth. All in all not a bad experience despite all of the horror stories you hear about JFK.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Peggy Marshall
content: Connected through JFK from Frankfurt (Delta). Customs was crowded poorly staffed and confusing - multiple international flights arriving of course. After numerous announcements and signage about which carrel to wait by our flight was sent to another carrel - by that time I was just thankful to see my luggage again. After finally passing through the zigzag line at Customs those of us who were connecting through Delta were sent to a small elevator to ascend to the Delta counter (does this place not have escalators? A second elevator was apparently inoperable.) It probably held 5 people with luggage at one time. Of course staff could bump ahead of you in line and take a spot in the elevator. Good luck if you are disabled. We met with some of the most rude and unprofessional staff that I've ever seen in any airport - it was telling that they were even rude to fellow employees. Start to finish: two hours. Then another horrible stretch of hours until our flight finally took off (from a gate that apparently boards like 5 flights at once and makes you walk up the steps outside.) Did I mention that the bathroom made truck stop restrooms look like the Ritz? Can't imagine that travelers from other countries find it a positive experience! I will never again accept a flight that routes through JFK!

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Sandro Dessi
content: I flew to JFK with BAWand so arrived at T7 and departed from the same terminal on my way home. After getting out of the plane I noticed the dirt on the walls and around the air outlets on the ceiling of the corridors not a nice way to great passengers at the "gate to the US". I had to wait for an hour and a half in that musty air to pass through passport control not even half of the desks were occupied. The televisions right next to you don't make the situation more comfortable as they are set to high volume. The officer was unfriendly never and recalled a trip I had made to Havana/Cuba.. On the day of departure I was surprised to stand in front of the gate within 15 minutes after arriving at the airport. BA staff was very friendly and helpful security checks were very lax compared to LHR for example which is kind of worrying. The departure level left a much better impression compared to the arrival level. It was clean bright and the air was better but why on earth do they set the ac to blizzard temperature at max flow? After getting on the plane I had headaches. The choice of food was bad. Fast food fast food fast food and one restaurant with exaggerated prices. Staff at Balducci's where I finaly bought a tasteless sandwich for $9 was unfriendly and annoying as they were complaining to customers about their working conditions. Overall I was very disappointed and happy to get in the plane. That terminal can not be compared with standards I'm used to at European airports even Havana was better!

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Dave Darcy
content: Possibly the worst airport in the world. Terminal 7 is dirty staff are rude there is nowhere to sit. Then when you fancy a beer or a glass of wine the tariff isn't on display the staff encourage you to leave a tab open and when you have had two beers and your wife has had two glasses of wine they hit you with a bill of almost 50 dollars. Gate way to the US country of customer service excellence - rubbish dreadful never again!

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Richard Vrolijk
content: JFK Airport T4. For departing flights it's really a nice terminal with quite a bit of choice on stores and 2 or 3 places to eat. Getting through check-in isn't a big problem and rarely takes long. On the times I've had to go through it took about 15 min on average. Arriving at T4 is a different story though. I forgot the exact number customs counters they have think it's about 22 they rarely are all open. Most times there were only 4 or 5 open at a time. Bare in mind that it takes roughly between 5 and 10 minutes at the counter itself to go through and that there's usually 3 or 4 flights coming in at the sametime it builds up a line of roughly 600 to 800 passenger. sometimes more sometimes a bit less. So you do the math of how long you'll have to wait in line. For me it was an avarage of 2 hour waiting whereas 30 minutes of them there was no movement at all. My advice to everyone traveling to JFK and arriving at Terminal 4 get a front row seat in the plane or as closest to the front as possible and when you're allowed to get off the plane hurry to the line as the difference between a front row seat and a rear row seat can easily add a few hours to your waiting time. Other than that JFK is a nice airport and the clerks are usually friendly at T4. Even though a lot of them seem to be really bored at doing their jobs.

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: Adam Rappaport
content: Terminal 5 - Jetblue Terminal. Best selection of restaurants in a US terminal. Free Wi-Fi. Great take-out food with the opportunity to have food to go delivered to you at the gate! Easy to navigate! Architecturally ok!

title: New York JFK Airport customer review
author: John Oram
content: JFK probably is not significantly different to other US aiRports but I am going to keep on posting similar comments until something filters through to the ghastly DHS. So much of what is done at security where there were avoidable delays again today is cosmetic futile and politically motivated. It has very little to do with keeping people safe and everything to do with what looks good even it does keep people waiting around in stockinged feet. There has never been a convincing argument for removing shoes and the DHS/TSA are clearly oblivious to the physical effort this requires for some. Laptops no longer need to be removed from bags at LHR but JFK clings on to another pointless process. At least we left at a good time of the day and after the delays inflicted on us by Delta were quickly airborne.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: S Warrier
content: Never seen the airport clean. The restrooms are filthy. Unflushed toilets, toilet paper all over. If the airport authorities are going to promote this airport, better start with the restrooms. The seating areas are equally nasty - torn seats, litter and so on.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Matt Mardanov
content: We had two-hour layover between flights from Frankfurt, Germany to St Louis. Immigration took 1.5 hours and security check 30 mins and we missed the departure time. On the passport control, 30% of kiosks worked and the process was extremely slow. Why does Homeland Security do nothing to improve airport passport control and security.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Oscar Cano
content: The ground staff are rude, there is no difference between business check-in and economy one, both with the minimum staff. There are almost no shops and it is impossible to buy international newspapers. The business lounges of United are well below standards.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Peter Cargo
content: Having passed through Newark twice in 2 weeks, it must be the worst airport in the USA or possibly the western hemisphere. My family and I had 3 hours after landing from Belfast NI on a United flight, to connect to a flight to Orlando, we missed it. 2.5 hours in immigration. The staff were disinterested in the fact you have a connecting flight, most of then can hardly speak English, so why are they there in the first place? The immigration officers are slow and there is not enough of them. We had to collect our baggage and then get through security even though we had a connecting flight. On the way back from Orlando we had a 2 hr 11 min flight and then a 3 hour wait to the flight back to Belfast, all with United Airlines. When we touched down (on time), there was no gate for our plane to go to, and then when we got a gate there was a plane at it, then when it left the pilot could not taxi to the gate, but had to be towed, but there was no one to tow the plane, then when we got to the get there was no one to attach the ramp to the plane. One hour later we finally got off the plane, Hang your head in shame Newark. You are not part of the American dream, in fact you are a nightmare to all that cross your threshold.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: M Yakan
content: What a bad airport. Horrible at best. It looks as if the last time it was renovated was in the 60s: small crowded waiting areas at the gates, broken chairs, torn padding, not enough outlets (people were huddled up over the few outlets that were available to charge their phones), small decrepit washrooms, very few food/shopping options, and no free wifi. Getting stuck in that airport for 5 hours while waiting for delayed flights is true torture. I was initially in Terminal A at gates A11-18, then A22-28. At least the lines at security weren't that long in the evening, but it is very hard to find anything real positive to say about this airport. I am now dreading the fact that I already have an international connection through it in the summer.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Ian Robinson
content: Just come back via Newark to the UK and I was bitterly disappointed with everything after Security ie on the air- side. We'd taken a fair amount of cash with us for a significant anniversary and had quite an amount we wanted to spend rather than change back to £'s at a pretty poor rate. Imagine my dismay to find you don't appear to be able to pay cash for the anything vaguely expensive so trying to pay for an expensive meal to get rid of your dollars was a total failure. The meal we had was expensive and 2 x major issues: We ordered some sides but they delivered one with the starters! Why? A starter was badly burnt - why would any decent chef even think about sending it out? It tasted so bad I had to send it back. The Duty Free is also really poor. We flew from Birmingham UK which probably has a fraction to the Newark passenger numbers but hugely bigger duty free areas. Perhaps its because Newark has 3 x sites? Also the Internet - why not free as Birmingham Uk or a really easy way to pay for a "one off event" rather than limit it to hours. You have no control over wether your flight will be delayed after all. If I go the the USA on business I'll ask our travel organisers if I can go another way.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: S Kamal
content: Other than its great location of being close to New York - Jersey City there are no real redeeming qualities. Customs - Queues are between 0 to infinitely long depending on how many CBP officers feel like working. I soon figured out which officers to ignore as they were prone to having lengthy "And I think...." talks versus the stamp "Welcome back Sir". Facilities - they are never clean enough terminal B mens room always has a broken stall (every week). Food options in departure are horrible. A Dunkin Donuts stall would actually elevate it to 3 star rating. The pre clearance area however has vastly improved. No one spends time in the pre-clearance area as the Clearance area can have line ups as long as 45mins - reason TSA. Usually commute via YTZ-EWR on Porter.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Kathie Schoenleben
content: Recently I experienced this airport for the first time - coming in from Germany to connect to a domestic flight. Why Lufthansa thinks 2 hours is sufficient to connect here do not ask me. Just changing buildings is a strike against you from the beginning. Immigration officer was among the rudest I have experienced. The customs officer knew I was in a hurry to try to make my connection and I think he intentionally sent me over to the customs desk for extra inspection. The customs officer at the inspection desk made some unbelievable comments about how "frantic passengers" tend to make the officer want to search them. I have never in my life been almost threatened by customs coming into the US and I have come into many other airports. In general coming into the USA is an awful experience for citizens and non-citizens but Newark tops anything I have experienced so far. I missed my connection of course and spent the night in a shabby hotel. Between the airlines Lufthansa and United and Newark airport this was a really terrible trip. I will avoid connecting in Newark in future.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Jan Trevor
content: Don't eat here. $40 for 2 beers and 2 hamburgers and they added a tip for my using the touch screen order pad. So called craft beer tasted like yesterdays slopping from a Munich beer hall. Going from the commuter terminal to United Airline's terminal is confusing. I gave one star for a very clean and bright terminal and 1/2 star for the lack of the old Continental club.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: T Patrick
content: Arrived late Friday from the CX flight waited about 40 minutes standard in USA but far better than Miami and JFK. Parking right outside airport so off pretty fast. Check in for the very late CX return took about ten seconds you are the last flight leaving so all very fast in airport lounge really good and the staff did a good job of managing an unruly mainland Chinese crowd who jostle and shove all the time a good experience as far as US entry goes. CX need To have a Chinese speaker at check in though.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Ian Hay
content: Please try to avoid this airport if you possibly can. The USA Immigration staff are lazy surly and arrogant people who have permanent scowls on their faces and cannot be bothered to man their booths in the face of hundreds of people trying to get through immigration quickly to catch connecting flights. The guy who was directing passengers from separate Edinburgh and Glasgow flights could not hide his embarrassment at the lazy immigration officers who he described as being more interested in their countless coffee and doughnut breaks than serving customers. Gangs of immigration officers seemed to hang out in an office but did not want to work. We were eventually taken after 80 minutes waiting and the immigration officer was slouched in his seat and could hardly be bothered mumbling to us. Unfortunately we have no choice from Glasgow to USA but I wish we did!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Craig Rooke
content: Has to be the worst airport I have travelled through. No security checks in baggage clothing no metal detectors absolutely anything could of been taken on our flight to Birmingham UK. There are about 6 duty free shops 4 of which of full of cheap market imitation souvenirs. No brand named shops I guess they don't want to be associated with the place. The so called food hall that must cost a fortune in heating bills as it was permanently on the highest heat setting. A restaurant with no clean glasses customer service with the most miserable attitudes from 99% of people who work there. Toilets never cleaned dirty disgusting environment to be in. No free wi-Fi to connect to. How this airport operates is beyond belief I shall not use it again.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: E King
content: The employees at security were very rude. If someone asked a question they remarked in a way as if they were disgusted or made a snide remark. I accidentally left a bottle of water in my bag and it seemed like the biggest deal. It was a mistake and I even said that. His response was "well if everyone made mistakes we'd be here all day". I understand they have a job to do and it needs to be done efficiently but there is no place for rudeness and attitude. There is a lot to be said for treating someone with dignity and respect and that is not what I saw today.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: F Savage
content: I fly all the time for work and unfortunately have to connect through this miserable excuse for an airport quite frequently. Out of all the times I've flown from EWR to BOS my flight has not once left on time. On average the flights I've taken are about an hour behind.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Wise Young
content: I use EWR frequently having flown over 2 million miles on United alone out of this airport in the past decade. I use this airport weekly. Over this period the airport has improved in many ways so that it has become the best airport serving New York better than LaGuardia and JFK. Access food service and ambience have been improving. However in the past six months it has declined significantly. In particular the recent switch to a single company providing all the food services has resulted in a decline in quality and an exorbitant increase in price of food. I am sitting in the Food Court in Terminal C. I just purchased a "Bovine & Swine" hamburger an Onion Ring and 1 fresh orange juice for $19.21 from "Make Your Own Hamburger". MacDonald's provided hamburgers at half the cost of this place. There use to be a Balducci's which made superb New York sandwiches. Now there are places that are more expensive and less good. The service is at best mediocre and occasionally insolent. It is sad that the airport has rented all its food vending space to a single company who can jack up the price on captive audience.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Kitty McKinsey
content: First and last time flying into Newark from abroad. In more than 30 years of flying into U.S. airports I have never had to wait more than eight minutes at Immigration. The wait here was one hour and 10 minutes for U.S. citizens and more than two hours for foreigners. Out of 26 counters for U.S. citizens three or four were staffed (depending on breaks). The entire time we were subjected to ads on TV screens encouraging us to pay $100 to avoid these lines. This is beyond outrageous. The amount I pay in income tax should entitle me to decent service - I should not have to pay extra for it. As a consequence of this totally unreasonable and unanticipated wait I missed my connecting flights (despite on paper a connecting time of more than two hours!). In the future I will do everything possible to avoid this airport.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: S Mogensen
content: This has got to be one of the worst immigration experiences ever. After a long flight from Europe the line for immigrations was 2 (two) hours. About 4 booths were open and the rest were closed. What is this? A third world country? I fly to EWR quite often both for pleasure and business and the immigration process is poor every time. This is far worse than any other US airport I have used.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Richard Ogden
content: I was on a flight at 21.20 with BA to Heathrow from terminal B. The terminal was quiet with no queues at check-in or security. The terminal was calm and nicely designed much less chaotic than JFK. The facilities air-side aren't fantastic but I've noticed that American airports in general aren't good at that. Plenty of places to charge your phone or iPad but as others have noted no wifi which is a pity. Transport from Manhattan to the airport is easy efficient and fast the only downside being the gruesome Penn Station. Overall I had a very happy experience here!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Derek Salter
content: Arrived from the UK and found the experience through immigration and baggage claim so simple - landed and being collected outside within 50mins. Return trip less straightforward. Security lines were long and in the confusion I mislaid my laptop. Waiting area for planes rather limited in seating and facilities. But would use it rather than JFK for easy of access and quick immigration on arrival.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Ronda Wright
content: If I could rate this airport a 0 I would! There were a number of problems here: luggage taking 25 minutes to be released from an international flight when so many people had connecting flights about to leave only 2 security lines open after 4 international flights just landed and over half those people trying to go back through security to catch a domestic flight. The absolute worst experience was due to a police office/security guard. As I was heading to the immigration line after securing my luggage I decided to head further up the side of the line to say goodbye to my friends that had already been in the massive line for awhile. As I started calling out to them the officer started yelling at me that I had no right to cut the line. I tried to explain to him that I wasn't cutting the line I was just trying to say goodbye. (In fact I have global entry so there is a separate much quicker line for me to enter through immigration.) He continued to engage with me and loudly yell that I have no right to cut people that have been in line the entire time. I kept trying to explain to him that I was not cutting and that I was trying to say goodbye but he would not listen in fact he kept cutting me off and loudly shouting at me. I eventually decided to just stop engaging with him but he I was so shocked at how he was trying to make a scene and wouldn't listen to anything I had to say. If this is how officers help you in the Newark airport I'd much rather fly through a different airport - in fact I will avoid this airport as much as I can in the future.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: L Poropatich
content: I had to catch a connecting flight in Newark travelling back from Canada. After we went through customs we were at the security checkpoint and there was only one person checking bags and one looking through the screening machine for TSA. They were the rudest people I have encountered any airport. It was taking so long and people were upset because they were going to miss connectors. They were making rude comments and screaming at passengers that they didn't care it was our problem and if we had beverages in our bag it would take even longer. they even screamed at a man who clearly did not understand English. I did miss my connector as I'm sure did many others. It took an hour to go through this process. I will be sure to avoid the New Jersey airport and surely will not spend any money in their airport. They should be reprimanded for their behavior.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: A Langley
content: Poor security and rude service all round - didn't have a great experience arriving and same again when flying back too the UK most of the staff I found in the airport weren't very helpful and came across as unprofessional. The United self check in service was great and fast but anything that involved human staff contact was poor.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Louise Davies
content: Dreadful experience - customs and immigration was overloaded no automated machines for passport scanning. Three international flights worth of passengers then had to queue to hand in the customs declaration - not surprisingly I missed my connection. Had to change terminals - no clear signage and lousy facilities at the domestic terminals. Avoid like the plague.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: K Goncharenko
content: Avoid this airport at all costs. I flew recently internationally through Newark and it was horrible. The airport is overcrowded and seems to be in a constant state of chaos. Customs is unbelievably bad - long wait and staff are rude. I was in a great hurry since I had a connection flight. Everything seems to be broken or in shabby condition the whole airport just inspires the desire to leave. Avoid at all costs.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: C Fleming
content: Avoid this airport at all costs. I flew twice internationally through Newark and both times were horrible. The airport is overcrowded and seems to be in a constant state of chaos. It was particularly irritating to sit waiting in the terminal and to have to hear general announcements over the PA system every thirty seconds. Customs is unbelievably bad - it seems that you have to walk a mile just to get from the plane to the customs area and then you have to wait forever for the arrogant and rude customs agents. Everything seems to be broken or in shabby conditions the whole airport just inspires the desire to leave but of course it also has one of the worst on- time records of any airport in the US.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Mark Porter
content: Worst airport ever! After a long flight from London we had to queue 2 hours to get through passport control there was insufficient staff to handle the volume of passengers. After 2 hours to get our passports checked we had missed our connecting flight to Latin America. The airline flew us from Newark to Houston we had to pay $280 for a hotel overnight as airport booked and got a morning flight. With extra cab fares and hotel $300 out of pocket tired after 3 flights to get from London to Panama City and a day lost- all because Newark can't get organised. Note to United Airlines I would get out of Newark as a hub. I won't fly via that airport again staff are unhelpful it has an air of chaos and a insufficient staff. No wifi to communicate delay had to go to Starbucks. Steer clear of Newark especially if connecting to another flight!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: S I'Anson
content: We landed here from UK following a 3 hour flight delay. The staff were rude and disinterested being told not to stop and keep moving like cattle being led to slaughter but in particular the horrible immigration control officer checking our passports. He was slumped back in the chair and 'arrogant' is too soft a word to describe his attitude. There was no greeting - he mumbled '4 fingers right hand' meaning you had to put your fingers onto the scanner then took a photo without requesting you look at the camera - assuming you were expected to know to do this. When my husband drew his attention to the mission statement on the front of the kiosk to his right which quoted you would be 'cordially greeted into the country' he was not aware of its presence. On going round to check it his retort was in essence if we expected pleasantries we should have used that kiosk instead - absolutely disgraceful and not an endearing first experience of America. On showing our immigration card at the next desk what a surprise we were pulled for security checking - our penance perhaps for speaking out at the previous kiosk. On leaving the area there was no signage displaying where to go so we were yelled at by another rude man who clearly felt that even having never been to the airport previously we should have had knowledge of it's layout. If NYC expects tourists to adhere to their tipping policy which is required to be factored into your spending money then a better level of greeting into the country in the first instance would go a long way to ensuring this. The return journey was not as bad with security staff being quite humorous and the staff at check in were quite helpful after the baggage self check in scanner failed to print off all our luggage labels or boarding cards. Would probably travel to this airport again if needed to having experienced it once and being prepared as to what to expect just not a very pleasant first experience.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: W Geist
content: This is an awful airport. The workers on the ground are disinterested in helping travelers. The TSA agents are useless and rude. The airport itself has horrible signage and difficult to navigate unless you have been here before. The bathrooms are dirty beyond belief especially for a major hub. The fixtures are in need of overhaul. I came in from Calgary and the first thing I saw getting off the plane was some nasty stains over the wall and carpet and half of the seat having rips and tears in them. Welcome to NJ!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: F Weiss
content: I arrived at terminal A with no idea where I was or how I was going to get to another terminal to catch my connecting flight. I looked but was unable to find an Information Center or Directional Signs so I stopped members of a flight crew walking by who pointed out the elevator I needed to take to get to a bus which would get me where I needed to be. When we arrived at the correct terminal located in an industrial-looking area the driver instructed me to walk up a metal staircase. At the top of the stairs sat an employee of my airline. I showed him my boarding pass he told me the gate number had been changed and I set off to find my way there. Upon arrival at the new gate I was surprised to see no airline employees at the desk and no other passengers waiting. Ten minutes before my connecting flight was to leave I walked across the terminal again showed my boarding pass only to be told the gate had been changed again. The employee berated me for not listening to the announcements which I don't remember hearing then showed me how I could quickly get to the correct gate. When I asked why the electronic sign for my airline did not show the third gate change I was told the City of Newark is responsible for those signs not the airport or the airline. Horrible experience! I will never fly there again!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: R McLean
content: I've travelled business class all over the world for business and leisure and Newark is by far the worst travelling experience I have had. Checking in and being directed to the economy queue (despite showing the uninterested services persons pass clearly showing it was business class I waited for 30 minutes to get through security rendering me late to dial into a meeting for work. The reason I travel business is that I am a busy person and speedily moving through security is a necessity. The lounge is crowded not clean and does not have the usual amenities that I would expect from a business class lounge. I can't stress heavily enough that people should not travel through Newark if it can be avoided.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Allan Poulter
content: This was the worst experience in 40 years of air travel. Three wide body jets landed within minutes of each other. All were directed to three baggage carousels in the same room. That is around a thousand people. There were 2 customs agents to check the customs forms for this group. It took over an hour to get through two disinterested slobs who would not even make eye contact! Three other customs agents were standing around having a conversation while people were yelling that they would miss connections. They ignored the passengers and left one airport worker to try and form an orderly line which was an impossible task. They just laughed among themselves. I ended up stranded in the airport for hours because United had a computer outage and cancelled my flight 6 hours before the departure and arbitrarily booked me on a flight for the following day that would have taken me on a tour of domestic airports that was longer than the transatlantic flight I had arrived on and I was only going to Savannah GA! I had three small beers and a salad in a Mexican restaurant for $46! Customer service by United was beyond abysmal. Two service agents in the lost baggage dept to sort out all the people who were stranded due to missed connections and the normal lost baggage passengers. The Immigration and Customs people need a lesson in work ethic and manners. They just looked bored and disinterested. If they are the first thing tourists see of the United States of America they wont be coming back.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Marina Shemesh
content: This was the worst experience in an airport. It took us more than an hour at passport control. The staff were yelling at people there were not enough agents checking passports lines moved very slowly. They explained that many United Airlines flights had landed at the same time. Why couldn't they have more agents in place knowing they will have more people? It was a big mess. Very disappointing.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: M Beiner
content: My wife and I call Newark the pit of despair. My mom lives in NJ and we fly there from St. Louis several times a year. Each and every time we fly there we have an issue. Long lines rude TSA employees long delays cancelled flights etc. Southwest only has a few gates in the A Terminal gates A10-A18. This has to be the worst terminal ever. Long walk to the gate and once you get there you are in an overcrowded hell hole. There is one bathroom for tons of people and the food "court" is a joke. Then we go through the process of waiting to get on the plane sitting on the plane sitting on the runway before finally taking off usually 2-4 hours late.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: R Loehr
content: Flew United into and out of Newark. What a disorganized mess. I felt like I was in a third world country. Use any other airport and airline!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: D Wong
content: It's been a long time since I flew out of Newark and this was a connecting flight from DCA (National Airport). The terminal C is not the most user friendly in terms of amenities. The choices of restaurants were pitiful and there isn't enough restrooms to handle the passengers and the inbound flights. The two restrooms I went to had no paper towels to dry your hands and the lines were long (for a men's restroom). Reading from other posts thank goodness I didn't have to check-in at the counter or go thru security.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Pascal Gienger
content: I waited for a friend in the international arrival section of Terminal C and the only shop they offer there is a small Starbucks outlet and no chairs and no benches. Nothing. The friend told me that immigration was fast and smooth better than at JFK. For those who want to go to New York City: There is a local NJ transit bus number 62 available at the public bus curb which goes directly to Newark Penn Station and from there you can use PATH directly to World Trade Center - or to Christopher St 9th 14th 23th and 33rd Street in Manhattan with 1 transfer. Total cost $4.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Ken Wilkins
content: A dreadful airport to go through the thinking seems to be that the more the passenger can be put through oppressively long queues the less chance there will be of an incident occurring. Firstly the wait at the BA check in was about an hour with only 3 desks open higher classes of travel had their own check in desks and the staff there were largely unemployed. Heathrow took five minutes. The wait to go through security was about 40 minutes there was only one desk with one officer and three belts Heathrow has approximately twenty belts and a myriad of security officers and again took five minutes. Another officer did come to help the one on her own but all too late and it looked very inefficient indeed it was also unsafe and I saw a large bottle of water go through on someone's hand baggage that went unchallenged. Signage was also inaccurate telling you to remove your shoes and belt but nothing about wallets pockets etc therefore time was wasted in operatives repeatedly having to get customers to rectify their mistakes they were also rude and overbearing in their manner. This airport is a throwback to the 1970's with staff who have a real attitude problem. Once through security we were charged over 20 dollars for two small lagers. Overall an awful experience.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: S Ruiz
content: Worst airport. When I arrived had to walk for a long time with luggage to the train. Train took 20 min to show up. I arrived to check in desk 42 min before departure and AA clerk did not even make eye contact just babbled something in her mouth and proceeded to inform me that I missed my flight. Was not nice or friendly. I missed my two flights had to beg for help and ended up in another completely different airport.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: A Mehta
content: How can anyone say anything good about this airport! Arrived in Terminal A - long slow and narrow walk to the baggage claim. Then had to go to Terminal B to catch an international flight. It took 6 elevator rides a train and a lot of walking with all our luggage to change the terminal. Queuing was terrible at check-in mainly because the airport does not have any room. Security was backed up and yet only 2 of the many counters were open. It took 45 minutes to go through the security. Food court is a joke. Extremely rude staff. On top of it the airport is old and dingy.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Jonathan Salim
content: The airport screening process took way too long. The longest screening queue that I ever encounter during my travel in US and Canada. Not enough TSA officers on ground to help out with the screening process.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: C Satak
content: This airport cannot handle any kind of traffic. I arrived from Miami at midnight went to the taxi line and the wait was 90 minutes. I have never experienced anything like this. I will never fly into Newark again.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Sonya Snyder
content: When I departed this airport the wait in security was long at least 45 min. To add insult to injury we had to endure listening to the airport employees repeatedly shout instructions for security procedures. Employees were also incredibly unfriendly to those who could not speak English very well as they didn't understand instructions. I'm sure it's annoying when passengers don't listen to instructions however a friendlier more polite atmosphere would be a great improvement. I am American but live in Norway and was extremely embarrassed by my countrymen's behaviour and poor quality of service.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Gregory Cleaver
content: Used Terminal B for BA departure. What a horrible airport! The layout is extremely confusing. There doesn't seem to be a general flow in direction where you move in one general direction. First have to go downstairs to check in which strangely is also mixed up with baggage reclaim and then go back up where you start when you enter the airport for security. Check-in area is stuck in the 20th century people needed to transfer baggage from scales to the conveyor belt. There is also a horrible fast-food stench that fills the building. Security is also painfully slow despite short lines. Building also poorly ventilated. Lack of any restaurants over priced duty-free and 8 gates crammed together so much that there is a shocking lack of seating. Only positive is that the airport is very well linked with Air Train Newark but other than that not the best way to leave New York/Jersey.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: J Becker
content: The employees at Newark were holding the line from going into the security checkpoint area creating a gap of sorts between the checkpoint and the rest of the line which stretched past numerous shops and restaurants and even into the ticketing area. I watched as several people walked right past the long line and into the checkpoint line ignoring the fact that they were cutting in front of a large group of people. The employees could not be bothered to ask them not to do so. I even saw one family start talking to the employee joking around and laughing and she just with a wink sent them into the security checkpoint line without making them stand in line. Security took forever the employees were aggressive and rude. Once into the terminal area things went as per usual but Newark needs to shape up their employees. Saw some electrical outlet spots for people to plug in which I know everybody appreciates these days.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Ian Hateley
content: Myself and my wife recently travelled via Newark. The arrival and process through immigration was pretty slick. The return however was not the best advert for an international airport. Check in was a trip from the top where the affluent are served. Economy is now a farce of a DIY job where you have to self check in and answer questions that appear on a screen. There are still as many staff as the process is painfully slow and poorly signed. Once we had completed the process the most ridiculous part is that you walk to the side of the area and leave your bags in the middle of the concourse next to a full baggage trolley completely open to anyone. There were at least 50 bags just left on the floor. Given the machine asks at check in if you packed the bag yourself and could it have been tampered with this makes a joke of security. There was no employee near the bags just a trolley. I also had a baggage receipt but could have easily walked off with anyone else's bag. Equally I could have not checked my bag and made a claim. We recently travelled to the Maldives and Male was far better organised for a tiny airport using open trolleys. When I arrived in Birmingham the lock was cut off and thrown inside my case it clearly had been opened and gone through but had no inspection tag. This system is a mess the floor area is unmarked unmanned or segregated/sterile. If you had to drop your bag on a conveyer it would be far better and safer. The security point is not much better my wife managed to leave a full bottle of water in the outer side pocket of her rucksack which went unnoticed through the scanner. The banter of the staff to each other shows minimal care and supervised management.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Paranj Kalyani
content: Arrived from Bombay at around 11 in the morning. Short walk to the immigration area which was bustling with passengers but the queues were handled so efficiently that I was actually amazed. There must have been about 300 passengers and I was done with immigration in about 15 minutes! If that is not perfection I don't know what is! Baggage claim was a little slow but nothing horrible. Didn't get time to check out the other facilities and haven't departed from here but I wouldn't mind arriving to Newark again. Definitely a pleasant experience!

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: Sam Hus
content: Flew to Newark Terminal C on United from Heathrow. It was the smoothest clearance of immigration and customs I have experienced in the US. I was literally out of the plane and in New York Penn Station in 1 hour.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: J Harvey-Hills
content: We flew into Newark Terminal B arriving at 7pm on a Thursday evening on the British Airways flight from London Heathrow. The terminal seemed perfectly adequate. There were no queues at immigration and luggage arrived quickly. Nor did we have to walk a million miles from plane to arrivals. We were at our hotel in Manhattan at 8.30pm. One thing to note if taking a cab is that the toll for the tunnel from NJ to Manhattan is USD 13 which adds to the cost. We have not departed from Newark.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: R Turnley
content: I feel exactly as the previous writers. Newark was a great airport to avoid the long waits at JFK but now it has got so much worse than JFK that I put it in the same basket as LAX and MIA. There are never enough people working on immigration the United lounges offer little peace or comfort and there seem to be always problems with delays on planes leaving or arriving. Maybe the airport has simply outgrown itself.

title: Newark Airport customer review
author: B Marcus
content: I have been using this airport for many years now and I am starting to dislike the place.
